subspace `X ⊆ X'`, for `a : X ⟶ Y` over `B`.  The sheaf of lifts it acts on is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.liftsSubfunctor` taken at the underlying morphism of presheaves
`a.hom`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def liftActionSheaf (Z : ClosedSubspaces C S hS X'.1) (q : Y ⟶ B)
    (a : (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) ⟶ Y) :
    Modules.{u, u + 1} C S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.2.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_liftActionSheafChart_addAction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 061D], the action.** Let `X ⊂ X'` be a first order thickening of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `p : X' ⟶ B` and `q : Y ⟶ B`, and let `a : X ⟶ Y`. The sheaf
`SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(a^*Ω_{Y/B}, 𝒞_{X/X'})`, read on the étale charts of `X'`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.liftActionSheafChart`), acts on the sheaf of lifts
`U' ↦ {a' : U' ⟶ Y over B with a'|_U = a|_U}` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.liftsSubfunctor`):

* for every chart `U'` the sections of the acting sheaf over `U'` act additively on the lifts
  over `U'` (`AddAction`: `0 · a' = a'` and `(θ₁ + θ₂) · a' = θ₁ · (θ₂ · a')`);
* the action commutes with the restriction maps of the two sheaves along every morphism of
  charts `U'' ⟶ U'`, so it is an action of the sheaf on the sheaf;
* it is the action of [Stacks Project, Tag 0CK6]: on every chart `m : T ⟶ U'` on which `a'`
  factors through an affine chart `ε : T ⟶ Q` of `Y` carrying an affine chart diagram over `B`,
  `θ · a'` factors through `Q` by a morphism `ψ` whose map of regular functions is
  `x ↦ ε^♯ x + ι_T (D x)`, where `D = θ ∘ d_{Y/B}` is the derivation of Equation (0619) read on
  the chart (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LiftChart.derivation`) and
  `ι_T : 𝒞_{X/X'}(T_X) ⟶ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` is the inclusion of the conormal module
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalChartIncl`). That is, the comorphisms of `θ · a'` and `a'`
  differ by the derivation `D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_liftActionSheafChart_addAction (hG : IsFirstOrderThickening C S hS X' G)
    (p : X' ⟶ Bs) (q : Y ⟶ Bs) (a : IsThickening.space C S hS hG.1 ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ act : ∀ U' : SmallEtale C S hS X'.1,
        AddAction ((liftActionSheafChart C S hS hG.1 q a).obj.obj (op U'))
          ((liftsSubfunctor C S hS p q a.hom).toFunctor.obj (op U')),
      (∀ {U' U'' : SmallEtale C S hS X'.1} (k : U'' ⟶ U')
          (θ : (liftActionSheafChart C S hS hG.1 q a).obj.obj (op U'))
          (x : (liftsSubfunctor C S hS p q a.hom).toFunctor.obj (op U')),
        (liftsSubfunctor C S hS p q a.hom).toFunctor.map k.op ((act U').vadd θ x) =
          (act U'').vadd ((liftActionSheafChart C S hS hG.1 q a).obj.map k.op θ)
            ((liftsSubfunctor C S hS p q a.hom).toFunctor.map k.op x)) ∧
      ∀ (U' : SmallEtale C S hS X'.1)
        (θ : (liftActionSheafChart C S hS hG.1 q a).obj.obj (op U'))
        (x : (liftsSubfunctor C S hS p q a.hom).toFunctor.obj (op U'))
        (T : SmallEtale C S hS X'.1) (m : T ⟶ U') (Q : SmallEtale C S hS Y.1)
        (ε : (SmallEtale.toOver C S hS X'.1).obj T ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver C S hS Y.1).obj Q)
        (w : yoneda.map ε ≫ Q.1.hom =
          yoneda.map ((SmallEtale.toOver C S hS X'.1).map m) ≫ yonedaEquiv.symm x.1),
        HasAffineChartDiagram C S hS q Q →
        ∃ ψ : (SmallEtale.toOver C S hS X'.1).obj T ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver C S hS Y.1).obj Q,
          yoneda.map ψ ≫ Q.1.hom = yoneda.map ((SmallEtale.toOver C S hS X'.1).map m) ≫
            yonedaEquiv.symm ((act U').vadd θ x).1 ∧
          ∀ f : (structureRingSheaf C S hS Y).obj.obj (op Q),
            ((BigFppfOver.toScheme C S hS).map ψ).appTop.hom f =
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme C S hS).map ε).appTop.hom f +
                (show Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme C S hS).obj
                    ((SmallEtale.toOver C S hS X'.1).obj T), ⊤) from
                  conormalChartIncl C S hS ⟨G, hG.1.1⟩ hG T
                    ((⟨T, m, Q, ε, w⟩ : LiftChart C S hS U' (yonedaEquiv.symm x.1)).derivation
                      (Z := ⟨G, hG.1.1⟩) (p := p) (q := q) (a := a) x.2 θ f))
declarations.comment: the action of SheafHom_{O_X}(a^*Omega_{Y/B}, C_{X/X'}) on the sheaf of lifts U' ↦ {a' : U' → Y over B with a'|_U = a|_U}: an additive action on the sections over every étale chart, commuting with the restriction maps of both sheaves, under which the comorphisms of θ · a' and a' differ by the derivation d_{Y/B} ∘ θ

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.formallyEtale_iff_formallySmooth_and_formallyUnramified
registrations.comment: the same equivalence for a morphism of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_of_isEtale_square
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061H.** Let `ψ : U ⟶ V`, `u : U ⟶ X`, `v : V ⟶ Y` and `f : X ⟶ Y` be morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S` forming a commuting square. If the two vertical arrows `u` and `v`
are étale and `f` is formally smooth, then `ψ` is formally smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_of_isEtale_square
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {U V X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U) (hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (ψ : U ⟶ V) (u : U ⟶ X) (v : V ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsq : u ≫ f = ψ ≫ v)
    (hu : IsEtale B S hS u) (hv : IsEtale B S hS v)
    (hf : FormallySmooth f) :
    FormallySmooth ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyProjective_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06B5.** The sheaf of relative differentials of a formally smooth morphism of
schemes is locally projective on its source. This is **Stacks 061I** for a morphism of
algebraic spaces that is a morphism of schemes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyProjective_sheafOfDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061I.**  The sheaf of relative differentials `Ω_{X/Y}` of a formally smooth
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` is locally projective on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_sheafOfDifferentials {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : FormallySmooth f.hom) :
    IsLocallyProjective B S hS X.2
      ⟨sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f, isQuasicoherentOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.subsingleton_sheafH_one_sheafHom_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061J for an associated module.**  Let `T` be an affine scheme and let `M` be a
locally projective quasi-coherent `𝒪_T`-module.  The first cohomology of the internal hom from
the associated module `M^a` to an `𝒪`-module `𝓖` on the small étale site of `T` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_sheafH_one_sheafHom_associatedModule
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine T] (M : T.Modules)
    [M.IsQuasicoherent] (hM : Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective M)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B T hT)) [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w}
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheaf B T hT)).obj
        (sheafHom B T hT ((associatedModule B T hT).obj M) G)) 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.subsingleton_sheafH_one_sheafHom_of_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061J.**  Let `T` be an affine scheme and let `𝓕` and `𝓖` be quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of `T`.  If `𝓕` is locally projective — that is, if its
restriction to the small Zariski site of `T` is a locally projective `𝒪_T`-module, which is what
Stacks 060R defines local projectivity to mean — then the first cohomology of the internal hom
`𝓗om_𝒪(𝓕, 𝓖)` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_sheafH_one_sheafHom_of_isLocallyProjective
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine T]
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B T hT)) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hF : Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective ((restrictModule B T hT).obj F)) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w}
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheaf B T hT)).obj (sheafHom B T hT F G)) 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_tfae_etaleCharts
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_tfae_etaleCharts (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [FormallySmooth f,
      HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS (@Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme.{u}) f,
      ∃ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (ψ : U ⟶ V),
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf b ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf b ∧
        yoneda.map ψ ≫ b = a ≫ f ∧
        Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ψ)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_iff_etaleCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061K, the equivalence of (1) and (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
formally smooth exactly when the morphism of schemes underlying every commuting square of étale
scheme charts is formally smooth, granted the scheme-level implication (3) ⟹ (1) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0D0F] and the triviality of the pseudo-torsor of lifts.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_iff_etaleCharts
    (h0D0F : ∀ {X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (g : X' ⟶ Y'),
      Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothAffineLocally g → Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g)
    (hGlue : ∀ {X' Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (g : X' ⟶ Y'),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X' → IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y' →
      FormallySmoothEtaleLocally B S hS g → FormallySmooth g)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    FormallySmooth f ↔
      HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS (@Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme.{u}) f
declarations.comment: condition (2), granted Stacks 0D0F (3) ⟹ (1) and the pseudo-torsor triviality of 03AJ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_iff_surjectiveEtaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061K, the equivalence of (1) and (3).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
formally smooth exactly when there is one commuting square of étale scheme charts, both chart
maps surjective, whose underlying morphism of schemes is formally smooth, granted the
scheme-level implication (3) ⟹ (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0F] and the triviality of the
pseudo-torsor of lifts.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_iff_surjectiveEtaleChart
    (h0D0F : ∀ {X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (g : X' ⟶ Y'),
      Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothAffineLocally g → Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme g)
    (hGlue : ∀ {X' Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (g : X' ⟶ Y'),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X' → IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y' →
      FormallySmoothEtaleLocally B S hS g → FormallySmooth g)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    FormallySmooth f ↔
      ∃ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (ψ : U ⟶ V),
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf b ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty
          Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf b ∧
        yoneda.map ψ ≫ b = a ≫ f ∧
        Stacks.Smooth.FormallySmoothScheme ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ψ)
declarations.comment: condition (3), granted Stacks 0D0F (3) ⟹ (1) and the pseudo-torsor triviality of 03AJ

declarations.name: regular_sequence_localize_away_of_atPrime
declarations.doc:
Regularity of a sequence over the localization at a prime spreads out to a localization away
from some element not in the prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_sequence_localize_away_of_atPrime
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (xs : List R)
    (hp : IsRegular (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M)
      (xs.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)))) :
    ∃ g ∈ p.primeCompl,
      IsRegular (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) M)
        (xs.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away g)))

declarations.name: quasiRegularCanonicalMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map** `φ : S → T`, the `(R/J)`-linear map induced by `canonicalBilin`. On a
monomial generator it sends `X^e ⊗ m̄ ↦ (f^e · m mod J^{|e|+1}M)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasiRegularCanonicalMap {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → R) :
    Source M f →ₗ[qrRbar f] Target M f

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular
declarations.doc:
A sequence `rs = f_1, …, f_c` of elements of a commutative ring `R` is **`M`-quasi-regular**,
for an `R`-module `M`, if the canonical map of graded `(R/J)[X_1, …, X_c]`-modules
`Φ_M : (R/J)[X_1, …, X_c] ⊗_{R/J} (M/JM) → ⨁_{n ≥ 0} J^n M / J^{n+1} M`,
`X_1^{e_1} ⋯ X_c^{e_c} ⊗ m̄ ↦ f_1^{e_1} ⋯ f_c^{e_c} m mod J^{e_1 + … + e_c + 1} M`, is an
isomorphism, where `J = (f_1, …, f_c)`. An `R`-quasi-regular sequence is called simply a
*quasi-regular sequence*.
declarations.statement:
def IsQuasiRegular {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (rs : List R) : Prop

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.exists_notMem_isQuasiRegular_away_of_isQuasiRegular_atPrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061Q.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `M` a finite `R`-module, `𝔭 ⊂ R` a prime and
`rs = x₁, …, x_c` a sequence of elements of `R` whose image in `R_𝔭` is `M_𝔭`-quasi-regular. Then
there is a `g ∈ R`, `g ∉ 𝔭`, such that the image of `rs` in `R_g` is `M_g`-quasi-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_notMem_isQuasiRegular_away_of_isQuasiRegular_atPrime {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (rs : List R) (Rₚ : Type*) [CommRing Rₚ] [Algebra R Rₚ]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rₚ p] (Mₚ : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mₚ] [Module R Mₚ] [Module Rₚ Mₚ]
    [IsScalarTower R Rₚ Mₚ] (fₚ : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ) [IsLocalizedModule p.primeCompl fₚ]
    (hp : IsQuasiRegular Mₚ (rs.map (algebraMap R Rₚ))) :
    ∃ g ∉ p,
      ∀ (Rg : Type*) [CommRing Rg] [Algebra R Rg] [IsLocalization.Away g Rg] (Mg : Type*)
        [AddCommGroup Mg] [Module R Mg] [Module Rg Mg] [IsScalarTower R Rg Mg] (fg : M →ₗ[R] Mg)
        [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) fg],
        IsQuasiRegular Mg (rs.map (algebraMap R Rg))

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular.quasiRegular_drop_mod_prev
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061R.** Let `M` be a module over a commutative ring `R` and let `rs = f_1, …, f_c` be
an `M`-quasi-regular sequence in `R`. For any `i`, the images `f̄_{i+1}, …, f̄_c` of the remaining
elements in `R̄ = R/(f_1, …, f_i)` form an `M̄`-quasi-regular sequence, where
`M̄ = M/(f_1, …, f_i)M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsQuasiRegular.quasiRegular_drop_mod_prev {R M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {rs : List R} (reg : IsQuasiRegular M rs) (i : ℕ) :
    IsQuasiRegular (M ⧸ (Ideal.ofList (rs.take i) • ⊤ : Submodule R M))
      ((rs.drop i).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.ofList (rs.take i))))

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular.of_isQuasiRegular_of_mem_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 061S.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local Noetherian ring and let `M` be a nonzero finite
`R`-module. An `M`-quasi-regular sequence `f_1, …, f_c` of elements of `𝔪` is an `M`-regular
sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegular.of_isQuasiRegular_of_mem_maximalIdeal {R M : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Nontrivial M]
    [Module.Finite R M] {rs : List R} (mem : ∀ r ∈ rs, r ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (reg : IsQuasiRegular M rs) : IsRegular M rs

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.IsGradedCommutative
declarations.doc:
A grading on a ring is *graded-commutative* when two homogeneous elements
commute unless both degrees are odd, in which case they anticommute.
declarations.statement:
public class IsGradedCommutative {ι : Type w} [Semiring ι]
    [DecidablePred (Odd : ι → Prop)] {A : Type u} [Ring A]
    {S : Type v} [Membership A S] (𝒜 : ι → S) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.IsStrictlyGradedCommutative
declarations.doc:
A grading is *strictly graded-commutative* when it is graded-commutative and
every homogeneous element of odd degree has square zero.
declarations.statement:
public class IsStrictlyGradedCommutative {ι : Type w} [Semiring ι]
    [DecidablePred (Odd : ι → Prop)] {A : Type u} [Ring A]
    {S : Type v} [Membership A S] (𝒜 : ι → S) extends IsGradedCommutative 𝒜

declarations.name: CochainComplex.Tor.exists_spectral_sequences_tor_homology_and_terms
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a bounded-below chain complex of `R`-modules and let `M` be an `R`-module. There
is a bounded-below free resolution `P` of `M`, and the two filtrations of `K ⊗[R] P` give
spectral sequences abutting to its homology.

The first has second page `Torⱼᴿ(Hᵢ(K), M)` and differential of bidegree `(1, -2)`. The second
has first page `Torⱼᴿ(Kᵢ, M)`; under the displayed identifications, its first differential is
the map on Tor induced by `Kᵢ ⟶ Kᵢ₋₁`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_spectral_sequences_tor_homology_and_terms
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, a < i → IsZero (K.X i))
    (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    let K' := ((ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{max u w, v} R).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K
    let M' := (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{max u v, w} R).obj M
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) ℤ),
      ∃ (ε : P ⟶ (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj M')
        (_ : QuasiIso ε),
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧
      Nonempty (P.homology 0 ≅ M') ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → IsZero (P.homology i)) ∧
      ∃ (E : FirstTorSpectralSequence (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R))
        (E' : SecondTorSpectralSequence (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R))
        (_e₂ : ∀ i j : ℤ, (E.page 2).X (i, j) ≅ TorInDegree.{u, max v w} R j (K'.homology (-i)) M')
        (e₁ : ∀ i j : ℤ, (E'.page 1).X (i, j) ≅ TorInDegree.{u, max v w} R j (K'.X (-i)) M'),
        let T := HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor K' P (moduleTensorBifunctor.{u, max v w} R)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
        ∃ (F F' : HomologicalFiltration T)
          (S : TorFiltrationData E F false)
          (S' : TorFiltrationData E' F' true),
          F.step = tensorFiltrationSteps.{u, max v w} R K' P false ∧
          F'.step = tensorFiltrationSteps.{u, max v w} R K' P true ∧
          (∀ n, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ F.step a n = ⊥ ∧ F.step b n = ⊤) ∧
          (∀ n, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ F'.step a n = ⊥ ∧ F'.step b n = ⊤) ∧
          S.Converges ∧ S'.Converges ∧
          ∀ i j : ℤ,
            (e₁ i j).inv ≫ (E'.page 1).d (i, j) (i - 1, j) ≫ (e₁ (i - 1) j).hom =
              torInDegreeMap.{u, max v w} R j (K'.d (-i) (-(i - 1))) M'

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorBaseChange.exists_tor_base_change_spectral_sequence
declarations.doc:
If `A → B` and the `B`-modules `M` and `N` are flat over `A`, then for
`B' = B ⊗[A] A'`, `M' = M ⊗[B] B'`, and `N' = N ⊗[B] B'`, there is a homological spectral sequence
`Torᴬᵢ(Torᴮⱼ(M, N), A') ⇒ Torᴮʳᵢ₊ⱼ(M', N')`.

Both sides are viewed as `A`-modules in order to state the spectral sequence in one abelian
category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_tor_base_change_spectral_sequence
    (A B A' : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A']
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A'] (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v} B)
    [Module.Flat A B]
    [Module.Flat A ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).obj M)]
    [Module.Flat A ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).obj N)] :
    ∃ (E : CochainComplex.Tor.FirstTorSpectralSequence (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
      (_e₂ : ∀ i j : ℤ,
        (E.page 2).X (i, j) ≅
          @CochainComplex.Tor.TorInDegree.{u, v} A _ j
            (restrictScalars A B
              (@CochainComplex.Tor.TorInDegree.{u, v} B _ i M N))
            (restrictScalars A A' (@regularModule.{u, v} A' _))),
      CochainComplex.Tor.HomologicalSpectralSequenceAbutsTo E
        (fun n ↦
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
            (algebraMap A (BaseChangedAlgebra A B A'))).obj
            (@CochainComplex.Tor.TorInDegree.{u, v} (BaseChangedAlgebra A B A') _ n
              (@baseChange.{u, v} A B A' _ _ _ _ _ M)
              (@baseChange.{u, v} A B A' _ _ _ _ _ N)))

declarations.name: Koszul.differentialGradedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The Koszul differential graded algebra `K•(φ)`: its underlying graded algebra is
the exterior algebra `⋀[R] E`, and its differential is contraction by `φ`.

The chain complex obtained from its homogeneous pieces is `Koszul.complex φ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def differentialGradedAlgebra (φ : E →ₗ[R] R) :
    HomologicalDifferentialGradedExteriorAlgebra φ

declarations.name: Koszul.seqDual
declarations.doc:
The functional `Rʳ →ₗ[R] R` attached to a sequence `f₁, …, f_r` of elements of `R`,
namely `v ↦ ∑ i, vᵢ * fᵢ`; it sends the `i`-th standard basis vector to `fᵢ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def seqDual (f : Fin r → R) : Module.Dual R (Fin r → R)

declarations.name: Koszul.seqComplex
declarations.doc:
The Koszul complex `K_•(f₁, …, f_r)` of a sequence of elements of `R`: the Koszul
complex of the functional `Koszul.seqDual f` on `Rʳ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def seqComplex (f : Fin r → R) : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℕ

declarations.name: koszul_map_comm
declarations.doc:
**Functoriality of the Koszul complex.**

Let `φ : E → R` and `φ' : E' → R` be `R`-module maps and let `ψ : E → E'` be an `R`-module
map with `φ' ∘ ψ = φ`. Then the induced graded-algebra homomorphism `∧(ψ)` commutes with the
Koszul differentials, i.e. `∧(ψ) ∘ d = d' ∘ ∧(ψ)`, where `d = Koszul.contraction φ` and
`d' = Koszul.contraction φ'`. Together with the fact that `∧(ψ) = ExteriorAlgebra.map ψ` is
automatically a unital graded `R`-algebra homomorphism, this exhibits `∧(ψ)` as a homomorphism
of differential graded `R`-algebras `K_•(φ) → K_•(φ')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem koszul_map_comm (φ : Module.Dual R E) (φ' : Module.Dual R E') (ψ : E →ₗ[R] E')
    (h : φ'.comp ψ = φ) (x : ExteriorAlgebra R E) :
    exteriorMap ψ (Koszul.contraction φ x) = Koszul.contraction φ' (exteriorMap ψ x)

declarations.name: Koszul.seqComplex_mulVec_iso
declarations.doc:
**Change of basis for a Koszul complex.** If `x` is an invertible `r × r` matrix over `R`, then
the Koszul complex of `f` is isomorphic to the Koszul complex of the sequence
`i ↦ ∑ j, x i j * f j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem seqComplex_mulVec_iso {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → R) (x : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R)
    (hx : IsUnit x) :
    Nonempty (Koszul.seqComplex f ≅ Koszul.seqComplex (Matrix.mulVec x f))

declarations.name: koszul_scalar_eq_homotopy
declarations.doc:
**Multiplication by `φ e` is null-homotopic on the Koszul complex.** Let `φ : E → R` be an
`R`-module map, let `e ∈ E`, and set `f = φ e`. As `R`-linear endomorphisms of
`K_•(φ) = ∧(E)`, `f = d ∘ e + e ∘ d`, i.e. for every `a`, `f • a = d (e ∧ a) + e ∧ d a`, where
`e ∧ -` is left multiplication by `ι R e` in the exterior algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem koszul_scalar_eq_homotopy (φ : Module.Dual R E) (e : E)
    (a : ExteriorAlgebra R E) :
    φ e • a =
      Koszul.contraction φ (ExteriorAlgebra.ι R e * a)
        + ExteriorAlgebra.ι R e * Koszul.contraction φ a

registrations.name: HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.d_fstX
registrations.comment: first projection of the mapping-cone differential

registrations.name: HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.d_sndX
registrations.comment: second projection of the mapping-cone differential

declarations.name: Stacks.MappingCone.NatIndexed.koszulComplex_phiPrime_iso_cone
declarations.doc:
The cone of multiplication by `f` on the Koszul complex of `phi` is isomorphic, as a chain
complex of `R`-modules, to the Koszul complex of `phi' : E ⊕ R → R`, by an isomorphism with the
prescribed components `Θₙ`: the inclusion on the `⋀ⁿ E` summand and wedging with `e₀ = (0,1)` on
the `⋀^{n-1} E` summand.
declarations.statement:
theorem koszulComplex_phiPrime_iso_cone (φ : Module.Dual R E) (f : R) :
    ∃ Θ : coneComplex (Koszul.complex φ) (Koszul.complex φ) (mulByF (Koszul.complex φ) f) ≅
        Koszul.complex (phiPrime φ f),
      (∀ x : (⋀[R]^0 E),
        (Θ.hom.f 0).hom (show ((Koszul.complex φ).X 0 : Type (max u v)) from x) = inclPow 0 x) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (b : (⋀[R]^(n+1) E)) (a : (⋀[R]^n E)),
        (Θ.hom.f (n+1)).hom
            (show ((Koszul.complex φ).X (n+1) × (Koszul.complex φ).X n : Type (max u v))
              from (b, a))
          = inclPow (n+1) b + wedgeE0Pow (n+1) a)

declarations.name: Koszul.seqComplex_snoc_iso_cone
declarations.doc:
The Koszul complex of a sequence obtained by appending `a` is isomorphic to the cone of
multiplication by `a` on the Koszul complex of the original sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem seqComplex_snoc_iso_cone {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → R) (a : R) :
    Nonempty
      (Koszul.seqComplex (Fin.snoc f a) ≅
        Stacks.MappingCone.NatIndexed.coneComplex (Koszul.seqComplex f) (Koszul.seqComplex f)
          (Stacks.MappingCone.NatIndexed.mulByF (Koszul.seqComplex f) a))

declarations.name: Koszul.exists_homotopyEquiv_mappingCone_comp
declarations.doc:
The cone of a composite of two endomorphisms is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a map
from the shifted cone of the first endomorphism to the cone of the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopyEquiv_mappingCone_comp
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C]
    [HasBinaryBiproducts C]
    (A : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f g : A ⟶ A) :
    ∃ (φ : (CochainComplex.mappingCone f)⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶
        CochainComplex.mappingCone g),
      Nonempty
        (HomotopyEquiv (CochainComplex.mappingCone (g ≫ f))
          (CochainComplex.mappingCone φ))

declarations.name: Koszul.exists_homotopyEquiv_koszulComplex_coprod_mul_mappingCone
declarations.doc:
After adjoining `f * g` to a linear functional, its Koszul complex is homotopy equivalent to
the mapping cone of a map from the shifted complex obtained by adjoining `f` to the complex
obtained by adjoining `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopyEquiv_koszulComplex_coprod_mul_mappingCone
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {E : Type v} [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (φ : E →ₗ[R] R) (f g : R) :
    let K (a : R) : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ :=
      (ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat.extendFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)).obj
        (Koszul.complex (φ.coprod (a • LinearMap.id)))
    ∃ ψ : (K f)⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ K g,
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv (K (f * g)) (CochainComplex.mappingCone ψ))

declarations.name: Koszul.exists_homotopyEquiv_koszulComplex_snoc_mul_mappingCone
declarations.doc:
The Koszul complex on a finite sequence ending in `f * g` is homotopy equivalent to the mapping
cone of a map from the shifted complex ending in `f` to the complex ending in `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopyEquiv_koszulComplex_snoc_mul_mappingCone
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → R) (f g : R) :
    let K (a : R) : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ :=
      (ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat.extendFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj
        (Koszul.complex (Fintype.linearCombination R (Fin.snoc s a)))
    ∃ ψ : (K f)⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ K g,
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv (K (f * g)) (CochainComplex.mappingCone ψ))

declarations.name: Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn
declarations.doc:
A sequence `f₁, …, f_r` is `M`-Koszul-regular if `Hᵢ(K_•(f) ⊗_R M) = 0` for all
`i ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: def IsKoszulRegularOn (f : Fin r → R) (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Koszul.IsH1RegularOn
declarations.doc: A sequence `f₁, …, f_r` is `M`-`H₁`-regular if `H₁(K_•(f) ⊗_R M) = 0`.
declarations.statement: def IsH1RegularOn (f : Fin r → R) (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Koszul.IsKoszulRegular
declarations.doc: A sequence `f₁, …, f_r` is Koszul-regular if `Hᵢ(K_•(f)) = 0` for all `i ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: def IsKoszulRegular (f : Fin r → R) : Prop

declarations.name: Koszul.IsH1Regular
declarations.doc: A sequence `f₁, …, f_r` is `H₁`-regular if `H₁(K_•(f)) = 0`.
declarations.statement: def IsH1Regular (f : Fin r → R) : Prop

declarations.name: Koszul.isKoszulRegularOn_and_isKoszulRegular_of_regular
declarations.doc:
If every term of a finite sequence acts injectively on the quotient of `M` by its predecessors,
then the sequence is `M`-Koszul-regular. In particular, an `M`-regular sequence is
`M`-Koszul-regular, and a regular sequence in `R` is Koszul-regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularOn_and_isKoszulRegular_of_regular
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {r : ℕ} {f : Fin r → R} :
    (RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular M (List.ofFn f) →
        Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn f M) ∧
      (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M (List.ofFn f) →
        Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn f M) ∧
      (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R (List.ofFn f) →
        Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)

declarations.name: Koszul.isH1RegularOn_and_isKoszulRegularOn_snoc_mul
declarations.doc:
Adjoining a product to a finite sequence preserves both `M`-`H₁`-regularity and
`M`-Koszul-regularity when adjoining each factor separately has the corresponding property.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularOn_and_isKoszulRegularOn_snoc_mul
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → R) (f g : R) :
    ((Koszul.IsH1RegularOn (Fin.snoc s f) M ∧
        Koszul.IsH1RegularOn (Fin.snoc s g) M) →
      Koszul.IsH1RegularOn (Fin.snoc s (f * g)) M) ∧
    ((Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn (Fin.snoc s f) M ∧
        Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn (Fin.snoc s g) M) →
      Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn (Fin.snoc s (f * g)) M)

declarations.name: KoszulC.isH1Regular_baseChange
declarations.doc:
For a flat ring map `φ : R → S`, if `f_1, ..., f_r` is `M`-`H_1`-regular over `R`, then
`φ(f_1), ..., φ(f_r)` is `(S ⊗_R M)`-`H_1`-regular over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1Regular_baseChange {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.Flat R S] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hf : IsH1RegularOn f M) :
    IsH1RegularOn (R := S) (fun i => algebraMap R S (f i)) (S ⊗[R] M)

declarations.name: KoszulC.isKoszulRegular_baseChange
declarations.doc:
For a flat ring map `φ : R → S`, if `f_1, ..., f_r` is `M`-Koszul-regular over `R`, then
`φ(f_1), ..., φ(f_r)` is `(S ⊗_R M)`-Koszul-regular over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegular_baseChange {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.Flat R S] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hf : IsKoszulRegularOn f M) :
    IsKoszulRegularOn (R := S) (fun i => algebraMap R S (f i)) (S ⊗[R] M)

declarations.name: Koszul.isQuasiRegular_of_isH1RegularOn
declarations.doc: **Stacks 062I.** An `M`-`H₁`-regular sequence is `M`-quasi-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiRegular_of_isH1RegularOn
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {r : ℕ} {f : Fin r → R} (hf : Koszul.IsH1RegularOn f M) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular M (List.ofFn f)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.koszulDifferentialGradedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**The Koszul complex `K_•(φ)` of an `O`-module map `φ : F → O`, as a sheaf of differential
graded algebras.** This is Stacks tag 062K. Its underlying graded algebra is the exterior algebra
`⋀(F)` of Section 17.21, read with the grading negated because the complex of a sheaf of
differential graded algebras is a cochain complex while the Koszul differential lowers the
exterior degree; that is
`SheafOfModules.koszulDifferentialGradedAlgebra_toGradedAlgebra`, and `⋀(F)` has the universal
property of the exterior algebra on `F` by
`SheafOfModules.isExteriorAlgebra_sheafifiedExteriorAlgebra`, which is item (1) of the tag. Its
differential is the Koszul differential of `φ`, which is the unique graded derivation of `⋀(F)`
taking a degree-one local section `e` to `φ(e)`
(`SheafOfModules.existsUnique_koszulDerivation`), which is item (2). The tag calls the result a
*commutative* differential graded algebra; `SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedAlgebra` is Stacks
tag 0FRF's notion and carries no commutativity axiom, and graded commutativity of `⋀(F)` is
`SheafOfModules.sheafifiedExteriorMul_comm`.

`SheafOfModules.ringedSpaceKoszulDifferentialGradedAlgebra` is the specialization to a ringed
space, which is the generality the tag is stated in.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def koszulDifferentialGradedAlgebra :
    DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{w, w} (toRingCat J Osharp)

declarations.name: PresheafOfModules.seqExteriorFunctional
declarations.doc:
**The functional `(f₁, …, f_r) : O^{⊕ r} → O`.** Over each object it is the ring-level
`Koszul.seqDual` of the family of sections restricted there.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def seqExteriorFunctional {r : ℕ} (f : Sequence O r) :
    ExteriorFunctional.{v, u, w, w} (finFree O r)
declarations.comment: the morphism `(f₁, …, f_r) : O^{⊕ r} → O` the Koszul complex is attached to, not the complex itself

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SeqKoszul.sheafComplex
declarations.doc:
**`K_•(O_X, f₁, …, f_r)` as a chain complex of sheaves of modules.** In degree `n` it is the
sheaf of exterior powers `U ↦ ⋀^n_{O_X(U)}(O_X(U)^r)` and the differential is contraction by
`(f₁, …, f_r)`. This is the complex whose acyclicity in positive degrees is Koszul-regularity of
the family, in the sense of Stacks tag 063D.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sheafComplex : ChainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X)) ℕ
declarations.comment: the complex `K_•(O_X, f₁, …, f_r)` itself, on a ringed space and as a chain complex of sheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundle
declarations.doc:
A vector bundle over `S`: a cone whose direct-image algebra is generated in degree one in the
strongest sense, namely that every canonical map `Sym^n(ℰ_1) ⟶ ℰ_n` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: structure VectorBundle (S : Scheme.{u}) extends AbstractCone S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundle.category
declarations.doc:
Vector bundles over a fixed base form a category, with the morphisms of the underlying
cones as its morphisms.
declarations.statement: instance category : Category (VectorBundle S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundle.degreeOneEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The category of vector bundles over a scheme `S` is anti-equivalent to the category of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules.

The anti-equivalence is recorded in the contravariant form `(VectorBundle S)ᵒᵖ ≌ QCoh(𝒪_S)`, the
functor being `V ↦ (π_* 𝒪_V)_1` and its quasi-inverse `ℰ ↦ 𝐕(ℰ) = Spec_S(Sym(ℰ))`. Of the two
standard forms of an anti-equivalence this is the one with the opposite taken on the *geometric*
side, which is the side the source's two functors are contravariant on, and it is the form of
Tag 01SA's `(AffineOver S)ᵒᵖ ≌ QuasicoherentAlgebra S` that this one restricts.
declarations.statement:
def degreeOneEquivalence (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    (VectorBundle S)ᵒᵖ ≌ Scheme.QuasicoherentModules S
declarations.comment: the anti-equivalence between vector bundles over S and quasi-coherent O_S-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GradedConeAlgebra.cone
declarations.doc:
The cone, or affine cone, associated to a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra `𝒜` whose
degree-zero part is `𝒪_S`: the relative spectrum `C(𝒜) = Spec_S(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def cone : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractCone
declarations.doc:
A cone over `S`: an affine morphism whose direct-image algebra is nonnegatively graded and
has degree-zero part `𝒪_S`.
declarations.statement: public structure AbstractCone (S : Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractCone.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of cones.  The map on direct images is the pullback on functions induced by the
displayed morphism of total spaces.
declarations.statement: public structure Hom {S : Scheme.{u}} (X Y : AbstractCone S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.conormalSequenceRightMap
declarations.doc:
**The right-hand map `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of the conormal sequence of
[Stacks Project, Tag 062S].** It is the canonical map of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] attached to
the square with horizontal maps `i` and `i ≫ j` and vertical maps `𝟙_Z` and `j`, read through the
identification of the pullback along the identity with the identity functor.

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.epi_conormalSequenceRightMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 062S]: the conormal sequence is exact at `𝒞_{Z/Y}`.** For immersions
`Z ⟶ Y ⟶ X` the canonical map `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` is an epimorphism, which is the `⟶ 0` at the
right-hand end of the canonical sequence `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0`.

The defining square is cartesian by `Stacks.Immersion.conormalSequence_isPullback`, so
`Stacks.Immersion.epi_immersionConormalSheafMap` applies; the pullback-identity isomorphism is an
epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalSequenceRightMap (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] :
    Epi (conormalSequenceRightMap i j)
declarations.comment: exactness at the right term: the canonical map 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} is epi

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.conormalSequence_comp_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 062S]: the two canonical maps of the conormal sequence compose to
zero.** For immersions `Z ⟶ Y ⟶ X` the composite
`i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` vanishes.

Transposing along `i^* ⊣ i_*` turns the statement into one about sections over opens of `Y`. Over
the preimage of a chart a section of `𝒞_{Y/X}` is the class of a function `k` cutting out `Y`, the
left-hand map carries it to the class of `k` as a function cutting out `Z` in `X`, and the
right-hand map carries that to the class of the restriction of `k` to the preimage of the chart
in `Y`, which is zero because `k` vanishes there. The charts refine every open of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_comp_zero (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] :
    conormalLeftMap i j ≫ conormalSequenceRightMap i j = 0
declarations.comment: the two canonical maps form a complex: the composite i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} is zero, for any immersions i : Z ⟶ Y and j : Y ⟶ X; the left-hand map is Stacks.Immersion.conormalLeftMap, equal to Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.conormalSequenceLeftMap by Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.conormalSequenceLeftMap_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.conormalSequenceShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**The conormal sequence of [Stacks Project, Tag 062S]** as a two-term complex of
`𝒪_Z`-modules, `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}`.
declarations.statement:
def conormalSequenceShortComplex (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] :
    ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
declarations.comment: the sequence as a short complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Immersion.conormalSequence_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 062S]: the conormal sequence is exact at `𝒞_{Z/X}`.** For immersions
`Z ⟶ Y ⟶ X` the kernel of the canonical map `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` is the image of the canonical
map `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}`.

Exactness is local, and it is tested over the preimages of the charts of the chain
(`Stacks.Immersion.exact_of_chartwise`). Over a chart the two maps are, on sections, the two maps
of conormal modules of the tower of rings `Γ(X, V) ⟶ Γ(X, V) ⟶ Γ(Y, j⁻¹V)`, whose exactness is
`Stacks.Conormal.exact_mapCotangent_comap`; that is
`Stacks.Immersion.ConormalChart.exists_leftMap_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_exact (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] :
    (conormalSequenceShortComplex i j).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness in the middle: for any immersions i : Z ⟶ Y and j : Y ⟶ X the image of i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} is the kernel of 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} (equality, as ShortComplex.Exact of the complex built from the two canonical maps of Tag 01R4); no hypothesis beyond the two immersions

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.conormalSequenceLeftMap
declarations.doc:
**The left-hand map `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of the conormal sequence of
[Stacks Project, Tag 062S].** It is the canonical map of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] attached to
the square with horizontal maps `i ≫ j` and `j` and vertical maps `i` and `𝟙 X`.
declarations.statement:
def conormalSequenceLeftMap (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] :
    (modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.conormalSheaf j.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom) ⟶
      Stacks.ClosedImmersion.conormalSheaf (i ≫ j).liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom
declarations.comment: the first arrow i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 062T.** A closed subscheme of `X` is a *relative effective Cartier
divisor* over `S` when it is an effective Cartier divisor on `X` and its structure morphism to
`S` is flat.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatAt_of_relativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 062U.**  The ambient morphism is flat at a point of a relative
effective Cartier divisor whose ambient local ring is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_of_relativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor f I)
    (x : X) (hx : x ∈ I.supportSet)
    (hNoetherian : IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_flat_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
A relative effective Cartier divisor lies in an open subscheme on which the ambient morphism is
flat, provided that morphism is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_flat_of_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor f I)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, I.supportSet ⊆ (U : Set X) ∧ Flat (U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_flat_off_relativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc: A morphism flat away from a relative effective Cartier divisor is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_flat_off_relativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor f I)
    (hf : ∀ x : X, x ∉ I.supportSet →
      IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    Flat f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonflatAmbient.not_flat_ambientRing
declarations.doc: The ring `B` is not flat over `k[t]`.
declarations.statement: theorem not_flat_ambientRing : ¬ RingHom.Flat (baseMap k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonflatAmbient.quotientByX_equiv_polynomial
declarations.doc:
The quotient `B / xB` is isomorphic to `k[t]` by a ring isomorphism carrying the class of `t`
to the coordinate and constants to constants.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientByX_equiv_polynomial :
    ∃ e : (ambientRing k ⧸ Ideal.span {x k}) ≃+* Polynomial k,
      e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {x k}) (t k)) = Polynomial.X ∧
        ∀ a : k,
          e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {x k})
            (algebraMap k (ambientRing k) a)) = Polynomial.C a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonflatAmbient.quotientByX_flat
declarations.doc: The quotient `B / xB` is flat over `k[t]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientByX_flat :
    RingHom.Flat
      ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {x k})).comp (baseMap k))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonflatAmbient.x_isRegular
declarations.doc: The element `x` is a nonzerodivisor of `B`.
declarations.statement: theorem x_isRegular : IsRegular (x k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonflatAmbient.divisor_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
The closed subscheme of `Spec B` cut out by `x` is a relative effective Cartier divisor over
`Spec k[t]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem divisor_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (baseMap k))) (divisor k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NonflatAmbient.no_flat_neighbourhood
declarations.doc: No open subscheme of `Spec B` containing the divisor is flat over `Spec k[t]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem no_flat_neighbourhood
    (U : (Spec (.of (ambientRing k))).Opens)
    (hU : (divisor k).supportSet ⊆ (U : Set (Spec (.of (ambientRing k))))) :
    ¬ Flat (U.ι ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (baseMap k)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_containing
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation, let `Z` be a closed subscheme of
`X` and let `x` be a point of `Z` whose fibre over `f x` is an effective Cartier divisor in a
neighbourhood of `x`.  Then there is an open neighbourhood `U` of `x` carrying a relative
effective Cartier divisor `D` over `S` with `Z ∩ U ⊆ D` and `Z_{f x} ∩ U = D_{f x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_containing (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (Z : X.IdealSheafData) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ Z.support)
    (hfib : ∃ N : (f.fiber (f x)).Opens, f.asFiber x ∈ N ∧
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor ((Z.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap N.ι)) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ U) (D : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor (U.ι ≫ f) D ∧ D ≤ Z.comap U.ι ∧
        (Z.comap U.ι).comap ((U.ι ≫ f).fiberι (f x)) =
          D.comap ((U.ι ≫ f).fiberι (f x))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_flat_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation, let `Z` be a closed subscheme of
`X` of finite presentation over `X` and let `x` be a point of `Z` at which `Z` is flat over `S` and
whose fibre over `f x` is an effective Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of `x`.  Then `Z`
restricts to a relative effective Cartier divisor over `S` on an affine open neighbourhood of
`x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_flat_of_finitePresentation (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (Z : X.IdealSheafData)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation Z.subschemeι] (x : X) (hx : x ∈ Z.support)
    (hfib : ∃ V : (f.fiber (f x)).Opens, f.asFiber x ∈ V ∧
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor ((Z.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap V.ι))
    (hflat : ((Z.subschemeι ≫ f).stalkMap (⟨x, hx⟩ : Z.subscheme)).hom.Flat) :
    ∃ V : X.Opens, x ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧
      IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor (V.ι ≫ f) (Z.comap V.ι)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_flat_of_fibres
declarations.doc:
A closed subscheme of a scheme flat and locally of finite presentation over `S`, itself flat
and locally of finite presentation over `S`, all of whose fibres are effective Cartier divisors, is
a relative effective Cartier divisor over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_flat_of_fibres (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (Z : X.IdealSheafData) [Flat (Z.subschemeι ≫ f)]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (Z.subschemeι ≫ f)]
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (Z.comap (f.fiberι s))) :
    IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor f Z

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_ideal_isPrincipal
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation, let
`Z` be a closed subscheme of `X` and let `x` be a point of `Z` whose fibre over `f x` is an
effective Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of `x`.  If the ideal of `Z` is principal on some
affine open neighbourhood of `x`, then `Z` restricts to a relative effective Cartier divisor over
`S` on an affine open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_ideal_isPrincipal (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (Z : X.IdealSheafData) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ Z.support)
    (hprin : ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ (U : X.Opens) ∧ (Z.ideal U).IsPrincipal)
    (hfib : ∃ V : (f.fiber (f x)).Opens, f.asFiber x ∈ V ∧
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor ((Z.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap V.ι)) :
    ∃ V : X.Opens, x ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧
      IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor (V.ι ≫ f) (Z.comap V.ι)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isLocallyPrincipal_of_fibres
declarations.doc:
A locally principal closed subscheme of a scheme flat and locally of finite presentation over
`S`, all of whose fibres are effective Cartier divisors, is a relative effective Cartier divisor
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isLocallyPrincipal_of_fibres (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (Z : X.IdealSheafData) (hZ : IsLocallyPrincipal Z)
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (Z.comap (f.fiberι s))) :
    IsRelativeEffectiveCartierDivisor f Z

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The conormal algebra of an immersion, together with its local associated-graded quotient
presentations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebra {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    ConormalAlgebraData i

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The conormal algebra of an immersion, together with its local associated-graded quotient
presentations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebra {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    ConormalAlgebraData i
declarations.comment: its degree-n piece: i_* C_{Z/X, n} = I^n/I^{n+1}

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalDegreeOneHom_isIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0632]: the conormal algebra in degree one is the conormal sheaf.** The
canonical morphism `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,1}` is an isomorphism.

This is the degree-one assertion of the canonical surjection `Sym^*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}`: the
identification of the degree-one piece of the conormal algebra with the conormal sheaf, which is
what makes that surjection an isomorphism in degree one.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalDegreeOneHom_isIso (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    IsIso (conormalDegreeOneHom i)
declarations.comment: degree one: the conormal algebra in degree one is the conormal sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalDegreeOneIso
declarations.doc: **[Stacks, Tag 0632]: the degree-one identification `𝒞_{Z/X} ≅ 𝒞_{Z/X,1}`.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalDegreeOneIso (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    conormalSheaf i ≅ (conormalAlgebra i).algebra.piece 1
declarations.comment: degree one: the identification as an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalSymmetricHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0632.** The canonical map `Sym*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of graded
`𝒪_Z`-algebras, the unital homomorphism which is the identity on degree-one generators.
declarations.comment: the canonical map Sym*(C_{Z/X}) → C_{Z/X,*} of graded algebras

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalSymmetricHom_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0632.** A unital homomorphism which is the identity on degree-one
generators is the canonical map, so the canonical map is well defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSymmetricHom_unique (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    {g : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.UnitalHom (conormalSymmetricAlgebra i)
      (conormalAlgebra i).algebra}
    (hg : Scheme.Modules.symmetricAlgebraGen Z ((conormalAlgebra i).algebra.piece 1) ≫
      g.app 1 = 𝟙 ((conormalAlgebra i).algebra.piece 1)) :
    g = conormalSymmetricHom i
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the canonical map Sym*(C_{Z/X}) → C_{Z/X,*}

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.isIso_conormalSymmetricHom_app_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0632.** The canonical map `Sym*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` is an
isomorphism in degree one. The degree-one generator `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ Sym¹(𝒞_{Z/X})` is an isomorphism,
and the canonical map is the identity on it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalSymmetricHom_app_one (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    IsIso ((conormalSymmetricHom i).app 1)
declarations.comment: the canonical map Sym*(C_{Z/X}) → C_{Z/X,*} is an isomorphism in degree 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.isIso_conormalSymmetricHom_app_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0632.** The canonical map `Sym*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` is an
isomorphism in degree zero. It is a monomorphism because both degree-zero pieces are generated
by their graded units, freely on the source and without torsion on the target, and an
epimorphism because on an affine closed-immersion chart every degree-zero section of the target
is a multiple of the unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalSymmetricHom_app_zero (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    IsIso ((conormalSymmetricHom i).app 0)
declarations.comment: the canonical map Sym*(C_{Z/X}) → C_{Z/X,*} is an isomorphism in degree 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.epi_conormalSymmetricHom_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0632.** The canonical map `Sym*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` is surjective:
an epimorphism of sheaves of modules in every degree. In a negative degree the target vanishes,
and in a nonnegative degree the map is locally surjective, because over an affine
closed-immersion chart `ℐⁿ/ℐⁿ⁺¹` is generated by products of `n` sections of `ℐ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalSymmetricHom_app (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (n : ℤ) :
    Epi ((conormalSymmetricHom i).app n)
declarations.comment: the canonical map Sym*(C_{Z/X}) → C_{Z/X,*} is surjective

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.conormalAlgebra_identifications
declarations.doc:
Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion and `U ⊆ X` an open
subscheme such that `i(Z) ⊆ U` is a closed subset of `U`; let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_U` be the quasi-coherent
ideal sheaf of the closed subscheme `i(Z) ⊂ U`.  Then
`𝒞_{Z/X,*} = i^*(⨁_{n ≥ 0} ℐⁿ) = i^{-1}(⨁_{n ≥ 0} ℐⁿ/ℐⁿ⁺¹)`:
* the conormal algebra is isomorphic to `i^*(⨁ₙ ℐⁿ)` as sheaves of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras, the
  isomorphism carrying the unit to the unit;
* the topological inverse image `i^{-1}(⨁ₙ ℐⁿ/ℐⁿ⁺¹)`, a sheaf of graded `i^{-1}𝒪_U`-algebras,
  is isomorphic to the conormal algebra read over `i^{-1}𝒪_U` along the structure map
  `i^{-1}𝒪_U ⟶ 𝒪_Z`, as sheaves of graded algebras, the isomorphism carrying the unit to the
  unit.

The isomorphisms are `Stacks.Conormal.conormalIsoReesPullback` and
`Stacks.Conormal.inverseImageGrIsoConormal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalAlgebra_identifications :
    (∃ e : (conormalAlgebra i).algebra ≅ openReesPullback i U hsub, ∀ W : Z.Opens,
      (e.hom.app 0).val.app (op W) ((conormalAlgebra i).algebra.one.eval (op W)) =
        (openReesPullback i U hsub).one.eval (op W)) ∧
    (∃ e : inverseImageGradedAlgebra (openLift i U hsub).base (U.toScheme).sheaf
          (grGradedAlgebra (openIdeal i U hsub)) ≅
        SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.scalarRestrict (openStructureMap i U hsub)
          (conormalAlgebra i).algebra, ∀ W : Z.Opens,
      (e.hom.app 0).val.app (op W)
          ((inverseImageGradedAlgebra (openLift i U hsub).base (U.toScheme).sheaf
            (grGradedAlgebra (openIdeal i U hsub))).one.eval (op W)) =
        (conormalAlgebra i).algebra.one.eval (op W))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
The homogeneous sections of the conormal algebra on an affine closed-immersion chart are
canonically the quotients `I^n/I^(n+1)`, compatibly with multiplication, unit, and scalars.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineSectionsEquiv {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] (U : X.affineOpens)
    (hU : IsClosedImmersion (i.resLE U.1 (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) le_rfl)) :
    AffineSectionsEquiv i U hU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.conormalAlgebra_on_closed_open
declarations.doc:
Both canonical identifications of the conormal algebra on an open where the immersion is
closed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebra_on_closed_open
    {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : IsClosed (Set.range (i.resLE U (i ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl))) :
    ClosedOpenIdentifications i U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.conormalAlgebraHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0634.** The unique morphism of conormal graded
algebras over a commutative square of immersions is induced on every affine
closed-immersion chart by the ring map on ideal-power quotients.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraHom {Z X Z' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X')
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion i'] (comm : f ≫ i' = i ≫ g) :
    CanonicalConormalAlgebraHom i i' f g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.conormalAlgebraMap_epi
declarations.doc:
The canonical map on each homogeneous piece of the conormal algebra is
locally surjective for a cartesian square of immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalAlgebraMap_epi {Z X Z' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X')
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion i'] (sq : IsPullback i f g i') (n : ℤ) :
    Epi ((canonicalPullbackHom i i' f g sq.w.symm).hom n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.conormalAlgebraMap_isIso_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Under flat base change the canonical map on every homogeneous piece is
an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalAlgebraMap_isIso_of_flat {Z X Z' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X')
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion i'] [Flat g]
    (sq : IsPullback i f g i') (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((canonicalPullbackHom i i' f g sq.w.symm).hom n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.normalBundle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0636.** **The normal bundle `N_ZX = Spec_Z(Sym(𝒞_{Z/X}))`** of an
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`: the relative spectrum over `Z` of the symmetric algebra on the conormal
sheaf `𝒞_{Z/X} = 𝒞_{Z/X,1}`, that is, the vector bundle of Tag 01M2 associated to `𝒞_{Z/X}`.
declarations.statement: def normalBundle : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.normalBundleVectorBundle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0636.** **`N_ZX` is a vector bundle over `Z`** in the sense of Tag
062M: it is the vector bundle `𝐕(𝒞_{Z/X})` of Tag 01M2 attached to the conormal sheaf, the
relative spectrum of `Sym(𝒞_{Z/X})` graded by the symmetric powers `Symⁿ(𝒞_{Z/X})`.
declarations.statement: def normalBundleVectorBundle : VectorBundle Z
declarations.comment: N_ZX is a vector bundle over Z in the sense of 062M

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.normalConeCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0636.** **`C_ZX` is a cone over `Z`** in the sense of Tag 062R: it is
affine over `Z`, and the homogeneous pieces `𝒞_{Z/X,n}` of the conormal algebra decompose the
direct image of its structure sheaf — uniquely over every open, locally surjectively, and
multiplicatively — with the degree-zero piece the structure sheaf of `Z`.
declarations.statement: def normalConeCone : AbstractCone Z
declarations.comment: C_ZX is a cone over Z in the sense of 062R

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.normalConeToNormalBundle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0637.** **The canonical morphism `C_ZX ⟶ N_ZX` from the normal cone to
the normal bundle of an immersion**, defined by the canonical map
`Sym*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of graded algebras of Tag 0632: it is the morphism of relative
spectra attached to that map of algebra sheaves, and
`Stacks.Conormal.ι_normalConeToNormalBundle` is its characterising property.
declarations.statement:
def normalConeToNormalBundle :
    normalCone i ⟶ Scheme.Modules.vectorBundle Z (conormalSheafDegreeOne i)
declarations.comment: the canonical surjection of graded algebras defines a morphism C_ZX → N_ZX

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.normalConeToNormalBundle_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0637.** The canonical morphism `C_ZX ⟶ N_ZX` is a morphism of schemes
over `Z`: it carries the projection of the normal bundle to the projection of the normal cone.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalConeToNormalBundle_toBase :
    normalConeToNormalBundle i ≫
        Scheme.Modules.vectorBundleToBase Z (conormalSheafDegreeOne i) =
      normalConeToBase i
declarations.comment: the morphism C_ZX → N_ZX is a morphism over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.regularSequenceMultiplication
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0639.** Multiplication by `f i` on
`O_X/(f₀, …, f_{i-1})`, for an arbitrary ringed space.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def regularSequenceMultiplication
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, v}) {n : ℕ}
    (f : Fin n → X.presheaf.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))) (i : Fin n) :
    RegularSequenceMultiplicationData X f i

registrations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SeqKoszul.sheafComplex
registrations.comment:
the notation `K_•(O_X, f_•)` of the section on regular ideal sheaves: the
Koszul complex of Modules, Definition 17.24.2 (Tag 062L) for the structure sheaf of a ringed
space and a finite family of its global sections.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiRegular.quasiRegularMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism of sheaves `(O_X / J)[T₁, ..., Tᵣ] ⟶ ⨁ d, J^d / J^(d+1)` associated to
global sections `f₁, ..., fᵣ`, sending `Tᵢ` to `fᵢ mod J²`.
declarations.statement:

    (f : Fin r → X.presheaf.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))) : QuasiRegularMapData X f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SeqKoszul.isH1RegularSequence_of_isKoszulRegularSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063C.** A Koszul-regular sequence is `H₁`-regular: degree `1` is one of
the positive degrees in which the Koszul complex of a Koszul-regular sequence is acyclic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularSequence_of_isKoszulRegularSequence
    (h : IsKoszulRegularSequence X f) : IsH1RegularSequence X f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularSequence_of_regularSequence
declarations.doc:
A regular sequence of global sections of the structure sheaf is a Koszul-regular sequence: if
multiplication by `f i` on `O_X/(f₁, …, f_{i-1})` is an injective map of sheaves for every `i`,
then the Koszul complex `K_•(O_X, f_•)` is acyclic in positive degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularSequence_of_regularSequence {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → X.presheaf.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X)))
    (hf : ∀ i : Fin r, Mono (regularSequenceMultiplication X f i).multiplication) :
    SeqKoszul.IsKoszulRegularSequence X f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isIso_quasiRegularMap_of_isH1RegularSequence
declarations.doc:
For an `H₁`-regular sequence of global sections the quasi-regularity morphism of Stacks tag
063B is an isomorphism, i.e. the sequence is quasi-regular.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The local quasi-regularity condition of Stacks tag 063D, part (4).** The ideal sheaf `J` is
quasi-regular when, near every point of the support of `O_X / J`, it is generated by a sequence
whose sheaf quasi-regularity map of Stacks tag 063B is an isomorphism.

    (J : (structureSheafModule X).Submodule) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063D, part (1).** The ideal sheaf `J` is regular when, near every point of the
support of `O_X/J`, it is generated by a regular sequence of sections.
declarations.statement: def IsRegularIdealSheaf (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (J : (structureSheafModule X).Submodule) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf

**Stacks tag 063D, part (2).** The ideal sheaf `J` is Koszul-regular when, near every point of
the support of `O_X/J`, it is generated by a sequence whose Koszul complex is acyclic in positive
degrees.
declarations.statement:

**Stacks tag 063D, part (3).** The ideal sheaf `J` is `H₁`-regular when, near every point of
the support of `O_X/J`, it is generated by a sequence whose Koszul complex is exact in degree

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_of_isRegularIdealSheaf

**A regular ideal sheaf is Koszul-regular.**  One implication of Stacks tag 063E, between

**Stacks Project, Tag 063E.**  A Koszul-regular ideal sheaf is `H₁`-regular: the local
