declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.H1RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularIdealSheaf_iff_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063G (`h1_regular`).** A sheaf of ideals on a scheme is `H₁`-regular if
and only if, around each point of the support of its quotient, it is generated on an affine open
by a sequence which is `H₁`-regular in the ring of sections of that open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularIdealSheaf_iff_affine (X : Scheme.{u})
    (J : (structureSheafModule X.toRingedSpace).Submodule) :
    IsH1RegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∈ idealQuotientSupport X.toRingedSpace J →
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_hx : x ∈ (U : Set X)) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → Γ(X, U.1)),
          IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U.1 f ∧ Koszul.IsH1Regular f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_iff_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063G (`koszul_regular`).** A sheaf of ideals on a scheme is
Koszul-regular if and only if, around each point of the support of its quotient, it is generated
on an affine open by a sequence which is Koszul-regular in the ring of sections of that open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_iff_affine (X : Scheme.{u})
    (J : (structureSheafModule X.toRingedSpace).Submodule) :
    IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∈ idealQuotientSupport X.toRingedSpace J →
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_hx : x ∈ (U : Set X)) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → Γ(X, U.1)),
          IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U.1 f ∧ Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_iff_exists_affine_generators
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of ideals on a scheme is quasi-regular
if and only if, around each point of the support of its quotient, it is generated on an affine
open by a quasi-regular sequence in the ring of sections of that open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_iff_exists_affine_generators (X : Scheme.{u})
    (J : (structureSheafModule X.toRingedSpace).Submodule) :
    IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∈ idealQuotientSupport X.toRingedSpace J →
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_hx : x ∈ (U : Set X)) (r : ℕ)
          (f : Fin r → X.toRingedSpace.presheaf.obj (op U.1)),
          IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U.1 f ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular
              (X.toRingedSpace.presheaf.obj (op U.1)) (List.ofFn f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheafAffine.isRegularIdealSheaf_iff_exists_affine_generators
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063G (regular).** A sheaf of ideals on a scheme is regular if and only
if, around each point of the support of its quotient, it is generated on an affine open by a
regular sequence in the ring of sections of that open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularIdealSheaf_iff_exists_affine_generators (X : Scheme.{u})
    (J : (structureSheafModule X.toRingedSpace).Submodule) :
    IsRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∈ idealQuotientSupport X.toRingedSpace J →
        ∃ (U : Opens X) (_hx : x ∈ U) (_hU : IsAffineOpen U) (r : ℕ)
          (f : Fin r → X.presheaf.obj (op U)),
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (X.presheaf.obj (op U)) (List.ofFn f) ∧
            IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_isGeneratedByOn_of_isFiniteType_of_le_sup_sq
declarations.doc:
**The Nakayama and shrinking step in the proof of Stacks tag 063H.**  Let `J ⊆ O_X` be a
sheaf of ideals of finite type on a locally ringed space and let `x` be a point of the support
of `O_X / J`.  Sections `f₁, …, f_r` of `J` over a neighbourhood `U` of `x` whose germs generate
`J_x` modulo `J_x²` generate `J` on a neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGeneratedByOn_of_isFiniteType_of_le_sup_sq
    (hJ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} J.toSheafOfModules) {x : X}
    (hne : stalkIdeal J x ≠ ⊤) {U : Opens X} (hxU : x ∈ U) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → X.presheaf.obj (op U)) (hf : ∀ i, f i ∈ J.obj (op U))
    (hle : stalkIdeal J x
      ≤ Jid (germFamily X.toRingedSpace U f x hxU) ⊔ stalkIdeal J x ^ 2) :
    ∃ (V : Opens X) (_ : x ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ U),
      IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J V
        (fun i => X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hVU).op (f i))
declarations.comment:
the Nakayama and shrinking step of the proof only: sections of a finite-type `J`
whose germs generate `J_x/J_x²` generate `J` near `x`. The characterization itself is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.Conormal.isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_iff`.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.Conormal.isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063H.** A sheaf of ideals is quasi-regular if and only
if it is of finite type, has finite locally free conormal sheaf, and has
isomorphic canonical symmetric-power-to-associated-graded maps in every degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_iff (X : LocallyRingedSpace.{u})
    (J : (Stacks.RingedSpace.structureSheafModule X.toRingedSpace).Submodule) :
    IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J ↔
      (J.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (conormalSheaf X.toRingedSpace J) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (conormalSymmetricToGradedMap X.toRingedSpace J n))
declarations.comment:
both directions of the characterization: quasi-regular iff of finite type,
with finite locally free conormal sheaf and isomorphic symmetric-power-to-graded maps

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.regular_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_tfae [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData) (x : X)
    (hx : x ∈ J.support) :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ (s : ℕ) (g : Fin s → X.presheaf.stalk x),
          stalkIdeal J x hx = Ideal.span (Set.range g) ∧
            IsRegular (X.presheaf.stalk x) (List.ofFn g),
        ∃ (s : ℕ) (g : Fin s → X.presheaf.stalk x),
          stalkIdeal J x hx = Ideal.span (Set.range g) ∧ Koszul.IsKoszulRegular g,
        ∃ (s : ℕ) (g : Fin s → X.presheaf.stalk x),
          stalkIdeal J x hx = Ideal.span (Set.range g) ∧ Koszul.IsH1Regular g,
        ∃ (s : ℕ) (g : Fin s → X.presheaf.stalk x),
          stalkIdeal J x hx = Ideal.span (Set.range g) ∧
            IsQuasiRegular (X.presheaf.stalk x) (List.ofFn g),
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (s : ℕ) (f : Fin s → Γ(X, U.1)),
          J.ideal U = Ideal.span (Set.range f) ∧ IsRegular Γ(X, U.1) (List.ofFn f),
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (s : ℕ) (f : Fin s → Γ(X, U.1)),
          J.ideal U = Ideal.span (Set.range f) ∧ Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f,
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (s : ℕ) (f : Fin s → Γ(X, U.1)),
          J.ideal U = Ideal.span (Set.range f) ∧ Koszul.IsH1Regular f,
        ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (s : ℕ) (f : Fin s → Γ(X, U.1)),
          J.ideal U = Ideal.span (Set.range f) ∧ IsQuasiRegular Γ(X, U.1) (List.ofFn f),
        ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (J.comap U.ι).subschemeι,
        ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsKoszulRegularImmersion (J.comap U.ι).subschemeι,
        ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsH1RegularImmersion (J.comap U.ι).subschemeι,
        ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsQuasiRegularImmersion (J.comap U.ι).subschemeι]

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_iff_of_open
declarations.doc:
An immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` is regular if and only if, for one — equivalently any — open
subscheme `U` of `X` through which `i` factors as a closed immersion `j : Z ⟶ U`, the defining
ideal of `j` is a regular ideal sheaf on `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_iff_of_open {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (U : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ U.ι = i) :
    IsRegularImmersion i ↔
      IsRegularIdealSheaf U.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (definingIdealOfHom j)
declarations.comment: part (1): independence of the chosen open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (1).** The immersion `i` is regular when the defining ideal sheaf of
its canonical closed factor is a regular ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: def IsRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (2).** The immersion `i` is Koszul-regular when the defining ideal
sheaf of its canonical closed factor is a Koszul-regular ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: def IsKoszulRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (3).** The immersion `i` is `H₁`-regular when the defining ideal
sheaf of its canonical closed factor is an `H₁`-regular ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: def IsH1RegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (4).** The immersion `i` is quasi-regular when the defining ideal
sheaf of its canonical closed factor is a quasi-regular ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: def IsQuasiRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_definingIdealOfHom_congr
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (2): independence of the chosen open.** For an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`
and two opens of `X` in which `i` is closed, the Koszul-regularity condition of Stacks tag 063D
on the restriction of the defining ideal sheaf of `i` is the same on both.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_definingIdealOfHom_congr (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (V V' : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ V.ι = i)
    (j' : Z ⟶ V'.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j'] (hij' : j' ≫ V'.ι = i) :
    IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf V.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (restrictSubmodule V (definingIdealOfHom i)) ↔
      IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf V'.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (restrictSubmodule V' (definingIdealOfHom i))
declarations.comment: part (2): independence of the chosen open, for the restricted defining ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularIdealSheaf_definingIdealOfHom_congr
declarations.doc: **Stacks tag 063J, part (3): independence of the chosen open.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularIdealSheaf_definingIdealOfHom_congr (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (V V' : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ V.ι = i)
    (j' : Z ⟶ V'.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j'] (hij' : j' ≫ V'.ι = i) :
    IsH1RegularIdealSheaf V.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (restrictSubmodule V (definingIdealOfHom i)) ↔
      IsH1RegularIdealSheaf V'.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (restrictSubmodule V' (definingIdealOfHom i))
declarations.comment: part (3): independence of the chosen open, for the restricted defining ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_definingIdealOfHom_congr
declarations.doc: **Stacks tag 063J, part (4): independence of the chosen open.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularIdealSheaf_definingIdealOfHom_congr (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (V V' : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ V.ι = i)
    (j' : Z ⟶ V'.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j'] (hij' : j' ≫ V'.ι = i) :
    IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf V.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (restrictSubmodule V (definingIdealOfHom i)) ↔
      IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf V'.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (restrictSubmodule V' (definingIdealOfHom i))
declarations.comment: part (4): independence of the chosen open, for the restricted defining ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularImmersion_iff_of_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (2): independence of the chosen open.** An immersion is
Koszul-regular exactly when the defining ideal sheaf of its closed factor through *any* open in
which it is closed is a Koszul-regular ideal sheaf — not only the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_iff_of_open (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (V : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ V.ι = i) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i ↔
      IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf V.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (definingIdealOfHom j)
declarations.comment: part (2): independence of the chosen open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularImmersion_iff_of_open
declarations.doc: **Stacks tag 063J, part (3): independence of the chosen open.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_iff_of_open (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (V : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ V.ι = i) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion i ↔
      IsH1RegularIdealSheaf V.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (definingIdealOfHom j)
declarations.comment: part (3): independence of the chosen open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff_of_open
declarations.doc: **Stacks tag 063J, part (4): independence of the chosen open.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff_of_open (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (V : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ V.ι = i) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion i ↔
      IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf V.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (definingIdealOfHom j)
declarations.comment: part (4): independence of the chosen open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularImmersion_resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (2): Koszul-regularity survives restricting the target to an
open.** If `i : Z ⟶ X` is a Koszul-regular immersion then so is its restriction
`i.resLE V (i ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl : i ⁻¹ᵁ V ⟶ V` to any open `V ⊆ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_resLE (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (h : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) (V : X.Opens) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion (i.resLE V (i ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
declarations.comment: part (2): stability under restricting the target to an open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularImmersion_resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (3): `H₁`-regularity survives restricting the target to an
open.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_resLE (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (h : IsH1RegularImmersion i) (V : X.Opens) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion (i.resLE V (i ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
declarations.comment: part (3): stability under restricting the target to an open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularImmersion_resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (4): quasi-regularity survives restricting the target to an
open.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_resLE (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (h : IsQuasiRegularImmersion i) (V : X.Opens) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion (i.resLE V (i ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
declarations.comment: part (4): stability under restricting the target to an open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063J, part (2): Koszul-regularity glues along an open cover of the target.**
If every restriction `i.resLE (V k) (i ⁻¹ᵁ V k) le_rfl` of the immersion `i` over a member of an
open cover `V` of `X` is a Koszul-regular immersion, then so is `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_resLE
    (h : ∀ k, IsKoszulRegularImmersion (i.resLE (V k) (i ⁻¹ᵁ V k) le_rfl)) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i
declarations.comment: part (2): gluing along an open cover of the target

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularImmersion_of_resLE
declarations.doc: **Stacks tag 063J, part (3): `H₁`-regularity glues along an open cover of the target.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_of_resLE
    (h : ∀ k, IsH1RegularImmersion (i.resLE (V k) (i ⁻¹ᵁ V k) le_rfl)) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion i
declarations.comment: part (3): gluing along an open cover of the target

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_resLE
declarations.doc: **Stacks tag 063J, part (4): quasi-regularity glues along an open cover of the target.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_resLE
    (h : ∀ k, IsQuasiRegularImmersion (i.resLE (V k) (i ⁻¹ᵁ V k) le_rfl)) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion i
declarations.comment: part (4): gluing along an open cover of the target

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff_of_open
declarations.doc:
An immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` is quasi-regular if and only if, for one — equivalently any — open
subscheme `U` of `X` through which `i` factors as a closed immersion `j : Z ⟶ U`, the defining
ideal of `j` is a quasi-regular ideal sheaf on `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff_of_open {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (U : X.Opens) (j : Z ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsClosedImmersion j] (hij : j ≫ U.ι = i) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion i ↔
      IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf U.toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace
        (definingIdealOfHom j)
declarations.comment: part (4): independence of the chosen open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_isRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**A regular immersion is Koszul-regular.**  The first implication of Stacks tag 063K, between
parts (1) and (2) of Stacks tag 063J.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_isRegularImmersion (h : IsRegularImmersion i) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularImmersion_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**A Koszul-regular immersion is `H₁`-regular.**  The second implication of Stacks tag 063K,
between parts (2) and (3) of Stacks tag 063J.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion (h : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_isH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**An `H₁`-regular immersion is quasi-regular.**  The third implication of Stacks tag 063K,
between parts (3) and (4) of Stacks tag 063J.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_isH1RegularImmersion (h : IsH1RegularImmersion i) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isRegularImmersion_iff_isKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063L, parts (1) and (2).** An immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is
regular if and only if it is Koszul-regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_iff_isKoszulRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsRegularImmersion i ↔ IsKoszulRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularImmersion_iff_isH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063L, parts (2) and (3).** An immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is
Koszul-regular if and only if it is `H₁`-regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_iff_isH1RegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i ↔ IsH1RegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isH1RegularImmersion_iff_isQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063L, parts (3) and (4).** An immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is
`H₁`-regular if and only if it is quasi-regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_iff_isQuasiRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsH1RegularImmersion i ↔ IsQuasiRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.regularImmersion_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063L.** For an immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme the four notions of
regularity — regular, Koszul-regular, `H₁`-regular and quasi-regular — are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularImmersion_tfae (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    List.TFAE [IsRegularImmersion i, IsKoszulRegularImmersion i, IsH1RegularImmersion i,
      IsQuasiRegularImmersion i]
declarations.comment: the four notions agree over a locally Noetherian base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFree_universalConormalSheaf_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
The conormal sheaf of a Koszul-regular immersion of schemes, in the sense of Stacks 04F4, is
finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_universalConormalSheaf_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion
    {Z P : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ P) [IsImmersion i] (hi : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (universalConormalSheaf i)
declarations.comment:
condition (2) for a Koszul-regular immersion, for the conormal sheaf of Tag
04F4. Condition (1) is at RegularImmersion/FinitePresentation.lean; condition (2) does not
need Tag 063H, and is
proved at RegularImmersion/ConormalLocallyFree.lean by a route through Tags 063G, 08RK, 01R3,
00NX and 05JM that never uses 063H

declarations.name: Stacks.Conormal.isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff
declarations.doc:
An immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of schemes is quasi-regular **if and only if** (1) it is locally of
finite presentation, (2) its conormal sheaf `𝒞_{Z/X}` is finite locally free, and (3) the
canonical map `Sym*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks, Tag 0632] is an isomorphism in every
degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] :
    Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsQuasiRegularImmersion i ↔
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation i ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (conormalSheaf i) ∧
          ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso ((conormalSymmetricHom i).app n)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: an immersion is quasi-regular iff it is locally of finite presentation, its conormal sheaf is finite locally free, and the map of 0632 is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 063M], condition (1) in the direction out of quasi-regularity.**  A
quasi-regular immersion of schemes is locally of finite presentation.

The canonical closed factor `i.liftCoborder` is locally of finite presentation by
[Stacks, Tag 01TV], since the quasi-regular defining ideal sheaf is finitely generated over
every affine open, and the remaining factor `i.coborderRange.ι` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isQuasiRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (h : IsQuasiRegularImmersion i) : LocallyOfFinitePresentation i
declarations.comment: condition (1) of the statement, in the direction out of quasi-regularity: a quasi-regular immersion is locally of finite presentation. The whole iff is proved at Stacks.Conormal.isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.mono_conormalLeftMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 063N]: the conormal sequence of an `H1`-regular immersion is exact at
its left-hand term.** For immersions `Z --i--→ Y --j--→ X` with `i` an `H1`-regular immersion,
the canonical map `i^* C_{Y/X} ⟶ C_{Z/X}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_conormalLeftMap (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j]
    (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion i) : Mono (conormalLeftMap i j)
declarations.comment: exactness at the left term: for an H₁-regular immersion `i` the canonical map `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` is a monomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.conormalSequence_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 063N]: the conormal sequence of an `H1`-regular immersion is short
exact.** For immersions `Z --i--→ Y --j--→ X` with `i` an `H1`-regular immersion, the canonical
sequence `0 ⟶ i^* C_{Y/X} ⟶ C_{Z/X} ⟶ C_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` of [Stacks Project, Tag 062S] is a short
exact sequence of `O_Z`-modules.

Exactness in the middle and surjectivity on the right are [Stacks Project, Tag 062S]; what
`H1`-regularity of `i` adds is injectivity on the left,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.mono_conormalLeftMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_shortExact (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j]
    (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion i) : (conormalSequenceShortComplex i j).ShortExact
declarations.comment: exactness: the canonical sequence `0 ⟶ i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` of an H₁-regular immersion is short exact

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.conormalSequence_locallySplit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 063N]: the conormal sequence of an `H1`-regular immersion is locally
split.** Every point of `Z` has an open neighbourhood over which the short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ i^* C_{Y/X} ⟶ C_{Z/X} ⟶ C_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` splits, the restriction to an open being the slice
restriction `SheafOfModules.over`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_locallySplit (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j]
    (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion i) (z : Z) :
    ∃ V : Z.Opens, z ∈ V ∧ Nonempty (((conormalSequenceShortComplex i j).map
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.overFunctor
        (structureSheafRing Z.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace) V)).Splitting)
declarations.comment: local splitness: on a neighbourhood of every point of `Z` the canonical sequence of an H₁-regular immersion splits

declarations.name: KoszulH1.cmp_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063Q.**  Let `A → B` be a ring map and `f_1, …, f_r` a
sequence in `B` such that `B/(f_1, …, f_r)` is flat as an `A`-module.  Let
`A → A'` be a ring map and set `B' = B ⊗_A A'`, `f'_i = f_i ⊗ 1`.  Then the
canonical comparison map

  Φ : H_1(K_•(B, f_1, …, f_r)) ⊗_A A' ⟶ H_1(K_•(B', f'_1, …, f'_r))

is surjective.

Here the flatness hypothesis is stated as `Module.Flat A (B ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))`,
the quotient being viewed as an `A`-module by restriction of scalars along `A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cmp_surjective
    {A B A' : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → B)
    (hflat : Module.Flat A (B ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))) :
    Function.Surjective (cmp (A := A) (A' := A') f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiRegularImmersion_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063R, the quasi-regular half.**  A quasi-regular immersion whose source
is flat over the base remains quasi-regular after any base change of the base scheme.

The `H₁`-regular half of the tag is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isH1RegularImmersion_baseChange_of_flat`, in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularImmersion.H1BaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_baseChange_of_flat {S X Z S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [Flat (i ≫ f)] (hi : IsQuasiRegularImmersion i) (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g f) i)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isH1RegularImmersion_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063R, the `H₁`-regular half.**  An `H₁`-regular immersion whose source
is flat over the base remains `H₁`-regular after any base change of the base scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_baseChange_of_flat {S X Z S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [Flat (i ≫ f)] (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion i) (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g f) i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRelativeH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks tag 063S.**  An immersion into a scheme over a base is a *relative
`H₁`-regular immersion* when the immersed scheme is flat over the base and the immersion is
`H₁`-regular.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRelativeH1RegularImmersion {Z X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of Stacks tag 063S.** An immersion into a scheme over a base is a *relative
quasi-regular immersion* when the immersed scheme is flat over the base and the immersion is
quasi-regular.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion {Z X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatAt_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `i : Z ⟶ X` a relative quasi-regular immersion
over `S`.  Then `f` is flat at every point of the image of `i` whose local ring on `X` is
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion
    {X S Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (hi : IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion f i)
    (x : X) (hx : x ∈ Set.range i.base)
    (hNoetherian : IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_baseChange_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063U, regularity after an arbitrary base change.**  A relative
quasi-regular immersion into a scheme flat and locally of finite presentation over the base
remains a regular immersion after any change of the base.

The base change is again a relative quasi-regular immersion over `S'`:  its quasi-regularity is
the quasi-regular half of Stacks tag 063R and the flatness of its source over `S'` is
`flat_comp_of_isPullback`.  Flatness and local finite presentation of `S' ×_S X ⟶ S'` are base
changes of those of `X ⟶ S`.  So the already-proved
`isRegularImmersion_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion` applies over `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_baseChange_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion {S X Z S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hi : IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion f i) (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    IsRegularImmersion (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g f) i)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
A relative quasi-regular immersion into a scheme flat and locally of finite presentation over
the base is a regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_of_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion {S X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hi : IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion f i) : IsRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_flat_of_isRelativeH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a relative
`H₁`-regular immersion over `S`.  Then there is an open subscheme of `X` containing the image of
`Z` on which `f` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_flat_of_isRelativeH1RegularImmersion
    {S X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRelativeH1RegularImmersion f i) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, Set.range i.base ⊆ (U : Set X) ∧ Flat (U.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: part (1): flat open neighbourhood of a relative H₁-regular immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_of_isRelativeH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063V, part (2): the immersion is regular.**  A relative `H₁`-regular
immersion into a scheme locally of finite presentation over the base is a regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_of_isRelativeH1RegularImmersion {S X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRelativeH1RegularImmersion f i) : IsRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularImmersion_baseChange_of_isRelativeH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 063V, part (2): regularity after an arbitrary base change.**  A
relative `H₁`-regular immersion into a scheme locally of finite presentation over the base
remains a regular immersion after any change of the base scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_baseChange_of_isRelativeH1RegularImmersion {S X Z S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hi : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRelativeH1RegularImmersion f i) (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    IsRegularImmersion (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g f) i)
declarations.comment: part (2): the immersion stays regular after any base change

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_le_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063W, item (1).**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation,
let `T` be a closed subscheme of `X` and let `x` be a point of `T` whose fibre over `f x` is a
quasi-regular immersion near `x`.  Then there is an open `U ∋ x` and a relative quasi-regular
immersion `Z ⊆ U` over `S` with `T ∩ U ⊆ Z` and `Z_s = T_s ∩ U_s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_le_comap (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (T : X.IdealSheafData) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ T.support)
    (hfib : ∃ V : (f.fiber (f x)).Opens, f.asFiber x ∈ V ∧ IsQuasiRegularImmersion
      (((T.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap V.ι).subschemeι)) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ U) (Z : U.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ f) Z.subschemeι ∧ Z ≤ T.comap U.ι ∧
        Z.comap ((f.fiberι (f x)).resLE U (f.fiberι (f x) ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl)
          = (T.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap (f.fiberι (f x) ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_of_dim_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063W, item (3).**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation,
let `T` be a closed subscheme of `X` and let `x` be a point of `T` such that the fibre of `T`
over `f x` is a quasi-regular immersion on a neighbourhood of `x`.  Assume that `T` is cut out on
an affine open neighbourhood of `x` by `n` equations, and that `n` is the drop in local dimension
from the fibre `X_s` to the fibre `T_s` at `x`.  Then there is an open `U ∋ x` on which `T`
itself is a relative quasi-regular immersion over `S`, and a regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_of_dim_eq (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (T : X.IdealSheafData) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ T.support)
    (hfib : ∃ V : (f.fiber (f x)).Opens, f.asFiber x ∈ V ∧ IsQuasiRegularImmersion
      (((T.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap V.ι).subschemeι))
    {n : ℕ} {U₀ : X.Opens} (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hxU₀ : x ∈ U₀) (g : Fin n → Γ(X, U₀))
    (hg : T.ideal ⟨U₀, hU₀⟩ = Ideal.span (Set.range g))
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDimAt (T.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).subscheme
          ⟨f.asFiber x, asFiber_mem_support_comap f T x hx⟩ + (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
        = topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x)) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
      IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ f) (T.comap U.ι).subschemeι ∧
        IsRegularImmersion (T.comap U.ι).subschemeι

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_of_flatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 063W, item (2).**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation,
let `T` be a closed subscheme of `X` whose closed immersion into `X` is locally of finite
presentation, and let `x` be a point of `T` such that the fibre of `T` over `f x` is a
quasi-regular immersion on a neighbourhood of `x` and `T` is flat over `S` at `x`.  Then there
is an open `U ∋ x` on which `T` itself is a relative quasi-regular immersion over `S`, and a
regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_of_flatAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (T : X.IdealSheafData)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation T.subschemeι] (x : X) (hx : x ∈ T.support)
    (hfib : ∃ V : (f.fiber (f x)).Opens, f.asFiber x ∈ V ∧
      IsQuasiRegularImmersion (((T.comap (f.fiberι (f x))).comap V.ι).subschemeι))
    (hflat : ((T.subschemeι ≫ f).stalkMap (⟨x, hx⟩ : T.subscheme)).hom.Flat) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
      IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ f) (T.comap U.ι).subschemeι ∧
        IsRegularImmersion (T.comap U.ι).subschemeι

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_subschemeι_of_forall_fiber
declarations.doc:
**The fibrewise criterion of Stacks tag 063W.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite
presentation and let `T` be a closed subscheme of `X` which is flat and locally of finite
presentation over `S`.  If every fibre of `T` is a quasi-regular closed subscheme of the
corresponding fibre of `X`, then `T` is a relative quasi-regular immersion over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion_subschemeι_of_forall_fiber (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (T : X.IdealSheafData) [Flat (T.subschemeι ≫ f)]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (T.subschemeι ≫ f)]
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, IsQuasiRegularImmersion (T.comap (f.fiberι s)).subschemeι) :
    IsRelativeQuasiRegularImmersion f T.subschemeι

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.flat_and_isPullback_of_isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 063Y], (2) ⟹ (1), for schemes.** Let
`(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (S ⊂ S')` be a morphism of first-order thickenings of schemes, with
`f = φ.left` and `f' = φ.right`, and let `f` be flat.  If the canonical map
`f^* 𝒞_{S/S'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` is an isomorphism, then `f'` is flat and `X = S ×_{S'} X'`.

The hypothesis is condition (2) of the tag and the conclusion is its condition (1): `Flat φ.right`
is flatness of `f'` and `IsPullback i φ.left φ.right j` is the base-change identity
`X = S ×_{S'} X'`.  The flatness of `f` is the tag's standing hypothesis, and here it is used: it
is what makes `Γ(S, j⁻¹V) ⟶ Γ(X, i⁻¹U)` flat, which is a hypothesis of the commutative algebra
`Ideal.bijective_fibreTensorSMulHomToKer_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_and_isPullback_of_isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap {i : X ⟶ X'}
    {j : S ⟶ S'} (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) (hj : IsFirstOrderThickening j)
    (φ : Arrow.mk i ⟶ Arrow.mk j) [Flat φ.left]
    (hiso : letI := hi.1
      letI := hj.1
      IsIso (firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap hi hj φ)) :
    Flat φ.right ∧ IsPullback i φ.left φ.right j

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.flat_and_isPullback_iff_isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 063Y] for schemes.** Let `(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (S ⊂ S')` be a morphism
of first-order thickenings of schemes with `f = φ.left` flat.  Then the following are equivalent:

* **(1)** `f'` is flat and `X = S ×_{S'} X'`;
* **(2)** the canonical map `f^* 𝒞_{S/S'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` is an isomorphism.

The two directions are
`Stacks.Thickenings.isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap` and
`Stacks.Thickenings.flat_and_isPullback_of_isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap`.  The
standing hypothesis that `f` be flat is not needed for (1) ⟹ (2), where it follows from the other
two; it is needed for (2) ⟹ (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_and_isPullback_iff_isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap {i : X ⟶ X'}
    {j : S ⟶ S'} (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) (hj : IsFirstOrderThickening j)
    (φ : Arrow.mk i ⟶ Arrow.mk j) [Flat φ.left] :
    letI := hi.1
    letI := hj.1
    (Flat φ.right ∧ IsPullback i φ.left φ.right j) ↔
      IsIso (firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap hi hj φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.epi_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**The surjectivity half of condition (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 063Y], for schemes.** For a
morphism of first-order thickenings whose square is cartesian, so that `X = S ×_{S'} X'`, the
canonical map `f^* 𝒞_{S/S'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` is an epimorphism.

No flatness is used: cartesianness alone gives surjectivity, by
`Stacks.Immersion.epi_immersionConormalSheafMap`, which is the surjectivity clause of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0473] for a cartesian square of immersions.  The cartesian hypothesis is
the second half of condition (1) of the tag, so this is the half of (1) ⟹ (2) that the flatness
hypotheses are not needed for.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (hj : IsFirstOrderThickening j) (φ : Arrow.mk i ⟶ Arrow.mk j)
    (sq : IsPullback i φ.left φ.right j) :
    letI := hi.1
    letI := hj.1
    Epi (firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap hi hj φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 063Y], (1) ⟹ (2), for schemes.**  Let `(f, f') : (X ⊂ X') → (S ⊂ S')`
be a morphism of first-order thickenings of schemes, with `f = φ.left` and `f' = φ.right`.  If
`f'` is flat and `X = S ×_{S'} X'`, then the canonical map `f^* 𝒞_{S/S'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` is an
isomorphism.

The two hypotheses are exactly the two halves of condition (1) of the tag: `Flat φ.right` is
flatness of `f'`, and `sq` is the base-change identity `X = S ×_{S'} X'`.  The conclusion is
condition (2).  The standing hypothesis of the tag that `f` be flat is not needed, because it is
a consequence of the other two.

This is `Stacks.Immersion.isIso_immersionConormalSheafMap_of_flat`, the flat base-change clause
of [Stacks Project, Tag 0473], applied to the square of immersions underlying the morphism of
thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (hj : IsFirstOrderThickening j) (φ : Arrow.mk i ⟶ Arrow.mk j) [Flat φ.right]
    (sq : IsPullback i φ.left φ.right j) :
    letI := hi.1
    letI := hj.1
    IsIso (firstOrderThickeningConormalSheafMap hi hj φ)

declarations.name: Ideal.bijective_tensorSMulHomToKer_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 063Y, the affine case.** Let `I ^ 2 = 0` in `A'`, write `A = A' ⧸ I`, let `B` be a
quotient of the `A'`-algebra `B'` which is compatibly an `A`-algebra, and let `J` be the kernel of
`B' → B`.  Assume `A → B` flat.  Then the canonical map `I ⊗[A'] B' → J` is an isomorphism if and
only if `A' → B'` is flat and `J = I B'`.

The second condition says that `X = Spec B` is the fibre product `S ×_{S'} X'`, and
`I ⊗[A'] B'` is the pullback to `X` of the conormal module of `S ⊂ S'` by
`Ideal.tensorEquivTensorQuot`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_tensorSMulHomToKer_iff (hI2 : I ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap B' B)) (hflat : Module.Flat (A' ⧸ I) B) :
    Function.Bijective (I.tensorSMulHomToKer B' B) ↔
      Module.Flat A' B' ∧
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B' B)).restrictScalars A' = I • (⊤ : Submodule A' B')

declarations.name: Ideal.bijective_fibreTensorSMulHomToKer_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 063Y in the affine case, with the source as the pullback of the conormal module.**
Let `I ^ 2 = 0` in `A'`, write `A = A' ⧸ I`, let `B` be a quotient of the `A'`-algebra `B'` which
is compatibly an `A`-algebra, and let `J` be the kernel of `B' → B`. Assume `J ^ 2 = 0` and
`A → B` flat. Then the canonical map `I ⊗[A'] B → J` is an isomorphism if and only if `A' → B'`
is flat and `J = I B'`.

This is `Ideal.bijective_tensorSMulHomToKer_iff` with the source replaced by the pullback
`I ⊗[A'] B` of the conormal module of `S ⊂ S'` to `X`, which is the module condition (2) of the
source speaks about; that form needs `J ^ 2 = 0`, which the version with source `I ⊗[A'] B'` does
not.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_fibreTensorSMulHomToKer_iff (hI2 : I ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hJ2 : RingHom.ker (algebraMap B' B) ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap B' B)) (hflat : Module.Flat (A' ⧸ I) B) :
    Function.Bijective (I.fibreTensorSMulHomToKer B' B hJ2 hsurj) ↔
      Module.Flat A' B' ∧
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B' B)).restrictScalars A' = I • (⊤ : Submodule A' B')
declarations.comment: affine case, with the source the pullback of the conormal module

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_regularSequence_with_common_annihilator_mod_last
declarations.doc:
A regular sequence in a local ring can have its first two terms annihilate a common nonzero
element modulo its last term.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_regularSequence_with_common_annihilator_mod_last :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsLocalRing R) (x y z : R),
      x ∈ maximalIdeal R ∧ y ∈ maximalIdeal R ∧ z ∈ maximalIdeal R ∧
        RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R [x, y, z] ∧
        ∃ δ : R ⧸ Ideal.span {z},
          δ ≠ 0 ∧
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {z}) x) * δ = 0 ∧
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {z}) y) * δ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_regular_sequence_flat_quotient_not_koszulRegular_fiber
declarations.doc:
A regular sequence in a local ring can give a flat quotient over a local
base while its closed-fiber sequence fails even Koszul regularity.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_regular_sequence_flat_quotient_not_koszulRegular_fiber :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : CommRing B)
      (_ : IsLocalRing A) (_ : IsLocalRing B) (_ : Algebra A B)
      (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)) (x y : B),
      let I : Ideal B := (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B)
      x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ∧
      y ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ∧
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular B [x, y] ∧
      Module.Flat A (B ⧸ Ideal.ofList [x, y]) ∧
      ¬ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (B ⧸ I)
        [Ideal.Quotient.mk I x, Ideal.Quotient.mk I y] ∧
      ¬ Koszul.IsKoszulRegular
        (fun i : Fin 2 =>
          if i = 0 then Ideal.Quotient.mk I x else Ideal.Quotient.mk I y)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_isDegreewiseSplitEpi_factorization
declarations.doc:
Let `α : K ⟶ L` be a morphism of cochain complexes of an additive category. Then there are a
complex `K'`, a factorization `α = i ≫ α'` of `α` through `K'` with `α'` a termwise split
surjection, and a retraction `s : K' ⟶ K` of `i` with `s ≫ i` homotopic to `𝟙 K'`. Moreover `K'`
inherits the vanishing bounds of `K` and `L`, so that `K'` is bounded below, bounded above or
bounded as soon as both `K` and `L` are.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDegreewiseSplitEpi_factorization [HasBinaryBiproducts A]
    {K L : CochainComplex A ℤ} (α : K ⟶ L) :
    ∃ (K' : CochainComplex A ℤ) (i : K ⟶ K') (α' : K' ⟶ L) (s : K' ⟶ K),
      i ≫ α' = α ∧ α'.IsDegreewiseSplitEpi ∧ i ≫ s = 𝟙 K ∧
        Nonempty (Homotopy (s ≫ i) (𝟙 K')) ∧
        (∀ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE a → L.IsStrictlyGE a → K'.IsStrictlyGE a) ∧
        (∀ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE a → L.IsStrictlyLE (a - 1) → K'.IsStrictlyLE a)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
A morphism of cochain complexes `α : P ⟶ K` in an abelian category is a
*projective resolution* of `K` if `P` is bounded above, all the terms of `P` are
projective objects, and `α` is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public class IsProjectiveResolution {P K : CochainComplex C ℤ} (α : P ⟶ K) : Prop
    extends QuasiIso α
declarations.comment: The case of a complex; for an object it is `ProjectiveResolution`.

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveResolution.CohomologyVanishing.cohomology_vanishes_of_isProjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0645, Lemma 13.19.2, part (1).**  If `K^•` has a projective
resolution, then `H^n(K^•) = 0` for `n ≫ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomology_vanishes_of_isProjectiveResolution
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) (h : IsProjectiveResolution K) :
    CohomologyVanishesForLargeN K

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveResolution.CohomologyVanishing.exists_boundedAbove_quasiIso_of_cohomologyVanishes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0645, Lemma 13.19.2, part (2).**  If `H^n(K^•) = 0` for
`n ≫ 0`, then there exists a quasi-isomorphism `L^• → K^•` with `L^•` bounded
above.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedAbove_quasiIso_of_cohomologyVanishes
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) (h : CohomologyVanishesForLargeN K) :
    ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : L ⟶ K), IsBoundedAboveComplex L ∧ QuasiIso f

declarations.name: ProjectiveResolutionLemma.statement3
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3.**
Assume `A` has enough projectives. Let `K^•` be a complex with `K^n = 0` for
`n > a`. Then there exists a projective resolution `α : P^• → K^•` (Definition 4)
bounded above by `a` such that, additionally, each component `α^n : P^n → K^n` is
an epimorphism.
declarations.statement: alias statement3

declarations.name: ProjectiveResolutionLemma.statement2
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.**
Assume `A` has enough projectives. Let `K^•` be a complex with `H^n(K^•) = 0`
for all `n ≫ 0`. Then `K^•` has a projective resolution in the sense of
Definition 4, i.e. there exists an upper bound `N` and a projective resolution
of `K^•` bounded above by `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2 [EnoughProjectives C] (K : CochainComplex C ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ M : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, M ≤ n → IsZero (K.homology n)) :
    ∃ N : ℤ, Nonempty (ProjectiveResolutionComplex K N)

declarations.name: ProjectiveResolutionLemma.statement1
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.**
If `A` has enough projectives, then every object `A` of `A` has a projective
resolution in the sense of Definition 3: there is a complex `P^•` of projectives
with `P^n = 0` for `n > 0` and a quasi-isomorphism `P^• → A[0]`. Viewing the
resolution as a projective resolution (Definition 4) of the complex `A[0]` with
upper bound `0` captures exactly conditions (1)–(4) of Definition 3.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1 [EnoughProjectives C] (A : C) :
    Nonempty (ProjectiveResolutionComplex (single₀ A) 0)

declarations.name: projective_into_acyclic_is_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be an acyclic complex and `P` a bounded above complex of projective objects. Then
every morphism of complexes `f : P ⟶ K` is homotopic to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_into_acyclic_is_zero
    {C : Type*} [CategoryTheory.Category C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C]
    (P K : CochainComplex C ℤ)
    (n : ℤ) (hP : P.IsStrictlyLE n)
    (hProj : ∀ i : ℤ, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i))
    (hK : HomologicalComplex.Acyclic K)
    (f : P ⟶ K) : Nonempty (Homotopy f 0)

declarations.name: bijective_postcomp_quotient_map
declarations.doc:
**Remark [Stacks 0648]** for a K-projective complex, the dual of [Stacks 05TF]. If `P` is a
K-projective cochain complex and `α : L ⟶ K` is a quasi-isomorphism, then postcomposition with
the image of `α` in the homotopy category is a bijection
`Hom_{K(A)}(P, L) → Hom_{K(A)}(P, K)`.

Its surjectivity is the first assertion of [Stacks 0649] and its injectivity is
[Stacks 064A].
declarations.statement:
lemma bijective_postcomp_quotient_map {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    {P K L : CochainComplex A ℤ} [P.IsKProjective] (α : L ⟶ K) [QuasiIso α] :
    Function.Bijective (fun β : (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj L ↦
      β ≫ (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).map α)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.IsKProjective.exists_lift_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0649.** Let `A` be an abelian category, let `α : L ⟶ K` be a quasi-isomorphism of
cochain complexes in `A` and let `P` be a K-projective cochain complex — for instance one which
is bounded above and consists of projective objects, by
`CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective`. Then, given `γ : P ⟶ K`:
(1) there is a `β : P ⟶ L` with `β ≫ α` homotopic to `γ`, and
(2) if the terms of `P` are projective and `α` is epimorphic in every degree, there is a
`β : P ⟶ L` with `β ≫ α = γ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CochainComplex.IsKProjective.exists_lift_of_quasiIso {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A]
    [Abelian A] {P K L : CochainComplex A ℤ} [P.IsKProjective] (α : L ⟶ K) [QuasiIso α]
    (γ : P ⟶ K) :
    (∃ β : P ⟶ L, Nonempty (Homotopy (β ≫ α) γ)) ∧
      ((∀ n : ℤ, Projective (P.X n)) → (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (α.f n)) → ∃ β : P ⟶ L, β ≫ α = γ)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.IsKProjective.nonempty_homotopy_of_comp_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064A.** Let `A` be an abelian category, let `α : L ⟶ K` be a quasi-isomorphism of
cochain complexes in `A` and let `P` be a K-projective cochain complex — for instance one which
is bounded above and consists of projective objects, by
`CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective`. Then two morphisms `β₁, β₂ : P ⟶ L` whose
composites with `α` are homotopic are themselves homotopic; in particular a lift of a given
`γ : P ⟶ K` through `α` up to homotopy is unique up to homotopy.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CochainComplex.IsKProjective.nonempty_homotopy_of_comp_quasiIso {A : Type u}
    [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] {P K L : CochainComplex A ℤ} [P.IsKProjective] (α : L ⟶ K)
    [QuasiIso α] {β₁ β₂ : P ⟶ L} (h : Homotopy (β₁ ≫ α) (β₂ ≫ α)) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy β₁ β₂)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isKProjective_iff_Qh_map_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064B.** Let `A` be an abelian category and let `P` be a cochain complex in `A`. Then
`P` is K-projective — which a bounded above complex of projective objects is, by
`CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective` — if and only if for every object `L` of the homotopy
category `K(A)` the localization functor `Qh : K(A) ⥤ D(A)` induces a bijection
`Mor_{K(A)}(P, L) → Mor_{D(A)}(P, L)`. The Stacks lemma is the forward implication.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CochainComplex.isKProjective_iff_Qh_map_bijective {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A]
    [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] (P : CochainComplex A ℤ) :
    P.IsKProjective ↔ ∀ L : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
      Function.Bijective (DerivedCategory.Qh.map :
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶ L) → _)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_shortExact_isProjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category with enough projectives, let
`S : 0 ⟶ S.X₁ ⟶ S.X₂ ⟶ S.X₃ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of cochain complexes
of `C` with `S.X₁` bounded above, and let `π : P ⟶ S.X₃` be a projective
resolution. Then there is a short exact sequence of complexes
`0 ⟶ P₁ ⟶ P₂ ⟶ P ⟶ 0` mapping to `S`, with `π` as its third component, whose
first two components `π₁ : P₁ ⟶ S.X₁` and `π₂ : P₂ ⟶ S.X₂` are projective
resolutions as well.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shortExact_isProjectiveResolution
    [EnoughProjectives C] (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ)) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (n : ℤ) [S.X₁.IsStrictlyLE n] {P : CochainComplex C ℤ} (π : P ⟶ S.X₃)
    [IsProjectiveResolution π] :
    ∃ (P₁ P₂ : CochainComplex C ℤ) (i : P₁ ⟶ P₂) (p : P₂ ⟶ P) (hip : i ≫ p = 0)
      (π₁ : P₁ ⟶ S.X₁) (π₂ : P₂ ⟶ S.X₂),
      (ShortComplex.mk i p hip).ShortExact ∧ IsProjectiveResolution π₁ ∧
        IsProjectiveResolution π₂ ∧ i ≫ π₂ = π₁ ≫ S.f ∧ p ≫ π = π₂ ≫ S.g

declarations.name: CochainComplex.IsKProjective.hom_eq_zero_of_isStrictlyGE_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064D.** Let `A` be an abelian category, let `P` be a K-projective cochain complex of
`A` with `P^i = 0` for `i < n` — for instance a bounded complex of projective objects with that
property, by `CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective` — and let `K` be a cochain complex with
`H^i(K) = 0` for `i > m`, where `m < n`. Then `Mor_{K(A)}(P, K) = Mor_{D(A)}(P, K) = 0`: every
morphism from `P` to `K` in the homotopy category, and every morphism from `P` to `K` in the
derived category, is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CochainComplex.IsKProjective.hom_eq_zero_of_isStrictlyGE_of_isLE {A : Type u}
    [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] (P K : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    [P.IsKProjective] (n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyGE n] (m : ℤ) (hmn : m < n) [K.IsLE m] :
    (∀ f : (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶
      (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K, f = 0) ∧
      (∀ f : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K, f = 0)

declarations.name: exists_lift_homotopy_of_projective
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 064E. Let `β : P^• → L^•` and `α : E^• → L^•` be maps of cochain
complexes in an abelian category `A`, and `n : ℤ`. Assume `P^•` is a bounded
complex of projectives with `P^i = 0` for `i < n`, and that `H^i(α)` is an
isomorphism for `i > n` and an epimorphism for `i = n`. Then there is a chain map
`γ : P^• → E^•` with `α ∘ γ` homotopic to `β`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_homotopy_of_projective (P E L : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (β : P ⟶ L) (α : E ⟶ L) (n : ℤ)
    (hProj : ∀ i, Projective (P.X i))
    (hBddAbove : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i, b < i → IsZero (P.X i))
    (hBelow : ∀ i, i < n → IsZero (P.X i))
    (hIso : ∀ i, n < i → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap α i))
    (hEpi : Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap α n)) :
    ∃ γ : P ⟶ E, Nonempty (Homotopy (γ ≫ α) β)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.ComputingTor.derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064G.** For every `R`-module `M`, the total left derived tensor product
`- ⊗ᴸ_R M : D⁻(R) ⟶ D⁻(R)` exists.
declarations.statement: public def derivedTensorProduct (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) : TotalDerivedTensor M

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.derivedExtensionScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064H.** Derived extension of scalars on bounded-above derived categories.
This is the dual of the bounded-below right derived functor of extension of scalars on
opposite module categories, where projective modules become injective objects.
declarations.statement:
public def derivedExtensionScalars (f : R →+* A)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wR} (ModuleCat.{max uA (max uR v)} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{max uA (max uR v)} A)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA (max uR v)} R)ᵒᵖ]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA (max uR v)} A)ᵒᵖ] :
    DerivedCategory.Minus (ModuleCat.{max uA (max uR v)} R) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Minus (ModuleCat.{max uA (max uR v)} A)

declarations.name: TotalTensorComplex.tensorTotal_preserves_homotopy_and_descends
declarations.doc:
Tensoring with a fixed complex and taking the total complex preserves homotopic maps,
and therefore induces an endofunctor of the homotopy category of complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorTotal_preserves_homotopy_and_descends {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    let T := (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{u} R)).map₂CochainComplex.flip.obj P
    (∀ {L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ} {f g : L ⟶ M},
      homotopic (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) f g →
        homotopic (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (T.map f) (T.map g)) ∧
    ∃ T' : HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤
        HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
      HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ T' =
        T ⋙ HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)

declarations.name: TotalTensorComplex.tleft_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
Tensoring on the left with a fixed complex and totalizing is an exact functor of
triangulated categories on the homotopy category.

Stated for an arbitrary preadditive monoidal category whose tensor product is additive in each
variable, which is the generality the statement holds in. Module categories are the case of
interest, at any module universe: the instances above hold for `ModuleCat.{max u v} R` as well
as for `ModuleCat.{u} R`.

declarations.name: TotalTensorComplex.tright_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
Tensoring on the right with a fixed complex and totalizing is an exact functor of
triangulated categories on the homotopy category. This is genuinely distinct from
`tleft_isTriangulated`: the two differ by the Koszul sign in the commutativity constraint.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.KFlat.kFlat_of_flat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 064K.** A bounded above cochain complex of flat modules is K-flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem kFlat_of_flat {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) (d : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d]
    [∀ n : ℤ, Module.Flat R (P.X n)] :
    P.KFlat

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.quasiIso_trightCochain_map
declarations.doc:
A quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes remains a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring on
the right with any complex. This is the companion of `quasiIso_tleftCochain_map` (Stacks 064L),
whose fixed factor is the left one.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_trightCochain_map
    {P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ} (α : P ⟶ Q) [QuasiIso α]
    (hP : P.KFlat) (hQ : Q.KFlat) (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) :
    QuasiIso ((TrightCochain L).map α)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.quasiIso_tleftCochain_map
declarations.doc:
A quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes remains a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring on
the left with any complex and taking the total complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiIso_tleftCochain_map {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ} (α : P ⟶ Q) [QuasiIso α]
    (hP : P.KFlat) (hQ : Q.KFlat) (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) :
    QuasiIso ((TleftCochain L).map α)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
The derived tensor product with `M`, computed by a K-flat resolution of a representative of
`M`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedTensorProduct
    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) :
    DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedTensorProduct_commShift
declarations.doc: The derived tensor product commutes with the shift functors.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance derivedTensorProduct_commShift
    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) :
    (derivedTensorProduct M).CommShift ℤ

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedTensorProduct_isTriangulated
declarations.doc: The derived tensor product is an exact functor of triangulated categories.
declarations.statement:
