    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) :
    (derivedTensorProduct M).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedTensorProduct_iso_lift_of_kFlat_resolution
declarations.doc:
A K-flat resolution of any representative of `M` computes the derived tensor product.
The comparison is a natural isomorphism, uniquely determined by its pullback to the homotopy
category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensorProduct_iso_lift_of_kFlat_resolution
    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (P K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ P) [QuasiIso f]
    (hK : K.KFlat)
    (_eP : (DerivedCategory.Qh (C := ModuleCat.{max u v} R)).obj
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ≅ M) :
    let W := HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let F := Tright K ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh
    let hF : W.IsInvertedBy F := fun _ _ g hg ↦
      Localization.inverts DerivedCategory.Qh W _
        (CochainComplex.KFlat.kFlat_tright_preserves_quasiIso K hK g hg)
    let F' := Localization.lift F hF DerivedCategory.Qh
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ derivedTensorProduct M ≅ F) ∧
      ∀ α : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ derivedTensorProduct M ≅ F,
        ∃! e : derivedTensorProduct M ≅ F',
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh e =
            α ≪≫ (Localization.fac F hF DerivedCategory.Qh).symm

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.HasFiniteFreeResolutionUpTo
declarations.doc:
A module has a finite free resolution through degree `n` if there is an exact sequence
`R^{a_n} → ⋯ → R^{a_0} → M → 0`. Exactness is required at `M` and at every finite free term
except the leftmost one.
declarations.statement:
def HasFiniteFreeResolutionUpTo
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
An object `K` of `D(R)` is *`m`-pseudo-coherent* when there is a bounded complex `E` of
finite free `R`-modules and a morphism `α : Q(E) ⟶ K` in `D(R)`, where `Q` sends a complex to its
image in the derived category, such that `Hⁱ(α)` is an isomorphism for every `i > m` and `Hᵐ(α)`
is surjective.
declarations.statement: def IsPseudoCoherentFrom (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (m : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
An object `K` of `D(R)` is *pseudo-coherent* when it is represented by a bounded-above
complex of finite free `R`-modules.
declarations.statement: def IsPseudoCoherent (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` is *`m`-pseudo-coherent* when the object of `D(R)` concentrated in
degree `0` with value `M` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement: def IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (m : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsModulePseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` is *pseudo-coherent* when the object of `D(R)` concentrated in degree `0`
with value `M` is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement: def IsModulePseudoCoherent (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished_one
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1).** If `K` is `(m+1)`-pseudo-coherent and `L` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent, and `(K, L, M, f, g, h)` is a distinguished triangle, then
`M` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.

Assembled from the three sub-lemmas above. The degree bookkeeping: with
`α : Q P ⟶ K` iso on `H^i` (`i > m+1`)/epi on `H^{m+1}` and `β : Q E ⟶ L` iso on
`H^i` (`i > m`)/epi on `H^m`, the cone `C` carries `μ = φ.hom₃ : Q C ⟶ M`. For
`i > m`: `H^i(α)` is epi (iso if `i > m+1`, epi if `i = m+1`), `H^i(β)` iso,
`H^{i+1}(α)` iso (since `i+1 > m+1`), `H^{i+1}(β)` mono (iso since `i+1 > m`), so
Sub-lemma B gives `H^i(μ)` iso. For `i = m`: `H^m(β)` epi, `H^{m+1}(α)` epi,
`H^{m+1}(β)` mono (iso since `m+1 > m`), so Sub-lemma C gives `H^m(μ)` epi. Hence
`(C, μ)` witnesses that `M` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished_one
    (m : ℤ) (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₁ (m + 1))
    (hL : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₂ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₃ m

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished_two
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2).** If `K` and `M` are both `m`-pseudo-coherent, and
`(K, L, M, f, g, h)` is a distinguished triangle, then `L` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent.

Reduction to (1): apply (1) to the (distinguished) inverse-rotated triangle
`(M⟦-1⟧, K, L)`, using that `M⟦-1⟧` is `(m+1)`-pseudo-coherent (shift of the
`m`-pseudo-coherent `M`) and `K` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished_two
    (m : ℤ) (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₁ m)
    (hM : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₃ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₂ m

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished_three
declarations.doc:
**Statement (3).** If `L` is `(m+1)`-pseudo-coherent and `M` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent, and `(K, L, M, f, g, h)` is a distinguished triangle, then
`K` is `(m+1)`-pseudo-coherent.

Reduction to (1): apply (1) to the (distinguished) rotated triangle
`(L, M, K⟦1⟧)`, concluding `K⟦1⟧` is `m`-pseudo-coherent; shifting back by `-1`
and transporting along the isomorphism `(K⟦1⟧)⟦-1⟧ ≅ K` yields that `K` is
`(m+1)`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished_three
    (m : ℤ) (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hL : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₂ (m + 1))
    (hM : IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₃ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom T.obj₁ (m + 1)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.finite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
Statement 1 (Stacks 064S). If `K^•` is `m`-pseudo-coherent and `H^i(K^•) = 0`
for all `i > m`, then `H^m(K^•)` is a finite type `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_homology_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (m : ℤ) (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, m < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) i).obj K)) :
    Module.Finite R ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) m).obj K)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.finitePresentation_homology_succ_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
Statement 2 (Stacks 064S). If `K^•` is `m`-pseudo-coherent and `H^i(K^•) = 0`
for all `i > m + 1`, then `H^{m+1}(K^•)` is a finitely presented `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_homology_succ_of_isPseudoCoherentFrom {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (m : ℤ) (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, m + 1 < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) i).obj K)) :
    Module.FinitePresentation R
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) (m + 1)).obj K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.modulePseudoCoherent_iff_finiteness_and_resolutions
declarations.doc:
Finite generation, finite presentation, finite free resolutions of a fixed length, and
infinite finite free resolutions characterize the corresponding forms of pseudo-coherence for a
module, represented in a universe containing both `R` and `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePseudoCoherent_iff_finiteness_and_resolutions
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R)] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (ULift.{u} M) 0 ↔ Module.Finite R M) ∧
    (IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (ULift.{u} M) (-1) ↔ Module.FinitePresentation R M) ∧
    (∀ d : ℕ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (ULift.{u} M) (-(d : ℤ)) ↔
      HasFiniteFreeResolutionOfLength (R := R) (ULift.{u} M) d) ∧
    (IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := R) (ULift.{u} M) ↔
      Nonempty (FiniteFreeModuleResolution R (ULift.{u} M)))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherent_iff_pseudoCoherentFrom_all_iff_finiteProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064U.** Pseudo-coherence is equivalent both to `m`-pseudo-coherence for every
integer `m` and to admitting a bounded-above finite projective representative. If cohomology
vanishes above `b`, a finite free representative can be chosen to vanish above `b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_iff_pseudoCoherentFrom_all_iff_finiteProjective
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) (b : ℤ) :
    let allDegrees := ∀ m : ℤ, IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m
    let finiteProjectiveRepresentative :=
      ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ,
        (∃ n : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE n) ∧
          (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X i) ∧ Module.Projective R (P.X i)) ∧
          Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K)
    (IsPseudoCoherent K ↔ allDegrees) ∧
      (IsPseudoCoherent K ↔ finiteProjectiveRepresentative) ∧
      (IsPseudoCoherent K →
        (∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) i).obj K)) →
        ∃ (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
          (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ⟶ K),
            (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (F.X i) ∧ Module.Free R (F.X i)) ∧
              F.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ IsIso α)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064V.** In a distinguished triangle in `D(R)`, if two of the three objects are
pseudo-coherent, then so is the third.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) :
    (IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₁ → IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₂ → IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₃) ∧
    (IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₁ → IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₃ → IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₂) ∧
    (IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₂ → IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₃ → IsPseudoCoherent T.obj₁)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_vanishing_and_finite_homology
declarations.doc:
Vanishing above degree `m`, with the appropriate finiteness assumptions on the cohomology
in degrees `m` and `m + 1`, implies `m`-pseudo-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_vanishing_and_finite_homology
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)] [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (m : ℤ) :
    ((∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℤ, m < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
      Module.Finite R ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) m).obj K) →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℤ, m + 1 < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
      Module.FinitePresentation R
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (m + 1)).obj K) →
      Module.Finite R ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) m).obj K) →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_of_biproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064X.** Each summand of an `m`-pseudo-coherent binary biproduct is
`m`-pseudo-coherent, and each summand of a pseudo-coherent binary biproduct is
pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_of_biproduct
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (m : ℤ) :
    (IsPseudoCoherentFrom (K ⊞ L) m →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m ∧ IsPseudoCoherentFrom L m) ∧
    (IsPseudoCoherent (K ⊞ L) → IsPseudoCoherent K ∧ IsPseudoCoherent L)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove
declarations.doc:
A bounded-above complex with suitably pseudo-coherent terms is pseudo-coherent in the
corresponding degrees. In particular, pseudo-coherence of every term implies pseudo-coherence
of the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (hK : ∃ b : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE b) :
    (∀ m : ℤ, (∀ i : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (K.X i) (m - i)) →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) m) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := R) (K.X i)) →
      IsPseudoCoherent (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_iff_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 064Z.** If `B` is pseudo-coherent as an `A`-module, restriction of scalars along
`A → B` preserves and reflects both `m`-pseudo-coherence and pseudo-coherence of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_iff_restrictScalars
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [Ring A] [Ring B] (f : A →+* B)
    (hB : IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := A)
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj (ModuleCat.of B B)))
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) ℤ) (m : ℤ) :
    let Kₐ := ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v w} f).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K
    (IsPseudoCoherentFrom (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) m ↔
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Kₐ) m) ∧
    (IsPseudoCoherent (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) ↔
      IsPseudoCoherent (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Kₐ))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.derivedExtensionScalars_preserves_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
Derived extension of scalars along a homomorphism `f : R →+* A` of commutative rings
preserves `m`-pseudo-coherent objects of the derived category for every integer `m`, and it
preserves pseudo-coherent objects. The source ring, the target ring and the module carrier live
in three independent universes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedExtensionScalars_preserves_pseudoCoherent
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] (f : R →+* A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) :
    (∀ m : ℤ, IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((derivedExtensionScalars f).obj K) m) ∧
      (IsPseudoCoherent K → IsPseudoCoherent ((derivedExtensionScalars f).obj K))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
An object `K` of `D(R)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` if, for every `R`-module `M`, the
cohomology of `K ⊗ᴸ[R] M[0]` vanishes in every degree outside `[a, b]`.

The `comparison` and `_isLeftDerived` arguments certify that `derivedTensor` is the total left
derived functor of ordinary tensor product in the first variable.
declarations.statement:
public def HasTorAmplitude {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (comparison : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (_isLeftDerived : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(R)` has finite Tor dimension if it has Tor amplitude in some finite
integer interval.
declarations.statement:
public def HasFiniteTorDimension {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (comparison : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` has Tor dimension at most `d` if `M[0]` has Tor amplitude in
`[-d, 0]`.
declarations.statement:
public def HasTorDimensionLE {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) (d : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.ModuleHasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` has finite Tor dimension if `M[0]` has finite Tor dimension as an
object of `D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
public def ModuleHasFiniteTorDimension {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.cokernel_flat_of_torAmplitude
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0653.** Let `R` be a ring, `a b : ℤ`, and `K` a bounded above cochain complex of
flat `R`-modules which, as an object of `D(R)`, has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` for some certified
derived tensor product. Then `Coker(d_K^{a-1}) = K^a / Im(d_K^{a-1})` is a flat `R`-module.

The ring universe `u` and the module universe are independent: `R : Type u` and the complex lives
in `ModuleCat.{max u v} R`. Flatness of the terms is spelled out rather than written as
`StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.Termwise.IsComplexOfFlats`, which is available only when the two
  universes agree.

The derived tensor product is an arbitrary certified one, so the statement does not depend on a
construction of it. Boundedness enters through the comparison: the counit of the total left
derived functor of termwise tensoring is invertible at a bounded above complex of flat modules
(`isIso_termwiseDerivedCounit_app_of_flat`), which makes the given comparison map a split
epimorphism there, and cohomology carries that split epimorphism from a vanishing source to a
vanishing target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cokernel_flat_of_torAmplitude
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (hbounded : BoundedAbove K) (hflat : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Flat R (K.X n))
    (hamp : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a b) :
    Module.Flat R (cokernel (K.d (a - 1) a) : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_iff_hasFlatRepresentative
declarations.doc:
An object `K` of `D(R)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` — at the canonical derived tensor
product of Stacks 0BYI — if and only if it is represented by a complex of flat
`R`-modules concentrated in degrees `[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_iff_hasFlatRepresentative (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (a b : ℤ) :
    HasTorAmplitudeCanonical R K a b ↔ HasFlatRepresentative K a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₃_of_obj₁_obj₂
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0655 (1).** Let `K → L → M → K[1]` be a distinguished triangle in `D(R)`. If `K`
has Tor amplitude in `[a + 1, b + 1]` and `L` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `M` has Tor
amplitude in `[a, b]`.

Tor amplitude is `StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude` of Stacks 0652, so the bifunctor
`derivedTensor` is certified by `comparison` and `isLeftDerived` to be the derived tensor
product. This is part (1) of the source statement; the mathematics is the long exact cohomology
sequence of the triangle `(K, L, M)` tensored with `M'[0]`, as in the uncertified-datum helper
`Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.hasTorAmplitudeIn_obj₃_of_obj₁_obj₂`, which this endpoint does not use
because that helper pins the module carriers to the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₃_of_obj₁_obj₂
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₁ (a + 1) (b + 1))
    (hL : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₂ a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₃ a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₂_of_obj₁_obj₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0655 (2).** Let `K → L → M → K[1]` be a distinguished triangle in `D(R)`. If `K`
and `M` both have Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `L` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`.

Tor amplitude is `StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude` of Stacks 0652, so the bifunctor
`derivedTensor` is certified by `comparison` and `isLeftDerived` to be the derived tensor
product. This is part (2) of the source statement; the mathematics is the long exact cohomology
sequence of the triangle `(K, L, M)` tensored with `M'[0]`, as in the uncertified-datum helper
`Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.hasTorAmplitudeIn_obj₂_of_obj₁_obj₃`, which this endpoint does not use
because that helper pins the module carriers to the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₂_of_obj₁_obj₃
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₁ a b)
    (hM : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₃ a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₂ a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_obj₁_of_obj₂_obj₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0655 (3).** Let `K → L → M → K[1]` be a distinguished triangle in `D(R)`. If `L`
has Tor amplitude in `[a + 1, b + 1]` and `M` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `K` has Tor
amplitude in `[a + 1, b + 1]`.

Tor amplitude is `StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude` of Stacks 0652, so the bifunctor
`derivedTensor` is certified by `comparison` and `isLeftDerived` to be the derived tensor
product. This is part (3) of the source statement; the mathematics is the long exact cohomology
sequence of the triangle `(K, L, M)` tensored with `M'[0]`, as in the uncertified-datum helper
`Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.hasTorAmplitudeIn_obj₁_of_obj₂_obj₃`, which this endpoint does not use
because that helper pins the module carriers to the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_obj₁_of_obj₂_obj₃
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))) (a b : ℤ)
    (hL : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₂ (a + 1) (b + 1))
    (hM : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₃ a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived T.obj₁ (a + 1) (b + 1)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0657 (1).** An object of the derived category of `R`-modules is *perfect* if it is
isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def IsPerfect {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0657 (2).** An `R`-module is *perfect* if the complex consisting of it placed in
degree zero is a perfect object of the derived category of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def IsPerfectModule {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)] : Prop

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_iff_pseudoCoherent_and_finiteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0658.** An object of `D(R)` is perfect if and only if it is pseudo-coherent and has
finite Tor dimension, the latter being recorded by the existence of a bounded flat representative.
Moreover a pseudo-coherent object whose Tor amplitude lies in `[a, b]` is represented by a complex
of finite projective modules concentrated in the degrees `[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_iff_pseudoCoherent_and_finiteTorDimension
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) :
    (IsPerfect K ↔
      StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K ∧
        ∃ a b : ℤ, HasFlatRepresentative K a b) ∧
      ∀ a b : ℤ, StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K →
        HasFlatRepresentative K a b →
        ∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ,
          (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (E.X i) ∧ Module.Projective R (E.X i)) ∧
            E.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ E.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
              Nonempty (K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj E)

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_away_of_away
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a finite type algebra over a localization `R_f`, and let `M` be an `A`-module
finitely presented relative to `R_f`. For `g : A` the localized module `M_g` over `A_g` is
finitely presented relative to `R`. The composite `R → R_f → A` is given by an `Algebra R A`
instance together with the scalar tower `R → R_f → A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentationRel_away_of_away {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f : R) {A : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [Algebra (Localization.Away f) A] [Algebra R A]
    [IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away f) A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType (Localization.Away f) A] (g : A) {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A M] (hM : Module.FinitePresentationRel (Localization.Away f) A M) :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R (Localization.Away g) (LocalizedModule.Away g M)

declarations.name: finitePresentation_relative_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `R → A` be a finite type ring map and `M` an `A`-module finitely presented relative
to `R`. For any ring map `R → R'`, set
`A' := A ⊗[R] R'` (an `R'`-algebra via the right factor and, canonically, an `A`-algebra via
the left factor) and `M' := A' ⊗[A] M` (an `A'`-module via the left tensor factor `A'`). Then
`R' → A'` is of finite type, and `M'` is finitely presented relative to `R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_relative_baseChange (R A R' M : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R R']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Algebra.FiniteType R A]
    (hM : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M) :
    letI : Algebra R' (TensorProduct R A R') := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    letI : Algebra A (TensorProduct R A R') := Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra
    Algebra.FiniteType R' (TensorProduct R A R') ∧
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R' (TensorProduct R A R')
      (TensorProduct A (TensorProduct R A R') M)

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_comp
declarations.doc:
Stacks 065C, Lemma 15.82.7. Given finite type ring maps `R → A` and `A → B` and a
`B`-module `M`, if `M` is finitely presented relative to `A` and `A` is of finite presentation
over `R`, then `M` is finitely presented relative to `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentationRel_comp {R A B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    (hM : Module.FinitePresentationRel A B M) : Module.FinitePresentationRel R B M

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_iff_of_span_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Relative finite presentation of a module over a finite type algebra can be checked on a
finite family of principal opens covering the spectrum: if `f : ι → A` generates the unit ideal,
then `M` is finitely presented relative to `R` exactly when each `M_{f i}` is finitely presented
relative to `R` over `A_{f i}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentationRel_iff_of_span_eq_top {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FiniteType R A] {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A M] {ι : Type x} [Finite ι] (f : ι → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) :
    (∀ i, Module.FinitePresentationRel R (Localization.Away (f i))
      (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ↔ Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.derivedTensorPolynomialEvalZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 065F.** If `R[X] → R` evaluates `X` at zero, then for every `K ∈ D(R)`,
the derived tensor product of `K`, regarded as an `R[X]`-complex, with `R` is isomorphic in
`D(R)` to `K ⊞ K[1]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensorPolynomialEvalZeroIso
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (D : KFlatDerivedTensoringDatum (Polynomial R))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
    let ev : Polynomial R →+* R := Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (RingHom.id R) 0
    letI : Module (Polynomial R) R := ev.toAlgebra.toModule
    Nonempty
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          (Polynomial.C : R →+* Polynomial R)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
            ((D.tensor.obj ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ev).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (Polynomial R)) 0).obj
                (ModuleCat.of (Polynomial R) R))) ≅
        Limits.biprod K
          ((shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (1 : ℤ)).obj K))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_restrictScalars_polynomial_evalZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 065G.** An object of `D(R)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent over `R` if and only if,
after letting `X` act by zero, it is `m`-pseudo-coherent over `R[X]`.

For an object represented by a complex, `Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactors` identifies the
right-hand object with the localization of that complex after restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_restrictScalars_polynomial_evalZero
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) (m : ℤ) :
    let ev : Polynomial R →+* R := Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (RingHom.id R) (0 : R)
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m ↔
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} ev).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) m

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_polynomialPresentation_independent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 065H.** For a finite-type `R`-algebra `A`, `m`-pseudo-coherence of an object of
`D(A)` after restriction to a finite polynomial presentation is independent of the presentation.
The same is true of pseudo-coherence. For an object represented by a complex,
`Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactors` identifies each restricted object below with the localization
of the representing complex after degreewise restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_polynomialPresentation_independent
    {R : Type u} {A : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (m : ℤ) :
    ((∃ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Function.Surjective α ∧
        IsPseudoCoherentFrom
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} α.toRingHom).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) m) ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Function.Surjective α →
        IsPseudoCoherentFrom
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} α.toRingHom).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) m) ∧
    ((∃ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Function.Surjective α ∧
        IsPseudoCoherent
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} α.toRingHom).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Function.Surjective α →
        IsPseudoCoherent
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} α.toRingHom).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 065I (1).** An object of `D(A)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `R` if its
restriction of scalars along every finite polynomial presentation of `A` over `R` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent. By Stacks 065H it is equivalent to require this of one presentation.
declarations.statement:
public def IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent

public def IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.Sequence.isRegular_append_of_isRegular_quotient
declarations.doc:
Let `f` be a regular sequence in `A` generating the ideal `I`, and let `g` be a list of
elements of `A` whose images in `A ⧸ I` form a regular sequence. Then `f ++ g` is a regular
sequence in `A`.

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular.of_flat_of_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 065L.** Let `R → S` be a flat ring map, `M` an `R`-module and `rs = f_1, …, f_r` an
`M`-quasi-regular sequence in `R`. Then the images of `f_1, …, f_r` in `S` form a
`M ⊗_R S`-quasi-regular sequence, where the base change is taken abstractly: `N` is any
`S`-module receiving an `R`-linear `f : M →ₗ[R] N` that exhibits it as the base change of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsQuasiRegular.of_flat_of_isBaseChange {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N]
    [IsScalarTower R S N] [Module.Flat R S] {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : IsBaseChange S f) {rs : List R}
    (reg : IsQuasiRegular M rs) : IsQuasiRegular N (rs.map (algebraMap R S))

declarations.name: isMQuasiregular_iff_isMQuasiregular_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 065N, Lemma 10.69.9).**
The sequence `f_1, ..., f_r` is `M`-quasi-regular (over `R`, with respect to `M`)
if and only if the image sequence `f̄_1, ..., f̄_r` is `M̄`-quasi-regular (over
`R̄ = R / I_R`, with respect to `M̄ = M / I_M`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isMQuasiregular_iff_isMQuasiregular_quotient {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → R) :
    letI := mbarModule (M := M) f
    IsMQuasiregular (M := M) f ↔
      IsMQuasiregular (R := Rbar f) (M := Mbar (M := M) f) (fbar f)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_enoughProjectives
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an object of an abelian category with enough projectives and let `n : ℕ`. If the
single group `Extⁿ(X, Y)` vanishes for every object `Y`, then `X` has projective dimension `< n`.
declarations.comment:
The implication `(3) ⇒ (1)`, proved the source's way: in an abelian category with
enough projectives, indexed by `HasProjectiveDimensionLT X n`, so that the source's `R`-modules of
projective dimension `≤ n` are the case `C = ModuleCat.{v} R` at `n + 1`. The converse `(1) ⇒ (2)`
and, at a single degree, `(2) ⇒ (3)` are `hasProjectiveDimensionLT_iff`; the sibling under enough
injectives is `hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_enoughInjectives`. Projective dimension is Ext-measured
here rather than defined by a finite projective resolution (Definition 00O4, Lemma 0CXC); see the
module docstring.

declarations.name: ringGlobalDimension_lt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 065T.** Let `R` be a ring and `n : ℕ`. The following are equivalent: the global
dimension of `R` is `< n`; every `R`-module has projective dimension `< n`; every finite
`R`-module has projective dimension `< n`; every cyclic `R`-module `R ⧸ I` has projective
dimension `< n`. The source's bound `≤ n` is the case `n + 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringGlobalDimension_lt_tfae (R : Type u) [Ring R] [Small.{v} R] (n : ℕ) :
    List.TFAE
      [(⨆ M : ModuleCat.{u} R, projectiveDimension M) < n,
       ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R, HasProjectiveDimensionLT M n,
       ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R, Module.Finite R M → HasProjectiveDimensionLT M n,
       ∀ I : Ideal R, HasProjectiveDimensionLT (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I)) n]
declarations.comment:
Indexed by `HasProjectiveDimensionLT _ n`, so that the source's `≤ n` is the case
`n + 1`; item (1) is the global dimension `⨆ M, projectiveDimension M` of Tag 00O6, and the
modules of items (2) and (3) range over an arbitrary universe `v` with `Small.{v} R`, of which the
source is the case `v = u`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: exact_mapCotangent_kerCotangentToTensor_and_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 065V (Lemma 10.134.7).** Let `A → B → C` be ring maps with `A → C`
surjective, and set `I = ker (A → C)` and `J = ker (B → C)`. Then the sequence
`I/I² → J/J² → Ω[B⁄A] ⊗_B B/J → 0` is exact: the image of `Ideal.mapCotangent` is the
kernel of `KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor`, and the latter is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_mapCotangent_kerCotangentToTensor_and_surjective
    (A B C : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hAC : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A C))
    (hle : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A C) ≤
      Ideal.comap (Algebra.ofId A B) (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B C))) :
    Function.Exact
      (Ideal.mapCotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A C)) (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B C))
        (Algebra.ofId A B) hle)
      (KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor A B C) ∧
    Function.Surjective (KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor A B C)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.tensorProductDifferential_tmul
declarations.doc:
On a pure tensor whose first factor has degree `p`, the tensor-product
differential is `d a ⊗ₜ b + (-1)^p • (a ⊗ₜ d b)`.
declarations.statement:
