declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.canonicalBaseChangeComparison_paste
declarations.doc:
**The pasting law of Tag 065Z.** For two commutative squares of commutative rings stacked on
top of one another, the comparison of the outer square agrees with the comparison of the lower
square, extended along the upper left map, followed by the comparison of the upper square — both
read through the composition isomorphisms of derived extension of scalars.

Both sides are determined by the same counit equation at K-flat complexes, so the identity
reduces to the underived comparison on pure tensors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalBaseChangeComparison_paste
    (f : R →+* A) (g₁ : R →+* R') (h₁ : A →+* A') (i₁ : R' →+* A')
    (g₂ : R' →+* R'') (h₂ : A' →+* A'') (i₂ : R'' →+* A'')
    (sq₁ : h₁.comp f = i₁.comp g₁) (sq₂ : h₂.comp i₁ = i₂.comp g₂)
    (X : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :
    (totalDerivedExtensionScalarsComp.{u, u} g₁ g₂).hom.app
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} f).mapDerivedCategory.obj X) ≫
      (canonicalBaseChangeComparison.{u, w} f (g₂.comp g₁) (h₂.comp h₁) i₂
        (comp_comp_eq_comp_comp f g₁ h₁ i₁ g₂ h₂ i₂ sq₁ sq₂)).app X =
    (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u} g₂).functor.map
        ((canonicalBaseChangeComparison.{u, w} f g₁ h₁ i₁ sq₁).app X) ≫
      (canonicalBaseChangeComparison.{u, w} i₁ g₂ h₂ i₂ sq₂).app
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u} h₁).functor.obj X) ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} i₂).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalarsComp.{u, u} h₁ h₂).hom.app X)
declarations.comment: the comparison of a horizontal composite of two commutative squares of rings is the composite of the two comparisons, read through the composition isomorphisms of derived extension of scalars; this is what compatibility of the comparison with localizing a square amounts to

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.canonicalBaseChangeComparison_localization
declarations.doc:
**Tag 065Z is compatible with localizing a square at a prime.** Pasting a commutative square
of rings with the localization square of its right-hand column at a prime `y` of `A'` composes
the two comparisons: the comparison of the square

`R → A`, `R → R'_{y ∩ R'}`, `A → A'_y`, `R'_{y ∩ R'} → A'_y`

is the comparison of the given square, extended along `R' → R'_{y ∩ R'}`, followed by the
comparison of the localization square.  This is
`RingTheory.TorIndependence.canonicalBaseChangeComparison_paste` with the localization square as
its second floor.

Note that the localization square is *not* a pushout square; Tag 065Z attaches a comparison to
every commutative square, and that is all this uses.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalBaseChangeComparison_localization
    (f : R →+* A) (g : R →+* R') (h : A →+* A') (i : R' →+* A')
    (sq : h.comp f = i.comp g) (y : Ideal A') [y.IsPrime]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.AtPrime (y.comap i)))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.AtPrime y))]
    (X : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :
    (totalDerivedExtensionScalarsComp.{u, u} g
          (algebraMap R' (Localization.AtPrime (y.comap i)))).hom.app
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} f).mapDerivedCategory.obj X) ≫
      (canonicalBaseChangeComparison.{u, w} f
        ((algebraMap R' (Localization.AtPrime (y.comap i))).comp g)
        ((algebraMap A' (Localization.AtPrime y)).comp h)
        (Localization.localRingHom (y.comap i) y i rfl)
        (comp_comp_eq_comp_comp f g h i (algebraMap R' (Localization.AtPrime (y.comap i)))
          (algebraMap A' (Localization.AtPrime y))
          (Localization.localRingHom (y.comap i) y i rfl) sq
          (comp_algebraMap_eq_localRingHom_comp i y))).app X =
    (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u}
          (algebraMap R' (Localization.AtPrime (y.comap i)))).functor.map
        ((canonicalBaseChangeComparison.{u, w} f g h i sq).app X) ≫
      (canonicalBaseChangeComparison.{u, w} i
          (algebraMap R' (Localization.AtPrime (y.comap i)))
          (algebraMap A' (Localization.AtPrime y))
          (Localization.localRingHom (y.comap i) y i rfl)
          (comp_algebraMap_eq_localRingHom_comp i y)).app
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u} h).functor.obj X) ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u}
            (Localization.localRingHom (y.comap i) y i rfl)).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalarsComp.{u, u} h
          (algebraMap A' (Localization.AtPrime y))).hom.app X)
declarations.comment: the comparison is compatible with localizing a square at a prime: pasting a square with the localization square of its right-hand column composes the two comparisons

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.derivedBaseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
Let `R → A`, `R → R'`, `A → A'`, and `R' → A'` be a commutative square of
commutative rings. There is a natural comparison
`K ⊗ᴸ_R R' ⟶ K ⊗ᴸ_A A'` in `D(R')`.

The first component of the result is the underived comparison, normalized on pure tensors.
The second is its canonical lift between any chosen models of the two total left-derived
functors; the displayed factorization records canonicity as well as functoriality in `K`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedBaseChangeComparison
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} {R' : Type uRp} {A' : Type uAp}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing R'] [CommRing A']
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R')]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A')]
    (f : R →+* A) (g : R →+* R') (h : A →+* A') (i : R' →+* A')
    (sq : h.comp f = i.comp g) :
    let Res_f := ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} f
    let Res_i := ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} i
    let Ext_g := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uRp, max v uR uA uRp uAp} g
    let Ext_h := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uA, uAp, max v uR uA uRp uAp} h
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} f).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj.{max v uR uA uRp uAp, uR, uA} f).isLeftAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} f).IsRightAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max v uR uA uRp uAp, uR, uA} f).isRightAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} i).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj.{max v uR uA uRp uAp, uRp, uAp} i).isLeftAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} i).IsRightAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max v uR uA uRp uAp, uRp, uAp} i).isRightAdjoint
    let F_R := Res_f ⋙ Ext_g
    let F_A := Ext_h ⋙ Res_i
    let U_g := Ext_g.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R')
    let U_h := Ext_h.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A')
    ∀ (L_g : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R'))
      (L_h : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A'))
      (alpha_g : DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R) ⋙ L_g ⟶ U_g)
      (alpha_h : DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) ⋙ L_h ⟶ U_h),
      [L_g.IsLeftDerivedFunctor alpha_g
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] →
      [L_h.IsLeftDerivedFunctor alpha_h
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] →
      let DRes_f := Res_f.mapDerivedCategory
      let DRes_i := Res_i.mapDerivedCategory
      let beta_R :
          DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) ⋙ (DRes_f ⋙ L_g) ⟶
            F_R.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
              DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R') :=
        (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight Res_f.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom L_g ≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).hom ≫
          Functor.whiskerLeft (Res_f.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) alpha_g ≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight
            (Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso (Iso.refl F_R)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom
            (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R'))
      let beta_A :
          DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) ⋙ (L_h ⋙ DRes_i) ⟶
            F_A.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
              DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R') :=
        (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight alpha_h DRes_i ≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).hom ≫
          Functor.whiskerLeft (Ext_h.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
            Res_i.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom ≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight
            (Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso (Iso.refl F_A)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).hom
            (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R'))
      Σ' (tau0 : F_R ⟶ F_A),
        {tau : DRes_f ⋙ L_g ⟶ L_h ⋙ DRes_i //
          (∀ (M : ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) (r' : R') (m : M),
            tau0.app M (r' ⊗ₜ[R,g] m) = (i r') ⊗ₜ[A,h] m) ∧
          Functor.whiskerLeft (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A)) tau ≫
            beta_A =
            beta_R ≫ Functor.whiskerRight
                (NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex tau0 (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
                (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R'))}

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent
declarations.doc:
Two `R`-algebras are Tor independent over `R` when their positive-degree
Tor modules over `R` vanish.
declarations.statement:
public def TorIndependent (R : Type uR) (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] : Prop

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorIndependence.derivedBaseChangeComparison_isIso_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0661.** If `A` and `R'` are Tor independent over `R`, then the canonical comparison
from derived base change over `R` to derived base change over `A` is an isomorphism, for every
pushout square with upper-right corner `A'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedBaseChangeComparison_isIso_of_torIndependent
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} {R' : Type uRp} {A' : Type uAp}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing R'] [CommRing A']
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R A'] [Algebra A A'] [Algebra R' A']
    [IsScalarTower R A A'] [IsScalarTower R R' A'] [Algebra.IsPushout R A R' A']
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A)]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R')]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A')]
    (hTor : TorIndependent R A R') :
    let f : R →+* A := algebraMap R A
    let g : R →+* R' := algebraMap R R'
    let h : A →+* A' := algebraMap A A'
    let i : R' →+* A' := algebraMap R' A'
    let sq : h.comp f = i.comp g := by
      exact (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R A A').symm.trans
        (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R R' A')
    let Ext_g := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uRp, max v uR uA uRp uAp} g
    let Ext_h := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uA, uAp, max v uR uA uRp uAp} h
    letI : Ext_g.IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max v uR uA uRp uAp, uR, uRp}
        g).isLeftAdjoint
    letI : Ext_h.IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max v uR uA uRp uAp, uA, uAp}
        h).isLeftAdjoint
    let U_g := Ext_g.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R')
    let U_h := Ext_h.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A')
    ∀ (L_g : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R'))
      (L_h : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A'))
      (alpha_g : DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R) ⋙ L_g ⟶ U_g)
      (alpha_h : DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A) ⋙ L_h ⟶ U_h),
      [L_g.IsLeftDerivedFunctor alpha_g
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} R)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] →
      [L_h.IsLeftDerivedFunctor alpha_h
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v uR uA uRp uAp} A)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] →
      let comparison := derivedBaseChangeComparison f g h i sq
        L_g L_h alpha_g alpha_h
      IsIso comparison.2.1

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensorSpectralSequence.exists_derived_tensor_spectral_sequences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0662.** For two bounded-above objects `K`, `L` of the derived category of a
commutative ring `R` there are two convergent spectral sequences
`'E_2^{p,q} = H^p(K ⊗^L H^q(L))` and `''E_2^{p,q} = H^p(H^q(K) ⊗^L L)`, both abutting to
`H^{p+q}(K ⊗^L L)`.

They are the spectral sequences of the two canonical filtrations of the total tensor complex
`P^• ⊗ Q^•` of bounded-above complexes of projectives representing `K` and `L`; the abutment
isomorphism is the one induced by those representatives and the canonical K-flat comparison of
the derived tensor product, and the derived second-page isomorphisms factor through the
filtered-complex second-page isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_derived_tensor_spectral_sequences
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (K L : DerivedCategory.Minus (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
    ∃ (P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (bP bQ : ℤ),
      P.IsStrictlyLE bP ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Projective (P.X i)) ∧
      Q.IsStrictlyLE bQ ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Projective (Q.X i)) ∧
      ∃ (hPflat : P.KFlat) (hQflat : Q.KFlat)
        (eK : K.1 ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
        (eL : L.1 ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)
        (E : AssociatedFiltrationSpectralSequence ((tensorLeft P).obj Q)
            (firstDegreeFiltration P Q bP bQ))
        (E' : AssociatedFiltrationSpectralSequence ((tensorLeft P).obj Q)
            (secondDegreeFiltration P Q bP bQ))
        (firstFilteredE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ,
          filteredPageObject ((tensorLeft P).obj Q) (firstDegreeFiltration P Q bP bQ)
              2 p q ≅
          ((tensorLeft P).obj ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (Q.homology q))).homology p)
        (secondFilteredE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ,
          filteredPageObject ((tensorLeft P).obj Q) (secondDegreeFiltration P Q bP bQ)
              2 p q ≅
          ((tensorLeft ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (P.homology q))).obj Q).homology p)
        (firstE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E.spectralSequence.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
          ((tensorLeft P).obj ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (Q.homology q))).homology p)
        (secondE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E'.spectralSequence.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
          ((tensorLeft ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (P.homology q))).obj Q).homology p)
        (abutmentIso : ∀ n : ℤ, ((tensorLeft P).obj Q).homology n ≅
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj
            (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj
              K.1).obj L.1))
        (firstOrdinaryToDerivedE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ,
          ((tensorLeft P).obj ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (Q.homology q))).homology p ≅
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) p).obj
            (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj K.1).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) q).obj L.1))))
        (secondOrdinaryToDerivedE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ,
          ((tensorLeft ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (P.homology q))).obj Q).homology p ≅
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) p).obj
            (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) q).obj K.1))).obj L.1))
        (firstDerivedE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E.spectralSequence.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) p).obj
            (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj K.1).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) q).obj L.1))))
        (secondDerivedE₂Iso : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E'.spectralSequence.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) p).obj
            (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) q).obj K.1))).obj L.1)),
        (∀ p q : ℤ, (firstE₂Iso p q).hom =
          (E.pageIso 2 p q (by omega)).hom ≫ (firstFilteredE₂Iso p q).hom) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, (secondE₂Iso p q).hom =
          (E'.pageIso 2 p q (by omega)).hom ≫ (secondFilteredE₂Iso p q).hom) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, (firstDerivedE₂Iso p q).hom =
          (firstE₂Iso p q).hom ≫ (firstOrdinaryToDerivedE₂Iso p q).hom) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, (secondDerivedE₂Iso p q).hom =
          (secondE₂Iso p q).hom ≫ (secondOrdinaryToDerivedE₂Iso p q).hom) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ,
          (abutmentIso n).symm =
            (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).mapIso
              (((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor
                  R).mapIso eK).app L.1 ≪≫
                ((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj
                  (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).mapIso eL ≪≫
                (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R).comparison P Q
                  hPflat hQflat) ≪≫
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).app
                ((tensorLeft P).obj Q))

declarations.name: Koszul.koszulSeq_smul_nullHomotopic_and_span_le_annihilator
declarations.doc:
Multiplication by each member of a finite sequence is null-homotopic on its Koszul complex,
and the ideal generated by the sequence annihilates every Koszul homology module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem koszulSeq_smul_nullHomotopic_and_span_le_annihilator
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) :
    (∀ i, Nonempty (Homotopy (f i • 𝟙 (Koszul.seqComplex f)) 0)) ∧
      ∀ n, Ideal.span (Set.range f) ≤
        Module.annihilator R ((Koszul.seqComplex f).homology n)

declarations.name: Koszul.seqComplex_append_iso_totTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0664.** The Koszul complex on the concatenation of two sequences
`f_1, ..., f_r` and `g_1, ..., g_s` (length `r + s`) is isomorphic, as a chain
complex of `R`-modules, to the total complex of the tensor product of the Koszul
complexes on `f` and on `g`; see `seqComplexAppendIsoTotTensor` for the isomorphism
itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem seqComplex_append_iso_totTensor {r s : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) (g : Fin s → R) :
    Nonempty
      (seqComplex (Fin.append f g) ≅ totTensor (seqComplex f) (seqComplex g))

declarations.name: Koszul.inf_span_eq_smul_span
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a commutative ring, `I` an ideal of `A`, and `g_1, ..., g_m` elements of `A`. If the
images of `g_1, ..., g_m` in `A/I` form an `H_1`-regular sequence, then
`I ⊓ (g_1, ..., g_m) = I (g_1, ..., g_m)` as ideals of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inf_span_eq_smul_span (I : Ideal A) (g : Fin m → A)
    (hreg : Koszul.IsH1Regular (fun i => Ideal.Quotient.mk I (g i))) :
    I ⊓ Ideal.span (Set.range g) = I * Ideal.span (Set.range g)

declarations.name: Koszul.inf_sq_eq_mul_of_quotient_generated_by_isH1Regular
declarations.doc: If `I ⊆ J` and `J / I` is generated by an H₁-regular sequence, then `I ∩ J² = I J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inf_sq_eq_mul_of_quotient_generated_by_isH1Regular
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (I J : Ideal A) (hIJ : I ≤ J)
    {m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → A ⧸ I)
    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) J)
    (hreg : Koszul.IsH1Regular g) :
    I ⊓ J ^ 2 = I * J

declarations.name: Koszul.isQuasiRegular_append_of_isH1Regular_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0667.** If `f` is quasi-regular and the image of `g` modulo the ideal generated
by `f` is H₁-regular, then the concatenation of `f` and `g` is quasi-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiRegular_append_of_isH1Regular_quotient
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {n m : ℕ} (f : Fin n → A) (g : Fin m → A)
    (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular A (List.ofFn f))
    (hg : Koszul.IsH1Regular
      (fun j => Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (g j))) :
    RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular A (List.ofFn (Fin.append f g))

declarations.name: Koszul.isH1Regular_append
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a commutative ring, let `f : Fin n → A` be an `H_1`-regular sequence, let
`I = (f_0, ..., f_{n-1})` be the ideal it generates, and let `g : Fin m → A` be such that the
images `(Ideal.Quotient.mk I) ∘ g` form an `H_1`-regular sequence in `A/I`. Then the concatenated
sequence `Fin.append f g : Fin (n + m) → A` is `H_1`-regular in `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1Regular_append {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {n m : ℕ}
    (f : Fin n → A) (g : Fin m → A)
    (hf : Koszul.IsH1Regular f)
    (hg : Koszul.IsH1Regular
      (fun j => (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f))) (g j))) :
    Koszul.IsH1Regular (Fin.append f g)

declarations.name: Koszul.koszul_regular_append
declarations.doc:
If `f` is Koszul-regular and the image of `g` modulo the ideal generated by `f` is
Koszul-regular, then the concatenation of `f` and `g` is Koszul-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem koszul_regular_append {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {n m : ℕ}
    (f : Fin n → A) (g : Fin m → A)
    (hf : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)
    (hg : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular
      (fun j => Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (g j))) :
    Koszul.IsKoszulRegular (Fin.append f g)

declarations.name: Koszul.regularity_of_generators_of_eq_span_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066A.** If an ideal generated by `r` elements admits a quasi-regular,
`H₁`-regular, or Koszul-regular generating sequence of length `r`, then every generating
sequence of length `r` has the corresponding property.
declarations.statement:
public theorem regularity_of_generators_of_eq_span_range
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ} (I : Ideal R) (f : Fin r → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    ((∃ g : Fin r → R, Ideal.span (Set.range g) = I ∧
        RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular R (List.ofFn g)) →
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular R (List.ofFn f)) ∧
    ((∃ g : Fin r → R, Ideal.span (Set.range g) = I ∧ Koszul.IsH1Regular g) →
      Koszul.IsH1Regular f) ∧
    ((∃ g : Fin r → R, Ideal.span (Set.range g) = I ∧ Koszul.IsKoszulRegular g) →
      Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove_cohomology
declarations.doc:
A cohomologically bounded-above derived object whose cohomology modules are
pseudo-coherent in the corresponding degrees is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherentFrom_and_pseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove_cohomology
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) :
    (∀ m : ℤ,
      (∀ i : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := R)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K) (m - i)) →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := R)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) →
      IsPseudoCoherent K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.extensionScalars_preserves_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066C.** Extension of scalars along a flat ring homomorphism preserves
`m`-pseudo-coherent modules for every integer `m` and preserves pseudo-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem extensionScalars_preserves_pseudoCoherent
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.Flat)
    (M : ModuleCat.{w} A) :
    (∀ m : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := A) M m →
      IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom (R := B) ((ModuleCat.extendScalars f).obj M) m) ∧
      (IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := A) M →
        IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := B) ((ModuleCat.extendScalars f).obj M))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isPseudoCoherent_of_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066D.** Both `m`-pseudo-coherence and pseudo-coherence descend from a finite
principal open cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isPseudoCoherent_of_localization
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (f : ι → R) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R)) (m : ℤ) :
    ((∀ i, IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, v} (f i)).obj K) m) →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m) ∧
    ((∀ i, IsPseudoCoherent ((localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, v} (f i)).obj K)) →
      IsPseudoCoherent K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherent_iff_boundedAbove_finite_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066E.** Over a Noetherian ring, pseudo-coherence from degree `m` means
bounded-above finite homology in degrees at least `m`; pseudo-coherence means bounded-above
finite homology in all degrees; and pseudo-coherence of a module is equivalent to its
finiteness.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_iff_boundedAbove_finite_homology
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (m : ℤ)
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m ↔
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i →
        Module.Finite R ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) ∧
    (IsPseudoCoherent K ↔
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ,
        Module.Finite R ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) ∧
    (IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := R) M ↔ Module.Finite R M)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorDimensionLECanonical_iff_hasFlatRepresentative
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` has Tor dimension at most `d` — at the canonical derived
tensor product — if and only if it admits a flat resolution of length `d`, that is, a complex of
flat modules concentrated in degrees `[-d, 0]` representing `M[0]`.  In particular `M` has Tor
dimension at most `0` if and only if `M` is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorDimensionLECanonical_iff_hasFlatRepresentative (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (d : ℕ) :
    (HasTorDimensionLECanonical R M d ↔
        HasFlatRepresentative
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M) (-(d : ℤ)) 0) ∧
      (HasTorAmplitudeCanonical R
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M) 0 0 ↔
        Module.Flat R M)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_of_biprod
declarations.doc:
If `K ⊕ L` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, then both `K` and `L` have Tor amplitude in
`[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitude_of_biprod {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (comparison : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ)
    (h : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived (K ⊞ L) a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived K a b ∧
      HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived L a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_and_finiteTorDimension_of_bounded_complex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066H.** A bounded complex whose term in degree `i` has Tor amplitude in
`[a - i, b - i]` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`. In particular, if every term of a bounded
complex has finite Tor dimension, then the complex has finite Tor dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_and_finiteTorDimension_of_bounded_complex
    {R : Type} [CommRing R] (D : Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.DerivedTensoring R)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{0} R) ℤ)
    (_hK : ∃ m n : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE m ∧ K.IsStrictlyLE n) :
    (∀ a b : ℤ, (∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} R) 0).obj (K.X i))
          (a - i) (b - i)) →
        Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a b) ∧
      ((∀ i : ℤ, ∃ aᵢ bᵢ : ℤ, Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} R) 0).obj (K.X i)) aᵢ bᵢ) →
        ∃ a' b' : ℤ, Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a' b')

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeIn_of_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066I.** A bounded derived object has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` if its degree-`i`
cohomology module has Tor amplitude in `[a - i, b - i]` for every `i`. In particular, if all
of its cohomology modules have finite Tor dimension, then so does the derived object.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitudeIn_of_cohomology (R : Type) [CommRing R]
    (D : Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.DerivedTensoring R)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Bounded (ModuleCat R)) :
    (∀ a b : ℤ,
      (∀ i : ℤ,
        Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat R) 0).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) i).obj K.obj))
          (a - i) (b - i)) →
        Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D K.obj a b) ∧
      ((∀ i : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ,
        Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat R) 0).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) i).obj K.obj)) a b) →
        ∃ a b : ℤ, Stacks.TorAmplitudeTriangle.HasTorAmplitudeIn D K.obj a b)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeIn_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066J.** A complex of `B`-modules with Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` retains that
Tor-amplitude bound after restriction of scalars along a flat ring map `A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitudeIn_restrictScalars
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [Module.Flat A B]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} B) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} B) ℤ,
      StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.Termwise.IsComplexOfFlats E ∧ E.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ E.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj E)) :
    ∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} A) ℤ,
      StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.Termwise.IsComplexOfFlats E ∧ E.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ E.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
        Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{w} (algebraMap A B)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) :
            DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{w} A)) ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj E)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift_restrictScalars_of_torDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
Let `f : A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `K` be a complex of `B`-modules; the
two rings and the carriers of `K` live in three independent universes. If `B` has Tor dimension
at most `d` as an `A`-module, that is, if `B` placed in degree zero has Tor amplitude in
`[-d, 0]` over `A`, then `K`, after restriction of scalars along `f`, has Tor amplitude in
`[a - d, b]` over `A`.

Tor amplitude is `HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift`, that is, Stacks 0652 at the canonical derived
tensor product of Stacks 0BYI on the ring lifted into the ambient universe.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift_restrictScalars_of_torDimensionLE
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} B) ℤ) (a b d : ℤ)
    (hB : HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift.{u, v, w}
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj (ModuleCat.of B B))) (-d) 0)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift.{v, w, u} (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a b) :
    HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift.{u, w, v}
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{w} f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))
      (a - d) b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_derivedExtendScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066L.** Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `K` be an object of
`D(A)` with Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`. Then `K ⊗_A^L B` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` as an
object of `D(B)`.

The derived tensor products over `A` and over `B` are certified as in Stacks 0652, and derived
extension of scalars is certified in the same style: `extendDerived` is equipped with a
comparison map `extendComparison` to termwise extension of scalars making it the total left
derived functor of the latter.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitude_derivedExtendScalars {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B]
    (extendDerived : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B))
    (extendComparison : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ extendDerived ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A B)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
    (extendIsLeftDerived : extendDerived.IsLeftDerivedFunctor extendComparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (derivedTensorA : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparisonA : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedTensorA.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerivedA : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensorA.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparisonA M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (derivedTensorB : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B))
    (comparisonB : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} B,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedTensorB.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerivedB : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} B,
      (derivedTensorB.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparisonB M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude derivedTensorA comparisonA isLeftDerivedA K a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensorB comparisonB isLeftDerivedB (extendDerived.obj K) a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorDimensionLECanonical_extendScalars_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `f : A →+* B` be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings.  If the
`A`-module `M` has Tor dimension at most `d`, then the `B`-module `B ⊗_A M` has Tor dimension at
most `d`.  Both Tor dimensions are read at the canonical derived tensor product of the ring in
question.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorDimensionLECanonical_extendScalars_of_flat {A B : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.Flat) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (d : ℕ)
    (hM : HasTorDimensionLECanonical A M d) :
    HasTorDimensionLECanonical B ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} f).obj M) d

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_of_localizationSpan
declarations.doc:
If a complex has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` after localization at every member of a set
generating the unit ideal, then it has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_of_localizationSpan
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (s : Set R) (hs : Ideal.span s = ⊤)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ f : s, StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.FaithfullyFlat.HasTorAmplitude
      ((CochainComplex.extendScalars
        (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (f : R)))).obj K) a b) :
    StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.FaithfullyFlat.HasTorAmplitude K a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.torAmplitude_and_finiteTorDimension_of_globalDimension_le
declarations.statement:
public theorem torAmplitude_and_finiteTorDimension_of_globalDimension_le
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (d : ℕ) (hR : ringGlobalDimension R ≤ d) :
    (∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.FaithfullyFlat.HasTorAmplitude
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M) (-(d : ℤ)) 0) ∧
    (∀ (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
      (∀ i : ℤ, (i < a ∨ b < i) → IsZero (K.homology i)) →
        StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.FaithfullyFlat.HasTorAmplitude K (a - d) b) ∧
    (∀ K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.FaithfullyFlat.HasTorAmplitude K a b) ↔
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)).bounded
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfectModule_iff_exists_finite_projective_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066Q.** An `R`-module is perfect if and only if it has a finite resolution by finite
projective `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectModule_iff_exists_finite_projective_resolution
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsPerfectModule (R := R) M ↔
      ∃ (d : ℕ) (F : ModuleResolution R M),
        (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite R (F.complex.X i) ∧ Module.Projective R (F.complex.X i)) ∧
          ∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066R.** In a distinguished triangle in `D(R)`, if two of the three objects are
perfect, then so is the third.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_distinguished
    {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) :
    (IsPerfect T.obj₁ → IsPerfect T.obj₂ → IsPerfect T.obj₃) ∧
    (IsPerfect T.obj₁ → IsPerfect T.obj₃ → IsPerfect T.obj₂) ∧
    (IsPerfect T.obj₂ → IsPerfect T.obj₃ → IsPerfect T.obj₁)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_of_biproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066S.** If a binary biproduct of objects of `D(R)` is perfect, then both summands are
perfect. Perfectness passes to the summands at arbitrary carrier universes: a small projective
coefficient quotient supporting the given bounded complex supplies the internal descent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_biproduct
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (h : IsPerfect (K ⊞ L)) :
    IsPerfect K ∧ IsPerfect L

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_of_bounded_of_isPerfectModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066T.** A bounded complex of perfect modules over a ring represents a perfect object
of the derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_bounded_of_isPerfectModule
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ a b : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ K.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i : ℤ, IsPerfectModule (R := R) (K.X i)) :
    IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_of_bounded_of_cohomology_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066U.** A bounded object of the derived category of modules whose cohomology modules
are all perfect is itself perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_bounded_of_cohomology_isPerfect
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : (∃ a : ℤ, K.IsGE a) ∧ ∃ b : ℤ, K.IsLE b)
    (hH : ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsPerfectModule (R := R)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) :
    IsPerfect K

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_restrictScalars_of_isPerfectModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066V.** Let `f : A → B` be a homomorphism of commutative rings and assume that `B` is
perfect as an `A`-module. Then every perfect complex of `B`-modules is perfect as a complex of
`A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_restrictScalars_of_isPerfectModule
    (hB : IsPerfectModule (R := A)
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{uB} f).obj (ModuleCat.of B B)))
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{uB} B) ℤ)
    (hK : IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) :
    IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{uB} f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_derivedExtensionScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066W.** Let `f : A → B` be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let `K` be a
perfect object of `D(A)`. Then the derived base change `K ⊗_A^L B` is a perfect object of
`D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedExtensionScalars (f : A →+* B)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v uA uB} A)) (hK : IsPerfect K) :
    IsPerfect ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{uA, uB, v}
      f).functor.obj K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfectModule_tensorProduct_of_flat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 066X.** Flat base change preserves perfect modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectModule_tensorProduct_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Flat A B]
    (hM : IsPerfectModule (R := A) M) :
    IsPerfectModule (R := B) (B ⊗[A] M)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_of_localizationSpan
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring, let the elements `f i` generate the unit ideal, and let `K` be
an object of the derived category of `R`-modules. If the derived localization `K ⊗_R R_{f i}` is
perfect for every `i`, then `K` is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_localizationSpan {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (f : ι → R) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i, IsPerfect ((PseudoCoherence.localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, v} (f i)).obj K)) :
    IsPerfect K

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfectModule_iff_finite_and_isPerfect_iff_bounded_finiteCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 066Z.** Over a regular ring, perfect modules are precisely finite modules, and
perfect derived objects are precisely the bounded objects with finite cohomology modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectModule_iff_finite_and_isPerfect_iff_bounded_finiteCohomology
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularRing R] :
    (∀ (M : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M],
      IsPerfectModule (R := R) M ↔ Module.Finite R M) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R),
      IsPerfect K ↔
        ((∃ a : ℤ, K.IsGE a) ∧ (∃ b : ℤ, K.IsLE b) ∧
          ∀ i : ℤ,
            Module.Finite R
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) i).obj K)))

declarations.name: finitelyPresentedRelative_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `R → A` be a ring map, `M` an `A`-module finitely presented relative to `R`, and
`A → A'` a ring map of finite presentation. Then the `A'`-module `A' ⊗[A] M` (here
`TensorProduct A A' M`, with its natural `A'`-module structure) is finitely presented relative
to `R`.

The finite type hypothesis on `R → A` of the Stacks statement is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitelyPresentedRelative_baseChange
    (R A A' : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing A']
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A A'] [Algebra R A'] [IsScalarTower R A A']
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (hM : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M)
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation A A'] :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R A' (TensorProduct A A' M)

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_two_of_three
declarations.doc:
Stacks 0671, part (1). Given a short exact sequence of `A`-modules
`0 → M' →[i] M →[p] M'' → 0` (so `i` is injective, `p` is surjective and
`range i = ker p`), if `M'` and `M''` are finitely presented relative to `R`, then `M` is
finitely presented relative to `R`.

By Stacks 05GY, `M'` and `M''` are finitely presented over `R[x_1, …, x_n]` for *every*
presentation `α`, so one may pick a single presentation and apply two-out-of-three over the
polynomial ring `R[x_1, …, x_n]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentationRel_two_of_three (i : M' →ₗ[A] M) (p : M →ₗ[A] M'')
    (hi : Function.Injective i) (hp : Function.Surjective p)
    (hex : LinearMap.range i = LinearMap.ker p)
    (hM' : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M')
    (hM'' : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M'') :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_of_surjective_of_finite
declarations.doc:
Stacks 0671, part (2). Given a short exact sequence of `A`-modules
`0 → M' →[i] M →[p] M'' → 0`, if `M'` is a finite type (finitely generated) `A`-module and `M`
is finitely presented relative to `R`, then `M''` is finitely presented relative to `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentationRel_of_surjective_of_finite {R A : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] {M' M M'' : Type*} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup M''] [Module A M'']
    (i : M' →ₗ[A] M) (p : M →ₗ[A] M'')
    (hp : Function.Surjective p)
    (hex : LinearMap.range i = LinearMap.ker p)
    (hM' : Module.Finite A M') (hM : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M) :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M''

declarations.name: Module.finitePresentationRel_of_prod
declarations.doc:
Stacks 0672 (Lemma 15.82.10).

Let `R → A` be a ring map (in Stacks, of finite type — the hypothesis is not needed here) and
let `M`, `M'` be `A`-modules. If the direct sum `M × M'` is finitely presented relative to `R`,
then both `M` and `M'` are finitely presented relative to `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.finitePresentationRel_of_prod {R A : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] {M M' : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M']
    (h : Module.FinitePresentationRel R A (M × M')) :
    Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M ∧ Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M'

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0673.** Restriction of scalars along a finite map of finite-type `R`-algebras
preserves and reflects relative `m`-pseudo-coherence and relative pseudo-coherence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_restrictScalars
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} {B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] [Module.Finite A B]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)) (m : ℤ) :
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R B :=
      Algebra.FiniteType.trans (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType R A)
        (Module.Finite.finiteType B)
    let Kₐ := (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m ↔
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) Kₐ m) ∧
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K ↔
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) Kₐ)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0674.** Relative pseudo-coherence is preserved around a distinguished triangle,
with the indicated shift in the degree bound. Without a degree bound it is a two-out-of-three
property.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_of_distinguished
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) :
    ((IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₁ (m + 1) →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₂ m →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₃ m) ∧
      (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₁ m →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₃ m →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₂ m) ∧
      (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₂ (m + 1) →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₃ m →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) T.obj₁ (m + 1))) ∧
    ((IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₁ →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₂ →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₃) ∧
      (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₁ →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₃ →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₂) ∧
      (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₂ →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₃ →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) T.obj₁))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.moduleRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_finiteness_and_resolutions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0675.** For a module over a finite-type `R`-algebra, relative
pseudo-coherence in degrees `0`, `-1`, and `-d` is equivalent respectively to finite
generation, relative finite presentation, and the existence over every polynomial presentation
of a finite free resolution through degree `d`. Relative pseudo-coherence is equivalent to the
existence over every polynomial presentation of an infinite finite free resolution.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_finiteness_and_resolutions
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    (IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := A) M 0 ↔
      Module.Finite A M) ∧
    (IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := A) M (-1) ↔
      Module.FinitePresentationRel R A M) ∧
    (∀ d : ℕ, IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := A)
      M (-(d : ℤ)) ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Function.Surjective α →
        @HasFiniteFreeResolutionOfLength _ _ M _
          (Module.compHom M α.toRingHom) d) ∧
    (IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := A) M ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Function.Surjective α →
        Nonempty (@FiniteFreeModuleResolution _ _ M _
          (Module.compHom M α.toRingHom)))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_of_biproduct
declarations.doc:
Each summand of a relatively `m`-pseudo-coherent binary biproduct is
relatively `m`-pseudo-coherent, and each summand of a relatively pseudo-coherent binary
biproduct is relatively pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_of_biproduct
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ) :
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (K ⊞ L) m →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m ∧
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) L m) ∧
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (K ⊞ L) →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K ∧
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) L)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.relativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_and_relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0677.** A bounded-above complex with suitably relatively pseudo-coherent terms is
relatively pseudo-coherent in the corresponding degrees. In particular, relative
pseudo-coherence of every term implies relative pseudo-coherence of the complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_and_relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ b : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE b) :
    (∀ m : ℤ,
      (∀ i : ℤ, IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := A) (K.X i) (m - i)) →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) m) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℤ, IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := A) (K.X i)) →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0678.** A cohomologically bounded-above derived object whose cohomology modules
are relatively pseudo-coherent in the corresponding degrees is relatively pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_boundedAbove_cohomology
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) :
    ((∀ i : ℤ, IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := A)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K) (m - i)) →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℤ, IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := A)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.localization_preserves_relativePseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0679.** Localizing a complex that is relatively `m`-pseudo-coherent, respectively
pseudo-coherent, over `R_f` produces a complex with the corresponding property relative to
`R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localization_preserves_relativePseudoCoherent
    {R : Type u} {Rf : Type u} {A : Type u} {Ag : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Rf] [CommRing A] [CommRing Ag]
    [Algebra R Rf] (f : R) [IsLocalization.Away f Rf]
    [Algebra Rf A] [Algebra.FiniteType Rf A]
    [Algebra R A] [IsScalarTower R Rf A]
    (g : A) [Algebra A Ag] [IsLocalization.Away g Ag]
    [Algebra R Ag] [IsScalarTower R A Ag]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ) :
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R Rf :=
      IsLocalization.finiteType_of_monoid_fg (Submonoid.powers f) Rf
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R A := Algebra.FiniteType.trans
      (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType R Rf) (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType Rf A)
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType A Ag :=
      IsLocalization.finiteType_of_monoid_fg (Submonoid.powers g) Ag
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R Ag := Algebra.FiniteType.trans
      (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType R A) (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType A Ag)
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := Rf) K m →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R)
        ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} (algebraMap A Ag)).functor.obj K) m) ∧
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := Rf) K →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R)
        ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} (algebraMap A Ag)).functor.obj
          K))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.derivedExtensionScalars_preserves_relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
A Tor-independent base change preserves relative `m`-pseudo-coherence for every integer `m`,
as well as relative pseudo-coherence.

The chosen `R'`-algebra `R' ⊗[R] A` is identified with the source's `A ⊗[R] R'` by
`Algebra.TensorProduct.commRight R R' A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedExtensionScalars_preserves_relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_torIndependent
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} {R' : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing R']
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra.FiniteType R A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hTor : TorIndependent R A R') :
    let A' := R' ⊗[R] A
    letI : Algebra R' A' := Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra
    let f : A →+* A' := Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom
    (∀ m : ℤ, IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R')
        ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} f).functor.obj K)
          m) ∧
      (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K →
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R')
          ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} f).functor.obj
            K))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.derivedExtensionScalars_preserves_relativelyPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
If `B` is pseudo-coherent relative to `A`, derived extension of scalars from `A` to `B`
preserves relative `m`-pseudo-coherence and relative pseudo-coherence over the base ring `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedExtensionScalars_preserves_relativelyPseudoCoherent
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} {B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ)
    (hB : IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent.{u}
      (R := A) (A := B) B) :
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R B :=
      Algebra.FiniteType.trans (R := R) (S := A) (A := B) inferInstance inferInstance
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R)
        ((derivedExtensionScalars hB).obj K) m) ∧
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K →
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R)
        ((derivedExtensionScalars hB).obj K))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.tensorProduct_preserves_relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Flat extension of scalars preserves relative `m`-pseudo-coherence and relative
pseudo-coherence for modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorProduct_preserves_relativelyPseudoCoherent_of_flat
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} {B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Flat A B] (m : ℤ)
    (hB : IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := A) (A := B) B) :
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R B :=
      Algebra.FiniteType.trans (R := R) (S := A) (A := B) inferInstance inferInstance
    (IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := A) M m →
      IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) (A := B)
        (TensorProduct A B M) m) ∧
    (IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := A) M →
      IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := B)
        (TensorProduct A B M))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.relativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 067D.** Relative pseudo-coherence is invariant under composition with a relatively
pseudo-coherent finite-type algebra, for every object of the derived category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_of_comp
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} {B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (hA : IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := A) A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)) (m : ℤ) :
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType R B :=
      Algebra.FiniteType.trans (R := R) (S := A) (A := B) inferInstance inferInstance
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := A) K m ↔
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m) ∧
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := A) K ↔
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.relativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_localizationAway_of_span_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 067E.** Relative `m`-pseudo-coherence and relative pseudo-coherence are local on
a finite principal cover of a finite-type algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_localizationAway_of_span_eq_top
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FiniteType R A]
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (f : ι → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ) :
    ((∀ i,
      letI : Algebra.FiniteType A (Localization.Away (f i)) :=
        IsLocalization.finiteType_of_monoid_fg (Submonoid.powers (f i)) _
      letI : Algebra.FiniteType R (Localization.Away (f i)) :=
        Algebra.FiniteType.trans (R := R) (S := A)
          (A := Localization.Away (f i)) inferInstance inferInstance
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R)
        ((localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, u} (f i)).obj K) m) ↔
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m) ∧
    ((∀ i,
      letI : Algebra.FiniteType A (Localization.Away (f i)) :=
        IsLocalization.finiteType_of_monoid_fg (Submonoid.powers (f i)) _
      letI : Algebra.FiniteType R (Localization.Away (f i)) :=
        Algebra.FiniteType.trans (R := R) (S := A)
          (A := Localization.Away (f i)) inferInstance inferInstance
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R)
        ((localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, u} (f i)).obj K)) ↔
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K)

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.relativePseudoCoherent_iff_boundedAbove_finite_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 067F.** For a finite-type algebra over a Noetherian ring, relative
pseudo-coherence from degree `m` means bounded-above finite homology in degrees at least `m`;
relative pseudo-coherence means bounded-above finite homology in every degree; and relative
pseudo-coherence of a module is equivalent to its finiteness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativePseudoCoherent_iff_boundedAbove_finite_homology
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (m : ℤ)
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom (R := R) K m ↔
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, m ≤ i →
        Module.Finite A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) ∧
    (IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) K ↔
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ,
        Module.Finite A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) ∧
    (IsModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent (R := R) (A := A) M ↔
      Module.Finite A M)

declarations.name: Algebra.PseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
An `A`-algebra `B` is *pseudo-coherent* if `B` is a quotient `A[x₁, …, xₙ] ⧸ I` of a
polynomial algebra such that the `A[x₁, …, xₙ]`-module `A[x₁, …, xₙ] ⧸ I` has a resolution by
finite free modules.

This is Stacks 067H (1) in the form of the remark that follows it, with `B` replaced by the
isomorphic `A[x₁, …, xₙ]`-module `A[x₁, …, xₙ] ⧸ I`, which lives in the universe of `A`. By
Stacks 0675 it says that `A → B` is of finite type and that `B`, as a module over itself, is
pseudo-coherent relative to `A` (for `A` and `B` in one universe,
`Algebra.pseudoCoherent_iff_exists_isModuleRelativelyPseudoCoherent`). The resolution then exists
over every finite polynomial presentation
(`Algebra.PseudoCoherent.nonempty_finiteFreeModuleResolution`). When `A` and `B` live in one
universe, the condition is the same for `B` itself, made an `A[x₁, …, xₙ]`-module through the
presentation (`Algebra.PseudoCoherent.nonempty_finiteFreeModuleResolution_quotient_iff_compHom`).
declarations.statement:
public class Algebra.PseudoCoherent (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.IsPerfectRingMap
declarations.doc:
A ring map `A → B` is perfect if it is pseudo-coherent and `B`, regarded as an `A`-module, has
finite Tor dimension, read off the certified derived tensor product `derivedTensor` on a model of
`D(A)`. Neither the model nor the certificate matters
(`RingHom.isPerfectRingMap_iff_exists_flat_roof`).
declarations.statement:
public def IsPerfectRingMap
    (A : Type u) (B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.tensorModuleRight N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.PseudoCoherent.of_finiteType
declarations.doc: **Stacks 067I.** A finite-type ring map whose source is Noetherian is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem of_finiteType
    (A : Type u) (B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] :
    Algebra.PseudoCoherent A B

declarations.name: RingHom.isPerfectRingMap_of_flat_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 067J.** A flat ring map of finite presentation is perfect: it is pseudo-coherent,
and its target has finite Tor dimension over its source for every certified derived tensor
product.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRingMap_of_flat_of_finitePresentation
    (A : Type u) (B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B] :
    Algebra.PseudoCoherent A B ∧
    ∀ (derivedTensor : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
      (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
          (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.tensorModuleRight N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
        (derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
          (comparison N)
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))),
      IsPerfectRingMap A B derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived

declarations.name: RingHom.isPerfectRingMap_of_finiteType_of_isRegularRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 067K.** A finite-type ring map out of a regular ring is perfect: it is
pseudo-coherent, and its target has finite Tor dimension as a module over its source, for every
certified derived tensor product.

The source assumes in addition that the regular ring has finite Krull dimension; that hypothesis
is not needed, because the bound on the length of the resolution is produced from
quasi-compactness of the prime spectrum of the polynomial ring rather than from a bound on its
global dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRingMap_of_finiteType_of_isRegularRing
    (A : Type u) (B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsRegularRing A] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (derivedTensor : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.tensorModuleRight N).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    IsPerfectRingMap A B derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceTwoImmersions.epi_conormalDifferential
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067L], surjectivity of the second arrow.** For immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and
`j : Z ⟶ Y` in a commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j`, the second arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}` of
the conormal sequence is an epimorphism, which is the `⟶ 0` at its right-hand end.

The sequence of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] for `i` over `p` is exact at `i^*Ω_{X/Y}` and continues by
`i^*Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Y}`, whose target vanishes because `j` is an immersion, hence formally
unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalDifferential {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    Epi (Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalDifferential i p)
declarations.comment:
surjectivity of the second arrow 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}, which is the ⟶ 0 at the
right-hand end of the sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceTwoImmersions.conormalTransitivityMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067L], the first arrow.** For immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` in a
commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j`, the canonical map `𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of conormal sheaves.

It is the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 01R4] for the square whose top morphism is `𝟙 Z`,
transported along the identification of pullback along an identity with the identity
functor.
declarations.statement:
def conormalTransitivityMap (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf j ⟶ Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf i

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceTwoImmersions.conormalDifferentialModules
declarations.doc:
**The second arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}` of [Stacks, Tag 067L]**, with its source in the
spelling the first arrow uses. The conormal differential of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is built on the
pullback of a *sectionwise* kernel and the first arrow on the pullback of the *categorical*
kernel; `Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.conormalSheafComparisonIso` identifies the two
presentations, and this arrow is the conormal differential read through it.

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceTwoImmersions.conormalTransitivityMapModules_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067L]: the two arrows of the conormal sequence form a complex.** The composite
`𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}` vanishes, for immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` in a
commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j` and with no hypothesis on `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalTransitivityMapModules_comp_eq_zero (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    conormalTransitivityMapModules i j p h ≫ conormalDifferentialModules i p = 0
declarations.comment:
the composite 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y} of the two arrows vanishes, so they
form a complex; only the commutative triangle i ≫ p = j of immersions is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceTwoImmersions.conormalShortComplexModules_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067L]: the conormal sequence of two immersions is exact at `𝒞_{Z/X}`.** The
kernel of the second arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}` is exactly the image of the first arrow
`𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}`, for immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` in a commutative triangle
`i ≫ p = j` and with no hypothesis on `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalShortComplexModules_exact (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
      (conormalTransitivityMapModules_comp_eq_zero i j p h)).Exact
declarations.comment:
exactness at the middle term 𝒞_{Z/X}: the image of the first arrow
𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} is the kernel of the second arrow 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}; only the commutative
triangle i ≫ p = j of immersions is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_quasiRegular_generators_of_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 067N, part (1).** Let `J` be a quasi-regular ideal sheaf on a locally
ringed space `X`, let `x ∈ X` and let `f₁, …, f_r ∈ J_x` be germs whose classes form a basis of
the cotangent fibre `J_x / 𝔪_x J_x`.  Then there is an open neighbourhood `U` of `x` on which the
`f_i` are the germs of sections of `J` which form a quasi-regular sequence generating `J`
over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiRegular_generators_of_basis (x : X) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → Stacks.RingedSpace.stalkIdeal J x)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin r)
      (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (Stacks.RingedSpace.idealCotangentFiber J x))
    (hf : ∀ i, b i = Submodule.Quotient.mk (f i))
    (hJ : IsQuasiRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J) :
    ∃ (U : Opens X) (hxU : x ∈ U) (fU : Fin r → J.obj (op U)),
      (∀ i, X.presheaf.germ U x hxU (fU i).1 = (f i).1) ∧
      IsIso (quasiRegularMap (X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)
        (fun i => sectionOnRestriction X.toRingedSpace U (fU i).1)).hom ∧
      IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U (fun i => (fU i).1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_h1Regular_generators_of_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 067N, part (2).** The `H₁`-regular case: for an `H₁`-regular ideal
sheaf the sections produced over `U` have a Koszul complex which is germwise exact in degree
`1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_h1Regular_generators_of_basis (x : X) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → Stacks.RingedSpace.stalkIdeal J x)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin r)
      (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (Stacks.RingedSpace.idealCotangentFiber J x))
    (hf : ∀ i, b i = Submodule.Quotient.mk (f i))
    (hJ : IsH1RegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J) :
    ∃ (U : Opens X) (hxU : x ∈ U) (fU : Fin r → J.obj (op U)),
      (∀ i, X.presheaf.germ U x hxU (fU i).1 = (f i).1) ∧
      IsKoszulSequenceExactOn X.toRingedSpace U (fun i => (fU i).1) (fun j => j = 1) ∧
      IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U (fun i => (fU i).1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_koszulRegular_generators_of_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 067N, part (3).** The Koszul-regular case: for a Koszul-regular ideal
sheaf the sections produced over `U` have a Koszul complex which is germwise exact in every
positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_koszulRegular_generators_of_basis (x : X) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → Stacks.RingedSpace.stalkIdeal J x)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin r)
      (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (Stacks.RingedSpace.idealCotangentFiber J x))
    (hf : ∀ i, b i = Submodule.Quotient.mk (f i))
    (hJ : IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace J) :
    ∃ (U : Opens X) (hxU : x ∈ U) (fU : Fin r → J.obj (op U)),
      (∀ i, X.presheaf.germ U x hxU (fU i).1 = (f i).1) ∧
      IsKoszulSequenceExactOn X.toRingedSpace U (fun i => (fU i).1) (fun j => 0 < j) ∧
      IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U (fun i => (fU i).1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_koszulRegular_sections_of_basis
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 067N] part (3).** Let `J` be an ideal subsheaf of the structure sheaf
of a locally ringed space, generated on a neighbourhood of `x` by a sequence that is
Koszul-regular at every point.  Then any lift of a basis of the cotangent fibre `J_x/𝔪_x J_x` is
realised on a neighbourhood of `x` by sections that generate `J` and are Koszul-regular at every
point.

Koszul-regularity of a family on an open is taken germwise, which
`isKoszulSequenceExactOn_iff_forall_germ_isKoszulRegular` identifies with exactness of its sheaf
Koszul complex.

Two departures from the source.  The hypothesis is the local witness at `x` that Koszul-regularity
of `J` supplies there, rather than Koszul-regularity of `J` itself; that is weaker, so a caller
with the source's hypothesis can supply it.  And `J_x ≠ 𝒪_{X,x}` is assumed, which the source does
not assume: in the excluded case the cotangent fibre is the residue field, so `r = 1` and `f 0` is
a unit, and the source's conclusion holds there too.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_koszulRegular_sections_of_basis {X : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}}
    (J : (structureSheafModule X.toRingedSpace).Submodule) (x : X) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → stalkIdeal J x)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin r)
      (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (idealCotangentFiber J x))
    (hf : ∀ i, b i = Submodule.Quotient.mk (f i))
    (hsupp : stalkIdeal J x ≠ ⊤)
    (V : Opens X) (hxV : x ∈ V) {s : ℕ} (g : Fin s → X.presheaf.obj (op V))
    (hgen : IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J V g)
    (hK : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ V), Koszul.IsKoszulRegular (germFamily X.toRingedSpace V g y hy)) :
    ∃ (U : Opens X) (hxU : x ∈ U) (fU : Fin r → X.presheaf.obj (op U)),
      (∀ i, X.presheaf.germ U x hxU (fU i) = (f i : X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
      IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace J U fU ∧
      ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ U), Koszul.IsKoszulRegular (germFamily X.toRingedSpace U fU y hy)
declarations.comment: part (3), with the local witness at x in place of Koszul-regularity of J, and assuming J_x is not the whole local ring
