declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.universalConormalTransitivityMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067V], the first arrow.** For formally unramified `i : Z ⟶ X` and
`j : Z ⟶ Y` in a commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j`, the canonical map `𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of
conormal sheaves in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 04F4] part (2).

It is the morphism of conormal sheaves of [Stacks, Tag 04F7] for the square whose top morphism
is `𝟙 Z` and whose bottom morphism is `p`, transported along the identification of pullback
along an identity with the identity functor and along the identifications of the conormal
sheaves of the two inclusions with those of their closed-immersion factorizations.
declarations.statement:
def universalConormalTransitivityMap (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    universalConormalSheaf j ⟶ universalConormalSheaf i

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.conormalSequenceSecondArrow
declarations.doc:
**The second arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}` of [Stacks, Tag 067V].** It is the conormal
differential of [Stacks, Tag 01UZ] for the closed immersion `Z ⟶ Z'` of `Z` into the ambient
scheme of its universal first-order thickening over `X`, taken over the ambient scheme `Z''` of
the universal first-order thickening over `Y` — that is, the second arrow of the sequence of
[Stacks, Tag 067L] that the proof of [Stacks, Tag 067V] reduces to — with its target moved onto
`i^*Ω_{X/Y}` by `Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.thirdTermIso` and its source read through
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.conormalSheafComparisonIso`.
declarations.comment:
the second arrow 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}, built as the conormal differential of Tag
01UZ for Z ⟶ Z' over Z'' and moved along the identification thirdTermIso of the third term

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.conormalSequenceComp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067V]: the two arrows form a complex.** The composite
`𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceComp_eq_zero (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    conormalSequenceFirstArrow i j p h ≫ conormalSequenceSecondArrow i j p h = 0
declarations.comment:
the composite of the two arrows 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y} vanishes, so the
two arrows form a complex

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.epi_conormalSequenceSecondArrow
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067V]: the second arrow is an epimorphism.** This is the `⟶ 0` at the
right-hand end of the sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalSequenceSecondArrow (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    Epi (conormalSequenceSecondArrow i j p h)
declarations.comment:
surjectivity of the second arrow 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y}, which is the ⟶ 0 at the
right-hand end of the sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.conormalSequenceShortComplex_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067V]: the sequence is exact at `𝒞_{Z/X}`.** The kernel of the second arrow is
the image of the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceShortComplex_exact (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (conormalSequenceComp_eq_zero i j p h)).Exact
declarations.comment:
exactness at the middle term 𝒞_{Z/X}: the kernel of the second arrow is the image
of the first

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.exists_retraction_restrict_universalConormalTransitivityMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067W]: the conormal sequence is locally split.** For formally unramified
`i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` in a commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j` with `p` formally smooth, every
point of `Z` has an open neighbourhood `V` over which the first arrow `𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of
[Stacks, Tag 067V] admits a retraction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_restrict_universalConormalTransitivityMap (h : i ≫ p = j)
    (hp : FormallySmooth p) (z : Z) :
    ∃ V : Z.Opens, z ∈ V ∧
      ∃ r : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (universalConormalSheaf i) ⟶
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (universalConormalSheaf j),
        (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map (universalConormalTransitivityMap i j p h) ≫ r =
          𝟙 _

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.mono_conormalSequenceFirstArrow
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067W]: the first arrow of the conormal sequence is a monomorphism.** This is
the `0 ⟶` at the left-hand end of the sequence, and the only strengthening of the right-exact
sequence of [Stacks, Tag 067V] to a short exact one.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_conormalSequenceFirstArrow (h : i ≫ p = j) (hp : FormallySmooth p) :
    Mono (conormalSequenceFirstArrow i j p h)
declarations.comment:
exact on the left: the first arrow 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} of Tag 067V is a
monomorphism, which is the only strengthening of Tag 067V's right-exact sequence to a short exact
one that this tag asserts; obtained from the local splitting

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.exists_retraction_restrict_conormalSequenceFirstArrow
declarations.doc:
**The local splitting, stated for
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.conormalSequenceFirstArrow`.** This is the `locallySplit`
clause in the shape the library uses for the sibling tag [Stacks, Tag 062S], namely
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSplitExactConormalSequence.locallySplit`.

theorem exists_retraction_restrict_conormalSequenceFirstArrow (h : i ≫ p = j)
    (hp : FormallySmooth p) (z : Z) :
    ∃ V : Z.Opens, z ∈ V ∧
      ∃ r : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (conormalSheafModules i) ⟶
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (conormalSheafModules j),
        (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map (conormalSequenceFirstArrow i j p h) ≫ r =

declarations.comment:
locally split, in the shape of the locallySplit clause the library uses for the
sibling tag 062S

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceUnramifiedPair.shortExact_of_comp_eq_zero_of_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 067W]: the conormal sequence is short exact.** For formally unramified
`i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` in a commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j` with `p` formally smooth, the
sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` of [Stacks, Tag 067V] is short exact.

Exactness at the middle term and surjectivity of the second arrow are the assertions of
[Stacks, Tag 067V]; what this tag adds is injectivity of the first arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_of_comp_eq_zero_of_exact (h : i ≫ p = j) (hp : FormallySmooth p) :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (conormalSequenceComp_eq_zero i j p h)).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
the sequence of Tag 067V is short exact: exactness at the middle term and
surjectivity of the second arrow are the assertions of Tag 067V, and injectivity of the first
arrow is what this tag adds, by way of the local splitting its proof produces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of schemes the following are equivalent: there is an affine open cover of the
base and, over each of its members, an affine open cover of its inverse image on which the maps on
sections are pseudo-coherent ring maps; and every compatible pair of affine opens has
pseudo-coherent map on sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pseudoCoherent_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    let pseudoCoherentOn := fun (V : S.Opens) (U : X.Opens)
        (h : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) ↦
      letI : Algebra Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) := (f.appLE V U h).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.PseudoCoherent Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U)
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j)),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i, pseudoCoherentOn (V j) (U i)
                ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le),
      ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U →
        ∀ (V : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen V →
          ∀ (h : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), pseudoCoherentOn V U h]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0682.** A pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes is locally of finite presentation.

On every compatible pair of affine opens the map on sections is a pseudo-coherent ring map,
hence of finite presentation by `RingHom.PseudoCoherent.finitePresentation`.

Followed by Mathlib's instance from `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation` to
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`, this is how type class search finds that a
pseudo-coherent morphism is locally of finite type, the clause of Stacks 067Y recorded by the
second tag.
declarations.statement:
public instance (priority := 100) locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_pseudoCoherent {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [hf : PseudoCoherent f] : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies the finite-type half of condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_tfae_three
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 067Y.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` the following are equivalent: there
are an affine open covering of `S` and, over each of its members, an affine open covering of its
inverse image on which the maps on sections are pseudo-coherent ring maps; the map on sections is
pseudo-coherent at every compatible pair of affine opens; and `f` is locally of finite type with
`𝒪_X` pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.

The equivalence of the first two conditions is `AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_tfae`, and the
third enters through `AlgebraicGeometry.relativeStructureSheafComparison`. This declaration states
the whole of the source's lemma, so it subsumes the two clauses of it tagged in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/PseudoCoherent.lean`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pseudoCoherent_tfae_three :
    let pseudoCoherentOn := fun (V : S.Opens) (U : X.Opens)
        (h : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) ↦
      letI : Algebra Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) := (f.appLE V U h).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.PseudoCoherent Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U)
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j)),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i, pseudoCoherentOn (V j) (U i)
                ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le),
      ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U →
        ∀ (V : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen V →
          ∀ (h : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), pseudoCoherentOn V U h,
      ∃ hft : LocallyOfFiniteType f,
        letI := hft
        Scheme.Hom.IsModulePseudoCoherent f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is pseudo-coherent if for every affine open `V ⊆ S` and every
affine open `U ⊆ X` with `U ⊆ f ⁻¹ᵁ V` the induced map on sections `Γ(S, V) ⟶ Γ(X, U)` is a
pseudo-coherent ring map.
declarations.statement: public class PseudoCoherent {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_isPullback_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0680.** A flat base change of a pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes is
pseudo-coherent: if `f : X ⟶ S` is pseudo-coherent, `g : S' ⟶ S` is flat and the square with
sides `g' : X' ⟶ X` and `f' : X' ⟶ S'` is cartesian, then `f'` is pseudo-coherent.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_comp
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0681.** A composition of pseudo-coherent morphisms of schemes is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
instance pseudoCoherent_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [hf : PseudoCoherent f] [hg : PseudoCoherent g] : PseudoCoherent (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0682.** A pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes is locally of finite presentation.

On every compatible pair of affine opens the map on sections is a pseudo-coherent ring map,
hence of finite presentation by `RingHom.PseudoCoherent.finitePresentation`.

Followed by Mathlib's instance from `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation` to
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`, this is how type class search finds that a
pseudo-coherent morphism is locally of finite type, the clause of Stacks 067Y recorded by the
second tag.
declarations.statement:
public instance (priority := 100) locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_pseudoCoherent {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [hf : PseudoCoherent f] : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0683.** If `X` and `Y` are pseudo-coherent over a base scheme `S`, then any morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` over `S` is pseudo-coherent.

Pseudo-coherence of `f` is checked around a point `x` of `X` on an affine open `U ∋ x` of `X`
contained in the preimage of an affine open `V` of `Y`, itself contained in the preimage of an
affine open `W` of `S`. The map `Γ(S, W) ⟶ Γ(X, U)` is the composite of `Γ(S, W) ⟶ Γ(Y, V)` with
`Γ(Y, V) ⟶ Γ(X, U)`, and the outer two are pseudo-coherent by hypothesis, so the algebra
cancellation lemma applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [PseudoCoherent (f ≫ g)] [PseudoCoherent g] : PseudoCoherent f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_iff_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0684.** A morphism of schemes whose target is locally Noetherian is pseudo-coherent
if and only if it is locally of finite type.

A pseudo-coherent morphism is always locally of finite type. Conversely, over a locally
Noetherian base the sections over an affine open form a Noetherian ring, so every map on sections
over a compatible pair of affine opens is a finite-type ring map out of a Noetherian ring, hence
pseudo-coherent by Stacks 067I.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_iff_locallyOfFiniteType {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) : PseudoCoherent f ↔ LocallyOfFiniteType f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0685.** A perfect morphism of schemes is locally of finite presentation: it is
pseudo-coherent, and a pseudo-coherent morphism is locally of finite presentation by Stacks
0682.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_perfect {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Perfect f] : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f
declarations.comment: the section's unnumbered assertion that a perfect morphism is pseudo-coherent, hence locally of finite presentation; the fifteen numbered items of the section carry their own tags

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_openCover_perfect_iff_forall
declarations.doc:
For a locally finite type morphism of schemes, perfectness on some affine open covering
of the target and affine open coverings of its preimages is equivalent to perfectness on every
pair of affine opens for which the source open maps into the target open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_openCover_perfect_iff_forall
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    (∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
      IsOpenCover V ∧
        (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
        ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
          (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j)),
          (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
            ∀ i,
              let g := (f.appLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)).hom
              letI := g.toAlgebra
              ∀ D : CertifiedDerivedTensoring Γ(S, V j),
                RingHom.IsPerfectRingMap Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i)
                  D.tensor D.comparison D.isLeftDerived) ↔
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
          let g := (f.appLE V U hUV).hom
          letI := g.toAlgebra
          ∀ D : CertifiedDerivedTensoring Γ(S, V),
            RingHom.IsPerfectRingMap Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U)
              D.tensor D.comparison D.isLeftDerived

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0687.** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is perfect if it is locally of finite
type and, for every affine open `U ⊆ X` and every affine open `V ⊆ S` with `U ⊆ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the
induced map on sections `Γ(S, V) ⟶ Γ(X, U)` is a perfect ring map, with respect to every
certified derived tensor product on `Γ(S, V)`.

This is condition (2) of Stacks 0686, which is the condition Stacks 0687 defines perfectness by.
declarations.statement: public class Perfect {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop extends LocallyOfFiniteType f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_isPullback_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0688.** A flat base change of a perfect morphism of schemes is perfect: if
`f : X ⟶ S` is perfect, `g : S' ⟶ S` is flat and the square with sides `g' : X' ⟶ X` and
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` is cartesian, then `f'` is perfect.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_comp
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0689.** A composition of perfect morphisms of schemes is perfect.
declarations.statement:
public theorem perfect_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [Perfect f] [Perfect g] : Perfect (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_and_perfect_iff_flat_and_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068A.** A morphism of schemes is flat and perfect if and only if it is flat and
locally of finite presentation.

Neither implication uses flatness on the side it starts from: a perfect morphism is always
locally of finite presentation, through `AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_perfect` and Stacks
0682, and a flat morphism locally of finite presentation is always perfect, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_flat_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_and_perfect_iff_flat_and_locallyOfFinitePresentation {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) : (Flat f ∧ Perfect f) ↔ (Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068B.** A morphism of schemes locally of finite type over a regular scheme is
perfect.
declarations.statement:
public theorem perfect_of_isRegular {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hS : IsRegular S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : Perfect f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068C.** A Koszul-regular immersion of schemes is a perfect morphism.

The immersion factors as its closed factor into the canonical open, whose defining ideal sheaf is
Koszul-regular by definition, followed by an open immersion, which is flat and locally of finite
presentation and hence perfect by Stacks 068A; perfectness composes by Stacks 0689.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfect_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion i]
    (hi : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) : Perfect i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_isRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068C.** A regular immersion of schemes is a perfect morphism, because a regular
immersion is Koszul-regular by Stacks 063K.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfect_of_isRegularImmersion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion i]
    (hi : IsRegularImmersion i) : Perfect i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_comp_eq_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068D.** In a commutative triangle of morphisms of schemes with `f ≫ q = p`, `q`
smooth and `p` perfect, the morphism `f` is perfect.
declarations.statement:
public theorem perfect_of_comp_eq_of_smooth {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ S)
    {p : X ⟶ S} (hfq : f ≫ q = p) [Smooth q] [Perfect p] : Perfect f

declarations.name: CochainComplex.Tor.ChangeOfRingsSpectralSequence.exists_tor_change_of_rings_spectral_sequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068F.** Let `R → S` be a homomorphism of commutative rings, `M` an `R`-module and
`N` an `S`-module. There is a free resolution `P^•` of `M` over `R` such that the homology of
`P^• ⊗_R S`, with its natural `S`-module structure, computes `Tor_*^R(M, S)`, and there is a
spectral sequence
```
Tor_n^S(Tor_m^R(M, S), N) ⟹ Tor_{n+m}^R(M, N).
```
The second-page identification is displayed, and the last clause records the abutment; the two
`Nonempty` clauses before it record that the homology of the two base-changed complexes is
`Tor_*^R(M, S)` and `Tor_*^R(M, N)` after restricting scalars along `R → S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_tor_change_of_rings_spectral_sequence
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (N : ModuleCat.{max u v} S) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ),
      ∃ (ε : P ⟶ (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj M)
        (_ : QuasiIso ε),
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧
      Nonempty (P.homology 0 ≅ M) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → IsZero (P.homology i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Nonempty
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj ((baseChangeComplex f P).homology (-i)) ≅
          TorInDegree.{u, v} R i M
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj (ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{v} S))))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj
            ((baseChangeTensorComplex f P N).homology (-n)) ≅
          TorInDegree.{u, v} R n M ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj N))) ∧
      ∃ (E : FirstTorSpectralSequence (ModuleCat.{max u v} S))
        (_e₂ : ∀ i j : ℤ, (E.page 2).X (i, j) ≅
          TorInDegree.{u, v} S j ((baseChangeComplex f P).homology (-i)) N),
        HomologicalSpectralSequenceAbutsTo E
          (fun n ↦ (baseChangeTensorComplex f P N).homology (-n))

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorProducts.derivedTorProduct
declarations.doc:
The products
`Torᴿₙ(K, A) ⊗[A] Torᴿₘ(L, A) ⟶ Torᴿₙ₊ₘ(K ⊗ᴸ_R L, A)` on the Tor of derived objects
`K, L ∈ D(R)`: the cocycle pairing over `A` carried along the base-change identification.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedTorProduct (f : R →+* A)
    (D : CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.TotalDerivedExtensionScalars f)
    (K L : DObj R) (n m : ℤ) :
    (derivedTor f D n).obj K ⊗ (derivedTor f D m).obj L ⟶
      (derivedTor f D (n + m)).obj (((canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment:
products on the Tor of derived objects, the last display of the paragraph
  following Equation 15.64.0.2

registrations.name: RingTheory.TorProducts.cohomologyTensorProduct
registrations.comment:
Equation 15.64.0.1: the pairing `Hⁱ(K) ⊗ Hʲ(L) ⟶ Hⁱ⁺ʲ(K ⊗ᴸ L)` sending the
  classes of cocycles `k, l` to the class of `k ⊗ l`.

registrations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedExtensionScalarsTensorIso
registrations.comment:
Equation 15.64.0.2: the canonical identification
  `(K ⊗ᴸ_R A) ⊗ᴸ_A (L ⊗ᴸ_R A) = (K ⊗ᴸ_R L) ⊗ᴸ_R A` in `D(A)`.

registrations.name: RingTheory.TorProducts.torProduct
registrations.comment:
Equation 15.64.0.3: the products
  `Torᴿₙ(M, A) ⊗[A] Torᴿₘ(N, A) ⟶ Torᴿₙ₊ₘ(M ⊗_R N, A)` for `R`-modules `M` and `N`.

registrations.name: GradedTor.existsUnique_algebra
registrations.comment:
The `A`-algebra structure on `Torᴿ_⋆(B, A)` for an `R`-algebra `B`, whose
  multiplication is the product of Equation 15.64.0.3 followed by the map induced by the
  multiplication `B ⊗_R B → B`.

registrations.name: GradedTor.canonical_mul_ofNat
registrations.comment:
The multiplication of the `A`-algebra `Torᴿ_⋆(B, A)` is the product of
  Equation 15.64.0.3 followed by the map induced by multiplication on `B`.

registrations.name: GradedTor.torPieceMap_isAlgebraHom
registrations.comment:
Lemma 15.64.1: for an `R`-algebra map `B → C` the induced map
  `Torᴿ_⋆(B, A) ⟶ Torᴿ_⋆(C, A)` is a homomorphism of `A`-algebras. The source omits the proof.

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorProducts.cohomologyTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068H.** For any two objects `K` and `L` of `D(R)`, tensoring cocycles gives the
canonical map
`Hⁱ(K) ⊗[R] Hʲ(L) ⟶ Hⁱ⁺ʲ(K ⊗ᴸ[R] L)`.

The representative witness in the result specifies the source's formula
`[p] ⊗ [q] ↦ [p ⊗ q]`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cohomologyTensorProduct
    (K L : DObj R) (i j : ℤ) : CohomologyTensorProduct K L i j

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.derivedExtensionScalarsTensorIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical base-change isomorphism
`(K ⊗ᴸ[R] A) ⊗ᴸ[A] (L ⊗ᴸ[R] A) ≅ (K ⊗ᴸ[R] L) ⊗ᴸ[R] A` in `D(A)`, natural in
`K, L ∈ D(R)` and represented on K-flat complexes by standard tensor base change.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedExtensionScalarsTensorIso (f : R →+* A)
    (T_R : DerivedTensorProductGeneral.{uR, max uA v} R)
    (T_A : DerivedTensorProductGeneral.{uA, max uR v} A)
    (D : CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.TotalDerivedExtensionScalars.{uR, v, uA} f) :
    DerivedExtensionScalarsTensorIso f T_R T_A D

declarations.name: RingTheory.TorProducts.torProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068J.** The canonical Tor product
`Torⁿᴿ(M, A) ⊗[A] Torᵐᴿ(N, A) → Torⁿ⁺ᵐᴿ(M ⊗[R] N, A)`, simultaneously for all `R`-modules
`M` and `N`. Packaging it as a natural transformation records its naturality in both
variables.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def torProduct (n m : ℕ) :
    (torBaseChange.{uR, uA, v} R A n).prod (torBaseChange.{uR, uA, v} R A m) ⋙
        tensorBifunctor.{uA, max uR v} A ⟶
      tensorBifunctor.{uR, max uA v} R ⋙ torBaseChange.{uR, uA, v} R A (n + m)

declarations.name: GradedTor.torPieceMap_isAlgebraHom
declarations.doc:
The maps on Tor induced by an `R`-algebra homomorphism assemble into a
homomorphism of the canonical graded `A`-algebras on Tor: they preserve the unit and the
homogeneous multiplication.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torPieceMap_isAlgebraHom {B C : AlgCat.{v, uR} R} (g : B ⟶ C) :
    torPieceMap.{uR, uA, v} R A g 0 (canonicalAlgebra.{uR, uA, v} R A B).one =
      (canonicalAlgebra.{uR, uA, v} R A C).one ∧
    ∀ (i j : ℤ) (x : torPiece.{uR, uA, v} R A B i)
        (y : torPiece.{uR, uA, v} R A B j),
      torPieceMap.{uR, uA, v} R A g (i + j)
          ((canonicalAlgebra.{uR, uA, v} R A B).mul i j (x ⊗ₜ[A] y)) =
        (canonicalAlgebra.{uR, uA, v} R A C).mul i j
          (torPieceMap.{uR, uA, v} R A g i x ⊗ₜ[A]
            torPieceMap.{uR, uA, v} R A g j y)

declarations.name: Koszul.isH1Regular_quotient_of_isH1Regular_append
declarations.doc:
If `f_1, ..., f_n, g_1, ..., g_m` is an `H₁`-regular sequence in `A`, then the images
`ḡ_1, ..., ḡ_m` of the `g_j` in the quotient `A / (f_1, ..., f_n)` form an `H₁`-regular sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1Regular_quotient_of_isH1Regular_append {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {n m : ℕ}
    (f : Fin n → A) (g : Fin m → A)
    (h : Koszul.IsH1Regular (Fin.append f g)) :
    Koszul.IsH1Regular
      (fun j : Fin m => Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (g j))

declarations.name: Koszul.koszulRegular_quotient_of_koszulRegular_append
declarations.doc:
If `f` and the concatenation of `f` and `g` are Koszul-regular, then the image
of `g` in the quotient by the ideal generated by `f` is Koszul-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem koszulRegular_quotient_of_koszulRegular_append
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {n m : ℕ} (f : Fin n → A) (g : Fin m → A)
    (hf : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)
    (hfg : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular (Fin.append f g)) :
    Koszul.IsKoszulRegular
      (fun j : Fin m => Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (g j))

declarations.name: Koszul.regular_ideals_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068N.** Koszul-regular, `H₁`-regular, and quasi-regular ideals descend along a
faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem regular_ideals_of_faithfullyFlat
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat)
    (I : Ideal A) :
    (Ideal.IsKoszulRegular (I.map f) → Ideal.IsKoszulRegular I) ∧
      (Ideal.IsH1Regular (I.map f) → Ideal.IsH1Regular I) ∧
      (Quasiregular.IsQuasiregularIdeal' (I.map f) →
        Quasiregular.IsQuasiregularIdeal' I)

declarations.name: Stacks.GenericLinearForm.linearForm_isNonZeroDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068P**.
If the only `x ∈ R` with `x a_i = 0` for all `i` is `x = 0`, then `f = ∑ a_i t_i` is a
nonzerodivisor in `R[t_1, ..., t_n]`: every `g` with `f * g = 0` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearForm_isNonZeroDivisor (a : Fin n → R)
    (hinj : ∀ x : R, (∀ i, x * a i = 0) → x = 0) :
    ∀ g : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R, linearForm a * g = 0 → g = 0

declarations.name: Koszul.isRegular_upperTriangular_of_isKoszulRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068Q.** A Koszul-regular sequence generating a proper ideal becomes a regular
sequence after a generic invertible upper-triangular change of generators. The resulting
polynomial localization is faithfully flat and smooth over the original ring, and the changed
sequence generates the extension of the original ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_upperTriangular_of_isKoszulRegular
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → R)
    (hf : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)
    (hproper : Ideal.span (Set.range f) ≠ ⊤) :
    let σ := {ij : Fin n × Fin n // ij.1 ≤ ij.2}
    let P := MvPolynomial σ R
    let d : P := ∏ i : Fin n, MvPolynomial.X ⟨(i, i), le_rfl⟩
    let S := Localization.Away d
    let g : Fin n → S := fun i ↦
      ∑ j : Fin n, if hij : i ≤ j then
        algebraMap P S (MvPolynomial.X ⟨(i, j), hij⟩) * algebraMap R S (f j)
      else 0
    Module.FaithfullyFlat R S ∧ Algebra.Smooth R S ∧
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular S (List.ofFn g) ∧
        Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) =
          Ideal.span (Set.range g)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isPseudoCoherent_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068R.** Both `m`-pseudo-coherence and pseudo-coherence descend along a faithfully
flat extension of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_and_isPseudoCoherent_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u w} R) ℤ) (m : ℤ) :
    (IsPseudoCoherentFrom
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max u w} f).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)) m →
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) m) ∧
    (IsPseudoCoherent
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max u w} f).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)) →
      IsPseudoCoherent (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
Tor amplitude descends along a faithfully flat ring map `f : R →+* S`: if the base change of
`K` along `f` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`, then so does `K`. Both sides are read at the
canonical derived tensor products of the two rings lifted by `ULift` into the universe of the
modules, and the base change is extension of scalars along the lifted ring map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_of_faithfullyFlat
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} (ULift.{max v w} R)) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (h : HasTorAmplitudeCanonical (ULift.{max u w} S)
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((CochainComplex.extendScalars (f.ulift.{max v w, max u w})).obj K)) a b) :
    HasTorAmplitudeCanonical (ULift.{max v w} R) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) a b

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings and let `K` be a complex of
`R`-modules. If `K ⊗_R S` is perfect, then `K` is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : f.FaithfullyFlat)
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) ℤ)
    (hK : IsPerfect
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max u v w} f).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))) :
    IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_localization_iso_biprod_truncGE_truncLE
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring, `p ⊂ R` a prime, `i ∈ ℤ` and let `K` be a pseudo-coherent
object of `D(R)` with `H^i(K ⊗_R^L κ(p)) = 0`. Then there is `f ∈ R`, `f ∉ p`, and a canonical
direct sum decomposition
`K ⊗_R R_f = τ_{≥ i+1}(K ⊗_R R_f) ⊕ τ_{≤ i-1}(K ⊗_R R_f)` in `D(R_f)`, in which
`τ_{≥ i+1}(K ⊗_R R_f)` is a perfect complex with Tor amplitude in `[i + 1, ∞]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_localization_iso_biprod_truncGE_truncLE
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (_hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) (i : ℤ)
    (hfibre : FibreCohomologyVanishes.{u, v} p K i) :
    ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧
      let Kf := (PseudoCoherence.localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, v} f).obj K
      let upper := (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (i + 1)).obj Kf
      let lower := (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE (i - 1)).obj Kf
      IsPerfect upper ∧
        (∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (Localization.Away f)) ℤ) (b : ℤ),
          P.IsStrictlyGE (i + 1) ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
            (∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite (Localization.Away f) (P.X j)) ∧
            (∀ j : ℤ, Module.Projective (Localization.Away f) (P.X j)) ∧
            Nonempty (upper ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ∧
            ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} (Localization.Away f)) (j : ℤ), j < i + 1 →
              IsZero ((TorAmplitude.tensorComplex P M).homology j)) ∧
        ∃! e : Kf ≅ upper ⊞ lower,
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (i + 1)).app Kf = e.hom ≫ biprod.fst ∧
            (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι (i - 1)).app Kf ≫ e.hom = biprod.inr

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_and_torAmplitude_iff_fibreCohomologyVanishes
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `a, b : ℤ` and let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of the
derived category of `R`-modules. Then `K` is perfect of Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` if and only if
the cohomology of the derived fibre `K ⊗_R^L κ(p)` vanishes outside `[a, b]` for every prime ideal
`p`, and it is enough to test this at the maximal ideals.

Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` is expressed, as in [stacks 0658], by the existence of a flat
representative supported in `[a, b]`; by [stacks 0654] this is exactly Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`,
and the third clause spells that out: every bounded above flat representative of `K` — which is
what computes `K ⊗_R^L M` — has vanishing cohomology outside `[a, b]` after tensoring with an
arbitrary module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_torAmplitude_iff_fibreCohomologyVanishes {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) (a b : ℤ) :
    let perfectWithTorAmplitude :=
      IsPerfect K ∧ HasFlatRepresentative K a b ∧
        ∀ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ, TorAmplitude.BoundedAbove E →
          TorAmplitude.IsComplexOfFlats E → Nonempty (K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj E) →
            TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeIn E a b
    let primeVanishes := ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum R, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i →
      FibreCohomologyVanishes.{u, v} q.asIdeal K i
    let maximalVanishes := ∀ m : MaximalSpectrum R, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i →
      FibreCohomologyVanishes.{u, v} m.asIdeal K i
    (perfectWithTorAmplitude ↔ primeVanishes) ∧ (primeVanishes ↔ maximalVanishes)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_iff_isPerfect_at_primes_of_isBoundedBelow_and_stalkwise_criteria
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `K` be a pseudo-coherent object of the derived category
of `R`-modules. Then `K` perfect implies that every stalk `K ⊗_R^L R_p` is perfect; perfectness at
all prime stalks, perfectness at all maximal stalks, and the vanishing of the cohomology of the
derived fibre `K ⊗_R^L κ(p)` in all sufficiently low degrees at every prime or at every maximal
ideal are equivalent; and if `K` is bounded below these are also equivalent to perfectness of `K`
itself.

The derived base change is the canonical one of [stacks 064H],
`CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_iff_isPerfect_at_primes_of_isBoundedBelow_and_stalkwise_criteria
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) :
    let perfect := IsPerfect K
    let perfectAtPrimes := ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum R,
      IsPerfect ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
        (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))).functor.obj K)
    let perfectAtMaximals := ∀ m : MaximalSpectrum R,
      IsPerfect ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
        (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime m.asIdeal))).functor.obj K)
    let fibreVanishesBelowAtPrimes := ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum R,
      ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{max u v} q.asIdeal.ResidueField) i).obj
            ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
              (algebraMap R q.asIdeal.ResidueField)).functor.obj K))
    let fibreVanishesBelowAtMaximals := ∀ m : MaximalSpectrum R,
      ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{max u v} m.asIdeal.ResidueField) i).obj
            ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
              (algebraMap R m.asIdeal.ResidueField)).functor.obj K))
    (perfect → perfectAtPrimes) ∧
      (perfectAtPrimes ↔ perfectAtMaximals) ∧
      (perfectAtPrimes ↔ fibreVanishesBelowAtPrimes) ∧
      (perfectAtMaximals ↔ fibreVanishesBelowAtMaximals) ∧
      ((∃ a : ℤ, K.IsGE a) → (perfect ↔ perfectAtPrimes))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_and_torAmplitude_of_flat_of_fibre_globalDimension_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068X.** Let `A → B` be a flat map of commutative rings, let `a, b : ℤ` and let `d ≥ 0`
be an integer such that for every prime `p` of `A` the fibre ring `B ⊗_A κ(p)` has global dimension
at most `d`. Let `K` be an object of the derived category of `B`-modules which is pseudo-coherent
as a complex of `B`-modules and has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` as a complex of `A`-modules. Then `K`
is perfect as a complex of `B`-modules with Tor amplitude in `[a - d, b]`.

Tor amplitude is recorded as in [stacks 068V]: by a flat representative supported in the window,
which by [stacks 0654] is exactly Tor amplitude, together with the termwise condition on every
bounded above flat representative. The hypothesis over `A` is the same condition for the complex of
`A`-modules underlying `K`, and `hasTorAmplitudeIn_flatRepresentative_of_hasTorAmplitude` derives
it from derived Tor amplitude against any certified derived tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_torAmplitude_of_flat_of_fibre_globalDimension_le [Module.Flat A B]
    (a b : ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hfibre : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
      ringGlobalDimension (TensorProduct A B p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤ (d : ℕ))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hamp : ∀ F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ, TorAmplitude.BoundedAbove F →
      TorAmplitude.IsComplexOfFlats F →
      Nonempty ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) → TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeIn F a b) :
    IsPerfect K ∧ HasFlatRepresentative.{u, u} K (a - (d : ℤ)) b ∧
      ∀ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ, TorAmplitude.BoundedAbove E →
        TorAmplitude.IsComplexOfFlats E → Nonempty (K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj E) →
          TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeIn E (a - (d : ℤ)) b

declarations.name: RingHom.isPerfectRingMap_iff_exists_finite_projective_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 068Y.** A ring map `A → B` is perfect if and only if there is a presentation
`B = A[x_1, …, x_n]/I` for which `B`, as a module over `A[x_1, …, x_n]`, admits a finite
resolution by finite projective `A[x_1, …, x_n]`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRingMap_iff_exists_finite_projective_resolution
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.tensorModuleRight N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    IsPerfectRingMap A B derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived ↔
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B), Function.Surjective α ∧
        let : Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) B := Module.compHom B α.toRingHom
        ∃ (d : ℕ) (F : ModuleResolution (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) B),
          (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) (F.complex.X i) ∧
            Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) (F.complex.X i)) ∧
          ∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 068Z], part (2).** For immersions `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` with `j`
locally of finite presentation whose conormal sequence is exact and locally split,
`H₁`-regularity of `i ≫ j` descends to `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation j]
    (hS : IsSplitExactConormalSequence i j) (hij : IsH1RegularImmersion (i ≫ j)) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion i
declarations.comment: (2) H₁-regularity descends to the first immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 068Z], part (3).** For immersions `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` with `j`
locally of finite presentation whose conormal sequence is exact and locally split, `i` is
Koszul-regular as soon as both `j` and `i ≫ j` are.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation j]
    (hS : IsSplitExactConormalSequence i j) (hj : IsKoszulRegularImmersion j)
    (hij : IsKoszulRegularImmersion (i ≫ j)) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 068Z], part (1).** For immersions `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` with `j`
locally of finite presentation whose conormal sequence is exact and locally split,
quasi-regularity of `i ≫ j` descends to `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
    (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation j]
    (hS : IsSplitExactConormalSequence i j) (hij : IsQuasiRegularImmersion (i ≫ j)) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion i
declarations.comment: (1) quasi-regularity descends to the first immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 068Z] part (3) for closed immersions, from injectivity on cotangent
fibres.** Let `Z --i--→ Y --j--→ X` be closed immersions with Koszul-regular defining ideal
sheaves for `j` and for `i ≫ j`.  If at every point of `Z` the induced map of cotangent fibres
`I_x/𝔪_x I_x → J_x/𝔪_x J_x` of the two defining ideals is injective, then the defining ideal
sheaf of `i` is Koszul-regular.

Over an affine open `U` of `X` around the image of the point, local generators `f` of the ideal
of `Y` extend to local generators `f, g` of the ideal of `Z`, both Koszul-regular, and the
images of the `g` under `j` on sections generate the ideal of `Z` in `Y` and are Koszul-regular
by [Stacks Project, Tag 068M].
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularIdealSheaf_of_comp (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j]
    (hinj : ∀ z : Z, Function.Injective (conormalFibreMap i j z))
    (hj : IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace (definingIdealOfHom j))
    (hij : IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf X.toRingedSpace (definingIdealOfHom (i ≫ j))) :
    IsKoszulRegularIdealSheaf Y.toRingedSpace (definingIdealOfHom i)
declarations.comment: part (3) for closed immersions: Koszul-regularity of `j` and of `i ≫ j` together with injectivity of the cotangent-fibre map `I_x/𝔪_x I_x ⟶ J_x/𝔪_x J_x` gives Koszul-regularity of `i`. That injectivity is a hypothesis here, not derived from exactness and local splitness of the conormal sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isSplitExactConormalSequence_of_split
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0690, `(2) ⇒ (3)`.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of schemes
and let `z : Z`.  If `i` and `i ≫ j` are regular immersions in a neighbourhood of `z`, then
`i ≫ j` is a regular immersion in a neighbourhood of `z` and the conormal sequence
`0 ⟶ i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` is exact and locally split in a neighbourhood
of `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isSplitExactConormalSequence_of_split (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] (z : Z)
    (hi : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i))
    (hji : ∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j))) :
    (∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j))) ∧
      ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsSplitExactConormalSequence (W.ι ≫ i) j

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_of_factors_of_split
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0690, `(2) ⇒ (1)`.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of schemes
with `X` locally Noetherian and let `z : Z`.  If `i` and `i ≫ j` are regular immersions in a
neighbourhood of `z`, then `i` is a regular immersion in a neighbourhood of `z` and `j` is one in
a neighbourhood of `i z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_of_factors_of_split (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (z : Z)
    (hi : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i))
    (hji : ∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j))) :
    (∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i)) ∧
      ∃ V : Y.Opens, i.base z ∈ V ∧ IsRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ j)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isSplitExactConormalSequence_of_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0690, `(1) ⇒ (3)`.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of schemes
with `X` locally Noetherian and let `z : Z`.  If `i` is a regular immersion in a neighbourhood of
`z` and `j` is one in a neighbourhood of `i z`, then `i ≫ j` is a regular immersion in a
neighbourhood of `z` and the conormal sequence of the pair is exact and locally split in a
neighbourhood of `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isSplitExactConormalSequence_of_factors (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (z : Z)
    (hi : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i))
    (hj : ∃ V : Y.Opens, i.base z ∈ V ∧ IsRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ j)) :
    (∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j))) ∧
      ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsSplitExactConormalSequence (W.ι ≫ i) j

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.tfae_isRegularImmersion_near
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0690.**  For immersions `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` with `X` locally Noetherian
and `z : Z`, the following are equivalent: (1) `i` is a regular immersion near `z` and `j` is one
near `i z`; (2) `i` and `i ≫ j` are regular immersions near `z`; (3) `i ≫ j` is a regular
immersion near `z` and the conormal sequence of the pair is exact and locally split near `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isRegularImmersion_near (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion j]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (z : Z) :
    List.TFAE
      [(∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i)) ∧
          ∃ V : Y.Opens, i.base z ∈ V ∧ IsRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ j),
        (∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i)) ∧
          ∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j)),
        (∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j))) ∧
          ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsSplitExactConormalSequence (W.ι ≫ i) j]

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_of_split_near
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0690, `(3) ⇒ (1)`.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of schemes
with `X` locally Noetherian, let `z : Z` and let `y = i z`.  If `i ≫ j` is a regular immersion in
a neighbourhood of `z` and the conormal sequence of the pair is exact and locally split in a
neighbourhood of `z`, then `i` is a regular immersion in a neighbourhood of `z` and `j` is one in
a neighbourhood of `y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_of_split_near (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsImmersion j] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (z : Z)
    (hji : ∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j)))
    (hS : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsSplitExactConormalSequence (W.ι ≫ i) j) :
    (∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i)) ∧
      ∃ V : Y.Opens, i.base z ∈ V ∧ IsRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ j)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_comp_of_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0690, `(1) ⇒ (2)`.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of schemes
with `X` locally Noetherian and let `z : Z`.  If `i` is a regular immersion in a neighbourhood of
`z` and `j` is one in a neighbourhood of `i z`, then `i ≫ j` is a regular immersion in a
neighbourhood of `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_comp_of_factors (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsImmersion j] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (z : Z)
    (hi : ∃ W : Z.Opens, z ∈ W ∧ IsRegularImmersion (W.ι ≫ i))
    (hj : ∃ V : Y.Opens, i.base z ∈ V ∧ IsRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ j)) :
    ∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧ IsRegularImmersion (U.ι ≫ (i ≫ j))

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.regular_immersion_not_permanent_in_middle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0691.** Regularity of an immersion is not inherited by the middle term of a
factorization. For `Z = Spec(k[x]/(x)) --i--→ Y = Spec(k[x]/(x²)) --j--→ X = 𝐀¹_k = Spec(k[x])`
the two outer immersions `j` and `j ∘ i` are regular immersions — at every point of their sources
and globally — while the middle one, `i`, is a regular immersion in no neighbourhood of any point
of `Z` and in particular not globally, and the conormal sequence of the pair is exact and split in
no neighbourhood of any point of `Z`; at the level of ideals, the ideals of `Y` in `X` and of `Z`
in `X` are each generated by a weakly regular sequence and the ideal of `Z` in `Y` is generated by
none. So each of the three parts of Stacks tag 0690 fails at every point of `Z` — parts (1) and
(2) through their common first half, regularity of `i` near the point, and part (3) through its
second half, the splitting, its first half being true — while "`j ∘ i` and `j` are regular
immersions at `z` and `y`" holds, which is the content of the remark.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_immersion_not_permanent_in_middle (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    -- `j` is a regular immersion at every point of `Y`, and `j ∘ i` at every point of `Z`
    (∀ y, IsRegularImmersionAt (doubleOriginLineImmersion k) y) ∧
      (∀ z, IsRegularImmersionAt
        (simpleOriginImmersion k ≫ doubleOriginLineImmersion k) z) ∧
      -- while `i` is a regular immersion in no neighbourhood of any point of `Z`
      (∀ z, ¬ IsRegularImmersionAt (simpleOriginImmersion k) z) ∧
      -- and the conormal sequence is exact and split in no neighbourhood of any point of `Z`
      (∀ z, ¬ ∃ W : (Spec (CommRingCat.of (SimpleOriginRing k))).Opens, z ∈ W ∧
        IsSplitExactConormalSequence (W.ι ≫ simpleOriginImmersion k)
          (doubleOriginLineImmersion k)) ∧
      -- so that each of the three parts of Stacks tag 0690 fails at every point of `Z`
      (∀ z, ¬ (IsRegularImmersionAt (simpleOriginImmersion k) z ∧
        IsRegularImmersionAt (doubleOriginLineImmersion k) ((simpleOriginImmersion k).base z))) ∧
      (∀ z, ¬ (IsRegularImmersionAt (simpleOriginImmersion k) z ∧
        IsRegularImmersionAt (simpleOriginImmersion k ≫ doubleOriginLineImmersion k) z)) ∧
      (∀ z, ¬ (IsRegularImmersionAt (simpleOriginImmersion k ≫ doubleOriginLineImmersion k) z ∧
        ∃ W : (Spec (CommRingCat.of (SimpleOriginRing k))).Opens, z ∈ W ∧
          IsSplitExactConormalSequence (W.ι ≫ simpleOriginImmersion k)
            (doubleOriginLineImmersion k))) ∧
      -- the same three facts globally
      RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion (doubleOriginLineImmersion k) ∧
      RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion
        (simpleOriginImmersion k ≫ doubleOriginLineImmersion k) ∧
      ¬ RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion (simpleOriginImmersion k) ∧
      -- and at the level of ideals, to which Stacks tag 063G reduces them
      (∃ rs : List (Polynomial k),
        Ideal.ofList rs = doubleOriginIdeal k ∧ IsWeaklyRegular (Polynomial k) rs) ∧
      (∃ rs : List (Polynomial k),
        Ideal.ofList rs = simpleOriginIdeal k ∧ IsWeaklyRegular (Polynomial k) rs) ∧
      (¬ ∃ rs : List (DoubleOriginRing k),
        Ideal.ofList rs = doubleOriginPointIdeal k ∧
          IsWeaklyRegular (DoubleOriginRing k) rs)
declarations.comment: The counterexample of the remark for `X = 𝐀¹_k`, `Y = Spec(k[x]/(x²))` and `Z = Spec(k[x]/(x))` over an arbitrary field `k`, at the level of schemes throughout. The three immersions are the `Spec` of the quotient maps `k[x] → k[x]/(x²)` (that is `j`), `k[x] → k[x]/(x)` (that is `j ∘ i`, identified with the composite by `Stacks.Examples.simpleOriginImmersion_comp_doubleOriginLineImmersion`) and `k[x]/(x²) → k[x]/(x)` (that is `i`). The predicate is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion`, part (1) of Stacks tag 063J and the one whose variants the statements carrying Stacks tag 0690 compare; the `in a neighbourhood of a point` form in which Stacks tag 0690 states its three parts is `Stacks.Examples.IsRegularImmersionAt`, and the splitting condition of its part (3) is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSplitExactConormalSequence` on a neighbourhood, the form in which the proved implications of Stacks tag 0690 state it. Both forms are delivered: regularity of `j` at every point of `Y`, of `i ≫ j` at every point of `Z` and of both globally, against the refutation of regularity of `i` at every point of `Z` and globally. All three parts of Stacks tag 0690 are refuted, each as a whole and at every point of `Z`: parts (1) and (2) through their common first half, part (3) through its second half, the splitting, since its first half holds here. That last refutation runs through the implication `(3) ⇒ (1)` of Stacks tag 0690, `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_of_split_near`, which is proved; nothing here rests on an unproved result. The three ideal-level statements are retained as the affine half to which that predicate reduces by Stacks tag 063G. No hypothesis is carried beyond `k` being a field.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_surjective_regular_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0692.**  A Koszul-regular closed immersion becomes a regular immersion
after a surjective smooth base change of its target.

Both conditions are stated with the classes of Stacks tag 063J, parts (2) and (1):
`RegularIdealSheaf.IsKoszulRegularImmersion` and `RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_surjective_regular_baseChange {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : RegularIdealSheaf.IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (g : X' ⟶ X),
      Surjective g ∧ Smooth g ∧
        RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion (pullback.snd i g)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isKoszulRegularImmersion_comp_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0693 for Koszul-regular immersions.** In a commutative triangle `Y ⟶ X ⟶ S` with
`X ⟶ S` smooth and both `Y ⟶ X` and `Y ⟶ S` immersions, the composite `Y ⟶ S` of a Koszul-regular
immersion `Y ⟶ X` is a Koszul-regular immersion.

Koszul-regularity is local on the source, and near a point of `Y` the immersion into `X` is pushed
into a relative affine space `𝔸ⁿ_V` over an affine open `V ⊆ S`.  Shrinking `V` to an affine open
`T` over which `Y` is closed, the lifted coordinates of that chart define a section `σ` of
`𝔸ⁿ_V ⟶ V` over `T` through which the chart factors, and Stacks tag 068Z for the retracted
immersion `σ` descends Koszul-regularity to `Y ⟶ T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_comp_of_smooth (i : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsImmersion (i ≫ f)] [Smooth f] (hi : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion (i ≫ f)

declarations.doc:

`X ⟶ S` smooth and both `Y ⟶ X` and `Y ⟶ S` immersions, the composite `Y ⟶ S` of an `H₁`-regular
immersion `Y ⟶ X` is an `H₁`-regular immersion.

`H₁`-regularity is local on the source, and near a point of `Y` the immersion into `X` is pushed
into a relative affine space `𝔸ⁿ_V` over an affine open `V ⊆ S`.  Shrinking `V` to an affine open
`T` over which `Y` is closed, the lifted coordinates of that chart define a section `σ` of
`𝔸ⁿ_V ⟶ V` over `T` through which the chart factors, and Stacks tag 068Z for the retracted
immersion `σ` descends `H₁`-regularity to `Y ⟶ T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_comp_of_smooth (i : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion i]
    [IsImmersion (i ≫ f)] [Smooth f] (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion i) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion (i ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isQuasiRegularImmersion_comp_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Smooth postcomposition.** In a commutative triangle `Y ⟶ X ⟶ S` with `X ⟶ S` smooth and
both `Y ⟶ X` and `Y ⟶ S` immersions, the composite `Y ⟶ S` of a quasi-regular immersion `Y ⟶ X`

declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_comp_of_smooth {Y X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isKoszulRegularImmersion_iff_of_fpqcZeroHypercover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0694, the Koszul-regular clause, for an immersion.** An immersion of
schemes is Koszul-regular if and only if its base changes along the members of an fpqc covering
of the target are, with no quasi-compactness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_iff_of_fpqcZeroHypercover
    {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (𝒰 : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{w} Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage X) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i ↔ ∀ k, IsKoszulRegularImmersion (pullback.snd i (𝒰.f k))
declarations.comment: koszul_regular, erratum: morphisms that are immersions; fpqc, no quasi-compactness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_flat_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0695.** A flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation is
pseudo-coherent.

On every compatible pair of affine opens the map on sections is flat and of finite presentation,
hence pseudo-coherent by `RingHom.PseudoCoherent.of_flat_of_finitePresentation`, the
pseudo-coherence half of Stacks 067J.
declarations.statement:
instance pseudoCoherent_of_flat_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] : PseudoCoherent f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0696.** Pseudo-coherence of a morphism of schemes is fpqc local on the base: a
morphism is pseudo-coherent if and only if its base change along every member of an fpqc
covering of its target is pseudo-coherent.

Both implications are part of `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget`; they are spelled
out as a single `Iff` by `AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_iff_of_fpqcCover`.
declarations.statement:
instance pseudoCoherent_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@PseudoCoherent : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: Algebra.pseudoCoherent_quotient_iff_isModulePseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0697.** Let `A → B` be a flat ring map of finite presentation and let `I` be an
ideal of `B`. Then `A → B ⧸ I` is pseudo-coherent if and only if `I` is pseudo-coherent as a
`B`-module.

Pseudo-coherence of `A → B ⧸ I` is pseudo-coherence of `B ⧸ I` relative to `A`; Stacks 0673
restricts that along the finite map `B → B ⧸ I`, Stacks 0DHQ makes it absolute over `B` because
`A → B` is itself pseudo-coherent by Stacks 067J, and Stacks 064V exchanges `B ⧸ I` for `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_quotient_iff_isModulePseudoCoherent
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Flat A B]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B] (I : Ideal B) :
    Algebra.PseudoCoherent A (B ⧸ I) ↔ IsModulePseudoCoherent (R := B) I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PseudoCoherent.isLocalAtSource_syntomicPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0698.** Pseudo-coherence of morphisms of schemes is local on the source for the
syntomic topology.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_isLocalAtSource_of_affine_descent`, the reduction of
the source's statement to the case of a surjective syntomic morphism of affine schemes, with
that case discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_comp_surjective_syntomic_of_isAffine`.
declarations.statement:
instance PseudoCoherent.isLocalAtSource_syntomicPrecoverage :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource (@PseudoCoherent.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (Scheme.precoverage (@Syntomic.{u}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PseudoCoherent.isLocalAtSource_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0699.** Pseudo-coherence of morphisms of schemes is local on the source for the
fppf topology: a morphism is pseudo-coherent exactly when its composites with the members of an
fppf covering of its source are.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_isLocalAtSource_fppf_of_finiteLocallyFree_descent`,
the reduction of the source's statement to descent along a surjective finite locally free
morphism, with that descent discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_comp_surjective_finiteLocallyFree`.
declarations.statement:
instance PseudoCoherent.isLocalAtSource_fppfPrecoverage :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource (@PseudoCoherent.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069B.** Perfectness of a morphism of schemes is fpqc local on the base: a morphism is
perfect if and only if its base change along every member of an fpqc covering of its target is
perfect.

Both implications are part of `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget`; they are spelled
out as a single `Iff` by `AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_iff_of_fpqcCover`.
declarations.statement:
public instance perfect_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@Perfect.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent:
1. `f` is perfect;
2. `𝒪_X` locally has finite Tor dimension as a sheaf of `f^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules, that is, the
   restriction of scalars of `𝒪_X[0]` along `f^{-1}𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X` locally has finite Tor dimension
   on the inverse-image ringed space `(X, f^{-1}𝒪_S)`, at the derived tensor product;
3. for every `x ∈ X` the local ring `𝒪_{X, x}` has finite Tor dimension as an
   `𝒪_{S, f x}`-module through the stalk map of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfect_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [PseudoCoherent f] :
    List.TFAE
      [Perfect f,
        Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base)
          ((derivedScalarRestriction f).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) 0).obj
              (structureModule X.toRingedSpace))),
        ∀ x : X,
          let _ : Algebra (S.presheaf.stalk (f.base x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
            (f.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
          HasFiniteTorDimensionCanonical (S.presheaf.stalk (f.base x))
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (S.presheaf.stalk (f.base x))) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of (S.presheaf.stalk (f.base x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect.isLocalAtSource_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
Perfectness of morphisms of schemes is local on the source for the fppf topology: a morphism
is perfect exactly when its composites with the members of an fppf covering of its source are.
declarations.statement:
instance Perfect.isLocalAtSource_fppfPrecoverage :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource (@Perfect.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isKoszulRegularImmersion_comp_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069E.** Let `i : U ⟶ P` and `i' : U ⟶ P'` be immersions over `S` of schemes smooth
over `S`. Then `i` is a Koszul-regular immersion in a neighbourhood of `u : U` if and only if
`i'` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isKoszulRegularImmersion_comp_iff
    {S U P P' : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ S) (p : P ⟶ S) (p' : P' ⟶ S)
    (i : U ⟶ P) (i' : U ⟶ P') [IsImmersion i] [IsImmersion i'] [Smooth p] [Smooth p']
    (hi : i ≫ p = f) (hi' : i' ≫ p' = f) (u : U) :
    (∃ V : U.Opens, u ∈ V ∧ IsKoszulRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ i)) ↔
      ∃ V : U.Opens, u ∈ V ∧ IsKoszulRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ i')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.KoszulAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069F, part (1).** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is *Koszul at* `x : X` if it is
of finite type at `x` and there are an open neighbourhood `U` of `x`, a scheme `P` smooth over
`S` and a Koszul-regular immersion `i : U ⟶ P` through which the restriction of `f` to `U`
factors.
declarations.statement: def KoszulAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069F, part (2).** A *local complete intersection morphism*, also called a *Koszul
morphism*, is a morphism of schemes that is Koszul at every point of its source.
declarations.statement: def IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_koszul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069G**, unconditionally: an immersion over `S` of an open of the source of a local
complete intersection morphism into a scheme smooth over `S` is Koszul-regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_koszul {X S P : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (π : P ⟶ S)
    [Smooth π] (U : X.Opens) (i : U.toScheme ⟶ P) [IsImmersion i]
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) (hi : U.ι ≫ f = i ≫ π) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.perfect_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069H, part (3).** A local complete intersection morphism of schemes is perfect.

Perfectness is Zariski-local on the source, and on a neighbourhood of each point the morphism
factors as a Koszul-regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism; the first is perfect by
Stacks 068C, the second is flat and locally of finite presentation and hence perfect by
Stacks 068A, and perfectness is stable under composition by Stacks 0689.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfect_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) : Perfect f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069H, part (2).** A local complete intersection morphism of schemes is
pseudo-coherent, because it is perfect and a perfect morphism is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) : PseudoCoherent f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069H, part (1).** A local complete intersection morphism of schemes is locally of
finite presentation, because it is pseudo-coherent and a pseudo-coherent morphism is locally of
finite presentation by Stacks 0682.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
A flat base change of a local complete intersection morphism is a local
complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_pullback_snd
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) [Flat g]
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069J.** A composition of local complete intersection morphisms is a local complete
intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f)
    (hg : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism g) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069K, the implication (2) ⇒ (1).** A syntomic morphism of schemes is flat and a
local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_syntomic {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    (hf : Syntomic f) : Flat f ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f
declarations.comment: (2) ⇒ (1): a syntomic morphism is flat and a local complete intersection morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_iff_flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069K.** A morphism of schemes is syntomic if and only if it is flat and a local
complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_iff_flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Syntomic f ↔ Flat f ∧ IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069L.** A Koszul-regular immersion of schemes is a local complete intersection
morphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_isRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069L.** A regular immersion of schemes is a local complete intersection
morphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_comp_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069M.**  In a commutative triangle of morphisms of schemes with `g : Y ⟶ S` smooth,
if the composite `f ≫ g` is a local complete intersection morphism then so is `f : X ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_comp_of_smooth {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ S) [Smooth g] (h : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism (f ≫ g)) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069N.** Being a local complete intersection morphism of schemes is fpqc local on the
target: a morphism is Koszul if and only if its base change along every member of an fpqc
covering of its target is Koszul.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (@IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_syntomic_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069P.** The property of being a local complete intersection morphism of schemes is
syntomic local on the source: a morphism is Koszul exactly when its composites with the members
of a syntomic covering of its source are.

All four inputs of the syntomic case of Stacks 036H are supplied: Zariski locality on the source
and on the target and preservation under precomposition with a syntomic morphism come from
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Descent.LocalOnSourceTopologies.LocalCompleteIntersection`, and
the affine descent is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_surjective_syntomic_of_isAffine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtSource_syntomic_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (@IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (Scheme.precoverage (@Syntomic.{u}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_isLocalAtSource_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 069P, restricted to étale coverings.** The property of being a local complete
intersection morphism of schemes is local on the source for the étale topology: a morphism is
Koszul exactly when its composites with the members of an étale covering of its source are.

All four inputs of the étale case of Stacks 036H are available: Zariski locality on the source
and on the target come from
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Descent.LocalOnSourceTopologies.LocalCompleteIntersection`,
preservation under precomposition with an étale morphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.respectsLeft_etale_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism`, and the affine
descent is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_surjective_smooth_of_isAffine` read at
an étale `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_isLocalAtSource_etale :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (@IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.etalePrecoverage
declarations.comment: the étale case, unconditionally: the Koszul property of morphisms of schemes is local on the source for the étale topology. The syntomic statement of the tag is not claimed here

declarations.name: Module.flat_and_flat_localization_of_flat_quotient_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Critère de platitude par fibres, nilpotent case**. Let `R → S` be a map of commutative rings,
let `M` be an `S`-module whose `R`-module structure comes from `R → S`, and let `I ⊆ R` be a
nilpotent ideal. If `M/IM` is flat over `S/IS` and `M` is flat over `R`, then `M` is flat over `S`,
and `S_q` is flat over `R` for every prime `q ⊆ S` with `M ⊗_S κ(q)` nonzero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.flat_and_flat_localization_of_flat_quotient_of_isNilpotent
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsNilpotent I)
    [Module.Flat (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S))
      (M ⧸ (I.map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))]
    [Module.Flat R M] :
    Module.Flat S M ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
        [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [Algebra R Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq],
        Nontrivial (M ⊗[S] q.ResidueField) → Module.Flat R Sq
declarations.comment:
The auxiliary ring `S'` of the source's triangle is dropped: `M` is taken to be an
`S`-module over `R → S`, which is equivalent and does not mention `S'`. `IM` is written as
`IS • ⊤` over `S`, and `S_q` is an abstract localization at `q`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.exists_retraction_kerCotangentToTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06A6.** If `S` is a formally smooth `R`-algebra and `P → S` is surjective with kernel
`J`, then the canonical map `J/J² → S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R]` of Stacks 00RU admits a retraction, so that the
sequence `0 → J/J² → S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] → Ω[S⁄R] → 0` is split exact. Nothing is required of `P`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem KaehlerDifferential.exists_retraction_kerCotangentToTensor (R P S : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing P] [CommRing S] [Algebra R P] [Algebra P S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsScalarTower R P S] [Algebra.FormallySmooth R S]
    (hf : Function.Surjective (algebraMap P S)) :
    ∃ l : S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] →ₗ[P] (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P S)).Cotangent,
      l ∘ₗ kerCotangentToTensor R P S = LinearMap.id
declarations.comment:
Split exactness, i.e. the two assertions of the tag that are not already in Mathlib
(exactness at `Ω_{B/A} ⊗_B C` is `KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange` and
surjectivity on the right is `KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange_surjective`), stated as the
existence of a retraction of the injection `J/J² → Ω_{B/A} ⊗_B C`: that single datum is at once its
injectivity and the splitting. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_retraction_mapCotangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06A7.** Let `A → B → C` be ring maps with `A → C` surjective and `A → B` formally
smooth, and put `I = ker (A → C)` and `J = ker (B → C)`. Then the map `ι : I/I² → J/J²` of
Stacks 065V admits a retraction; in particular `ι` is injective, so that the sequence
`0 → I/I² → J/J² → Ω[B⁄A] ⊗[B] B/J → 0` of Stacks 065V is split short exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_retraction_mapCotangent
    (A B C : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C]
    [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C] [Algebra.FormallySmooth A B]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A C)) :
    ∃ ρ : (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B C)).Cotangent →ₗ[A]
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A C)).Cotangent,
      ρ ∘ₗ Ideal.mapCotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A C))
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B C)) (Algebra.ofId A B)
        (((RingHom.comap_ker (algebraMap B C) (algebraMap A B)).trans
          (congrArg RingHom.ker (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq A B C).symm)).ge) =
        LinearMap.id
declarations.comment:
Split exactness, i.e. the part of the tag that is not already the neighbouring tag
065V, stated as the existence of a retraction of the injection `I/I² → J/J²`: given 065V's exactness
that single datum is at once its injectivity and the splitting. Exactness at `J/J²` and surjectivity
