of `KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor A B C` are 065V, hold with no hypothesis on `A → B`,
and are not restated. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.split_exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06A8.** Let `R → P → S` be ring maps with `R → S` smooth and `P → S` surjective with
kernel `J`. Then the exact sequence `0 → J/J² → S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] → Ω[S⁄R] → 0` of Stacks 00RU is
split short exact: its left hand map `J/J² → S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R]` is injective and its right hand map
`S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R] → Ω[S⁄R]` admits an `S`-linear section. Only formal smoothness of `R → S` is used,
and nothing is required of `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem KaehlerDifferential.split_exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange
    (R P S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing P] [CommRing S] [Algebra R P] [Algebra P S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsScalarTower R P S] [Algebra.FormallySmooth R S]
    (hf : Function.Surjective (algebraMap P S)) :
    Function.Injective (kerCotangentToTensor R P S) ∧
      ∃ σ : Ω[S⁄R] →ₗ[S] S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R], mapBaseChange R P S ∘ₗ σ = LinearMap.id
declarations.comment:
Stated for a formally smooth `R → S`, which is the source's own generalisation
06A6, and with no hypothesis on `P`. Split exactness is recorded as injectivity of the left hand
map together with an `S`-linear section of the right hand map, the exactness of the sequence of
00RU in the middle and on the right being Mathlib's
`KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange` and
`KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange_surjective`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_leftInverse_mapCotangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06A9.** Let `A → B → C` be ring maps with `A → C` surjective and `A → B` smooth, and
put `I = ker (A → C)` and `J = ker (B → C)`. Then the map `I/I² → J/J²` of Stacks 065V admits an
`A`-linear left inverse; in particular it is injective, so that the sequence
`0 → I/I² → J/J² → Ω[B⁄A] ⊗[B] B/J → 0` of Stacks 065V is exact, indeed split exact. Only formal
smoothness of `A → B` is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_leftInverse_mapCotangent
    (A B C : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C]
    [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C] [Algebra.FormallySmooth A B]
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A C)) :
    ∃ ρ : (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B C)).Cotangent →ₗ[A]
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A C)).Cotangent,
      ρ ∘ₗ Ideal.mapCotangent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A C))
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap B C)) (Algebra.ofId A B)
        (((RingHom.comap_ker (algebraMap B C) (algebraMap A B)).trans
          (congrArg RingHom.ker (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq A B C).symm)).ge) =
        LinearMap.id
declarations.comment:
Stated for a formally smooth `A → B`, which is the source's own generalisation
06A7, and with the retraction that generalisation asserts rather than bare injectivity, the latter
following by `Function.LeftInverse.injective`. Exactness at `J/J²` and surjectivity of
`KaehlerDifferential.kerCotangentToTensor A B C` are the neighbouring tag 065V and are not
restated. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06AA].** For an immersion of schemes `i : Z ⟶ X` over `p : X ⟶ S` with `Z`
smooth over `S`, the conormal sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0` of
[Stacks, Tag 01UZ] is short exact.

A smooth morphism is formally smooth by [Stacks, Tag 02H6], and formal smoothness is all the
proof uses.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalShortComplex_shortExact {Z X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (p : X ⟶ S) (hZ : AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth (i ≫ p)) :
    (conormalShortComplex i p).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceTwoImmersions.mono_conormalTransitivityMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06AB], exactness on the left.** For immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y`
in a commutative triangle `i ≫ p = j` with `p` smooth, the canonical map
`𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of [Stacks, Tag 067L] is a monomorphism.

A smooth morphism induces a smooth, hence formally smooth, ring map on every compatible pair of
affine opens, so this is `mono_conormalTransitivityMap_of_formallySmooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_conormalTransitivityMap [Smooth p] (h : i ≫ p = j) :
    Mono (conormalTransitivityMap i j p h)
declarations.comment:
exactness on the left, that is, that the first arrow `𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of the
sequence of 067L is a monomorphism. Exactness at `𝒞_{Z/X}` and surjectivity onto `i^*Ω_{X/Y}`
are the content of 067L and are not restated here; they are proved in the modules named in the
module docstring, which also says where the second arrow of the sequence is.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A morphism over a stage of a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes with affine transition morphisms, essentially small in the universe of the schemes, which
is locally of finite presentation and whose base change to the limit is finite locally free, is
finite locally free after base change to some later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_baseChange_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left
declarations.comment: the plain statement; the degree-d refinement is exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_baseChange_of_isLimit. Carries the essential smallness of the index category, a hypothesis of the inputs without which the statement is false and which the source, having no universe hierarchy, states implicitly by indexing on a directed set

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
A morphism over a stage of a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes with affine transition morphisms, indexed in the universe of the schemes, which is locally
of finite presentation and whose base change to the limit is finite locally free of degree `d`, is
finite locally free of degree `d` after base change to some later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_baseChange_of_isLimit
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (d : ℕ)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
      ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left d] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
        ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left d
declarations.comment: the degree-d refinement. Narrower than the plain statement in the index universes: the objects and the morphisms of the index category are both in the universe of the schemes, which is the form in which the cofiltered Tag 05F4 used to descend the degree stratum along the system of base changes of Y₀ is available, that system being indexed by the over category, which inherits both universes. The plain statement's essential smallness is implied by this narrowing rather than assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_overPullbackObj_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06AC, fixed-degree form, for the structure morphism of an object over a
stage.** Let `D` be a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with
affine transition morphisms and limit cone `c`, and let `Z` be of finite presentation over the
stage `D.obj i₀`. If the base change of `Z` to the limit is finite locally free of degree `d` over
the limit, then its base change to `D.obj i` is finite locally free of degree `d` over `D.obj i`
for some later stage `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_overPullbackObj_of_isLimit
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I) (Z : Over (D.obj i₀))
    (hZ : FinitePresentation Z.hom) (d : ℕ)
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).obj Z).hom d] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).obj Z).hom d
declarations.comment: the fixed-degree refinement, for a morphism whose target is the stage itself

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isAffine_of_isThickening_of_surjective_appTop
declarations.doc:
**A thickening of an affine scheme whose map on global sections is surjective has affine
ambient scheme.**  This is [Stacks Project, Tag 06AD] with its cohomological content — the
surjectivity of `i.appTop` — as the explicit hypothesis `hsurj`, which is the only thing assumed:
everything else in the tag is proved here, through the affineness criterion of
[Stacks Project, Tag 01QF].  The hypothesis is not needed for the tag itself: it is dropped in
`Stacks.Thickenings.isAffine_of_isThickening`, which proves Tag 06AD outright from
[Stacks Project, Tag 01ZT].
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isThickening_of_surjective_appTop [IsAffine X] {i : X ⟶ X'}
    (hi : IsThickening i) (hsurj : Function.Surjective i.appTop.hom) : IsAffine X'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isAffine_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Any finite-order thickening of an affine scheme is affine.** The adic filtration of the
defining ideal sheaf interpolates between the closed subscheme and the ambient scheme by
first-order thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isFiniteOrderThickening {i : X ⟶ X'} (hi : IsFiniteOrderThickening i)
    [IsAffine X] : IsAffine X'
declarations.comment: the finite-order case, the second proof the source gives (EGA I, Prop 5.1.9)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isAffine_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
**A thickening of an affine scheme is affine.** A closed immersion is a finite morphism, and
a thickening is surjective, so this is the affineness of the target of a finite surjective
morphism with affine source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isThickening {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {i : X ⟶ X'} (hi : IsThickening i)
    [IsAffine X] : IsAffine X'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityMap
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `Z' ⟶ Y'` of part (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE].** For a universal
first-order thickening `Z ⊂ Z'` of `Z` over `X` and one `Y ⊂ Y'` of `Y` over `X`, this is the
canonical morphism of [Stacks Project, Tag 04F7] for the square over `X` with vertical maps `i`
and `𝟙 X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def transitivityMap (tZ : UniversalFirstOrderThickening (i ≫ p))
    (tY : UniversalFirstOrderThickening p) : tZ.ambient ⟶ tY.ambient

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isUniversal_relative
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE].** Let `Z --i--→ Y --p--→ X` be morphisms of
schemes, let `Z ⊂ Z'` be a universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `X` and `Y ⊂ Y'` one of
`Y` over `X`. Then the fibre product `Y ×_{Y'} Z'` along the morphism
`Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityMap` is a universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversal_relative :
    IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening i (relativeInclusion i p tZ tY)
      (relativeToBase i p tZ tY)
declarations.comment: part (1): Y ×_{Y'} Z' is the universal first-order thickening of Z over Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityConormalLeftMap
declarations.doc:
**The first arrow `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of the conormal sequence of part (2) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 06AE].** It is the canonical map of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] for the
square of inclusions with vertical maps `i` and the morphism `Z' ⟶ Y'` of
`Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityMap`.
declarations.statement:
def transitivityConormalLeftMap :
    (modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (conormalSheaf tY.inclusion.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom) ⟶
      conormalSheaf tZ.inclusion.liftCoborder.toLRSHom.toShHom
declarations.comment: part (2): the first arrow i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityConormalRightMap
declarations.doc:
**The second arrow `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of the conormal sequence of part (2) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 06AE].** It is the canonical map of [Stacks Project, Tag 01R4] for the
square of inclusions with vertical maps `𝟙 Z` and the projection `Y ×_{Y'} Z' ⟶ Z'`, read
through the identification of pullback along the identity with the identity functor.
declarations.comment: part (2): the second arrow 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.epi_transitivityConormalRightMap
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE], exactness at `𝒞_{Z/Y}`.** The second arrow
`𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of the conormal sequence is an epimorphism, which is the `⟶ 0` at the
right-hand end of the canonical sequence `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_transitivityConormalRightMap :
    Epi (transitivityConormalRightMap i p tZ tY)
declarations.comment: part (2): exactness at the right term

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityConormalLeftMap_comp_rightMap
declarations.doc:
**The two arrows of the conormal sequence of part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE] compose
to zero.**
declarations.statement:
theorem transitivityConormalLeftMap_comp_rightMap :
    transitivityConormalLeftMap i p tZ tY ≫ transitivityConormalRightMap i p tZ tY = 0
declarations.comment: part (2): the two arrows of the sequence compose to zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityConormalShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**The conormal sequence of part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE]** as a two-term complex of
`𝒪_Z`-modules, `i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}`.
declarations.statement:
def transitivityConormalShortComplex :
    ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
declarations.comment: part (2): the sequence as a short complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityConormalShortComplex_exact
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE], exactness at `𝒞_{Z/X}`.** The conormal sequence
`i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` is exact at its middle term; with
`Stacks.Thickenings.epi_transitivityConormalRightMap` this makes
`i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem transitivityConormalShortComplex_exact :
    (transitivityConormalShortComplex i p tZ tY).Exact
declarations.comment: part (2): exactness at the middle term

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_flat_reduction
declarations.doc:
Flatness of a morphism lifts from its reduction over a finite-order
thickening when its source is flat over the thickened base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_flat_reduction
    (hiX : IsThickening iX)
    (hiY : IsThickening iY)
    (hiS : IsFiniteOrderThickening iS)
    (hX : IsPullback iX pX pX' iS)
    (hY : IsPullback iY pY pY' iS)
    (hf : iX ≫ f' = f ≫ iY)
    (hfbase : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hf'base : f' ≫ pY' = pX')
    (hflatX' : Flat pX') (hflatf : Flat f) : Flat f'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flatAt_target_of_flat_reduction
declarations.doc:
The thickened target is flat over the thickened base at every point in
the image of the upper morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flatAt_target_of_flat_reduction
    (hiX : IsThickening iX)
    (hiY : IsThickening iY)
    (hiS : IsFiniteOrderThickening iS)
    (hX : IsPullback iX pX pX' iS)
    (hY : IsPullback iY pY pY' iS)
    (hf : iX ≫ f' = f ≫ iY)
    (hfbase : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hf'base : f' ≫ pY' = pX')
    (hflatX' : Flat pX') (hflatf : Flat f)
    (x' : X') : IsFlatAt pY'.toLRSHom.toShHom (f' x')
declarations.comment: flatness of the upper target along the image

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff
declarations.doc:
Local finite presentation is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation when the
enlarged source is flat over the enlarged base.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff
    (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f ↔ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.locallyOfFiniteType_iff
declarations.doc: Local finite type is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFiniteType_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType D.f ↔ LocallyOfFiniteType D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.locallyQuasiFinite_iff
declarations.doc:
Local quasi-finiteness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation with flat
enlarged source.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    (LocallyOfFiniteType D.f ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite D.f) ↔
      (LocallyOfFiniteType D.f' ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite D.f')

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isProper_iff
declarations.doc: Properness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_iff (d : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    IsProper d.f ↔ IsProper d.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isAffineHom_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, affine case.** Affineness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    IsAffineHom D.f ↔ IsAffineHom D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isIntegralHom_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, integral case.** Integrality is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source: it is universal closedness together with affineness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    IsIntegralHom D.f ↔ IsIntegralHom D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isFinite_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, finite case.** Finiteness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source: it is integrality together with local finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    IsFinite D.f ↔ IsFinite D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.etale_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, étale case.** Étaleness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.etale_iff
    (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) : Etale D.f ↔ Etale D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian finite-order deformation diagram, `f` is finite, flat and locally of finite
presentation if and only if `f'` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    (IsFinite D.f ∧ Flat D.f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f) ↔
      (IsFinite D.f' ∧ Flat D.f' ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f')

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian finite-order deformation diagram, `f` is finite locally free of rank `d` if and
only if `f'` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u})
    (d : ℕ) :
    (IsFinite D.f ∧ Flat D.f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f ∧
        ∀ y : D.Y, D.f.finrank y = d) ↔
      (IsFinite D.f' ∧ Flat D.f' ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f' ∧
        ∀ y' : D.Y', D.f'.finrank y' = d)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.flat_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, flat case.** Flatness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation
with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.flat_iff
    (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) : Flat D.f ↔ Flat D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isOpenImmersion_iff
declarations.doc:
Being an open immersion is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation with flat
ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    IsOpenImmersion D.f ↔ IsOpenImmersion D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.isIso_iff
declarations.doc:
Being an isomorphism is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation with flat ambient
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    IsIso D.f ↔ IsIso D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.mono_iff
declarations.doc:
Being a monomorphism is invariant under a cartesian finite-order deformation with flat ambient
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    Mono D.f ↔ Mono D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.relativeDimension_iff
declarations.doc:
Being locally of finite type of relative dimension `d` is invariant under a cartesian
finite-order deformation with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimension_iff (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) (d : ℕ) :
    (∃ _ : LocallyOfFiniteType D.f, RelativeDimension D.f d) ↔
      (∃ _ : LocallyOfFiniteType D.f', RelativeDimension D.f' d)

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.smooth_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, smooth case.** Smoothness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.smooth_iff
    (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) : Smooth D.f ↔ Smooth D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.syntomic_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, syntomic case.** Syntomicity is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.syntomic_iff
    (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) : Syntomic D.f ↔ Syntomic D.f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.unramified_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06AG, unramified case.** Unramifiedness is invariant under a cartesian finite-order
deformation with flat ambient source.
declarations.statement:
theorem CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.unramified_iff
    (D : CartesianFiniteOrderDeformationDiagram.{u}) : Unramified D.f ↔ Unramified D.f'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyProjective_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06B5.** The sheaf of relative differentials of a formally smooth morphism of
schemes is locally projective on its source. This is **Stacks 061I** for a morphism of
algebraic spaces that is a morphism of schemes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toRelativeDifferentials_shortExact
declarations.doc:
For morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ S` with `f` formally smooth, the canonical
sequence `0 ⟶ f^* Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` of `𝒪_X`-modules is short exact. The case of a
smooth `f` is the special case obtained from
`Stacks.Smooth.smooth_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_formallySmooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toRelativeDifferentials_shortExact (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) (hf : FormallySmooth f) :
    ∃ h : relativeDifferentialsMap f g (f ≫ g) (𝟙 S) (Category.comp_id (f ≫ g)).symm ≫
        f.toRelativeDifferentials g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.UnramifiedConormalSequence.exists_localRetraction_of_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
**A local left inverse `Z' ⟶ Z` over `S`, from formal smoothness of `Z` over `S`.** Let
`i : Z ⟶ Z'` with structure morphism `h' : Z' ⟶ X` be a universal first-order thickening of
`h : Z ⟶ X`, let `p : X ⟶ S`, and assume `Z` is formally smooth over `S`, that is
`h ≫ p : Z ⟶ S` has the lifting property of [Stacks, Tag 02H0]. Then every point `z` of `Z` has
an open neighbourhood `V` and an open `W ⊆ Z'` such that `i` restricts to `j : V ⟶ W` and `j`
admits a left inverse `g : W ⟶ V` over `S`.

This is the step of the proof of [Stacks, Tag 06B7] reading "by formal smoothness of `Z` over `S`
there exists, after replacing `Z'` by an open neighbourhood, a left inverse `Z' ⟶ Z` over `S`".
`V` is any affine open neighbourhood of `z` and `W` is the open of `Z'` attached to it by
`Stacks.Thickenings.UniversalFirstOrderThickening.ambientOpens`, which is affine because
`V ⟶ W` is a first-order thickening of `V`; the lifting property applies to that affine
first-order thickening, and the resulting lift `W ⟶ Z` factors through `V` because `V ⟶ W` is
surjective on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_localRetraction_of_formallySmooth {Z' : Scheme.{u}} {h : Z ⟶ X} {i : Z ⟶ Z'}
    {h' : Z' ⟶ X} (hi : Stacks.Thickenings.IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening h i h') (p : X ⟶ S)
    (hZ : FormallySmooth (h ≫ p)) (z : Z) :
    ∃ (V : Z.Opens) (W : Z'.Opens) (j : V.toScheme ⟶ W.toScheme)
      (g : W.toScheme ⟶ V.toScheme), z ∈ V ∧ V.ι ≫ i = j ≫ W.ι ∧
        j ≫ g = 𝟙 V.toScheme ∧ g ≫ (V.ι ≫ (h ≫ p)) = W.ι ≫ (h' ≫ p)
declarations.comment:
the step of the proof using formal smoothness of Z over S: locally on the
universal first-order thickening Z' there is a left inverse Z' ⟶ Z over S

declarations.name: Stacks.UnramifiedConormalSequence.forall_exists_isSplitEpi_restrict_relativeDifferentialsMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06B7]: the conormal sequence of a formally unramified morphism with formally
smooth source is locally split.** Let `h : Z ⟶ X` be formally unramified, let `p : X ⟶ S`, and
assume `Z` is formally smooth over `S`. Then the second arrow `h^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S}` of the
sequence of [Stacks, Tag 04FC] — the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 01UV] — restricts to a *split*
epimorphism on a neighbourhood of every point of `Z`.

A split epimorphism being an epimorphism, this contains local surjectivity of that arrow, which
[Stacks, Tag 01UZ] supplies only for a morphism surjective on stalks; splitness is what formal
smoothness buys, and it is the source's "hence the sequence is locally split". Left exactness of
the sequence, which is the assertion of the tag, is not proved here; it is
`Stacks.UnramifiedConormalSequence.conormalShortComplex_shortExact` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.MoreMorphisms.FormallySmooth.UnramifiedConormalShortExact`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_exists_isSplitEpi_restrict_relativeDifferentialsMap (h : Z ⟶ X)
    [FormallyUnramified h] (p : X ⟶ S) (hZ : FormallySmooth (h ≫ p)) (z : Z) :
    ∃ V : Z.Opens, z ∈ V ∧ IsSplitEpi ((Scheme.Modules.pullback V.ι).map
      (relativeDifferentialsMap h p (h ≫ p) (𝟙 S)
        (show h ≫ p = (h ≫ p) ≫ 𝟙 S by simp)))
declarations.comment:
the conclusion of the source's proof before Tag 0474 is invoked: the sequence is
locally split, i.e. the second arrow h^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} restricts to a split epimorphism on a
neighbourhood of every point of Z. Left exactness, the assertion of the tag, is not this
declaration: it is conormalShortComplex_shortExact of
StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.MoreMorphisms.FormallySmooth.UnramifiedConormalShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.UnramifiedConormalSequence.conormalShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `h : Z ⟶ X` be a formally unramified morphism of schemes over `p : X ⟶ S` and assume
`Z` is formally smooth over `S`. Then the canonical sequence

```
0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ h^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0
```

is short exact: the first arrow is a monomorphism, the sequence is exact at `h^*Ω_{X/S}`, and the
second arrow is an epimorphism. Here `𝒞_{Z/X}` is the conormal sheaf of the inclusion of `Z`
into the universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalShortComplex_shortExact
    (hZ : AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth (h ≫ p)) :
    (conormalShortComplex h p).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_koszulAt
declarations.doc:
**The Koszul locus is open.** A witness for `KoszulAt f x` — an open `U ∋ x` on which `f`
factors through a Koszul-regular immersion into a scheme smooth over the target — witnesses
`KoszulAt f z` for every `z` in `U`, because Koszul-regularity is a condition on the immersion
and not on the point. Intersecting `U` with the affine open witnessing finite type at `x` gives
a neighbourhood of `x` inside the locus.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_koszulAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsOpen {x : X | KoszulAt f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.koszulAt_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
**The formation of the Koszul locus commutes with arbitrary base change.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y`
be a morphism of schemes over `S` with `X` and `Y` both flat and locally of finite presentation
over `S`. For any `g : S' ⟶ S`, the base change of `f` is Koszul at a point of `X ×_S S'`
exactly when `f` is Koszul at its image in `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem koszulAt_baseChange_iff {X Y S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : X ⟶ S)
    (q : Y ⟶ S) (h : f ≫ q = p) [Flat p] [Flat q] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation q] (g : S' ⟶ S) (x' : (pullback p g : Scheme.{u})) :
    KoszulAt (pullback.map p g q g f (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _)
        (by simpa only [Category.comp_id] using h.symm) (by simp)) x' ↔
      KoszulAt f ((pullback.fst p g).base x')
declarations.comment: formation of the Koszul locus commutes with arbitrary base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramified_iff_formallyUnramified_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
A local complete intersection morphism of schemes is unramified if and only if it is
formally unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramified_iff_formallyUnramified_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    Unramified f ↔ FormallyUnramified f
declarations.comment:
the equivalence: a local complete intersection morphism is unramified if and
only if it is formally unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFree_universalConormalSheaf_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
The conormal sheaf of a formally unramified local complete intersection morphism of schemes
is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_universalConormalSheaf_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [FormallyUnramified f]
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (universalConormalSheaf f)
declarations.comment:
finite local freeness of the conormal sheaf of a local complete intersection
morphism. Tag 063H is NOT needed: the Koszul-regular factor is quasi-regular, and condition (2)
of Tag 063M is available for those

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.mono_transitivityConormalLeftMap
declarations.doc:
**The first arrow of the conormal sequence of part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE] is a
monomorphism** when `Z ⟶ Y` is a local complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_transitivityConormalLeftMap (hi : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism i) :
    Mono (transitivityConormalLeftMap i p tZ tY)
declarations.comment: the left arrow of the sequence of Stacks 06AE is a monomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.transitivityConormalShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `Z --i--→ Y --p--→ X` be morphisms of schemes with universal first-order thickenings
`Z ⊂ Z'` of `Z` over `X` and `Y ⊂ Y'` of `Y` over `X`, and assume `i` is a local complete
intersection morphism. Then the conormal sequence
```
0 ⟶ i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0
```
of part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 06AE] is **short exact**: its left arrow is a monomorphism,
it is exact at the middle term, and its right arrow is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem transitivityConormalShortComplex_shortExact
    (hi : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism i) :
    (transitivityConormalShortComplex i p tZ tY).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the conormal sequence of Stacks 06AE is short exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyLimitPreserving_iff_affineLimit_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The affine-limit comparison square characterizes relative limit
preservation of a transformation of presheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyLimitPreserving_iff_affineLimit_isPullback
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
    (a : F ⟶ G) :
    RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, v, max w w', w'} B S hS a ↔
      ∀ (I : Type (max w w')) [Category.{w'} I] [IsCofiltered I]
        (D : I ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (c : Cone D),
        IsLimit ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).mapCone c) →
        (∀ i, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i))) →
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj c.pt) →
          let U := CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.{max w w', v}
          let F' := F ⋙ U
          let G' := G ⋙ U
          IsPullback
            (colimit.desc (D.op ⋙ F') (F'.mapCocone c.op))
            (colimMap (Functor.whiskerLeft D.op (Functor.whiskerRight a U)))
            (U.map (a.app (Opposite.op c.pt)))
            (colimit.desc (D.op ⋙ G') (G'.mapCocone c.op))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap_closedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**Exactness at the right term of [Stacks Project, Tag 06BD].**  Let `Y` and `Z` be closed
subspaces of an algebraic space `X` with `Z ⊆ Y`.  The canonical map `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04CP], the right-hand map of the conormal sequence of the pair, is an
epimorphism.

This is the surjectivity clause of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CQ] at the fibre product square whose
morphism of ambient spaces is the inclusion `j : Y ⟶ X`: the inverse image `j⁻¹(Z)` is `Z` read
as a closed subspace of `Y`, and `𝒞_{Z/Y}` is its conormal module there.  The subspace of `Y` is
taken as that inverse image rather than as `Z` itself because this development has no
composition of closed subspaces, so no closed subspace of `Y` is attached to `Z` by any other
route.  The hypothesis `Z ⊆ Y` is what makes that inverse image the subspace the source calls
`Z`, and it is carried for that reason alone: the proof is the instance of Stacks 04CQ, which
holds for any pair, so the hypothesis is not used and its name is prefixed accordingly.

The exactness in the middle is not proved; see the "What is not proved" section of this file,
which also names the composite-is-zero clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalMap_closedSubspaces (Y Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (_hZY : Z.1 ≤ Y.1) :
    Epi (conormalMap B S hS
      (preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z) Z
      (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y)
      (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)
      (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_closedSubspaces_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The composite-is-zero clause of [Stacks Project, Tag 06BD].**  Let `Y` and `Z` be closed
subspaces of an algebraic space `X` with `Z` contained in `Y` through `f : Z ⟶ Y`.  The composite
of the two maps `i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of the conormal sequence of the pair is zero,
so that the sequence is a complex; together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap_closedSubspaces` this makes it a complex, exact at its
right term.

Both maps are maps of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CP], the left one at the square of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspacesConormal_square` and the right one at the fibre product
square of the inclusion `j : Y ⟶ X`.  By part (3) of [Stacks Project, Tag 04G2] their composite
is the conormal map of the outer rectangle, whose morphism of ambient spaces is `j ≫ 𝟙 X = j`;
that factors through the inclusion of `Y`, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_conormalMap_eq_zero_of_factors` applies.

Exactness in the middle is not proved; see the "What is not proved" section of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ConormalModuleBaseChangeEpi.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_closedSubspaces_eq_zero
    (hf : f ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y = subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z) :
    (modulePullback B S hS
          (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)).map
        (conormalMap B S hS Z Y (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X) f
          (closedSubspacesConormal_square B S hS Y Z f hf)) ≫
      conormalMap B S hS
        (preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z) Z
        (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y)
        (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)
        (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z) = 0
declarations.comment: the sequence is a complex: the composite of i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} and 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} is zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceImmersion_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 06BD].**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of algebraic
spaces over `S`.  The canonical sequence of `𝒪_Z`-modules

`i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0`

of the conormal modules of Stacks 04CN, with the maps of Stacks 04CP
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceImmersionFirstMap` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequenceImmersionSecondMap`), is exact: the two maps compose to
zero, the resulting short complex is exact, and the second map is an epimorphism.

It is isomorphic to the sequence `i^*c^*Ker(c^♯) ⟶ (i ≫ c)^*Ker((i ≫ c)^♯) ⟶ i^*Ker(i^♯) ⟶ 0` of
the closed factorisation `c : Y ⟶ X ∖ ∂Y` of `j`, which is exact by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelConormalSequenceShortComplex_exact`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequenceImmersion_exact :
    ∃ h : conormalSequenceImmersionFirstMap B S hS hX hY hZ i j hi hj ≫
        conormalSequenceImmersionSecondMap B S hS hX hY hZ i j hi hj = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).Exact ∧
        Epi (conormalSequenceImmersionSecondMap B S hS hX hY hZ i j hi hj)
declarations.comment: the canonical exact sequence i^*C_{Y/X} → C_{Z/X} → C_{Z/Y} → 0 for immersions Z → Y → X of algebraic spaces, with the maps of Tag 04CP: the composite is zero, the sequence is exact at C_{Z/X}, and C_{Z/X} → C_{Z/Y} is an epimorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The vanishing of the composite in Stacks 06BD.**  Let `Y` and `Z` be closed subspaces of
an algebraic space `X` with `Z ⊆ Y`, let `j : Y ⟶ X` be the inclusion and let `p : j⁻¹(Z) ⟶ Z`
be the projection.  The two arrows of the conormal sequence of the pair,

`p^*(i^*𝒞_{Y/X}) ⟶ p^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{j⁻¹(Z)/Y}`,

compose to zero.  The first is the inverse image along `p` of the map of [Stacks Project,
Tag 04CP] at the square of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subspaceInclusion_homOfLe_square`, the
second is the map of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CP] at the inverse-image square, whose surjectivity
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap_closedSubspaces`.

By the composition law of part (3) of [Stacks Project, Tag 04G2],
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp`, the composite is the map of [Stacks Project,
Tag 04CP] attached to the outer rectangle, read through the composition comparison of
[Stacks Project, Tag 03LU], which is an isomorphism.  The lower edge of that rectangle is
`j ≫ 𝟙 X = j`, which factors through `Y` by the identity of `Y`, so the map of the outer
rectangle vanishes by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_eq_zero_of_factorization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (Y Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hZY : Z.1 ≤ Y.1) :
    (modulePullback B S hS
          (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)).map
        (conormalMap B S hS Z Y (𝟙 X)
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (Subfunctor.homOfLe hZY))
          (subspaceInclusion_homOfLe_square B S hS Y Z hZY)) ≫
      conormalMap B S hS (preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z) Z
        (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y)
        (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)
        (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z) = 0
declarations.comment: the vanishing of the composite of the two maps of the sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_conormalShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Exactness in the middle of [Stacks Project, Tag 06BD].**  Let `Y` and `Z` be closed
subspaces of an algebraic space `X` with `Z ⊆ Y`, let `j : Y ⟶ X` be the inclusion and let
`p : j⁻¹(Z) ⟶ Z` be the projection.  The conormal sequence of the pair,

`p^*(i^*𝒞_{Y/X}) ⟶ p^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{j⁻¹(Z)/Y}`,

is exact in the middle.

The sequence is the inverse image along `j`, and then along the inclusion of `j⁻¹(Z)`, of the
sequence of defining ideal sheaves `(𝟙 X)^*𝓘_Y ⟶ 𝓘_Z ⟶ j_*𝓘_{j⁻¹(Z)}`, which is exact in the
middle and whose second map is an epimorphism, so exactness in the middle survives both inverse
images (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_map_idealSheafSequence`, written out as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_mk_map_idealSheafSequence`).  The identification of the two
sequences is the pair of squares
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_comparison_square₁₂` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalSequence_comparison_square₂₃`, whose vertical maps are
isomorphisms — the inverse image along `p` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalPullbackComparison` followed by a component of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalPullbackCompIso`, that component at the defining ideal sheaf of
`Z`, and the identity — and the transport along them is
`CategoryTheory.Limits.exact_mk_of_squares`.

The companion clauses of the tag are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero`, which says that the two arrows
compose to zero, and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap_closedSubspaces`, which says the
second is an epimorphism; with this clause the tag carries all three.

The source and target of the inverse-image functor along `p` are supplied explicitly, as the
projections of the two subspaces, and the vanishing is taken from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero_chain` rather than from the
clause-one instance; the implementation notes record why.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_conormalShortComplex :
    (ShortComplex.mk
      ((@modulePullback B S hS
          (⟨(preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z).1.toFunctor,
              (preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z).2.1⟩ :
            AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
          (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
          (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)).map
        (conormalMap B S hS Z Y (𝟙 X) (ObjectProperty.homMk (Subfunctor.homOfLe hZY))
          (subspaceInclusion_homOfLe_square B S hS Y Z hZY)))
      (conormalMap B S hS (preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z) Z
        (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y)
        (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)
        (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z))
      (conormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero_chain B S hS Y Z hZY
        (preimageSubspace B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)
        (preimageProjection B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z)
        (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Y) Z))).Exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_conormalPairSequence_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BE.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` be formally unramified morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S` with `i ≫ g = j`, presented by universal first-order thickenings
`ti` of `i` and `tj` of `j`.  Then the canonical sequence

```
  𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0
```

is exact: the composite of the two arrows is zero, the sequence is exact at `𝒞_{Z/X}`, and the
second arrow is an epimorphism.  The first arrow is the map of conormal modules of Stacks 060A
attached to the canonical morphism `Z' ⟶ Z''` of the two thickenings, written as the conormal map
of Stacks 04CP of its square of closed subspaces; the second is the canonical first arrow of
Stacks 060F.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_conormalPairSequence_exact (g : X ⟶ Y) {i : Z ⟶ X} {j : Z ⟶ Y}
    (hij : i ≫ g = j) (ti : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS i)
    (tj : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS j) :
    ∃ hc : conormalMap B S hS (thickeningClosedSubspace B S hS ti.isUniversal)
          (thickeningClosedSubspace B S hS tj.isUniversal)
          (universalThickeningComparison B S hS g hij ti tj)
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (universalThickeningSourceMap B S hS ti tj))
          (universalThickeningComparison_square B S hS g hij ti tj) ≫
        thickeningConormalFirstMap B S hS ti.isUniversal g
          (ti.isUniversal.isIso_thickeningSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS g) = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ hc).Exact ∧
        Epi (thickeningConormalFirstMap B S hS ti.isUniversal g
          (ti.isUniversal.isIso_thickeningSheafOfDifferentialsMap B S hS g))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompConormalSequence_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The composite of the two arrows of the conormal sequence of the composition vanishes.**
By the composition law of part (3) of Stacks 04G2,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_comp`, the composite is the map of Stacks 04CP attached to
the outer rectangle, read through the composition comparison of Stacks 03LU, which is an
isomorphism.  The lower edge of that rectangle is the inclusion of the fibre product
`Y ×_{Y'} Z'` into `Z'` followed by the morphism `h : Z' ⟶ Y'` of clause (1) of Stacks 06BF, and
that composite factors through the closed subspace `Y ⊆ Y'` by the structure morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompStructure` of the fibre product — which is what
makes the fibre product a fibre product.  So the map of the outer rectangle vanishes by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap_eq_zero_of_factorization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universalThickeningCompConormalSequence_comp_eq_zero :
    modulePullbackMap B S hS
          (preimageProjection B S hS
            (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
            ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩)
          (universalThickeningCompConormalLowerMap B S hS i hZ hY hfac) ≫
      universalThickeningCompConormalRightMap B S hS i hZ hY hfac = 0
declarations.comment: clause (2): the composite of the two maps of the sequence vanishes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_universalThickeningCompConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**Exactness at `𝒞_{Z/X}` of the conormal sequence of the composition** — the middle clause of
Stacks 06BD in this presentation.  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_conormalShortComplex_preimage`
is that clause for a closed subspace inside the inverse image of a closed subspace downstairs,
which is what the fibre product `Y ×_{Y'} Z'` presents; its four comparison arguments are
discharged by the structural equations above, each of them an equation of single arrows.

With `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompConormalSequence_comp_eq_zero` above, which
supplies the vanishing the short complex is formed from, this is the middle-exactness assertion
of clause (2) of Stacks 06BF; the companion clauses of that tag are registered in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/UniversalThickeningComposition.lean`.
declarations.comment: clause (2): exactness at the middle term

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BF, clause (1), the morphism `Z' ⟶ Y'`.**  Let `Z ⊂ Z'` be a universal
first-order thickening of `Z` over `X` and let `Y ⊂ Y'` be a universal first-order thickening of
`Y` over `X`, and let the structure morphism of `Z` factor through `Y`.  The morphism
`h : Z' ⟶ Y'` is the canonical morphism of Stacks 060A for the square with `g = 𝟙 X`, that is
the unique morphism restricting to `i : Z ⟶ Y` and lying over `X`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def universalThickeningCompMap : Z' ⟶ Y'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversalFirstOrderThickening_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BF, clause (1), the universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `Y`.**  With the
morphism `h : Z' ⟶ Y'` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompMap`, the fibre
product `Y ×_{Y'} Z'` is a universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `Y`, with structure
morphism the projection to `Y`.

A morphism `T' ⟶ Y ×_{Y'} Z'` is a pair of morphisms to `Y` and to `Z'` agreeing over `Y'`.
Given a solid diagram over `Y` built from a first-order thickening `T ⊂ T'` and a morphism
`T ⟶ Z`, the morphism to `Y` is the one the diagram supplies and the morphism `e : T' ⟶ Z'` is
the unique one furnished by the universal property of `Z ⊂ Z'` over `X`.  That the two agree
over `Y'` is uniqueness in the universal property of `Y ⊂ Y'`: both composites restrict to
`Z ⟶ Y` on `T` and lie over `X`, the first because `h` restricts to `i` and lies over `X`.
Uniqueness of the resulting morphism is uniqueness of `e` together with the fact that the
inclusion of the fibre product into `Z'` is a monomorphism.

That the copy of `Z` is a first-order thickening of `Y ×_{Y'} Z'` is a hypothesis; see the
implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversalFirstOrderThickening_comp
    (hfirst : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS
      (universalThickeningCompFibre B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
      (universalThickeningCompSub B S hS i hZ hY hfac)) :
    IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS
      (universalThickeningCompSub B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
      (universalThickeningCompStructure B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
declarations.comment: clause (1): Y ×_{Y'} Z' is the universal first-order thickening of Z over Y, the square-zero condition inside the fibre product being hypothesised

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BF, clause (2), at the right term.**  The canonical map
`𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of Stacks 04CP — the right-hand map of the conormal sequence of the
composition — is surjective.

By Stacks 0607 the conormal module of a formally unramified morphism is the conormal module of
its source inside its universal first-order thickening, so `𝒞_{Z/X}` is the conormal module of
`Z` in `Z'` and, by clause (1), `𝒞_{Z/Y}` is the conormal module of the copy of `Z` inside
`Y ×_{Y'} Z'`.  The map between them is the one of Stacks 04CP for the inclusion
`Y ×_{Y'} Z' ⟶ Z'`, and surjectivity is the surjectivity clause of Stacks 04CQ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalMap`, for that inverse-image configuration.

The left-hand map of the sequence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningConormalMap`
for the square of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningComp_square`; exactness in the
middle is not proved, see the "What is not proved" section of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalMap_comp :
    Epi (conormalMap B S hS
      (preimageSubspace B S hS
        (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
        ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩)
      ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩
      (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
      (preimageProjection B S hS
        (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
        ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩)
      (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS
        (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
        ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩))
declarations.comment: clause (2): exactness at the right term, the canonical map 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} being surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversalFirstOrderThickening_comp'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BF, clause (1), the universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `Y`.**  With the
morphism `h : Z' ⟶ Y'` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompMap`, the fibre
product `Y ×_{Y'} Z'` is a universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `Y`, with structure
morphism the projection to `Y`.

A morphism `T' ⟶ Y ×_{Y'} Z'` is a pair of morphisms to `Y` and to `Z'` agreeing over `Y'`.
Given a solid diagram over `Y` built from a first-order thickening `T ⊂ T'` and a morphism
`T ⟶ Z`, the morphism to `Y` is the one the diagram supplies and the morphism `e : T' ⟶ Z'` is
the unique one furnished by the universal property of `Z ⊂ Z'` over `X`.  That the two agree
over `Y'` is uniqueness in the universal property of `Y ⊂ Y'`: both composites restrict to
`Z ⟶ Y` on `T` and lie over `X`, the first because `h` restricts to `i` and lies over `X`.
Uniqueness of the resulting morphism is uniqueness of `e` together with the fact that the
inclusion of the fibre product into `Z'` is a monomorphism.

That the copy of `Z` is a first-order thickening of `Y ×_{Y'} Z'` needs nothing of the fibre
product: it is the inverse image of `Z ⊂ Z'` along the inclusion `Y ×_{Y'} Z' ⟶ Z'`, so it is
one by the inverse-image clause of Stacks 09ZX,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFirstOrderThickening_preimage`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversalFirstOrderThickening_comp' :
    IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS
      (universalThickeningCompSub B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
      (universalThickeningCompStructure B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
declarations.comment: clause (1): Y ×_{Y'} Z' is the universal first-order thickening of Z over Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningConormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BF, clause (2): the sequence is a complex.**  The composite of the two maps
`i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y}` of the conormal sequence of the composition is zero.

The left-hand map is the inverse image, along the projection of the copy of `Z` inside
`Y ×_{Y'} Z'`, of the canonical map of Stacks 060A at the square of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningComp_square`, and the right-hand map is the map of
Stacks 04CP for the inclusion `Y ×_{Y'} Z' ⟶ Z'`.  So the composite is the conormal map of the
outer rectangle of those two stacked squares, by part (3) of Stacks 04G2, and the ambient
morphism of that rectangle is `Y ×_{Y'} Z' ⟶ Z' ⟶ Y'`, which factors through the inclusion of
`Y` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion_comp_map`.  A conormal map
whose ambient morphism factors through the lower closed subspace is zero, the defining ideal of
that subspace being the kernel of the comorphism of its inclusion; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_conormalMap_eq_zero_of_factors`.

The left-hand map is written here as that map of Stacks 04CP rather than as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningConormalMap`; the two are the same morphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompConormalMap_eq`.  Writing it the second way makes
the statement one the kernel cannot check: the definitional comparison would then sit inside the
inverse image of modules and inside a composition, which is exactly what the implementation notes
of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ConormalModuleBaseChangeEpi.lean` record as beyond the
budget.

A consumer wanting the arrows of this sequence should take them from *this* theorem, as
`CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.f` and `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.g` of
`CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.mk _ _` applied to it, which is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompConormalSequence_shortExact'`, Stacks 06CC, does.
Crossing the two spellings by rewriting with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompConormalMap_eq` is *not* an available route once
the arrow sits under the inverse image of modules, and neither is naming either arrow in a
definition of its own — the section *How the sequence is written* of the file of that theorem
records what each of those costs.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalThickeningConormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero :
    (modulePullback B S hS
          (preimageProjection B S hS
            (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
            ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩)).map
        (conormalMap B S hS ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩
          ⟨Y, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hY.firstOrder).1⟩
          (universalThickeningCompMap B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
          (ObjectProperty.homMk i)
          (universalThickeningComp_subspace_square B S hS i hZ hY hfac)) ≫
      conormalMap B S hS
        (preimageSubspace B S hS
          (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
          ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩)
        ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩
        (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
        (preimageProjection B S hS
          (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
          ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩)
        (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS
          (universalThickeningCompFibreInclusion B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
          ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩) = 0
declarations.comment: clause (2): the sequence is a complex, the composite of i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} and 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} being zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_and_epi_universalThickeningCompConormalMapSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BF, clause (2).**  Let `Z ⟶ Y ⟶ X` be morphisms of algebraic spaces, `Z ⊂ Z'`
and `Y ⊂ Y'` universal first-order thickenings over `X`, and `h : Z' ⟶ Y'` the morphism of
clause (1).  The conormal sequence

`i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0`

is exact: exact at `𝒞_{Z/X}`, and its right-hand map is an epimorphism.  Here `𝒞_{Z/X}` is the
conormal module of `Z ⊂ Z'`, `𝒞_{Y/X}` that of `Y ⊂ Y'`, and `𝒞_{Z/Y}` that of the copy of `Z`
inside the universal first-order thickening `Y ×_{Y'} Z' = h⁻¹(Y)` of clause (1); the two maps
are those of Stacks 04CP, for the square of `Z ⊆ Z'` over `Y ⊆ Y'` with ambient morphism `h`
(pulled back to the copy of `Z`) and for the inclusion `h⁻¹(Y) ⟶ Z'`.  They are the arrows of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningConormalMap_comp_conormalMap_eq_zero`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningCompConormalSequence_f_eq` and `..._g_eq`.

Exactness in the middle is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_conormalMap_square` at that square;
the epimorphism is the surjectivity clause of Stacks 04CQ for the inclusion `h⁻¹(Y) ⟶ Z'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_and_epi_universalThickeningCompConormalMapSquare :
    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (conormalMap_square_comp_eq_zero B S hS
        (universalThickeningCompMap B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
        ⟨Y, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hY.firstOrder).1⟩
        ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩
        (ObjectProperty.homMk i)
        (universalThickeningComp_subspace_square B S hS i hZ hY hfac))).Exact ∧
      Epi (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (conormalMap_square_comp_eq_zero B S hS
        (universalThickeningCompMap B S hS i hZ hY hfac)
        ⟨Y, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hY.firstOrder).1⟩
        ⟨Z, (IsNthOrderThickening.isThickening B S hS hZ.firstOrder).1⟩
        (ObjectProperty.homMk i)
        (universalThickeningComp_subspace_square B S hS i hZ hY hfac))).g
declarations.comment: clause (2): the conormal sequence i^*𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0 is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalMap_firstOrderThickening_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
Let `(f, f') : (X ⊆ X') → (Y ⊆ Y')` be a morphism of first-order thickenings of algebraic
spaces in which `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`, that is in which the upper closed subspace is the inverse image
`g⁻¹(Y)` of the lower one along `g = f'` and `f` is the projection. If `f'` is flat, as a morphism
of small étale ringed topoi, then the canonical map of conormal modules `f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}`
is an isomorphism. The first-order thickening conditions on `Y ⊆ Y'` and on `g⁻¹(Y) ⊆ X'` are
taken as hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalMap_firstOrderThickening_of_isFlat
    (_hY : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Y' Y.1)
    (_hX : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X' (preimageSubspace B S hS g Y).1)
    (hg : (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g).IsFlat) :
    IsIso (conormalMap B S hS (preimageSubspace B S hS g Y) Y g
      (preimageProjection B S hS g Y)
      (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS g Y))
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2), with f' flat as a morphism of small etale ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_and_isPullback_iff_isIso_conormalMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 06BH].**  Let `(f, f') : (X ⊆ X') → (Y ⊆ Y')` be a morphism of
first-order thickenings of algebraic spaces over `S` — `X ⊆ X'` and `Y ⊆ Y'` first-order
thickenings, `f' = g : X' ⟶ Y'` and `f : X ⟶ Y` with commuting square of inclusions — and let
`f` be flat.  Then the following are equivalent:

1. `f'` is flat and `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`;
2. the canonical map `f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CP] is an
   isomorphism.

Both flatness conditions are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat` of [Stacks Project, Tag 03ML],
`X = Y ×_{Y'} X'` is cartesianness of the square of inclusions, and the canonical map is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalMap`.  The first-order thickening hypotheses are used only in
(2) ⟹ (1), and so is the flatness of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isPullback_iff_isIso_conormalMap
    (hX : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X' X.1) (hY : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Y' Y.1)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) :
    (IsFlat B S hS g.hom ∧
        IsPullback (subspaceInclusion B S hS X' X) f g (subspaceInclusion B S hS Y' Y)) ↔
      IsIso (conormalMap B S hS X Y g f hsq)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_and_isPullback_iff_isIso_conormalMapOfImmersions
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 06BH].**  Let `(f, g) : (X ⊆ X') → (Y ⊆ Y')` be a morphism of
first-order thickenings of algebraic spaces over `S` (a commutative square of inclusions of
closed subspaces which are first-order thickenings, [Stacks Project, Tag 05ZK]), and assume
that `f` is flat.  Then the following are equivalent:

1. `g` is flat and `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'`;
2. the canonical map `f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CP] is an isomorphism.

Flatness is that of [Stacks Project, Tag 03ML], the equality `X = Y ×_{Y'} X'` is the square
being cartesian, and the canonical map is that of the two inclusions read as immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isPullback_iff_isIso_conormalMapOfImmersions
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion B S hS X' X ≫ g = f ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS Y' Y)
    (hX : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X' X.1) (hY : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS Y' Y.1)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) :
    (IsFlat B S hS g.hom ∧
        IsPullback (subspaceInclusion B S hS X' X) f g (subspaceInclusion B S hS Y' Y)) ↔
      IsIso (conormalMapOfImmersions B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X' X)
        (subspaceInclusion B S hS Y' Y) f g (isImmersion_subspaceInclusion B S hS X' X)
        (isImmersion_subspaceInclusion B S hS Y' Y) hsq)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangleDifferentials_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BI.** For morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `f` formally smooth, the transitivity sequence
`0 ⟶ f^*Ω_{Y/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/B} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` of Stacks 05Z8 is short exact.

Short exactness adds monomorphy of the first map to the three clauses of Stacks 05Z8, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDifferentialsMap_mono_of_formallySmooth` supplies it from the
case of schemes by étale localization, granted the chart comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleDifferentials_shortExact (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hf : FormallySmooth f.hom)
    (hchart : PullbackDifferentialsMapChartComparison B S hS f g) :
    ∃ h : pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS f g ≫ toRelativeDifferentials B S hS f g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
granted as `hchart` the étale localization of 04CU and 04CS identifying the
  restriction of the comparison map of Ω to a surjective étale chart with the chart morphisms'
  own comparison map of Ω

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangleDifferentials_shortExact_of_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BI.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `f` formally smooth.  Then the sequence `0 ⟶ f^*Ω_{Y/Z} ⟶ Ω_{X/Z} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` of
Stacks 05Z8 is short exact.

The first map is a monomorphism étale locally: on compatible étale charts `U ⟶ V ⟶ W` with
`U ⟶ V` formally smooth (Stacks 061K) it is the scheme statement (Stacks 02HP), carried to the
spaces by Stacks 04CU and 04CS
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDifferentialsMapSchemeSpaceComparison`); exactness at the other
two terms is Stacks 05Z8.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangleDifferentials_shortExact_of_formallySmooth (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : FormallySmooth f.hom) :
    ∃ h : pullbackDifferentialsMap B S hS f g ≫ toRelativeDifferentials B S hS f g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening.conormalSequence_shortExact_of_formallySmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BJ.**  Let `h = ι ≫ h' : Z ⟶ X` be a formally unramified morphism of algebraic
spaces over `Y`, with universal first order thickening `Z ⊂ Z'` over `X` given by `hZ`, and
assume `Z` is formally smooth over `Y`.  Then the canonical exact sequence
```
  0 ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ h^*Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ Ω_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0
```
of Stacks 060F, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening.conormalSequence`, is
short exact.

Exactness at the middle and the epimorphism on the right are Stacks 060F.  The first arrow
followed by the isomorphism of Stacks 060E is the first arrow of Stacks 05ZA for `Z ⊂ Z'`, which
is a monomorphism by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_conormalSequenceFirstMap_of_formallySmooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalSequence_shortExact_of_formallySmooth
    (hZ : IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS Z h') (p : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsm : FormallySmooth (universalThickeningInclusion B S hS hZ ≫ h' ≫ p).hom) :
    ShortComplex.ShortExact (C := Modules.{u, u} B S hS (universalThickeningSubSpace B S hS hZ).obj
      (universalThickeningSubSpace B S hS hZ).property) (hZ.conormalSequence B S hS p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_retraction_modulePullback_conormalMap_universalThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BK: the first arrow of the conormal sequence is étale-locally split.**  Let
`i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y` sit in a commutative triangle `i ≫ g = j` with `g` formally
smooth, let `Z ⊂ Z'` be a universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `X` and `Z ⊂ Z''` one of
`Z` over `Y`, and let `V ⟶ Z''` be an étale chart with `V` affine.  Then the inverse image
along the projection `Z ×_{Z''} V ⟶ Z` of the first arrow `𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of the conormal
sequence of [Stacks Project, Tag 06BE] admits a retraction.

The first arrow is named here through its definition: it is the conormal map of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04CP] for the square of [Stacks Project, Tag 060A] built from the canonical
morphism `Z' ⟶ Z''` and the identification of the two smaller spaces, which is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalThickeningConormalMap` abbreviates.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_modulePullback_conormalMap_universalThickening (g : X ⟶ Y)
    {i : Z ⟶ X} {j : Z ⟶ Y} (hij : i ≫ g = j)
    (ti : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS i)
    (tj : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS j) (hg : FormallySmooth g.hom)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (v : yoneda.obj V ⟶ tj.ambient.obj) (hv : IsEtale B S hS v)
    (hV : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) :
    ∃ r, (modulePullback B S hS (thickeningChartProjection B S hS ti tj V v)).map
        (@conormalMap B S hS ti.ambient tj.ambient ti.closedSub tj.closedSub
          (universalThickeningComparison B S hS g hij ti tj)
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (universalThickeningSourceMap B S hS ti tj))
          (universalThickeningComparison_square B S hS g hij ti tj)) ≫ r = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: the first arrow of the conormal sequence is split over an affine étale chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_retraction_cover_modulePullback_conormalMap_universalThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BK, in a covering form.**  Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_retraction_modulePullback_conormalMap_universalThickening`, an
arbitrary étale chart `V ⟶ Z''` is covered by affine étale charts over whose chart of `Z` the
first arrow of the conormal sequence admits a retraction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_cover_modulePullback_conormalMap_universalThickening (g : X ⟶ Y)
    {i : Z ⟶ X} {j : Z ⟶ Y} (hij : i ≫ g = j)
    (ti : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS i)
    (tj : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS j) (hg : FormallySmooth g.hom)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (v : yoneda.obj V ⟶ tj.ambient.obj) (hv : IsEtale B S hS v) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (V' : I → BigFppfOver B S hS) (π : ∀ k, V' k ⟶ V),
      Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows V' π) ∈ BigFppfOver.topology B S hS V ∧
        ∀ k, ∃ r, (modulePullback B S hS
              (thickeningChartProjection B S hS ti tj (V' k) (yoneda.map (π k) ≫ v))).map
            (@conormalMap B S hS ti.ambient tj.ambient ti.closedSub tj.closedSub
              (universalThickeningComparison B S hS g hij ti tj)
              (ObjectProperty.homMk (universalThickeningSourceMap B S hS ti tj))
              (universalThickeningComparison_square B S hS g hij ti tj)) ≫ r = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: the first arrow of the conormal sequence is split over a covering by affine étale charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_conormalMap_universalThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BK: the conormal sequence is exact on the left.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` and
`j : Z ⟶ Y` sit in a commutative triangle `i ≫ g = j` with `g` formally smooth, and let
`Z ⊂ Z'` be a universal first-order thickening of `Z` over `X` and `Z ⊂ Z''` one of `Z` over
`Y`.  Then the first arrow `𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}` of the conormal sequence of
[Stacks Project, Tag 06BE] is a monomorphism.

The first arrow is named through its definition, as the conormal map of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04CP] for the square of [Stacks Project, Tag 060A]; see the implementation
notes of this file.  It is split injective over each affine étale chart of `Z''` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_retraction_modulePullback_conormalMap_universalThickening`, and
the charts of `Z` cut out by the affine étale charts of an atlas of `Z''` form an étale covering
of `Z`, so the two inverse images of a pair of morphisms it equalises agree on that covering and
the pair is equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_conormalMap_universalThickening (g : X ⟶ Y) {i : Z ⟶ X} {j : Z ⟶ Y}
    (hij : i ≫ g = j) (ti : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS i)
    (tj : UniversalFirstOrderThickening B S hS j) (hg : FormallySmooth g.hom) :
    Mono (@conormalMap B S hS ti.ambient tj.ambient ti.closedSub tj.closedSub
      (universalThickeningComparison B S hS g hij ti tj)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (universalThickeningSourceMap B S hS ti tj))
      (universalThickeningComparison_square B S hS g hij ti tj))
declarations.comment: the conormal sequence is exact on the left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.property_on_all_etale_charts_iff_exists_atlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BM, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2).** For a property `P` of
scheme morphisms which is étale local on the target and a representable morphism `f` of
algebraic spaces over `S`, the projection of the represented fibre product has `P` over
every étale scheme chart of the target if and only if it has `P` over some surjective étale
chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_on_all_etale_charts_iff_exists_atlas (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.etalePrecoverage]
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    (∀ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q →
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (hf.snd q))) ↔
    (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q ∧
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (hf.snd q)))
declarations.comment: equivalence of all charts and one surjective chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.property_on_all_etale_charts_iff_of_schemes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BM, the comparison with the scheme-theoretic property.** When the source and
target of a representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` are representable, the
condition of Stacks 06BM on all étale charts holds exactly when the morphism of schemes
they represent has the property.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_on_all_etale_charts_iff_of_schemes (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.etalePrecoverage]
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} [X.IsRepresentable] [Y.IsRepresentable]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    (∀ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj W ⟶ Y),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q →
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (hf.snd q))) ↔
    P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
      (yoneda.preimage (X.reprW.hom ≫ f ≫ Y.reprW.inv)))
declarations.comment: comparison when both spaces are schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BN, part (1).** A representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a
*Koszul-regular immersion* when its base change to every étale scheme chart of the target
is a Koszul-regular immersion of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsKoszulRegularImmersion (i : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BN, part (2).** A representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is an
*`H₁`-regular immersion* when its base change to every étale scheme chart of the target is
an `H₁`-regular immersion of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsH1RegularImmersion (i : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BN, part (3).** A representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a
*quasi-regular immersion* when its base change to every étale scheme chart of the target is
a quasi-regular immersion of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiRegularImmersion (i : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 06BP, the first implication.**  A Koszul-regular immersion of algebraic spaces
over `S` is an `H₁`-regular immersion:  degree `1` is a positive degree, so the condition on each
étale chart becomes weaker.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_of_isKoszulRegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (h : IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i) : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_isH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 06BP, the second implication.**  An `H₁`-regular immersion of algebraic spaces
over `S` is a quasi-regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_isH1RegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (h : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i) : IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BR, part (1).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
*pseudo-coherent* when every commuting square of étale scheme charts induces a
pseudo-coherent scheme morphism.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsPseudoCoherent (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPseudoCoherentAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BR, part (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
*pseudo-coherent at* a point `x` of its source when it is pseudo-coherent on an open
subspace of the source containing `x`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsPseudoCoherentAt (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : points B S hS X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_baseChange_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BS.** A flat base change of a pseudo-coherent morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
is pseudo-coherent: in a cartesian square with `g : Y ⟶ Z` pseudo-coherent and `f : X ⟶ Z` flat,
the base change `g' : Y' ⟶ X` of `g` along `f` is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_baseChange_of_isFlat
    {X Y Y' Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Z} {g : Y ⟶ Z} {f' : Y' ⟶ Y} {g' : Y' ⟶ X}
    (sq : IsPullback f' g' g f) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
    (hf : IsPseudoCoherent B S hS g.hom) :
    IsPseudoCoherent B S hS g'.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06BT.** A composition of pseudo-coherent morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is
pseudo-coherent.
