    {K : BigFppfOver B S hS} {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj K ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (p : X ⟶ yoneda.obj K) :
    UniversallyOpen B S hS p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_of_isFlatAt
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_of_isFlatAt (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F)
    (hf : IsFlatAt B S hS f x) (hx : IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt B S hS F x) :
    IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt B S hS G (pointsMap B S hS F f x)

declarations.name: minimalPrimes_strictHenselization_tensorProduct_bijOn
declarations.doc:
The minimal primes of the strict henselization of the localization of `A ⊗[k] B` at the
maximal ideal induced by the residue maps correspond bijectively, by contraction, to pairs of
minimal primes of `A` and `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem minimalPrimes_strictHenselization_tensorProduct_bijOn
    (k A B : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [HenselianLocalRing A] [IsSepClosed (ResidueField A)]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [HenselianLocalRing B] [IsSepClosed (ResidueField B)]
    (resA : A →ₐ[k] k) (resB : B →ₐ[k] k)
    (hresA : RingHom.ker resA.toRingHom = maximalIdeal A)
    (hresB : RingHom.ker resB.toRingHom = maximalIdeal B)
    (R C : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [CommRing C] [IsLocalRing C]
    [Algebra (A ⊗[k] B) R]
    [IsLocalization
      (Submonoid.comap
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift resA resB (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _)).toRingHom
        (nonZeroDivisors k)) R]
    [Algebra R C]
    (ksep : Type v) [Field ksep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) ksep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) ksep]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization R ksep C] :
    Set.BijOn
      (fun q : Ideal C ↦
        (q.comap ((algebraMap R C).comp
          ((algebraMap (A ⊗[k] B) R).comp
            (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : A →ₐ[k] A ⊗[k] B).toRingHom)),
         q.comap ((algebraMap R C).comp
          ((algebraMap (A ⊗[k] B) R).comp
            (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[k] A ⊗[k] B).toRingHom))))
      (minimalPrimes C) ((minimalPrimes A) ×ˢ (minimalPrimes B))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.faithful_of_faithful_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06DV**. In a 2-cartesian diagram of categories fibred in groupoids over a site with
`𝒯₁` a stack, if every object of a fibre of `𝒮₁` is locally in the essential image of
`F : 𝒮₂ ⥤ 𝒮₁` and the first projection `𝒮₂ ×_{𝒮₁} 𝒯₁ ⥤ 𝒮₂` is faithful, then `G : 𝒯₁ ⥤ 𝒮₁` is
faithful.

By Stacks 003Z faithfulness may be checked on the fibres; there the fibres of `𝒯₁` are groupoids,
so two morphisms `α`, `β : y ⟶ y'` with `G α = G β` differ by the endomorphism `β ∘ α⁻¹` of `y`,
which `G` sends to the identity and which is therefore the identity by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.eq_id_of_map_eq_id_of_locallyEssSurj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_of_faithful_fst (hFeq : F ⋙ p𝒮₁ = p𝒮₂) (hGeq : G ⋙ p𝒮₁ = p𝒯₁)
    (hgpd₁ : p𝒮₁.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hgpdT : p𝒯₁.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} (hstack : p𝒯₁.IsStack J)
    (hloc : LocallyEssSurjOnFibers hgpd₁.isFibered hFeq J)
    (hfst : (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒮₂ p𝒯₁ p𝒮₁ F G).Faithful) :
    G.Faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 043H.** Group algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `B`.  An
object is a group object in presheaves over `B` whose underlying presheaf is an algebraic
space; morphisms are group-object morphisms over `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev GroupAlgebraicSpace (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : 𝒞.Contains S) (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B)
declarations.comment: the situation: this notion at the base Spec k for a field k over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidOverField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06DY.** A groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `B` over a scheme
`S`, whose space of objects is the spectrum of a field `k` regarded as an algebraic space over
`S` through Yoneda.
declarations.statement:
structure GroupoidOverField (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
declarations.comment: groupoid in algebraic spaces over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.actionGroupoid
declarations.doc:
The action groupoid `(X, G ×_B X, pr₁, a, m)` of an action `A` of a group algebraic space `G`
over `B` on an algebraic space `X` over `B`, with the projection as its source and the action
morphism as its target.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev actionGroupoid (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) (X : Over B)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) (A : ModObj G.obj.X X) :
    GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces 𝒞 S hS ⟨B, hB⟩
declarations.comment: the groupoid `(Spec k, G, p, p, m)` of a group over a field, at the trivial

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E0**, second assertion. For a field `k` over the scheme `S`, the multiplication
of a group algebraic space over `Spec k` is flat and universally open.

The first assertion of the same tag, for the composition of a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose
object space is the spectrum of a field, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isFlat_comp_of_objects_eq_spec_field`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_mul {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : C.Contains S) (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (hk : C.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace C S hS
      (schemeSpace (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS))).obj
      (schemeSpace (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS))).property) :
    IsFlat C S hS μ[G.obj.X].left ∧ UniversallyOpen C S hS μ[G.obj.X].left
declarations.comment: second assertion: the group law of a group space over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isFlat_comp_of_objects_eq_spec_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E0**, first assertion. Composition in a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose
object space is the spectrum of a field is flat and universally open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_comp_of_objects_eq_spec_field {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (hk : C.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (objects_eq : G.objects =
      schemeSpace (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS))) :
    Space.IsFlat C S hS G.comp.hom ∧ Space.UniversallyOpen C S hS G.comp.hom
declarations.comment: first assertion: the composition of a groupoid over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_of_restrictionDiagramMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E1.** Every arrow of the diagram defining the restriction of a groupoid in
algebraic spaces whose object space is the spectrum of a field, over a field extension, is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_restrictionDiagramMap
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : RestrictionDiagramMap C hS hk hk' structureMap i G hU f) :
    IsSurjective C S hS f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_restrictionDiagramMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E1.** Every arrow of the diagram defining the restriction of a groupoid in
algebraic spaces whose object space is the spectrum of a field, over a field extension, is
flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_restrictionDiagramMap
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : RestrictionDiagramMap C hS hk hk' structureMap i G hU f) :
    IsFlat C S hS f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyOpen_of_restrictionDiagramMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E1.** Every arrow of the diagram defining the restriction of a groupoid in
algebraic spaces whose object space is the spectrum of a field, over a field extension, is
universally open.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_of_restrictionDiagramMap
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : RestrictionDiagramMap C hS hk hk' structureMap i G hU f) :
    UniversallyOpen C S hS f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_restrictionArrowsToArrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E1.** The canonical map from the arrows of the restriction of a groupoid in
algebraic spaces over a field extension to the arrows of the groupoid is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_restrictionArrowsToArrows :
    IsAffineHom C S hS
      (restrictionArrowsToArrows G
        (restrictionObjectMap C hS hk hk' structureMap i G hU)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.exists_isIso_source_target_over_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E2.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` whose
object space `U` is the algebraic space represented by the spectrum of a field `k`. Every
point `r` of the arrow space `R` has, after an algebraically closed field extension `k'/k`,
a representative `r'` in the arrow space of the restriction `(U', R', s', t', c')` of the
groupoid along `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`: it maps to `r` in the points of `R`, and both its source
`s' ∘ r'` and its target `t' ∘ r'` are automorphisms of `Spec k'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_source_target_over_isAlgClosed {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) {S : Scheme.{u}} (hS : C.Contains S)
    (structureMap : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ S)
    (hk : C.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (objects_eq : G.objects = schemeSpace
      (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS)))
    (r : Space.points C S hS G.arrows.obj) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (field' : Field k') (_ : IsAlgClosed k')
      (i : k →+* k') (hk' : C.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))),
      let T : BigFppfOver C S hS :=
        Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : C.obj hk ⟶ C.obj hS)
      let T' : BigFppfOver C S hS :=
        Over.mk (⟨Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i).op ≫ structureMap⟩ :
          C.obj hk' ⟶ C.obj hS)
      let g : schemeSpace T' ⟶ G.objects :=
        schemeSpaceMap
          (Over.homMk (⟨Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i).op⟩ :
            C.obj hk' ⟶ C.obj hk) rfl : T' ⟶ T) ≫
          eqToHom objects_eq.symm
      ∃ r' : (restrictionArrows G g).obj.obj (Opposite.op T'),
        let p : Space.FieldValuedPoint C S hS G.arrows.obj :=
          { carrier := k'
            field := field'
            contained := hk'
            toBase := Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i).op ≫ structureMap
            value := (restrictionArrowsToArrows G g).hom.app (Opposite.op T') r' }
        let sourceEnd : T' ⟶ T' := (restrictionSource G g).hom.app (Opposite.op T') r'
        let targetEnd : T' ⟶ T' := (restrictionTarget G g).hom.app (Opposite.op T') r'
        p.class C S hS G.arrows.obj = r ∧ IsIso sourceEnd ∧ IsIso targetEnd

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.translationByArrow_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E3.** Translation by a family of arrows whose source and target are both
isomorphisms of the object space is an automorphism of the arrow space.
declarations.statement:
theorem translationByArrow_isIso (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (r : G.objects ⟶ G.arrows) [IsIso (r ≫ G.source)] [IsIso (r ≫ G.target)] :
    IsIso (translationByArrow G r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.translationByArrow_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E3.** Translation by `r` takes the identity arrow at the source of `r` to `r`
itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem translationByArrow_identity (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (r : G.objects ⟶ G.arrows) [IsIso (r ≫ G.source)]
    (T : (BigFppfOver C S hS)ᵒᵖ) (x : G.toGroupoidInFunctors.Evaluation T) :
    (translationByArrow G r).hom.app T
      (G.toGroupoidInFunctors.identity T ((r ≫ G.source).hom.app T x)) = r.hom.app T x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.identityArrow_comp_translationByArrow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E3, as an equation of morphisms.**  Left translation by a family `r` of arrows
whose source is an isomorphism, precomposed with the identity arrow at the source of `r`, is `r`
itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem identityArrow_comp_translationByArrow (H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (r : H.objects ⟶ H.arrows) [IsIso (r ≫ H.source)] :
    ((r ≫ H.source) ≫ identityArrow H) ≫ translationByArrow H r = r
declarations.comment: image of the identity, as an equation of morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isGeometricallyUnibranch_arrows_of_splitAtIds
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E4, the groupoid case.**  The arrow space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose
object space is the spectrum of a field is geometrically unibranch.

The last step of the source proof is [Stacks Project, Tag 06DU] for the étale local rings
`𝒪_{R, e}` and `𝒪_{R ×_{s, U, t} R, (e, e)}` of each restriction of the groupoid along an
algebraically closed extension of the field; it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.minimalPrimesSplitAtIdentityArrow_restriction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyUnibranch_arrows_of_splitAtIds :
    Space.IsGeometricallyUnibranch C S hS G.arrows.obj
declarations.comment: groupoid case, for a groupoid whose object space is the spectrum of a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidOverField.isGeometricallyUnibranch_arrows
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E4, the groupoid case.**  In the situation of [Stacks Project, Tag 06DY] — a
groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)` whose object space `U` is the spectrum of a field
`k` — the arrow space `R` is geometrically unibranch.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyUnibranch_arrows (G : GroupoidOverField C S hS B) :
    Space.IsGeometricallyUnibranch C S hS G.arrows.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyUnibranch_groupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E4, the group case.**  A group algebraic space over a field is geometrically
unibranch.

A group `G` over `Spec k` is the arrow space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose object space
is `Spec k`: the group acts trivially on the base, and the arrow space of the resulting action
groupoid is `G ×_{Spec k} Spec k`, which the first projection identifies with `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyUnibranch_groupAlgebraicSpace :
    IsGeometricallyUnibranch C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_formallyEtale_surjective_mulKernel_ne_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E6**, the example. There is a formally étale surjective map of commutative rings
`A → B` whose kernel `J` has `Ker(J ⊗_A J → J²) ≠ 0`; equivalently, `J` is idempotent but not
weakly regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_formallyEtale_surjective_mulKernel_ne_bot :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B),
      Algebra.FormallyEtale A B ∧ Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B) ∧
        LinearMap.ker (Submodule.mulMap' (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B))
          (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B))) ≠ ⊥
declarations.comment: the example: a formally étale surjection with Ker(J ⊗_A J → J²) ≠ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_formallyEtale_surjective_not_isZero_torTwo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06E6**, the example, with the nonvanishing read on `Tor₂`. There is a formally étale
surjective map of commutative rings `A → B` with `Tor₂^A(B, B) ≠ 0`. By Tag 09D6 this is the same
statement as `exists_formallyEtale_surjective_mulKernel_ne_bot`; it is the input from which the
source deduces, via the five-term exact sequence of Quillen's spectral sequence, that
`L_{B/A} ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_formallyEtale_surjective_not_isZero_torTwo :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B),
      Algebra.FormallyEtale A B ∧ Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B) ∧
        ¬ IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) 2).obj (ModuleCat.of A B)).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A B))
declarations.comment: the example: a formally étale surjection with Tor₂^A(B, B) ≠ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_flat_finiteType_groupScheme_not_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06E8.** There is a flat group scheme of finite type over the affine
line that is not separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_flat_finiteType_groupScheme_not_isSeparated (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ∃ G : CategoryTheory.Over (Spec (.of (Polynomial k))),
      Nonempty (GrpObj G) ∧ Flat G.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom ∧
        QuasiCompact G.hom ∧ ¬ IsSeparated G.hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonSeparatedGroupSpace.exists_isFiniteType_groupAlgebraicSpace_not_isSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06EA.** Over a field of characteristic zero there is a group
algebraic space of finite type over the field which is neither separated, nor quasi-separated,
nor locally separated.

The witness is the quotient `𝔸¹_k/ℤ` of the affine line by the integer translations, realized
as the fppf sheafification of the presheaf of global sections modulo the integers: addition of
sections makes that sheafification a group object, while the quotient fails to be decent, and a
quasi-separated or locally separated algebraic space is decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteType_groupAlgebraicSpace_not_isSeparatedOver
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k] (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hG : B.Contains (Spec (.of (RatFunc k)))) :
    ∃ G : Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS
        (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS))))
        (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B (Spec (.of k)) hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))),
      Space.IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of k)) hS G.obj.X.hom ∧
      ¬ Space.IsSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS G.obj.X.left ∧
      ¬ Space.IsQuasiSeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS G.obj.X.left ∧
      ¬ Space.IsLocallySeparatedOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS G.obj.X.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.image_finiteTypePoints_eq
declarations.doc:
A surjective morphism which is locally of finite type maps the finite type points of its
source onto those of its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_finiteTypePoints_eq {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [Surjective f] :
    f.base '' T.finiteTypePoints = S.finiteTypePoints

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundaryComplement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC, the open subspace.** The open subspace of `X` obtained by removing the
boundary `closure T \ T` of a set `T` of points of `X`: its point set is Mathlib's
`coborder T`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openSubspaceOfPoints` at `coborder T`; the definition needs
no hypothesis on `T`, local closedness entering only through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_boundaryComplement`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boundaryComplement (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) : Subfunctor X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_ι_boundaryComplement
declarations.doc:
**The point set of the complement of the boundary of `T` is `coborder T`**, that is, the
complement of `closure T \ T`. This is the defining property `|U| = |X| ∖ ∂T` of the open
subspace `U` of Stacks 06EC.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_ι_boundaryComplement (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).toFunctor
      (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).ι) = coborder T
declarations.comment: the point set of U is the complement of the boundary of T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_boundaryComplement
declarations.doc:
**The complement of the boundary of a locally closed set of points of an algebraic space is
an open subspace of it.** This is the open subspace `U` of Stacks 06EC, whose existence the
source takes from Stacks 03BZ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_boundaryComplement (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (boundaryComplement B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: U is an open subspace of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reducedInducedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC, the reduced induced subspace `Z`.** The *reduced induced subspace structure*
on a locally closed set `T` of points of an algebraic space `X` over `S`: the reduced induced
closed subspace of Stacks 03IQ on `T`, formed inside the open subspace
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundaryComplement` complementary to the boundary of `T`, where `T`
is closed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reducedInducedSubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    Subfunctor (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).toFunctor
declarations.comment: the reduced induced subspace Z on a locally closed set of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_reducedInducedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC.** The reduced induced subspace on `T` is a closed subspace of the open
subspace complementary to the boundary of `T`, so `Z ⟶ U` is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubspace_reducedInducedSubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS (reducedInducedSubspace B S hS hX hT)
declarations.comment: Z is a closed subspace of U, so Z ⟶ U is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_reducedInducedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC.** The reduced induced subspace on `T` is reduced, in the étale-local sense
of Stacks 03E6.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced_reducedInducedSubspace
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS (reducedInducedSubspace B S hS hX hT).toFunctor
      (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)
declarations.comment: Z is a reduced algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_comp_ι_reducedInducedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC.** The point set of the reduced induced subspace on `T` is `T` itself, as a
subset of the points of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_comp_ι_reducedInducedSubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (reducedInducedSubspace B S hS hX hT).toFunctor
      ((reducedInducedSubspace B S hS hX hT).ι ≫ (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).ι)) = T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isImmersion_comp_ι_reducedInducedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC.** The composite `Z ⟶ U ⟶ X` of the reduced induced subspace on `T` with the
open subspace complementary to the boundary of `T` is an immersion: a closed immersion
followed by an open immersion, by Stacks 02YV.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_comp_ι_reducedInducedSubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    IsImmersion B S hS ((reducedInducedSubspace B S hS hX hT).ι ≫
      (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).ι)
declarations.comment: Z ⟶ U ⟶ X is an immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_reducedInducedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC, uniqueness.** A reduced closed subspace of the open subspace complementary
to the boundary of `T` whose point set in `|X|` is `T` is the reduced induced subspace on
`T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_reducedInducedSubspace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T)
    (W : Subfunctor (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).toFunctor)
    (hWc : IsClosedSubspace B S hS W)
    (hWT : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor
      (W.ι ≫ (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).ι)) = T)
    (hWr : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS W.toFunctor (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    W = reducedInducedSubspace B S hS hX hT
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the reduced induced subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_reducedInducedSubspace_of_isLocallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EC.** A locally closed set `T` of points of an algebraic space `X` over `S`
carries a unique reduced closed subspace structure inside the open subspace complementary to
its boundary, and that subspace is an immersion into `X` with point set `T`. This is the
*reduced induced subspace structure* on `T`, and it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reducedInducedSubspace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_reducedInducedSubspace_of_isLocallyClosed
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) :
    ∃! W : Subfunctor (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).toFunctor,
      IsClosedSubspace B S hS W ∧
        HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS W.toFunctor (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y) ∧
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor
            (W.ι ≫ (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).ι)) = T ∧
            IsImmersion B S hS (W.ι ≫ (boundaryComplement B S hS X T).ι)
declarations.comment: existence and uniqueness of the reduced induced subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06ED.** An immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite type.
Each of its represented base changes is an immersion of schemes, hence locally of finite
type, and being locally of finite type passes from the represented base changes to the étale
charts by the implication of Stacks 03MJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isImmersion (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_isClosed_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EF**, and the assertion of **Stacks 06EH** for arbitrary scheme charts. A point
of an algebraic space over `S` is a finite type point exactly when it is the image of a closed
point of a scheme étale over the space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_isClosed_etaleChart
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    IsFiniteTypePoint B S hS X x ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
        (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U)),
        IsEtale B S hS φ ∧
          IsClosed ({schemePoint B S hS U p} : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) ∧
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) φ (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFiniteTypePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EG.** A point of an algebraic space over `S` is a *finite type point* when some
field-valued point representing it has a morphism to the space which is locally of finite
type.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFiniteTypePoint (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (x : points B S hS X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finiteTypePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EG.** The set `X_{ft-pts}` of finite type points of an algebraic space
over `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev finiteTypePoints (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Set (points B S hS X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_isClosed_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EF**, and the assertion of **Stacks 06EH** for arbitrary scheme charts. A point
of an algebraic space over `S` is a finite type point exactly when it is the image of a closed
point of a scheme étale over the space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_isClosed_etaleChart
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    IsFiniteTypePoint B S hS X x ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
        (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U)),
        IsEtale B S hS φ ∧
          IsClosed ({schemePoint B S hS U p} : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) ∧
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) φ (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_isAffine_isClosed_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EH**, the assertion for affine scheme charts. A point of an algebraic space
over `S` is a finite type point exactly when it is the image of a closed point of an affine
scheme étale over the space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_isAffine_isClosed_etaleChart
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    IsFiniteTypePoint B S hS X x ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
        (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj U)),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧ IsEtale B S hS φ ∧
          IsClosed ({schemePoint B S hS U p} : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) ∧
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) φ (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj U)) = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mapsTo_finiteTypePoints
declarations.doc:
A locally finite type morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` carries finite type points to
finite type points. This is the algebraic-space counterpart of Stacks 02J3, and is the easy
inclusion of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.image_finiteTypePoints_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapsTo_finiteTypePoints {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    Set.MapsTo (pointsMap B S hS X f) (finiteTypePoints B S hS X)
      (finiteTypePoints B S hS Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.image_finiteTypePoints_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EJ.** A surjective morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of
finite type maps the finite type points of its source onto the finite type points of its
target.

One inclusion is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mapsTo_finiteTypePoints`. For the other, a
finite type point of the target is represented by a locally finite type morphism from a field
spectrum; the fibre product of the source with that field spectrum over the target is a
nonempty algebraic space locally of finite type over the source, so it has a finite type point
by Stacks 06EK, whose image in the source is the required point.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_finiteTypePoints_eq {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    pointsMap B S hS X f '' finiteTypePoints B S hS X = finiteTypePoints B S hS Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.inter_finiteTypePoints_nonempty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EK**, locally closed subsets. A nonempty locally closed set of points of an
algebraic space over `S` contains a finite type point.

The set is pulled back to a surjective étale scheme chart, where it is again nonempty and
locally closed because the map on points is continuous and surjective and the point topology
of a represented presheaf is the topology of the representing scheme; Stacks 02J4 produces a
finite type point there and its image in `|X|` is a finite type point by Stacks 02J3.
declarations.statement:
theorem inter_finiteTypePoints_nonempty (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {T : Set (points B S hS X)}
    (hT : IsLocallyClosed T) (hne : T.Nonempty) :
    (T ∩ finiteTypePoints B S hS X).Nonempty

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closure_inter_finiteTypePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EK**, closed subsets. The finite type points lying in a closed set of points of
an algebraic space over `S` are dense in it.
declarations.statement:
theorem closure_inter_finiteTypePoints (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsClosed T) :
    closure (T ∩ finiteTypePoints B S hS X) = T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `x` be a point of
`X`. The following are equivalent:

1. `x` is a finite type point;
2. there is an algebraic space `Z` whose space of points is a singleton and a morphism
   `f : Z ⟶ X` which is locally of finite type with `{x}` the image of `|f|`;
3. there is an algebraic space `Z` and a morphism `f : Z ⟶ X` such that `Z` carries a
   surjective étale morphism from the spectrum of a field, `f` is locally of finite type, `f`
   is a monomorphism, and `x` is the image under `|f|` of the point of that field spectrum.

Conditions (1) and (2) are equivalent by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_iff_exists_singleton_space`; condition (1) implies
condition (3) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mono_isLocallyOfFiniteType_etale_fieldPoint_of_isFiniteTypePoint`,
and condition (3) implies condition (1) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypePoint_pointsMap_of_isSurjective_fieldPoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypePoint_tfae (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X) :
    [IsFiniteTypePoint B S hS X x,
      ∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : Z ⟶ X),
        Nonempty (points B S hS Z) ∧ Subsingleton (points B S hS Z) ∧
          IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z f) = {x},
      ∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : Z ⟶ X)
          (z : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z),
        IsSurjective B S hS (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value) ∧
          IsEtale B S hS (yonedaEquiv.symm z.value) ∧
          IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Mono f ∧
          x = pointsMap B S hS Z f (z.class B S hS Z)].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.prop_fiberProduct_fst_of_isLocalAtTarget
declarations.doc:
A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is local on the base for `τ` is
inherited by the base change along any morphism of the kind belonging to `τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem prop_fiberProduct_fst_of_isLocalAtTarget
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (τ : Topology) (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (τ.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)]
    {X Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hf : P f)
    (hg : match τ with
      | .fpqc => IsFlat B S hS g.hom
      | .fppf => IsFlat B S hS g.hom ∧ IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g.hom
      | .syntomic => IsSyntomic B S hS g.hom
      | .smooth => IsSmooth B S hS g.hom
      | .etale => IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    P (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst g.hom f.hom) :
      AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS g f ⟶ Y')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EQ**, the fpqc case. A property fpqc local on the source is stable under
precomposition with a flat morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_isFlat [P.IsLocalAtSource (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)]
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ Z)
    (ha : IsFlat B S hS a.hom) (hf : P f) : P (a ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EQ**, the fppf case. A property fppf local on the source is stable under
precomposition with a flat morphism which is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    [P.IsLocalAtSource (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fppf B S hS)]
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS a.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS a.hom) (hf : P f) : P (a ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_isSyntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EQ**, the syntomic case. A property syntomic local on the source is stable under
precomposition with a syntomic morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_isSyntomic [P.IsLocalAtSource (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .syntomic B S hS)]
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ Z)
    (ha : IsSyntomic B S hS a.hom) (hf : P f) : P (a ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EQ**, the smooth case. A property smooth local on the source is stable under
precomposition with a smooth morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_isSmooth [P.IsLocalAtSource (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .smooth B S hS)]
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ Z)
    (ha : IsSmooth B S hS a.hom) (hf : P f) : P (a ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EQ**, the étale case. A property étale local on the source is stable under
precomposition with an étale morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_isEtale [P.IsLocalAtSource (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .etale B S hS)]
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (a : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ Z)
    (ha : IsEtale B S hS a.hom) (hf : P f) : P (a ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.isLocalAtSource_holdsOnEveryEtaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06ER.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of schemes over `S` which is étale local
on the source and target, and let `τ` be one of the five topologies of Stacks 03YH. If `P` is
local on the source for the counterpart of `τ` on schemes, then the associated property of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` of Stacks 03MJ is local on the source for `τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Topology.isLocalAtSource_holdsOnEveryEtaleChart (τ : Topology)
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    (hlocal : P.IsLocalAtSource τ.schemePrecoverage) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} τ B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_isLocalAtSource_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06ET.** Flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the source
for the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance isFlat_isLocalAtSource_fpqc
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) => IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.fpqc.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtSource_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EV.** Being locally of finite presentation, for a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S`, is local on the source for the fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtSource_fppf :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFiniteType_isLocalAtSource_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EW.** Being locally of finite type, as a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
over `S`, is local on the source for the fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyOfFiniteType_isLocalAtSource_fppf :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fppf B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenMorphism_isLocalAtSource_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EX.** Being open, for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, is local on the
source for the fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
instance isOpenMorphism_isLocalAtSource_fppf :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) ↦ IsOpenMorphism B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06EY.** Being universally open, for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, is

instance universallyOpen_isLocalAtSource_fppf :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) ↦ UniversallyOpen B S hS f.hom)

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06F0.** Syntomicity of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06F2.** Smoothness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the source

One application of the smooth case of Stacks 06ER to smoothness of morphisms of schemes, which

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06F8.** A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is *smooth local on
the source-and-target* when it is stable under smooth precomposition and smooth base change, and
can be checked in smooth neighbourhoods of every point of the source.
declarations.statement:
structure IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalAtSource
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06F9**, smooth locality on the source. A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is smooth local on the source-and-target is local at the source for the smooth
precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalAtSource
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P) :
    (P.inverseImage (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F))).IsLocalAtSource
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .smooth B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalAtTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06F9**, smooth locality on the target. A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is smooth local on the source-and-target is local at the target for the smooth
precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalAtTarget
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P) :
    (P.inverseImage (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F))).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .smooth B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comp_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06F9**, smooth postcomposition. A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S` which is smooth local on the source-and-target is preserved by postcomposition with a smooth
morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_smooth
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : P f) (hg : IsSmooth B S hS g) : P (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FA.** Seven equivalent criteria for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` to
have a property which is smooth local on the source-and-target: the property itself; a smooth
neighbourhood of every point of the source on which it holds; one smooth diagram surjective on
the source; every smooth comparison into a fibre product over a smooth base change; a smooth
covering of the target over which the base changes have it; a smooth covering of the source whose
composites have it; and a smooth covering of the target refined by smooth coverings of the
corresponding fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_tfae
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      P f,
      (∀ x : points B S hS X,
        ∃ (U V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (_hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
          (_hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
          (a : U ⟶ X) (b : V ⟶ Y) (h : U ⟶ V)
          (u : points B S hS U),
          IsSmooth B S hS a ∧
            IsSmooth B S hS b ∧
            pointsMap B S hS U a u = x ∧
            h ≫ b = a ≫ f ∧ P h),
      (∃ (U V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (_hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
          (_hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
          (a : U ⟶ X) (b : V ⟶ Y) (h : U ⟶ V),
          IsSmooth B S hS a ∧
            IsSurjective B S hS a ∧
            IsSmooth B S hS b ∧
            h ≫ b = a ≫ f ∧ P h),
      (∀ (U V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (_hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
          (_hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
          (b : V ⟶ Y) (k : U ⟶ pullback f b),
          IsSmooth B S hS b →
          IsSmooth B S hS k →
          P (k ≫ pullback.snd f b)),
      (∃ (I : Type v)
          (V : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (b : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Y),
          IsSmoothCovering B S hS V b ∧
          ∀ i, P (pullback.snd f (b i))),
      (∃ (I : Type v)
          (U : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (a : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X),
          IsSmoothCovering B S hS U a ∧
          ∀ i, P (a i ≫ f)),
      (∃ (I : Type v)
          (V : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (b : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Y)
          (J : I → Type w)
          (U : ∀ i, J i → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (a : ∀ i j, U i j ⟶ pullback f (b i)),
          IsSmoothCovering B S hS V b ∧
          (∀ i, IsSmoothCovering B S hS (U i) (a i)) ∧
          (∀ i j, P (a i j ≫ pullback.snd f (b i))))
    ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FB.** A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is local at the
source and at the target for the smooth topology, and is preserved by postcomposition with a
smooth morphism, is smooth local on the source-and-target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    [hSource : (P.inverseImage (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F))).IsLocalAtSource
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} .smooth B S hS)]
    [hTarget : (P.inverseImage (ObjectProperty.ι
      (fun F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u =>
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F))).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} .smooth B S hS)]
    (hcomp : ∀ {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
      (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
      (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
      (_hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
      (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z),
      P f → IsSmooth B S hS g → P (f ≫ g)) :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSyntomic_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FC**, the syntomic case. Syntomicity of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
is smooth local on the source-and-target.

The source locality hypothesis of Stacks 06FB comes from the syntomic one, Stacks 06F0, along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.precoverage_smooth_le_syntomic`; the target locality one
comes from the fpqc one, Stacks 0428, along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.precoverage_smooth_le_fpqc`; and the postcomposition
hypothesis is composition of syntomic morphisms (Stacks 03Z8) applied to the fact that a
smooth morphism is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSyntomic_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsSyntomic B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyOpen_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FC**, the universally-open case. Being universally open is, for morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S`, smooth local on the source-and-target.

The source locality hypothesis of Stacks 06FB comes from the fppf one, Stacks 06EY, along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.precoverage_smooth_le_fppf`; the target locality one comes
from the fpqc one, Stacks 041P, along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.precoverage_smooth_le_fpqc`; and the postcomposition
hypothesis is composition of universally open morphisms (Stacks 03Z4) applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyOpen_of_isSmooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun _ _ f => UniversallyOpen B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FC**, the flat case. Flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is smooth
local on the source-and-target.

The two locality hypotheses of Stacks 06FB come from the fpqc ones (Stacks 06ET and 041W) along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_precoverage_le_fpqc`, and the postcomposition hypothesis is
composition of flat morphisms (Stacks 03MN) applied to the flatness of a smooth morphism
(Stacks 04TA).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_flat :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsFlat B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FC**, the locally-of-finite-type case. Being locally of finite type for morphisms
of algebraic spaces over `S` is smooth local on the source-and-target.

The source locality hypothesis of Stacks 06FB is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFiniteType_isLocalAtSource_smooth`; the target locality one
comes from the fpqc statement of Stacks 041S along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_precoverage_le_fpqc`, and the postcomposition hypothesis is
composition of morphisms locally of finite type (Stacks 03XG) applied to the fact that a smooth
morphism is locally of finite type (Stacks 06MH).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_locallyOfFiniteType :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun _ _ f => IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FC**, the locally-of-finite-presentation case. Being locally of finite
presentation for morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is smooth local on the
source-and-target.

The source locality hypothesis of Stacks 06FB is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocalAtSource_smooth`; the target
locality one comes from the fpqc statement of Stacks 041T along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_precoverage_le_fpqc`, and the postcomposition hypothesis is
composition of morphisms locally of finite presentation (Stacks 03XQ) applied to the fact that a
smooth morphism is locally of finite presentation (Stacks 04AJ).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_locallyOfFinitePresentation :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun _ _ f => IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FC**, the smooth case. Smoothness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is
smooth local on the source-and-target.

The source locality hypothesis of Stacks 06FB is Stacks 06F2; the target locality one comes from
the fpqc one (Stacks 0429) along `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smooth_precoverage_le_fpqc`, and the
postcomposition hypothesis is composition of smooth morphisms (Stacks 03ZD).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_smooth :
    IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS (fun _ _ f => IsSmooth B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_dimensionAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FD.** Let `G` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` whose space of objects
is the spectrum of a field `k`, viewed as an algebraic space through Yoneda, and whose source
and target are locally of finite type. Then the dimension of the space of arrows of `G` equals
its dimension at every one of its points.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_eq_dimensionAtPoint
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A)
    (objects_eq : G.objects = _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace
      (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))
    (_hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.source.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.target.hom)
    (r : points B S hS G.arrows.obj) :
    dimension B S hS G.arrows.obj G.arrows.property =
      dimensionAtPoint B S hS G.arrows.obj G.arrows.property r
declarations.comment: constant dimension of the arrow space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_source_iff_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FD, part (2).** Let `G` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` whose space
of objects is the spectrum of a field `k`, viewed as an algebraic space through Yoneda, and
whose source and target are locally of finite type. Then the transcendence degree over `k` of a
point of the space of arrows is the same whether it is measured through the source or through
the target.

Both are read on one étale chart of the arrow space whose chart of the object space is the
field spectrum itself, where they become the two transcendence degrees of the residue field at
a point of a scheme over two morphisms to the spectrum of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_source_iff_target
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A)
    (objects_eq : G.objects = _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace
      (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.source.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.target.hom)
    (r : points B S hS G.arrows.obj) (n : ℕ∞) :
    HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS G.source.hom r n ↔
      HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS G.target.hom r n
declarations.comment: part (2): the transcendence degree through the source and through the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_localRingDimension_of_hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FD, part (3).** Let `G` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` whose space of
objects is the spectrum of a field `k`, viewed as an algebraic space through Yoneda, and whose
source and target are locally of finite type. At a point of the space of arrows whose
transcendence degree over `k` is zero, the dimension of the space of arrows is the dimension of
the local ring there.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_eq_localRingDimension_of_hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_zero
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A)
    (objects_eq : G.objects = _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace
      (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.source.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.target.hom)
    (r : points B S hS G.arrows.obj)
    (htr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS G.source.hom r 0) :
    dimension B S hS G.arrows.obj G.arrows.property =
      (localRingDimension B S hS r : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: part (3): the dimension of the local ring at a point of transcendence degree 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_dimensionAtPoint_of_groupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FE, part (1).** A group algebraic space over a field which is locally of finite
type has the same dimension at every one of its points, namely its dimension.

Constant dimension of the arrow space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces whose object space is
the spectrum of a field is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_dimensionAtPoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_eq_dimensionAtPoint_of_groupAlgebraicSpace {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : C.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk (terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).obj
      (terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).property)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom)
    (g : points C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left) :
    dimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left G.property =
      dimensionAtPoint C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left G.property g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_eq_localRingDimension_of_groupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FE, part (2).** At a point of a group algebraic space locally of finite type over
a field whose transcendence degree over that field is zero, the dimension of the group is the
dimension of the local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_eq_localRingDimension_of_groupAlgebraicSpace {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hk : C.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk (terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).obj
      (terminalSpace C (Spec (.of k)) hk).property)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom)
    (g : points C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left)
    (htr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.hom g 0) :
    dimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk G.obj.X.left G.property =
      (localRingDimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk g : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: part (2): dimension of the local ring at a point of transcendence degree zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_arrows_eq_dimension_stabilizer_of_objects_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FF.** Let `G` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` whose space of objects
is the spectrum of a field `k`, viewed as an algebraic space through Yoneda, and whose source
and target are locally of finite type. Then the space of arrows of `G` and the stabilizer of `G`
have the same dimension.

The hypothesis is an *isomorphism* of the object space with the spectrum of the field, not an
equality of algebraic spaces; the equality case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_arrows_eq_dimension_stabilizer`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_arrows_eq_dimension_stabilizer_of_objects_iso {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A)
    (objects_iso : G.objects ≅ _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace
      (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.source.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.target.hom) :
    dimension B S hS G.arrows.obj G.arrows.property =
      dimension B S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerOverBase G).obj
        (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerOverBase G).property
declarations.comment: with the space of objects isomorphic to the spectrum of the field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_arrows_eq_dimension_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` whose space of objects
is the spectrum of a field `k`, viewed as an algebraic space through Yoneda, and whose source
and target are locally of finite type. Then the space of arrows of `G` and the stabilizer of `G`
have the same dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_arrows_eq_dimension_stabilizer {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (structureMap : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    {A : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces B S hS A)
    (objects_eq : G.objects = _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSpace
      (Over.mk (⟨structureMap⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))
    (hs : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.source.hom)
    (ht : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.target.hom) :
    dimension B S hS G.arrows.obj G.arrows.property =
      dimension B S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerOverBase G).obj
        (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerOverBase G).property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isFlat_relativeProperty
declarations.doc:
**The quotient-stack projection is flat.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic
spaces over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site and assume its source and target maps `s`, `t` are flat
and locally of finite presentation. Then the canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R
is flat in the sense of Stacks 03YK: every algebraic space representing a base change of `π` along
a scheme-valued point of `[U/R]` has flat structural morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_relativeProperty (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.target.hom) :
    RelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1} C S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => Space.IsFlat C S hS f.hom)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeProperty
declarations.doc:
**The quotient-stack projection is locally of finite presentation.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)`
be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site and assume its source and
target maps `s`, `t` are flat and locally of finite presentation. Then the canonical projection
`π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R is locally of finite presentation in the sense of Stacks 03YK:
every algebraic space representing a base change of `π` along a scheme-valued point of `[U/R]` has
structural morphism locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeProperty (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (_hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.target.hom)
    (hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.target.hom) :
    RelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1} C S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS f.hom)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isSurjective_relativeProperty
declarations.doc:
**The quotient-stack projection is surjective.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in
algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site and assume its source and target maps `s`,
`t` are flat and locally of finite presentation. Then the canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of
Stacks 044R is surjective in the sense of Stacks 03YK: every algebraic space representing a base
change of `π` along a scheme-valued point of `[U/R]` has surjective structural morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_relativeProperty (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (_hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.target.hom) :
    RelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1} C S hS
      (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty C S hS)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FH, flatness.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over
`S` presented as in Stacks 04M9. If the source map `s` is flat, then the canonical projection
`π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R is flat in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (A : Presentation G)
    (hs : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom) :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, max u t} C S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => Space.IsFlat C S hS f.hom)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G) A.representable
declarations.comment: flatness; Stacks 04M9 and the representability of the projection carried as the hypothesis `Presentation`, and only the source map constrained

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FH, local finite presentation.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in
algebraic spaces over `S` presented as in Stacks 04M9. If the source map `s` is locally of finite
presentation, then the canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R is locally of finite
presentation in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B}
    (A : Presentation G) (hs : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom) :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, max u t} C S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) =>
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS f.hom)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G) A.representable
declarations.comment: locally of finite presentation; Stacks 04M9 and the representability of the projection carried as the hypothesis `Presentation`, and only the source map constrained

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.QuotientAtlas.isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FH, surjectivity.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces
over `S` presented as in Stacks 04M9. The canonical projection `π : S_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R
is surjective in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK, with no hypothesis on the groupoid: the
source map is surjective because the identity arrow at a point of the object space is a preimage
of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (A : Presentation G) :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, max u t} C S hS
      (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty C S hS)
      (quotientStackProjectionHom G) A.representable
declarations.comment: surjectivity; Stacks 04M9 and the representability of the projection carried as the hypothesis `Presentation`, and no hypothesis on the groupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FI.** Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic
space `A` over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site. If the source and the target of `G` are flat and
locally of finite presentation, then the quotient stack `[U/R]` is an algebraic stack over `S`.

Artin's theorem **Stacks 06DC** is carried as `h06DC`, **Stacks 06FH** as `h06FH`, and
**Stacks 04TB** as `h04TB`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack {A : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A)
    (h06DC : Theorem06DC.{u, w} C S hS) (h06FH : Lemma06FH C S hS)
    (h04TB : QuotientStackIsomSheavesAlgebraic C S hS G)
    (hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.target.hom)
    (hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom)
    (htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.target.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G)
declarations.comment: Artin's theorem Stacks 06DC, Stacks 06FH and Stacks 04TB are carried as the hypotheses h06DC, h06FH and h04TB; what is discharged is the representability of the source and of the projection (Stacks 04SV and Stacks 04WZ) and the four stack clauses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forall_isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FI, quantified over the groupoids on a fixed base.** Every groupoid in algebraic
spaces over `A` whose source and target are flat and locally of finite presentation has an
algebraic quotient stack.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack` with the three carried
hypotheses pulled in front of the quantifier, which is the shape a consumer of Stacks 06FI — for
instance Stacks 06PL for the trivial action — takes it in.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack (A : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (h06DC : Theorem06DC.{u, w} C S hS) (h06FH : Lemma06FH C S hS)
    (h04TB : Lemma04TB C S hS) :
    ∀ H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A,
      Space.IsFlat C S hS H.source.hom → Space.IsFlat C S hS H.target.hom →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.source.hom →
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.target.hom →
            IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack H)
declarations.comment: quantified over the groupoids on a fixed base; Artin's theorem Stacks 06DC, Stacks 06FH and Stacks 04TB are carried as the hypotheses h06DC, h06FH and h04TB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `A` over
a scheme `S` of a big fppf site. If the source and the target of `G` are flat and locally of finite
presentation, then the quotient stack `[U/R]` is an algebraic stack over `S`.

The source states it for a groupoid over `S`; a groupoid over `A` is the more general statement,
`S` itself being an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_flat {A : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS}
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A)
    (hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.target.hom)
    (hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom)
    (htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.target.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G)
declarations.comment: stated for a groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space over S, which contains the source's groupoid over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.isOpen_pointSet
declarations.doc:
The rule of Stacks 06FJ is defined. The set of points of an algebraic stack lying in an
open substack is open: it is the range of the map on points of the inclusion, which is an open
map because the inclusion is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_pointSet (W : OpenSubstack 𝒳) :
    @IsOpen _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) (W.pointSet B S hS)
declarations.comment: the point set of an open substack is open, so the rule is defined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.opens
declarations.doc:
**The rule `𝒰 ↦ |𝒰|` of Stacks 06FJ**: the point set of an open substack of `𝒳`, as an open
subset of the topological space of points of `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def opens (W : OpenSubstack 𝒳) :
    letI := pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val
    TopologicalSpace.Opens (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.pointSet_mono
declarations.doc:
The rule of Stacks 06FJ preserves inclusions. An open substack contained in another has a
smaller point set.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointSet_mono {U V : OpenSubstack 𝒳} (h : U.property ≤ V.property) :
    U.pointSet B S hS ⊆ V.pointSet B S hS
declarations.comment: inclusion-preservation for the point set of an open substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.opens_mono
declarations.doc:
The rule of Stacks 06FJ preserves inclusions, for the rule `𝒰 ↦ |𝒰|` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.opens`.
declarations.statement:
theorem opens_mono {U V : OpenSubstack 𝒳} (h : U.property ≤ V.property) :
    letI := pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val
    opens B S hS U ≤ opens B S hS V
declarations.comment: inclusion-preservation for the rule U goes to |U| as an open subset of the point space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.bijective_opens_and_opens_le_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FJ.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack. The rule `𝒰 ↦ |𝒰|` defines an inclusion
preserving bijection between open substacks of `𝒳` and open subsets of `|𝒳|`: the rule
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.opens` is bijective, and `|𝒰| ⊆ |𝒱|` holds exactly when
`𝒰 ⊆ 𝒱`.

Injectivity, and the reflection of inclusions, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.property_le_of_pointSet_subset`; surjectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.ofIsOpen` with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.pointSet_ofIsOpen`; preservation of inclusions is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.pointSet_mono`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_opens_and_opens_le_iff :
    letI := pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val
    Function.Bijective (opens B S hS (𝒳 := 𝒳)) ∧
      ∀ U V : OpenSubstack 𝒳, opens B S hS U ≤ opens B S hS V ↔ U ≤ V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_reducedInducedSubstack
declarations.doc:
**The reduced induced substack structure on a locally closed set of points.**
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `T` be a locally closed subset of its space of
points, with boundary `∂T = T̄ \ T`. Then there are

* an open substack `𝒰` of `𝒳` with `|𝒰| = |𝒳| \ ∂T` (Mathlib's `coborder T`), and
* a reduced induced algebraic stack structure `𝒵` (**Stacks 050C**) on the part of `T` inside
  `|𝒰|`, that is, a reduced closed substack of `𝒰` with that set of points,

such that the composite `𝒵 ⟶ 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` of the two inclusions is an immersion, `𝒵` is reduced, and
the image of `|𝒵|` in `|𝒳|` is exactly `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_reducedInducedSubstack
    (T : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳))
    (hT : @IsLocallyClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) T) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : OpenSubstack 𝒳)
      (P : ObjectProperty
        (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒰.property 𝒰.isAlgebraic).val.val.obj)
      (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
        (fullSubcategoryBased (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒰.property 𝒰.isAlgebraic) P)),
      𝒰.pointSet B S hS = @coborder _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) T ∧
      IsReducedInducedStackStructure B S hS
        (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS 𝒰.inclusion ⁻¹' T) P ∧
      AlgebraicStacks.IsImmersion B S hS
        (fullSubcategoryInclusion (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒰.property 𝒰.isAlgebraic)
          P hP ≫ 𝒰.inclusion) ∧
      IsReducedStack B S hS
        (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒰.property 𝒰.isAlgebraic)
          P hP) ∧
      Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
        (fullSubcategoryInclusion (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 𝒰.property 𝒰.isAlgebraic)
          P hP ≫ 𝒰.inclusion)) = T
declarations.comment: a locally closed T in |X|: the open substack U with |U| = |X| minus the boundary of T, the reduced induced closed substack Z of U on the points of T (Stacks 050C), the immersion Z -> U -> X, Z reduced, and |Z| = T in |X|

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnEverySmoothDiagram_iff_some
declarations.doc:
For a property `P` of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is smooth local on the
source-and-target and a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`: every diagram of
algebraic spaces over `f` with smooth vertical 1-morphisms whose comparison to the 2-fibre product
is smooth has `P` on its top horizontal morphism if and only if some such diagram with left
vertical 1-morphism surjective on objects does.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnEverySmoothDiagram_iff_some
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    HasPropertyOnEverySmoothDiagram B S hS P f ↔ HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_iff_relative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FM, the assertion for a representable morphism.** Let `P` be a property of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` smooth local on the source-and-target which is moreover
stable under base change and local at the target for the fppf precoverage, and let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`
be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic spaces. Then `f` passes
the existential smooth-diagram test of condition (2) exactly when it has the relative property
`P` in the sense of Stacks 03YK, i.e. of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.

Algebraicity of the source is not used in either direction; it is kept because it is part of the
statement of the tagged assertion.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_iff_relative
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    [(spaceProperty B S hS P).IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [(spaceProperty B S hS P).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)]
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (_h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P f ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, v} B S hS (spaceProperty B S hS P) f hf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_iff_represented
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06FM, the assertion for representable source and target.** For a property `P` of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` smooth local on the source-and-target, and a 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` whose source and target are representable by algebraic
spaces `F` and `G`, the existential smooth-diagram test of condition (2) holds for `f` exactly
when the induced morphism `F ⟶ G` of representing presheaves has `P`.

Forward: the given diagram becomes a diagram of morphisms of algebraic spaces and criterion (3)
of Stacks 06FA applies. Backward: test condition (2) on the diagram given by the two representing
equivalences.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_iff_represented
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (_h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (_h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val)
    (F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (eX : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒳.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eY : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒴.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P f ↔
      P (representingMap B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F G eX eY f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 06FM, and the definition of Stacks 06FN.** There is a
2-commutative square of algebraic spaces over `f` whose two vertical 1-morphisms are smooth,
