`k`-vector space structure on the tangent space available, so that the finite dimensionality
of `Tℱ` can be stated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_minimalPresentation [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Module.Finite Λ k]
    (p : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v v₃ w, w} Λ k)
    (hp : IsDeformationCategory.{u, max v v₃, w} p)
    [h𝓕 : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory.{u, max v v₃, w} (BasedCategory.ofFunctor p).p)]
    [Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (CategoryOfElements.π
      (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor p) h𝓕.out.cofibered)))]
    [FiniteDimensional k (tangentSpaceArtinian.{u, w, max v v₃} Λ k
      (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor p) h𝓕.out.cofibered))]
    (hInf : ∀ (x : F) (_hbase : p.obj x = residueFieldObject.{u, max v v₃, w} Λ k)
      (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt p x), FiniteDimensional k
        ↥((infinitesimalAutomorphismLinearLift.{u, max v v₃, w} PF hp.satisfiesRS).functor.obj
          (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{max v v₃} k)))) :
    Nonempty (MinimalPresentation.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} p hp.predeformation.cofibered)

declarations.name: Deformation.GroupoidInFunctors.nonempty_iso_of_presentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L3.** Let `ℱ` be a category cofibered in groupoids over `𝒞_Λ`.
If `ℱ` admits presentations by minimal smooth prorepresentable groupoids in functors
`(U, R, s, t, c)` and `(U', R', s', t', c')`, then the two are isomorphic.

The two presentations compose to an equivalence `[U/R] → [U'/R']` over `𝒞_Λ`. Both its
forward and its backward 1-morphism of quotients is induced, up to isomorphism of functors, by
a morphism of groupoids in functors, so the forward morphism induces an equivalence of the
quotients whose quasi-inverse is induced as well, and it is therefore an isomorphism by
Tag 06KR.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_of_presentations [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Module.Finite Λ k]
    {ℱ : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} ℱ] (p : ℱ ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k)
    (hp : Deformation.IsCofiberedInGroupoids p)
    (G H : GroupoidInFunctors.{_, max v w, max v w}
      (ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k))
    (hGpro : IsProrepresentable G) (hGsmooth : IsSmooth G) (hGmin : IsMinimal.{u, v, w, v} G)
    (hGpres : Deformation.Presentation G p)
    (hHpro : IsProrepresentable H) (hHsmooth : IsSmooth H) (hHmin : IsMinimal.{u, v, w, v} H)
    (hHpres : Deformation.Presentation H p) :
    Nonempty (G ≅ H)
declarations.comment: the statement is specialised to third universe `max v w`, that is `IsMinimal.{u, v, w, v}`, which is where Stacks 06KR and the Stacks 06KQ under it are fixed; `IsNoetherianRing Λ` and `Module.Finite Λ k` are the chapter's standing assumptions on Λ, which Stacks 06KQ consumes

declarations.name: Deformation.satisfiesRS_twoFibreProductOver
declarations.doc:
A 2-fibre product of categories satisfying condition (RS) again satisfies condition
(RS).
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesRS_twoFibreProductOver
    {Lambda : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Lambda] [Field k] [Algebra Lambda k]
    {H : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} H]
    {G : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} G]
    {F : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} F]
    (pH : H ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, v, w} Lambda k)
    (pG : G ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, v, w} Lambda k)
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, v, w} Lambda k)
    (f : H ⥤ F) (g : G ⥤ F)
    (hf : f ⋙ pF = pH) (hg : g ⋙ pF = pG)
    (hH : SatisfiesRS pH)
    (hG : SatisfiesRS pG)
    (hF : SatisfiesRS pF) :
    SatisfiesRS
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor pH pG pF f g)

declarations.name: Deformation.boundaryLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (2): the boundary map `δ : Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲` of the six-term
sequence, as a `k`-linear map**, at an arbitrary coordinate module. At the rank-one module this
is the third map of the six-term exact sequence of the `2`-fibre product.

This is the form of `δ` that the sequence of `k`-vector spaces asks for;
`Deformation.boundaryFun`, of which it is the linear reading, is a map of sets.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def boundaryLinearMap
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k) (f : H ⥤ F) (g : G ⥤ F)
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {y₀ : H} {z₀ : G} (hzy : (g ⋙ pF).obj z₀ = (f ⋙ pF).obj y₀)
    {cmp : f.obj y₀ ≅ g.obj z₀}
    (hcmp : pF.IsHomLift (𝟙 ((f ⋙ pF).obj y₀)) cmp.hom)
    (PH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) y₀) (PG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) z₀)
    (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj y₀)) (M : FGModuleCat.{max v w} k) :
    ↥((infinitesimalAutomorphismLinearLift PF hF.satisfiesRS).functor.obj M) →ₗ[k]
      ↥((productTangentLift.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).obj M)
declarations.comment: part (2), the boundary map `Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲` of the six-term exact sequence, as a `k`-linear map of the vector spaces of Tag 06IH

declarations.name: Deformation.isDeformationCategory_twoFibreProductOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (1).** The `2`-fibre product `𝒲 = ℋ ×_ℱ 𝒢` of two
`1`-morphisms of deformation categories over `𝒞_Λ` is again a deformation category.

Condition (RS) is Tag 06L4, and it carries the cofibered-in-groupoids condition with it; the
special fibre `𝒲(k)` has a unique isomorphism class because `ℋ(k)`, `𝒢(k)` and `ℱ(k)` do.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeformationCategory_twoFibreProductOver
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    {H : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} H]
    {G : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} G]
    {F : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} F]
    (pH : H ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k)
    (pG : G ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k)
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k)
    (f : H ⥤ F) (g : G ⥤ F)
    (hf : f ⋙ pF = pH) (hg : g ⋙ pF = pG)
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory pH)
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory pG)
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory pF) :
    IsDeformationCategory (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor pH pG pF f g)

declarations.name: Deformation.injective_infProjPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (2): exactness at `Inf(𝒲)`.** The map
`a : Inf(𝒲) → Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)` of the six-term sequence is injective, which is the `0 →` at
its source.

This is the source's "injectivity of the first map comes from the fact that
`f × g : 𝒲 → ℋ × 𝒢` is faithful": the induced map on infinitesimal automorphisms is
conjugation by the comparison of dual-number pushforwards
(`Deformation.inducedInfinitesimalLinearMap_apply`), so a tangent vector in the kernel of both
components is an automorphism of a pushforward of `w₀` whose two projections are identities,
and a self-arrow of the `2`-fibre product is determined by its two components
(`CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.Hom.ext'`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_infProjPair
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {w₀ : TwoFibreProductOver (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g}
    (PW : ChosenPushforwardsAt
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g) w₀)
    (QH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) w₀.x)
    (QG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) w₀.y) :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup PW
      (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule PW
      (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule QG hG.satisfiesRS
    Function.Injective (infProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF PW QH QG)
declarations.comment: part (2), the map `Inf(𝒲) → Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)` of the six-term exact sequence and the injectivity of it asserted at the first spot

declarations.name: Deformation.exact_infProjPair_infLegDiff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (2): exactness at `Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)`.** In the
`Inf`-row

`Inf(𝒲) → Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢) → Inf(ℱ)`

of the six-term sequence of the `2`-fibre product `𝒲 = ℋ ×_ℱ 𝒢`, the kernel of the difference
of the two outer legs is the image of the pair of the two projections.

This is the source's "if `(β, γ)` map to the same element of `Inf_{x₀}(ℱ)` then `(β, γ)`
defines an automorphism of `w'₀ = (k[ε], y'₀, z'₀, c' ∘ b')`". Each of the five maps in sight is
conjugation by a comparison of chosen pushforwards
(`Deformation.inducedInfinitesimalLinearMapOfEq_spec_iso`,
`Deformation.canonicalLocalizedTangentAutomorphismLinearEquiv_spec`), and
`Deformation.pushforwardIso_eq_comparison_comp` identifies the composite of those comparisons
with the comparison isomorphism carried by the chosen pushforward of `w₀`. The two halves are
then the two readings of one square: the comparison square of a self-arrow of that pushforward
gives the vanishing of the composite (`Deformation.eq_of_conjugation`), and conversely a pair
with equal images satisfies that square (`Deformation.square_of_conjugation`), hence defines a
self-arrow, which is automatically infinitesimal because the special fibre of `𝒲` is thin
(`Deformation.ker_transportAutHom_eq_top_of_isThin`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_infProjPair_infLegDiff
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {w₀ : TwoFibreProductOver (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g}
    (PW : ChosenPushforwardsAt
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g) w₀)
    (QH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) w₀.x)
    (QG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) w₀.y)
    (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj w₀.x))
    (PF' : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (g.obj w₀.y))
    (hw₀ : (f ⋙ pF).obj w₀.x = residueFieldObject.{u, v, w} Λ k) :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w} PW
      (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w} PW
      (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₁, v₁} QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₁, v₁} QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₂, v₂} QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₂, v₂} QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} PF hF.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} PF hF.satisfiesRS
    Function.Exact (infProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF PW QH QG)
      (infLegDiff.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF PF' hw₀)
declarations.comment: part (2), exactness at `Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)` of the six-term exact sequence

declarations.name: Deformation.exact_boundaryLinearMap_tangentProjPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (2), for the `k`-linear boundary map: exactness at `T𝒲`.**
The kernel of `c : T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢` is the image of the `k`-linear boundary map
`δ : Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲`.

That the composite vanishes is `Deformation.tangentProjPair_boundaryFun_eq_zero`, which holds for
every automorphism of `x'₀`. Conversely an element of the kernel is the class of a quadruple
`(k[M], y'₀, z'₀, c' ∘ α ∘ b')` by `Deformation.exists_aut_boundaryObject_tangentClassAt_eq`, and
that `α` is in the image of the linear lift because
`Deformation.ker_transportAutHom_squareZeroUnderRed_eq_top` makes the lift's value *all* of the
automorphisms of the pushforward, transport along
`Deformation.squareZeroCrossUnderIso` matching the two normalizations of the square-zero
extension.

This is the statement of part (2) at `T𝒲`: both of its maps are `k`-linear maps of the vector
spaces of Tag 06IH, and it carries neither the splitting of `k ⟶ k[M]` nor the hypothesis that
the basepoint lies over the residue field that the set-level
`Deformation.exact_boundaryFun_tangentProjPair` needs.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_boundaryLinearMap_tangentProjPair
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k) (f : H ⥤ F) (g : G ⥤ F)
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {y₀ : H} {z₀ : G} (hzy : (g ⋙ pF).obj z₀ = (f ⋙ pF).obj y₀)
    {cmp : f.obj y₀ ≅ g.obj z₀}
    (hcmp : pF.IsHomLift (𝟙 ((f ⋙ pF).obj y₀)) cmp.hom)
    (PH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) y₀) (PG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) z₀)
    (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj y₀)) (M : FGModuleCat.{max v w} k) :
    Function.Exact (boundaryLinearMap.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF hzy hcmp PH PG PF M)
      (tangentProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF M)
declarations.comment: part (2), exactness at `T𝒲` of the six-term exact sequence, for the `k`-linear boundary map `Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲` and the map `T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢`

declarations.name: Deformation.exact_tangentProjPair_tangentLegDiff
declarations.doc:
In the tangent row `T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢 → Tℱ` of the six-term sequence of the `2`-fibre product
`𝒲 = ℋ ×_ℱ 𝒢`, the kernel of the difference of the two outer legs is the image of the pair of
the two projections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_tangentProjPair_tangentLegDiff
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF) (M : FGModuleCat.{max v w} k) :
    Function.Exact (tangentProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF M)
      (tangentLegDiff.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF M)
declarations.comment: part (2), the tangent row `T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢 → Tℱ` of the six-term exact sequence and its exactness at `Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢`

declarations.name: Deformation.tangentProjPair_boundaryFun_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The boundary map `δ : Aut(x'₀) → T𝒲` of the six-term sequence lands in the kernel of the
map `c : T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tangentProjPair_boundaryFun_eq_zero
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k) (f : H ⥤ F) (g : G ⥤ F)
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {y₀ : H} {z₀ : G} (hzy : (g ⋙ pF).obj z₀ = (f ⋙ pF).obj y₀)
    {cmp : f.obj y₀ ≅ g.obj z₀}
    (hcmp : pF.IsHomLift (𝟙 ((f ⋙ pF).obj y₀)) cmp.hom)
    (PH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) y₀) (PG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) z₀)
    (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj y₀)) (M : FGModuleCat.{max v w} k)
    (α : Aut (PF.obj (squareZeroCrossUnder.{u, v, w} ((f ⋙ pF).obj y₀) M))) :
    tangentProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF M
        (boundaryFun.{u, v, w} f g hzy hcmp PH PG PF hF.predeformation.cofibered
          (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).predeformation
          (tangentConditionS2.{u, v, w}
            (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF)) M α) = 0
declarations.comment: part (2), that the boundary map of the six-term exact sequence lands in the kernel of `T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢`

declarations.name: Deformation.exact_infLegDiff_infBoundaryLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (2): exactness at `Inf(ℱ)`.** In the six-term sequence of
the `2`-fibre product `𝒲 = ℋ ×_ℱ 𝒢`, the kernel of the boundary map `δ : Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲` is the
image of the difference `b : Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢) → Inf(ℱ)` of the two outer legs.

This is the source's "if `α` gives the trivial deformation `(k[ε], y'₀, z'₀, c' ∘ α ∘ b')` of
`w₀`, then the isomorphism `w'₀ → δ(α)` produces a pair `(β, γ)` which is a preimage of `α`",
together with its converse. The class of the quadruple `δ(α)` vanishes exactly when `α`
satisfies the boundary square for some pair of automorphisms of `y'₀` and `z'₀`
(`Deformation.tangentClassAt_boundaryObject_eq_zero_iff`), and the boundary square says exactly
that `α` is the value of `b` on the pair those automorphisms define
(`Deformation.eq_comp_inv_iff_boundary_square`): the two maps `b` is the difference of are
conjugation by the comparisons of Tag 07W6 and Tag 06JV (2) at the dual numbers, and the three
transports `Deformation.transportAut_comp_boundaryCompareFst`,
`Deformation.map_cross_comp_boundaryCompareSnd` and
`Deformation.transportAut_comp_boundaryCompareSnd` carry those conjugations to the re-based
square-zero extension at which `δ` is built.

Every automorphism of a chosen pushforward to the dual numbers is infinitesimal, the special
fibre of a predeformation category being thin
(`Deformation.ker_transportAutHom_eq_top_of_isThin`), so the pair of automorphisms the square
produces does come from `Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)`. The sign the source defers is absorbed by reading
the difference as `-c(g(γ)) + f(β)`; the two orders agree because the tangent space is an
abelian group.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_infLegDiff_infBoundaryLinearMap
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {w₀ : TwoFibreProductOver (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g}
    (PW : ChosenPushforwardsAt
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g) w₀)
    (QH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) w₀.x)
    (QG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) w₀.y)
    (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj w₀.x))
    (PF' : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (g.obj w₀.y))
    (hw₀ : (f ⋙ pF).obj w₀.x = residueFieldObject.{u, v, w} Λ k) :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₁, v₁} QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₁, v₁} QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₂, v₂} QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₂, v₂} QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} PF hF.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} PF hF.satisfiesRS
    Function.Exact (infLegDiff.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF PF' hw₀)
      (infBoundaryLinearMap.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF)
declarations.comment: part (2), exactness at `Inf(ℱ)` of the six-term exact sequence, for the map `Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢) → Inf(ℱ)` and the boundary map `Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲`

declarations.name: Deformation.twoFibreProduct_sixTermExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L5, part (2): the six-term sequence**

`0 → Inf(𝒲) → Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢) → Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢 → Tℱ`

of the `2`-fibre product `𝒲 = ℋ ×_ℱ 𝒢` of deformation categories, with all five of its
`k`-linear maps and the exactness at every one of its five spots in one statement.

The five conjuncts are, in order: injectivity of `a` at `Inf(𝒲)` (the source's `0 →`,
`Deformation.injective_infProjPair`), exactness at `Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)`
(`Deformation.exact_infProjPair_infLegDiff`), exactness at `Inf(ℱ)`
(`Deformation.exact_infLegDiff_infBoundaryLinearMap`), exactness at `T𝒲`
(`Deformation.exact_boundaryLinearMap_tangentProjPair`, read through the model bridge of
`Deformation.infBoundaryLinearMap`) and exactness at `Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢`
(`Deformation.exact_tangentProjPair_tangentLegDiff`).

The basepoints are the images of one object `w₀` of `𝒲`, as in the source's "let `x₀, y₀, z₀`
be the image of `w₀`", and the tangent terms are taken at the rank-one coordinate module, at
which they are the tangent spaces of Tag 06IH.
declarations.statement:
public theorem twoFibreProduct_sixTermExact
    (hH : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (f ⋙ pF))
    (hG : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} (g ⋙ pF))
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF)
    {w₀ : TwoFibreProductOver (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g}
    (PW : ChosenPushforwardsAt
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (f ⋙ pF) (g ⋙ pF) pF f g) w₀)
    (QH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) w₀.x)
    (QG : ChosenPushforwardsAt (g ⋙ pF) w₀.y)
    (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj w₀.x))
    (PF' : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (g.obj w₀.y))
    (hw₀ : (f ⋙ pF).obj w₀.x = residueFieldObject.{u, v, w} Λ k) :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w} PW
      (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w} PW
      (isDeformationCategory_productBased.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₁, v₁} QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₁, v₁} QH hH.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₂, v₂} QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₂, v₂} QG hG.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} PF hF.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule.{u, v, w, u₃, v₃} PF hF.satisfiesRS
    Function.Injective (infProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF PW QH QG) ∧
      Function.Exact (infProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF PW QH QG)
          (infLegDiff.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF PF' hw₀) ∧
        Function.Exact (infLegDiff.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF PF' hw₀)
            (infBoundaryLinearMap.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF) ∧
          Function.Exact (infBoundaryLinearMap.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF QH QG PF)
              (tangentProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{v} k))) ∧
            Function.Exact
              (tangentProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{v} k)))
              (tangentLegDiff.{u, v, w} pF f g hH hG hF (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{v} k)))
declarations.comment: part (2), the six-term exact sequence `0 → Inf(𝒲) → Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢) → Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲 → Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢 → Tℱ` of a 2-fibre product of deformation categories, with its five `k`-linear maps and the exactness at all five of its spots: at `Inf(𝒲)`, at `Inf(ℋ) ⊕ Inf(𝒢)`, at `Inf(ℱ)`, at `T𝒲` and at `Tℋ ⊕ T𝒢`

declarations.name: Deformation.isDeformationFunctor_twoFibreProductOver_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L6, part (1).** Let `U : 𝒞_Λ → Sets` be a deformation functor,
`ℱ` a deformation category and `f : U → ℱ` a `1`-morphism of categories cofibered in
groupoids over `𝒞_Λ`. Then `𝒲 = U ×_{f, ℱ, f} U` is a deformation functor: it is a
deformation category, and every one of its infinitesimal automorphism groups vanishes, which
by Tag 06K0 is exactly the statement that it is cofibered in setoids, i.e. that it is a
functor.

The deformation-category half is Tag 06L5 part (1),
`Deformation.isDeformationCategory_twoFibreProductOver`, read through
`Deformation.isDeformationCategory_iff` for the two outer legs. The vanishing is the source's
"the fact that `Inf(U) = (0)`": the fibres of the category of elements of a set-valued functor
are thin (`Deformation.elementsFiber_isThin`), hence so are the fibres of the `2`-fibre
product (`Deformation.isThin_fibre_twoFibreProductOver`), and over a thin fibre there is no
room for a nontrivial automorphism at all.

The cofibered-in-groupoids witness is quantified over rather than taken from the first
component because `Deformation.IsCofiberedInGroupoids` is a proposition, so the infinitesimal
automorphism group does not depend on which witness is supplied.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeformationFunctor_twoFibreProductOver_self
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (U : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k ⥤ Type t)
    {F : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} F]
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k)
    (f : U.Elements ⥤ F)
    (hf : f ⋙ pF = CategoryOfElements.π U)
    (hU : IsDeformationFunctor U)
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory pF) :
    let p𝒲 := TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
      (CategoryOfElements.π U) (CategoryOfElements.π U) pF f f
    IsDeformationCategory p𝒲 ∧
      ∀ (hcof : IsCofiberedInGroupoids p𝒲)
        {A₀ Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k}
        {w₀ : p𝒲.Fiber A₀} {wε : p𝒲.Fiber Aε}
        (g : A₀ ⟶ Aε) (e : Aε ⟶ A₀) (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
        (i : w₀.1 ⟶ wε.1) (hi : p𝒲.IsHomLift g i),
        infinitesimalAutomorphisms hcof g e hpair i hi = ⊥
declarations.comment: part (1), that the 2-fibre product is a deformation functor; the exact sequence 0 → Inf(ℱ) → T(U ×_{f,ℱ,f} U) → TU ⊕ TU of part (2) is not covered

declarations.name: Deformation.exact_selfBoundaryLinearMap_tangentProjPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L6, part (2).** Let `U : 𝒞_Λ → Sets` be a deformation functor, `ℱ` a
deformation category and `f : U → ℱ` a `1`-morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids over
`𝒞_Λ`. Then the tangent space of `𝒲 = U ×_{f, ℱ, f} U` fits into an exact sequence of
`k`-vector spaces

`0 → Inf(ℱ) → T𝒲 → TU ⊕ TU`,

where the first map is the `k`-linear boundary map `δ` of the six-term sequence and the second
is the pair of the maps induced by the two projections. Exactness at `Inf(ℱ)` is injectivity of
`δ` and exactness at `T𝒲` is the kernel-equals-image statement; both maps are `k`-linear, and
the three terms are the `k`-vector spaces of Tag 06IH, taken at an arbitrary coordinate module.

Exactness at `T𝒲` is part (2) of Tag 06L5 for the two legs
(`Deformation.exact_boundaryLinearMap_tangentProjPair`). Exactness at `Inf(ℱ)` is what the self
`2`-fibre product adds, and it is the source's `Inf(U) = (0)`: the fibres of the category of
elements of a set-valued functor are thin
(`Deformation.isThin_fiber_comp_elementsProjection`), so an isomorphism between two quadruples
`(k[M], y'₀, y'₀, c' ∘ α ∘ b')` has both components the identity and its comparison square reads
`α = α'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_selfBoundaryLinearMap_tangentProjPair
    (U : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k ⥤ Type t)
    (pF : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w} Λ k) (f : U.Elements ⥤ F)
    (hf : f ⋙ pF = CategoryOfElements.π U) (hU : IsDeformationFunctor.{u, v, w} U)
    (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} pF) {y₀ : U.Elements}
    (PH : ChosenPushforwardsAt (f ⋙ pF) y₀) (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj y₀))
    (M : FGModuleCat.{max v w} k) :
    Function.Injective (selfBoundaryLinearMap.{u, v, w} pF U f
        (isDeformationCategory_comp_of_isDeformationFunctor.{u, v, w} U pF f hf hU) hF PH PF M) ∧
      Function.Exact
        (selfBoundaryLinearMap.{u, v, w} pF U f
          (isDeformationCategory_comp_of_isDeformationFunctor.{u, v, w} U pF f hf hU) hF PH PF M)
        (tangentProjPair.{u, v, w} pF f f
          (isDeformationCategory_comp_of_isDeformationFunctor.{u, v, w} U pF f hf hU)
          (isDeformationCategory_comp_of_isDeformationFunctor.{u, v, w} U pF f hf hU) hF M)
declarations.comment: part (2), the exact sequence of k-vector spaces 0 → Inf(ℱ) → T(U ×_{f,ℱ,f} U) → TU ⊕ TU

declarations.name: Deformation.isProrepresentable_presentationGroupoid
declarations.doc:
Let `ℱ` be a deformation category, let `U : 𝒞_Λ → Sets` be a prorepresentable functor and let
`f : U → ℱ` be a `1`-morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids. Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be the
groupoid in functors on `𝒞_Λ` constructed from `f` in Stacks 06KY. If `dim_k Inf(ℱ) < ∞`, then
`(U, R, s, t, c)` is prorepresentable.

The finite-dimensionality hypothesis is read at one basepoint `y₀` of `U` and one choice `PF` of
pushforwards there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProrepresentable_presentationGroupoid
    (hU : IsProrepresentable U) (hF : IsDeformationCategory.{u, max v v₃, w} pF)
    {y₀ : U.Elements} (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt pF (f.obj y₀))
    (hInf : FiniteDimensional k
      ↥((infinitesimalAutomorphismLinearLift.{u, max v v₃, w} PF hF.satisfiesRS).functor.obj
        (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{max v v₃} k)))) :
    GroupoidInFunctors.IsProrepresentable
      ((presentationGroupoid pF U f hover hF.predeformation.cofibered).toGroupoidInFunctors)
declarations.comment: the hom-set universe of ℱ is at most that of 𝒞_Λ: the base is written ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v v₃ w, w} with v₃ the hom-set universe of ℱ, because the criterion of 06KG part (2) is available only at value universe equal to the hom-set universe

declarations.name: Deformation.hasSmoothPresentation_iff_isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L8.** Let `ℱ` be a category cofibered in groupoids over `𝒞_Λ`.
Then `ℱ` admits a presentation by a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on `𝒞_Λ` if
and only if `ℱ` is a deformation category, `dim_k Tℱ` is finite and `dim_k Inf(ℱ)` is finite.

The direction from the three conditions to a presentation is Tag 06L2, whose minimal
presentation is in particular a smooth prorepresentable one; the converse is
`Deformation.isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory_of_hasSmoothPresentation`, which is parts
(1), (2) and (3) of Tag 06KU transported along the presentation. Being cofibered in groupoids
is not a hypothesis here: it is part of condition (1) on one side and a consequence of the
presentation on the other.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSmoothPresentation_iff_isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [Module.Finite Λ k] :
    HasSmoothPresentation.{u, v, w} p ↔ IsFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory.{u, v, w} p
declarations.comment: the tag in full: ℱ admits a presentation by a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on 𝒞_Λ iff (1) ℱ is a deformation category, (2) dim_k Tℱ is finite and (3) dim_k Inf(ℱ) is finite. Both directions, at the general universes of the chapter: ℱ has hom-set universe v and the base is ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, max v w, w}, with no universe equation imposed. The standing hypothesis of the source that ℱ be cofibered in groupoids is not carried: it is part of condition (1) on one side, and on the other it is derived from the presentation by Deformation.isCofiberedInGroupoids_of_equivalenceOver. The forward direction goes through Stacks 06L2 rather than through the construction of Stacks 06L8 itself, which Deformation.exists_isSmooth_isProrepresentable_presentation carries at the restricted universe

declarations.name: Deformation.exists_isSmooth_isProrepresentable_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06L8**, the existence direction. A category `ℱ` cofibered in
groupoids over `𝒞_Λ` which is a deformation category and whose tangent space and space of
infinitesimal automorphisms are finite-dimensional over `k` has a presentation by a smooth
prorepresentable groupoid in functors on `𝒞_Λ`.

The proof of the source. Condition (RS) gives (S1) and (S2) by Tag 06J7, so Schlessinger's
existence theorem, Tag 06IW, produces a versal formal object `ξ` over a complete local algebra
`R` from the finite-dimensionality of the tangent space. Put `U = R̲|_{𝒞_Λ}`; the associated
morphism `ξ̲ : U → ℱ` of Tag 06HC is smooth, which is what versality of `ξ` says, and the
groupoid in functors `(U, R, s, t, c)` built from it is the one of Tag 06KY. Tag 06L1 makes it
smooth and its quotient morphism an equivalence — the quotient morphism is an equivalence
because `ξ̲` is essentially surjective, which follows from smoothness together with essential
surjectivity on the special fibre, and the latter holds because the special fibre of `ℱ` is
equivalent to a point. Tag 06L7 makes it prorepresentable from the finite-dimensionality of
the infinitesimal automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSmooth_isProrepresentable_presentation
    (p : F ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k)
    (hp : IsDeformationCategory.{u, w, w} p)
    (hT : FiniteDimensional k
      ↥(tangentModuleAt.{u, w, w} (BasedCategory.ofFunctor p) hp
        (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{w} k))))
    (hInf : ∀ (x : F) (P : ChosenPushforwardsAt p x),
      p.obj x = residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k →
      FiniteDimensional k
        ↥((infinitesimalAutomorphismLinearLift.{u, w, w} P hp.satisfiesRS).functor.obj
          (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{w} k)))) :
    ∃ G : GroupoidInFunctors.{_, w, w} (ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k),
      GroupoidInFunctors.IsSmooth G ∧
        GroupoidInFunctors.IsProrepresentable.{u, w, w, w} G ∧
          Nonempty (Presentation G p)
declarations.comment: the construction of the tag's existence direction: (1)(2)(3) ⟹ ℱ admits a presentation by a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on 𝒞_Λ, built as the source builds it, from a versal formal object and the groupoid in functors of 06KY. Only that direction, and only when the hom-set universe of ℱ equals that of k, the restriction 06L7 carries here. The tag in full — the biconditional, at the general universes, both directions — is Deformation.hasSmoothPresentation_iff_isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory, whose existence direction goes through 06L2 instead and whose converse direction is Deformation.isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory_of_hasSmoothPresentation, proved from part (3) of 06KU, Inf([U/R]) = Ker(ds ⊕ dt), which the library now has as Deformation.quotientInfinitesimalBoundary_exact

declarations.name: exists_isRegular_map_length_eq_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
The main theorem (Stacks Tag 06LC).  Reduce to the engine lemma at `d` the finite value

declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRegular_map_length_eq_ringKrullDim {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.flat_directSum
declarations.doc:
For a Noetherian ring `R` and an ideal `I`, the `I`-adic completion `(⊕_{α ∈ A} R)^∧` of an

    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (A : Type v) [IsNoetherianRing R] :

declarations.doc:
A zero-dimensional scheme locally of finite type over a field is, over that field, a
coproduct of spectra of finite-dimensional local Artinian algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_coproduct_spec_local_artinian_of_dimension_zero
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 0) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (A : I → Type u)

      (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k (A i))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_regularImmersion_flat_of_isRegular_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 37.24.1 (Tag 06LI).**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite
presentation and flat at `x : X`, and let `h : Fin r → 𝒪_{X, x}` be a family whose image in the
local ring of the fibre `X_{f x}` at `x` is a regular sequence.  Then there is an affine open `U`
containing `x` and global sections `a : Fin r → Γ(U, ⊤)` whose germs at `x` are the `h i`, such
that `x` lies on the zero scheme `V(a)`, the closed immersion of `V(a)` into `U` is a regular
immersion, `V(a)` is flat and locally of finite presentation over `S`, and the base change of
the immersion along any `S' ⟶ S` is again a regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_regularImmersion_flat_of_isRegular_fiber
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) {r : ℕ}
    (h : Fin r → X.presheaf.stalk x) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x)
    (hregular : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular
      ((f.fiber (f x)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber x))
      (List.ofFn fun i : Fin r =>
        ((f.fiberι (f x)).stalkMap (f.asFiber x)).hom ((f.fiberι_asFiber x).symm ▸ h i))) :
    ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (hx : x ∈ U.1) (a : Fin r → Γ(U.1.toScheme, ⊤)),
      let y : U.1.toScheme := ⟨x, hx⟩
      let I : U.1.toScheme.IdealSheafData :=
        Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop (Ideal.ofList (List.ofFn a))
      (∀ i : Fin r, (U.1.ι.stalkMap y).hom ((show U.1.ι y = x by rfl).symm ▸ h i) =
          U.1.toScheme.presheaf.germ ⊤ y (by trivial) (a i)) ∧
      y ∈ I.support ∧
      IsRegularImmersion I.subschemeι ∧
      Flat (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι ≫ f) ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (I.subschemeι ≫ U.1.ι ≫ f) ∧
      ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S),
        IsRegularImmersion (pullback.snd I.subschemeι (pullback.fst (U.1.ι ≫ f) g))

declarations.name: isNoetherianRing_iff_henselizations_and_completion_properties
declarations.doc:
A local ring is Noetherian if and only if its henselization is, if and only if its strict
henselization is. In that case the latter two rings have complete Noetherian local completions;
completion does not change the henselization, both completion maps are flat, the map from the
completed ring to the completed strict henselization is formally smooth, strict henselization
commutes with base change to the completion, and completing once more gives the completed strict
henselization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNoetherianRing_iff_henselizations_and_completion_properties.{u, v, w}
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh] :
    let Rhat := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R
    let Rhhat := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Rh) Rh
    let Rshhat := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Rsh) Rsh
    ((IsNoetherianRing R ↔ IsNoetherianRing Rh) ∧
      (IsNoetherianRing R ↔ IsNoetherianRing Rsh)) ∧
    (∀ [Algebra Rh Rsh] [IsScalarTower R Rh Rsh]
      [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Rh Rsh)], IsNoetherianRing R →
      ∃ (hRhatLocal : IsLocalRing Rhat)
        (hRhhatLocal : IsLocalRing Rhhat)
        (hRshhatLocal : IsLocalRing Rshhat),
      letI : IsLocalRing Rhat := hRhatLocal
      letI : IsLocalRing Rhhat := hRhhatLocal
      letI : IsLocalRing Rshhat := hRshhatLocal
      IsNoetherianRing Rhhat ∧ IsNoetherianRing Rshhat ∧
      IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal Rhhat) Rhhat ∧
      IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal Rshhat) Rshhat ∧
      ∃ e : Rhat ≃+* Rhhat,
        (∀ x : R, e (algebraMap R Rhat x) =
          algebraMap Rh Rhhat (algebraMap R Rh x)) ∧
        RingHom.Flat (algebraMap Rh Rhhat) ∧
        RingHom.Flat (algebraMap Rsh Rshhat) ∧
        (∃ f : Rhat →+* Rshhat,
          (∀ x : R, f (algebraMap R Rhat x) =
            algebraMap Rsh Rshhat (algebraMap R Rsh x)) ∧
          (letI : TopologicalSpace Rhat := (maximalIdeal Rhat).adicTopology
           letI : IsTopologicalRing Rhat :=
             (maximalIdeal Rhat).nonarchimedean.toIsTopologicalRing
           letI : IsLinearTopology Rhat Rhat := (maximalIdeal Rhat).isLinearTopology
           letI : TopologicalSpace Rshhat := (maximalIdeal Rshhat).adicTopology
           letI : IsTopologicalRing Rshhat :=
             (maximalIdeal Rshhat).nonarchimedean.toIsTopologicalRing
           letI : IsLinearTopology Rshhat Rshhat := (maximalIdeal Rshhat).isLinearTopology
           IsFormallySmooth.{w} f)) ∧
        (let algRhRhat : Algebra Rh Rhat :=
            (e.symm.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap Rh Rhhat)).toAlgebra
         letI : Algebra Rh Rhat := algRhRhat
         ∃ hRhatMapLocal : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R Rhat),
           letI : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R Rhat) := hRhatMapLocal
           ∃ algKhat : Algebra (ResidueField Rhat) κsep,
           letI : Algebra (ResidueField Rhat) κsep := algKhat
           (∀ x : ResidueField R,
             algebraMap (ResidueField Rhat) κsep
                 (ResidueField.map (algebraMap R Rhat) x) =
               algebraMap (ResidueField R) κsep x) ∧
           IsSepClosure (ResidueField Rhat) κsep ∧
           ∃ hTensorLocal : IsLocalRing (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh),
           letI : IsLocalRing (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh) := hTensorLocal
           IsHenselization Rhat κsep (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh) ∧
           ∃ ef : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh))
               (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh) ≃+* Rshhat,
             ∀ x : Rsh,
               ef (algebraMap (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh)
                   (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh))
                     (Rhat ⊗[Rh] Rsh))
                   (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight x)) =
                 algebraMap Rsh Rshhat x))

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_eq_henselization_eq_strictHenselization
declarations.doc: A local ring, its henselization, and its strict henselization have equal Krull dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_eq_henselization_eq_strictHenselization
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (κpsep : Type v) [Field κpsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κpsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κpsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κpsep Rsh] :
    ringKrullDim R = ringKrullDim Rh ∧ ringKrullDim Rh = ringKrullDim Rsh

declarations.doc: A Noetherian local ring, its henselization, and its strict henselization have equal depth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringDepth_eq_henselization_eq_strictHenselization
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh] :
    ringDepth R = ringDepth Rh ∧ ringDepth Rh = ringDepth Rsh

declarations.name: isMaximalCohenMacaulay_iff_henselizations
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if its henselization is, and if and
only if its strict henselization is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMaximalCohenMacaulay_iff_henselizations
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (ksep : Type v) [Field ksep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) ksep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) ksep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R ksep Rsh] :
    (Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R ↔ Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay Rh Rh) ∧
      (Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R R ↔ Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay Rsh Rsh)

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_iff_henselizations
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local ring is regular if and only if its henselization is regular, and if and
only if its strict henselization is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularLocalRing_iff_henselizations
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh] :
    (IsRegularLocalRing R ↔ IsRegularLocalRing Rh) ∧
      (IsRegularLocalRing R ↔ IsRegularLocalRing Rsh)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFiniteAt_of_dimensionAtPoint_fiber_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06LS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type, let `p` be a field-valued point of `Y` — a morphism `Spec k ⟶ Y` from
the spectrum of a field over `S` — and let `z` be a point of the fibre `X ×_Y Spec k` at which
that fibre has dimension `0` in the sense of Stacks 04N5. Then `f` is quasi-finite at the image
of `z`: after replacing `X` by an open subspace containing that image, `f` is locally
quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFiniteAt_of_dimensionAtPoint_fiber_eq_zero (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS G)
    (z : points B S hS (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)))
    (hz : dimensionAtPoint B S hS (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value))
      (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) hX
        (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS (p.siteObject B S hS G)) hY) z = 0) :
    IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f
      (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value))
        (pullback.fst f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)) z)

Only the target has to be an algebraic space, where the source requires both.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_of_isFlat_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06LU.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
presentation, flat and unramified is étale.

Lift an atlas `q` of the target through `f` by [Stacks Project, Tag 02X1] to a surjective
étale chart `p` of the source over a morphism `α` of the site. The three hypotheses, read on
that one square, say that the scheme morphism underlying `α` is locally of finite
presentation, flat and unramified, hence formally unramified by [Stacks Project, Tag 02HE]
and therefore étale. One such square suffices by condition (4) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 03FS].
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_of_isFlat_of_isUnramified (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hunr : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsEtale B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isFlat_vanishingSubfunctor_of_isRegular_geometricFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06LW, the flatness half of the conclusion.**  Let `g : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat and locally of finite presentation, let
`f₁, …, f_r ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, let `Spec k ⟶ Y` be a field-valued point of the target, let
`ξ : F ⟶ X` and `π : F ⟶ Spec k` present `F` as the fibre `X ×_Y Spec k` and let `z` be a
geometric point of `F` at which the images of the `f_i` in the étale local ring `𝒪_{F, z̄}` form
a regular sequence.

Then there is an open subspace `W ⊆ X` containing the image of `z` such that
`V(f₁, …, f_r) ∩ W ⟶ Y` is flat.

The hypothesis is taken in the form the source's conclusion is used in — quantified over the
small étale neighbourhoods of the image of `z` in `X` — which is the same condition for one
neighbourhood as for all, the image of a germ of a global function under the comparison
homomorphism of Stacks 04NG not depending on the neighbourhood.  It is the form in which
Stacks 06MD states it, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FibreIsRegularSequenceAt`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isFlat_vanishingSubfunctor_of_isRegular_geometricFiber
    (X Y F : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X.1 ⟶ Y.1)
    (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g) (hglfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    {r : ℕ} (fs : Fin r → (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)).sections)
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (t : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ Y.1)
    (ξ : F ⟶ X) {π : F.1 ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS))}
    (sq : IsPullback ξ.hom π g t)
    (z : GeometricPoint B S hS F.1)
    (hreg : ∀ Nx : SmallEtaleNeighborhood (geometricPointMap ξ.hom z),
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (etaleLocalRing B S hS F.1 z)
        (List.ofFn fun i : Fin r => etaleLocalRingMap F.2 ξ.hom z
          (etaleLocalRingGerm B S hS X.1 (geometricPointMap ξ.hom z) (op Nx)
            ((fs i).eval (op Nx.chart))))) :
    ∃ (W : Subfunctor X.1) (_ : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W),
      pointsMap B S hS F.1 ξ.hom z.image ∈
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι) ∧
        IsFlat B S hS (((vanishingSubfunctor B S hS X fs).preimage W.ι).ι ≫ W.ι ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the flatness half of the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_vanishingSubfunctor_comp
declarations.doc:
If `X ⟶ Y` is locally of finite presentation and the closed immersion of the subspace
`V(f₁, …, f_r) ⊆ X` cut out by global regular functions `f₁, …, f_r` is locally of finite
presentation, then so is `V(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_vanishingSubfunctor_comp (X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (g : X.1 ⟶ Y.1) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)).sections)
    (hslice : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (vanishingSubfunctor B S hS X f).ι)
    (hg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS ((vanishingSubfunctor B S hS X f).ι ≫ g)
declarations.comment: locally of finite presentation, given it for V(f₁,…,f_r) ⟶ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_openSubspace_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_vanishingSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `X ⟶ Y` be flat and locally of finite presentation, let a cartesian square exhibit `F`
as the fibre `X ×_Y Spec(k)` over a field-valued point of `Y`, and let `z` be a geometric point of
`F` at which the `f_i` map to a regular sequence in `𝒪_{F, z̄}`.  Then there is an open subspace
`V ⊆ X` containing `p(z)` over which `V(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ Y` is flat and locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubspace_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_vanishingSubfunctor
    (X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X.1 ⟶ Y.1) (pt : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y.1)
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (p : F ⟶ X.1)
    (q : F ⟶ yoneda.obj (FieldValuedPoint.siteObject B S hS Y.1 pt))
    (hcart : IsPullback p q g (yonedaEquiv.symm pt.value)) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)).sections)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS g) (hg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (z : GeometricPoint B S hS F)
    (hreg : FibreIsRegularSequenceAt B S hS X f hF p z) :
    ∃ (V : Subfunctor X.1) (_ : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V),
      pointsMap B S hS F p z.image ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        IsFlat B S hS (((vanishingSubfunctor B S hS X f).preimage V.ι).ι ≫ V.ι ≫ g) ∧
          IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
            (((vanishingSubfunctor B S hS X f).preimage V.ι).ι ≫ V.ι ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_of_comp_of_cover
declarations.doc:
A relative property local on the source descends along a representable
covering of the intermediate fibred category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasRelativeProperty_of_comp_of_cover
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage B S hS)]
    (τ : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Topology)
    (hτ : τ = .etale ∨ τ = .smooth ∨ τ = .syntomic ∨ τ = .fppf)
    [P.IsLocalAtSource (τ.precoverage B S hS)]
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (hg : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom)
    (hcover :
      ∀ (U : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.based.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.based.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.based.p 𝒴.based.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        let a := AlgebraicGeometry.algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((AlgebraicGeometry.spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2
            hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSurjective B S hS a.hom ∧
          (match τ with
          | .etale => AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale B S hS a.hom
          | .smooth => AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmooth B S hS a.hom
          | .syntomic => AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSyntomic B S hS a.hom
          | .fppf =>
              AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat B S hS a.hom ∧
                AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS a.hom
          | .fpqc => False)))
    (hcomp : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRelativeProperty B S hS P (f ≫ g)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comp B S hS f g hf hg)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRelativeProperty B S hS P g hg

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isRelativePropertyLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M3, assertion (A), uniqueness of the maximal open substack.** Two open substacks
of `𝒳` on which `f` has `P` and which are maximal with that property coincide: each is contained
in the other, and an open substack is determined by its object property.

This is what makes the definite article in *the* maximal open substack of the source legitimate,
and it needs no input beyond those of the ambient site.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_isRelativePropertyLocus (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage B S hS)]
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    {hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom} {W W' : OpenSubstack 𝒳}
    (h : IsRelativePropertyLocus B S hS P f hf W)
    (h' : IsRelativePropertyLocus B S hS P f hf W') :
    W = W'
declarations.comment: assertion (A), uniqueness of the maximal open substack on which f has P; unconditional

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isRelativePropertyLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M3, assertion (A), the existence of the maximal open substack.** A 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic spaces has an open substack
of `𝒳` on which it restricts to a 1-morphism with the relative property `P` of **Stacks 03YK**
and which contains every open substack with that property.

It is the union `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.iUnion` (**Stacks 05UQ**) of the set of
all open substacks on which `f` has `P`: that `f` has `P` on it is the carried `hLocal`, and
maximality is the first clause of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.OpenSubstack.IsUnion` and does not
need it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativePropertyLocus (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage B S hS)]
    (hLocal : IsRelativePropertyLocalOnOpenSubstackUnions.{u, w} B S hS P)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    ∃ W : OpenSubstack 𝒳, IsRelativePropertyLocus B S hS P f hf W
declarations.comment: assertion (A), existence of the maximal open substack on which f has P, with the locality of P along a union of open substacks carried as `hLocal`; the property Q of the source is not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativePropertyLocus_baseChange_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M3, assertion (B), the containment `g'^{-1}𝒳' ⊆ 𝒳''`.** Let `Q` be a 2-fibre
product square over the cospan `(g, f)`, so that `Q.fst` is the base change of
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` along `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` and `Q.snd` is the projection to `𝒳`. Let `W` be the `P`-locus
of `f` and `W'` the `P`-locus of `Q.fst`. Then every object of the apex carried by `Q.snd` into
`W` lies in `W'`.

This is one of the two containments assertion (B) asserts, and it holds for an **arbitrary** base
change: the property `R` of the source is not used, nor is `Q`. The inverse image of `W` along
`Q.snd` is the 2-fibre product `(𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳) ×_𝒳 W`, which by pasting (**Stacks 003Q**) is also
`W ×_𝒴 𝒵`, so its projection to `𝒵` is a base change of `f|_W` and has `P` by **Stacks 045C**;
maximality of `W'` finishes.

The reverse containment, which is where the hypotheses on `R` enter, is not proved; see the
module documentation.
declarations.comment: assertion (B), the containment 𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳' ⊆ W(P, f') of the base change of the maximal open substack in the maximal open substack of the base change, for an arbitrary base change and with neither the property R nor the property Q used; the reverse containment, which is where R enters, is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isRelativePropertyLocus_of_hasRelativePropertyLocusOnSpaces
declarations.doc:
**The existence of the maximal open substack on which a relative property holds.** Let `P`,
`Q`, `R` be properties of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which are fppf local on the target
and stable under arbitrary base change, with smoothness implying `R`, with every morphism of
algebraic spaces having `Q` carrying a greatest open subspace of its source on which it has `P`,
and with that greatest open subspace compatible with base change along a morphism with `R`. Then
a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic spaces and
having `Q` has an open substack of `𝒳` on which it restricts to a 1-morphism with the relative
property `P` of **Stacks 03YK** and which contains every open substack with that property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativePropertyLocus_of_hasRelativePropertyLocusOnSpaces
    (P Q R : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)]
    [Q.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [Q.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)]
    [R.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [R.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)]
    (hsmR : SmoothImplies B S hS R)
    (h3 : HasRelativePropertyLocusOnSpaces B S hS P Q)
    (h4 : RelativePropertyLocusBaseChange B S hS P Q R)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom)
    (hQf : HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS Q f.hom hf) :
    ∃ W : OpenSubstack 𝒳, IsRelativePropertyLocus B S hS P f hf W
declarations.comment: assertion (A), the existence of the largest open substack of the source on which a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces and having Q has P, from the four hypotheses of the source on P, Q and R, by the chart construction of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativePropertyLocus_baseChange_apply_symm
declarations.doc:
**The locus of a base change is carried into the locus.** Let `P`, `Q`, `R` be properties of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` satisfying the hypotheses of Stacks 06M3, let
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces having `Q`, let `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be
representable by algebraic spaces having `R` and let `D` be a 2-fibre product square over the
cospan `(g, f)`. If `W` is the `P`-locus of `f` and `W'` the `P`-locus of the base change
`D.fst`, then every object of the apex lying in `W'` is carried by `D.snd` into `W`: that is,
`W(P, f') ⊆ 𝒵 ×_𝒴 W(P, f)`.
declarations.comment: assertion (B), the maximality half: the locus of the base change is carried into the locus of the 1-morphism, so that together with the containment proved above the base change of the locus is the locus of the base change. From the four hypotheses of the source on P, Q and R, with Q for the 1-morphism and R for the base change as the source has them, by the source's chart construction run at one more base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.le_maximalFlatOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M4, the instantiation: maximality in hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at
`P = flat` and `Q = empty`.** Every open subspace of the source on which the morphism is flat
is contained in the largest flat open: it is a member of the family that open is the supremum
of. No hypothesis on the morphism is needed, which is what `Q = empty` means.
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at P = flat, Q = empty: maximality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_maximalFlatOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M4, the instantiation: openness in hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at
`P = flat` and `Q = empty`.** The largest flat open of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
is an open subspace of the source. No hypothesis on the morphism is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_maximalFlatOpen (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f)
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at P = flat, Q = empty: openness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_maximalFlatOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M4, the instantiation: flatness in hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at
`P = flat` and `Q = empty`.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat on its largest
flat open. No hypothesis on the morphism is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_maximalFlatOpen (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsFlat B S hS ((maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at P = flat, Q = empty: flatness on the open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_eq_interior
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M4, the warning.** The point set of the largest open subspace of the source on
which a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat is the *interior*, in the point space of
Stacks 03BU, of the set of points at which the morphism is flat.

This is the structural statement behind the warning of Stacks 06M4: the open subspace that the
construction of Stacks 06M3 produces at `P = flat` is characterised by a universal property —
largest open on whose restriction the morphism is flat — and that universal property computes
the interior of the pointwise flat locus, not the locus. Flatness at a point is the germ
condition of Stacks 03ML part (2), which does not quantify over neighbourhoods, so no
hypothesis on the morphism makes the interior superfluous for free.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_eq_interior (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).toFunctor
        (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).ι) =
      interior {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: the warning: the largest flat open is the interior of the flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_eq_setOf_isFlatAt_iff_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M4, the warning.** The largest open subspace of the source on which a morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat has the pointwise flat locus as its point set if and only
if that locus is open.

This is the warning of Stacks 06M4 in sharp form. The literal reading of the remark — that
the two are *not* equal — is the statement that the right-hand side fails for some morphism,
i.e. that the flat locus of some morphism of algebraic spaces is not open; such a morphism
exists, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_ne_setOf_isFlatAt` derives the
literal reading from this equivalence by `Iff.not`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_eq_setOf_isFlatAt_iff_isOpen
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).toFunctor
        (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x} ↔
      IsOpen {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: the warning: equality with the flat locus holds exactly when it is open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_ne_setOf_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M4, the warning, in its literal form.** There is a morphism of algebraic spaces
whose largest flat open subspace does *not* have as its point set the set of points at which
the morphism is flat.

The witness is the morphism of schemes of `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flat_locus_not_open` —
the inclusion of `ℤ` into the trivial square-zero extension of `ℤ` by `⨁_p ℤ/p` — read as a
morphism of representable algebraic spaces over a big fppf site large enough to contain its
source and target. By
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_eq_setOf_isFlatAt_iff_isOpen` it is
enough that its pointwise flat locus is not open, and for a morphism of representable
presheaves the flat locus of the morphism of algebraic spaces is cut out by the flat locus of
the morphism of schemes, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_yoneda_iff` and the correspondence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_yoneda_iff_isSchemeOpen` of Stacks 03BX.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_range_pointsMap_maximalFlatOpen_ne_setOf_isFlatAt :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
      (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y),
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).toFunctor
          (maximalFlatOpen B S hS f).ι) ≠
        {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: the warning: for some morphism the largest flat open is not the flat locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isGreatest_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (2), hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3.** For `𝒬 = ` locally of finite
type and `𝒫 = ` locally quasi-finite: every morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is locally of finite type has a largest open subspace of `X` on which it is locally
quasi-finite.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart`, the open subspace of **Stacks 04NW**,
which is the case `d = 0` of the first entry by **Stacks 04NV**.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
        IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (2), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3.** In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite type, any largest
open subspace of the source of the base change `f'` on which `f'` is locally quasi-finite is the
inverse image of any largest open subspace of `X` on which `f` is locally quasi-finite.

The source writes `ℛ = ∅` for this entry, and no condition is imposed on the base change. Both
greatest elements are the canonical open subspaces of **Stacks 04NW**, whose formation commutes
with arbitrary base change,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinitePart_preimage_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W)
    (W' : {W' : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W'})
    (hW' : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f')} W') :
    W'.1 = W.1.preimage g'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isGreatest_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (3), hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3.** For `𝒫 = ` unramified: every
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` has a largest open subspace of `X` on which it
is unramified, and its point set is the set of points at which `f` is unramified.

This is **Stacks 05W2**, part (1): the set of points at which `f` is unramified is open, the
corresponding open subspace (**Stacks 03BZ**) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedLocus`, and
an open subspace on which `f` is unramified is one at all of whose points `f` is unramified. The
entry's `𝒬`, locally of finite type, is not needed for this hypothesis; it is needed for (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_isUnramified
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
        IsUnramified B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.1.toFunctor W.1.ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X | IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (3), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3.** In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite type, any largest
open subspace of the source of the base change `f'` on which `f'` is unramified is the inverse
image of any largest open subspace of `X` on which `f` is unramified.

The source writes `ℛ = ∅` for this entry, and no condition is imposed on the base change. By
hypothesis (3) both open subspaces are the loci of points at which the morphisms are
unramified, and those correspond under base change by **Stacks 05W2**, part (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramifiedAt_iff_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isUnramified
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsUnramified B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W)
    (W' : {W' : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W'})
    (hW' : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsUnramified B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f')} W') :
    W'.1 = W.1.preimage g'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isGreatest_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (4), hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3.** For `𝒬 = ` locally of finite
presentation and `𝒫 = ` flat: every morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite presentation has a largest open subspace of `X` on which it is flat, and its
point set is exactly the set of points at which `f` is flat.

The set of points at which `f` is flat is open by **Stacks 05WV** for the structure sheaf,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_isFlatAt`, and an open subspace on which `f` is flat is one
at all of whose points `f` is flat. The second clause is the source's remark that, because `f`
has `𝒬`, `W(𝒫, f)` is the set of points at which `f` is flat; without `𝒬` it is only the interior
of that set, which is the warning of **Stacks 06M4**.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_isFlat
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
        IsFlat B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.1.toFunctor W.1.ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X | IsFlatAt B S hS f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (4), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3.** In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite presentation and
whose bottom arrow `g` is flat, any largest open subspace of the source of the base change `f'`
on which `f'` is flat is the inverse image of any largest open subspace of `X` on which `f` is
flat.

The entry's `ℛ` is flat and locally of finite presentation; only flatness of `g` is used. By
hypothesis (3) both open subspaces are the loci of points at which the morphisms are flat, the
base change being locally of finite presentation as well, and those correspond under a flat
base change, which is **Stacks 05WW** for the structure sheaf,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_iff_of_isPullback_of_isFlat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isFlat
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsFlat B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W)
    (W' : {W' : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W'})
    (hW' : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsFlat B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f')} W') :
    W'.1 = W.1.preimage g'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isGreatest_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (5), hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3.** For `𝒬 = ` locally of finite
presentation and `𝒫 = ` étale: every morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite presentation has a largest open subspace of `X` on which it is étale, and its
point set is the set of points at which `f` is both unramified and flat.

This combines entries (3) and (4): the two sets of points are open, and on an open subspace `f`
is étale exactly when it is unramified and flat there, because an unramified morphism which is
flat and locally of finite presentation is étale (**Stacks 06LU**).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_isEtale
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
        IsEtale B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.1.toFunctor W.1.ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X | IsUnramifiedAt B S hS f x ∧ IsFlatAt B S hS f x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, entry (5), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3.** In a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of finite presentation and
whose bottom arrow `g` is flat, any largest open subspace of the source of the base change `f'`
on which `f'` is étale is the inverse image of any largest open subspace of `X` on which `f` is
étale.

The entry's `ℛ` is flat and locally of finite presentation; only flatness of `g` is used. By
hypothesis (3) both open subspaces are the loci of points at which the morphisms are unramified
and flat, and both conditions correspond under the base change: unramifiedness under any base
change (**Stacks 05W2**, part (2)) and flatness under a flat one (**Stacks 05WW** for the
structure sheaf).
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_isEtale
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsEtale B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W)
    (W' : {W' : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W'})
    (hW' : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      IsEtale B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f')} W') :
    W'.1 = W.1.preimage g'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isGreatest_hasRelativeDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, first entry, hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3.** For `𝒬 = ` locally of finite
type and `𝒫 = ` relative dimension `≤ d` (**Stacks 06LR**): every morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type has a largest open subspace of `X` on
which it has relative dimension `≤ d`.

The open subspace is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeDimensionPart`, built from the
openness statement **Stacks 04NT** through the correspondence of **Stacks 03BZ**; the two
clauses of being greatest are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeDimensionLE_boundedRelativeDimensionPart` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.le_boundedRelativeDimensionPart`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_hasRelativeDimensionLE (d : ℕ)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W},
      IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
        HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W
declarations.comment: entry (1), hypothesis (3) of Stacks 06M3 at 𝒬 = locally of finite type and 𝒫 = relative dimension ≤ d: the existence of a largest open subspace of the source on which the morphism has relative dimension ≤ d, from Stacks 06LR and Stacks 04NT

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeDimensionPart_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, first entry, hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3, for the canonical open
subspace.** In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f`
is locally of finite type, the base change `f'` is locally of finite type and its open subspace
of relative dimension `≤ d` is the inverse image of that of `f`.

No condition is imposed on the base change: the source writes `ℛ = ∅` for this entry, and
**Stacks 04NS** gives the invariance of the relative dimension at a point under an arbitrary
base change. On points both sides are the locus of relative dimension at most `d`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_boundedRelativeDimensionPart` and the identification of
the point set of an inverse image; the two open subspaces then agree because **Stacks 03BZ** is
injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedRelativeDimensionPart_preimage_of_isPullback (d : ℕ)
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ hf' : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f',
      (boundedRelativeDimensionPart B S hS d hX' hY' f' hf').1 =
        (boundedRelativeDimensionPart B S hS d hX hY f hf).1.preimage g'
declarations.comment: entry (1), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3 at 𝒬 = locally of finite type and 𝒫 = relative dimension ≤ d, for the canonical open subspace: the formation of the largest open subspace commutes with base change, for an arbitrary base change since the entry's ℛ is ∅, from Stacks 04NS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_hasRelativeDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, first entry, hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3, in the form the lemma consumes.**
