In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f` is locally of
finite type, any largest open subspace of the source of the base change on which the base
change has relative dimension `≤ d` is the inverse image of any largest open subspace of `X` on
which `f` has relative dimension `≤ d`.

**Stacks 06M3** takes hypothesis (4) in this shape, quantified over largest open subspaces
rather than over a chosen one. A greatest element of an ordered type is unique, so both are the
canonical `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeDimensionPart` and the statement reduces to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.boundedRelativeDimensionPart_preimage_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_preimage_of_isGreatest_hasRelativeDimensionLE (d : ℕ)
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (W : {W : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W})
    (hW : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f)} W)
    (W' : {W' : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W'})
    (hW' : IsGreatest {V : {V : Subfunctor X' // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V} |
      HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS (V.1.ι ≫ f')} W') :
    W'.1 = W.1.preimage g'
declarations.comment: entry (1), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3 at 𝒬 = locally of finite type and 𝒫 = relative dimension ≤ d, quantified over largest open subspaces as the lemma takes it, for an arbitrary base change since the entry's ℛ is ∅

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedLocus_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06M5, third entry, hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3, for the canonical open
subspace.** In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical arrow `f`
is locally of finite type, the open unramified locus of the base change `f'` is the inverse
image of the open unramified locus of `f`.

No condition is imposed on the base change: the source writes `ℛ = ∅` for this entry, and
part (2) of **Stacks 05W2**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setOf_isUnramifiedAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback`, gives the invariance
of the set of points of unramifiedness under an arbitrary base change. On points both sides are
that set, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_unramifiedLocus` and the identification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsRange_preimage` of the point set of an inverse image; the two
open subspaces then agree because part (1) of **Stacks 03BZ** is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramifiedLocus_preimage_of_isPullback
    {X' X Y' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    (unramifiedLocus B S hS hX' f').1 = (unramifiedLocus B S hS hX f).1.preimage g'
declarations.comment: entry (3), hypothesis (4) of Stacks 06M3 at 𝒬 = locally of finite type and 𝒫 = unramified, for the canonical open subspace: the formation of the largest open subspace commutes with base change, for an arbitrary base change since the entry's ℛ is ∅, from Stacks 05W2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_of_isUnramified_flatCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MB, part (1).** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `f : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳` be
surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation with `𝒲` representable by an algebraic space.
If `f` is unramified in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK, then `𝒳` is Deligne–Mumford.

Unramifiedness passes from `f` to the absolute diagonal of `𝒳` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_diagonal_of_flatCover`, the cancellation of first
factors being Stacks 06G6; the absolute diagonal and the relative diagonal of the structure
1-morphism have the same relative properties, and Stacks 050N part (1) turns DM over `S` into
DM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_of_isUnramified_flatCover
    {𝒳 𝒲 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (h𝒲 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒲.val)
    (hSurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hFlat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hLfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hUnr : haveI : (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS).IsStableUnderBaseChange :=
        Space.isUnramified_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS
      haveI : (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
          (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS) :=
        (Space.isUnramified_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc.{u, u} B S hS).of_le
          (Space.fppfPrecoverage_le_fpqcPrecoverage.{u, u} B S hS)
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.unramifiedMorphismProperty B S hS)
        f.hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.property h𝒲 f.hom)) :
    IsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_flatCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MB, part (2).** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `f : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳` be
surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation with `𝒲` representable by an algebraic space.
If `f` is locally quasi-finite in the relative sense of Stacks 03YK, then `𝒳` is quasi-DM.

This is the argument of part (1) with the cancellation of first factors supplied by
Stacks 03XN.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_flatCover
    {𝒳 𝒲 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (h𝒲 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒲.val)
    (hSurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hFlat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hLfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hQf : haveI : (Space.locallyQuasiFiniteProperty B S hS).IsStableUnderBaseChange :=
        Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
        (Space.locallyQuasiFiniteProperty B S hS) f.hom
        (isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isAlgebraicStack B S hS 𝒳.property h𝒲 f.hom)) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubspace_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_zeroLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MD, the locally-of-finite-presentation conjunct.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack
over `S`, let `U` be an algebraic space with a 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` which is flat and locally
of finite presentation, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a field-valued point, and let `F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k`
with projection `p : F ⟶ U`. Let `f₁, …, f_r ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` and let `z` be a geometric point of
`F` at which the `f_i` map to a regular sequence in `𝒪_{F, z̄}`. Then, after replacing `U` by an
open subspace containing `p(z)`, the 1-morphism `V(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ 𝒳` is locally of finite
presentation.

Only that conjunct is proved; flatness of `V(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ 𝒳` is not claimed, and the
implementation notes say why. The flatness and regular-sequence hypotheses of the source are
recorded and unused — the conjunct proved here needs no shrinking of `U` either, so the open
subspace produced is the whole of `U` and the stronger statement over an arbitrary open subspace
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_zeroLocusOnOpenToStack`. Local finite
presentation of the closed immersion `V(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ U`, the hypothesis `hslice` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_vanishingSubfunctor_comp` which reduces
to the surjectivity half of Stacks 03MB, is carried.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubspace_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_zeroLocus
    (_hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (z : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS Fsp)
    (_hreg : FibreIsRegularSequenceAt.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g a Fsp hFsp eF z)
    (hslice : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (chartZeroLocus B S hS U hU a).ι) :
    ∃ (V : Subfunctor U) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V),
      Space.pointsMap B S hS Fsp
          (fibreSpaceProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g Fsp eF) z.image ∈
        Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
      AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (zeroLocusOnOpenToStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU f a V hV)
declarations.comment: the locally-of-finite-presentation conjunct ONLY: `V(f₁,…,f_r) ⟶ 𝒳` is locally of finite presentation. Flatness of it is NOT proved and no part of that conjunct is claimed. Local finite presentation of the closed immersion `V(f₁,…,f_r) ⟶ U`, which reduces to the surjectivity half of Stacks 03MB, is carried as a hypothesis.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubspace_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_zeroLocus_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MD.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `U` be an algebraic space with a
1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` which is flat and locally of finite presentation, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a
field-valued point, and let `F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` with projection `p : F ⟶ U`. Let
`f₁, …, f_r ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` and let `z` be a geometric point of `F` at which the `f_i` map to a
regular sequence in the étale local ring `𝒪_{F, z̄}`. Then, after replacing `U` by an open
subspace containing `p(z)`, the 1-morphism `V(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ 𝒳` is **flat and locally of finite
presentation**.

Nothing is carried. Local finite presentation holds over *every* open subspace,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_zeroLocusOnOpenToStack`. For flatness the
proof is the source's: base change along a smooth chart of `𝒳` by an algebraic space surjective
on objects, apply the flatness half of **Stacks 06LW** to the morphism of algebraic spaces
`U ×_𝒳 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒲` at the fibre which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_chartFibre_isPullback_isRegular` produces, take the open subspace
of `U` swept out by the open subspace Stacks 06LW returns — open because the projection
`U ×_𝒳 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒲` is a base change of the smooth chart, hence flat and locally of finite
presentation, hence open on points — and read flatness back point by point through the chart
independence of **Stacks 0CIC**.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubspace_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_zeroLocus_of_isRegular
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (z : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS Fsp)
    (hreg : FibreIsRegularSequenceAt.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g a Fsp hFsp eF z) :
    ∃ (V : Subfunctor U) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V),
      Space.pointsMap B S hS Fsp
          (fibreSpaceProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g Fsp eF) z.image ∈
        Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
      AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS
          (zeroLocusOnOpenToStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU f a V hV) ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
          (zeroLocusOnOpenToStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU f a V hV)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06ME.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack, let `U` be an algebraic space with a
1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` which is locally of finite type, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a field-valued
point, and let `F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` with projection `p : F ⟶ U` and structure 1-morphism
`q : F ⟶ Spec k`. If `z ∈ |F|` has `dim_z(F) = 0` then, after replacing `U` by an open subspace
containing `p(z)`, the 1-morphism `U ⟶ 𝒳` is locally quasi-finite.

The proof is the source's. The open substack `W` is the locus `W(f)` of **Stacks 06M5** on which
`f` is locally quasi-finite, carried as the data `W` together with `hW`; the compatibility of
that locus with the base change along `g`, which is the second clause of Stacks 06M5, is carried
as `hBaseChange`. Given those, the conclusion is exactly that `p(z) ∈ |W|`, and that follows
because the fibre hypothesis puts `z` in an open substack of `F` which is locally quasi-finite
over `Spec k`, hence inside the preimage of `|W|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    (_hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (W : OpenSubstack (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU))
    (hW : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (W.inclusion ≫ f))
    (hBaseChange : ∀ V : OpenSubstack (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g),
      AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS
          (V.inclusion ≫ fibreStructureMorphism B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) →
        V.pointSet B S hS ⊆
          AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
              (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) ⁻¹' W.pointSet B S hS)
    (z : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g))
    (hz : FibreIsLocallyQuasiFiniteNear.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g z) :
    AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
        (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) z ∈ W.pointSet B S hS ∧
      AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (W.inclusion ≫ f)
declarations.comment: after replacing the algebraic space by an open subspace containing the image of the given point of the fibre, a 1-morphism locally of finite type whose fibre over a field-valued point has dimension zero at that point is locally quasi-finite. The two clauses of Stacks 06M5 are carried, as the data `W` with `hW` (the open locus on which the 1-morphism is locally quasi-finite) and the hypothesis `hBaseChange` (that locus commutes with the base change along the field-valued point), since Stacks 06M5 is absent from this library; the deduction of the conclusion from them is proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06ME at the source's own hypothesis, with the conclusion read on an open substack.**
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack, let `U` be an algebraic space with a 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳`
locally of finite type, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a field-valued point, let `Fsp` represent the fibre
`F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` through `eF`, and let `z` be a point of `|Fsp|` with `dim_z(F) = 0` — the
dimension of **Stacks 04N5** of the algebraic space `Fsp` at `z`. Then there is an open substack
`W` of the algebraic stack of `U` whose point set contains `p(z)` and for which `W.inclusion ≫ f`
is locally quasi-finite.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isLocallyQuasiFinite_unconditional` with its
fibre
hypothesis `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FibreIsLocallyQuasiFiniteNear` replaced by the source's
`dim_z(F) = 0`, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fibreIsLocallyQuasiFiniteNear_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero`. Nothing is
added and nothing is weakened: the finite-type hypothesis is the source's, and the hypothesis on
`z` is the source's. The point of `|F|` is the image of `z` under the comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.spacePointMap` of the representing equivalence, which is a bijection by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.bijective_spacePointMap_representing`, so every point of `|F|` is
reached.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (z : Space.points B S hS Fsp)
    (hz : Space.dimensionAtPoint B S hS Fsp hFsp z = 0) :
    ∃ W : OpenSubstack (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU),
      AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
          (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g)
          (spacePointMap B S hS Fsp
            (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g).val
            (representingEquivalence B S hS Fsp
              (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g).val eF).functor z) ∈
        W.pointSet B S hS ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (W.inclusion ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the source's own hypotheses, with the conclusion read on an open substack of the stack of the algebraic space: the 1-morphism is locally of finite type and the given point z of the fibre has dim_z(F) = 0, the dimension of Stacks 04N5 of a representing algebraic space Fsp of the fibre at z. Nothing is added and nothing is weakened. The proof is exists_openSubstack_isLocallyQuasiFinite_unconditional of ChartShrinkingQuasiFiniteEtaleUnconditional -- which states the same conclusion at the intermediate condition the source's own proof extracts from dim_z(F) = 0, that some open substack of the fibre containing z is locally quasi-finite over Spec k -- composed with the step the source's proof takes from dim_z(F) = 0 to that condition by Stacks 04NV, which is fibreIsLocallyQuasiFiniteNear_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero above. The source's open subspace of the algebraic space is rendered here as an open substack of the stack of that space, with the same point set, both directions of that passage being proved as exists_openSubstack_algebraicSpaceStack_of_isOpenImmersion and exists_isOpenSubspace_property_eq_essImage; the conclusion read on an open subspace, as the source reads it, is exists_isOpenSubspace_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero below. The point of the fibre is the image of z under the comparison spacePointMap of the representing equivalence, which bijective_spacePointMap_representing makes a bijection, so no point of the fibre is excluded by stating the hypothesis on Fsp

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isOpenSubspace_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06ME at the source's own hypothesis, with the conclusion read on an open subspace.**
The statement of the source: with `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` locally of finite type and `z` a point of the
fibre `F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` at which the dimension of `F` is zero, there is an open subspace
`V ⊆ U` of **Stacks 02YU**, part (2), whose point set contains `p(z)` and for which the
composite of the 1-morphism of **Stacks 0458** induced by `V` with `f` is locally quasi-finite.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isOpenSubspace_isLocallyQuasiFinite` with its fibre
hypothesis replaced by the source's, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fibreIsLocallyQuasiFiniteNear_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero`. Both
hypotheses are now the source's and the conclusion is the source's.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (z : Space.points B S hS Fsp)
    (hz : Space.dimensionAtPoint B S hS Fsp hFsp z = 0) :
    ∃ (V : Subfunctor U) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V),
      AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
          (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g)
          (spacePointMap B S hS Fsp
            (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g).val
            (representingEquivalence B S hS Fsp
              (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g).val eF).functor z) ∈
        spacePointMap B S hS U (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU).val
            (BasedFunctor.id (fibredCategory B S hS U).val) ''
          Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS hV.1 hU V.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the statement of the source, hypotheses and conclusion: the 1-morphism out of the algebraic space is locally of finite type, the given point z of the fibre has dim_z(F) = 0 -- the dimension of Stacks 04N5 of a representing algebraic space Fsp of the fibre at z -- and after replacing the algebraic space by an open subspace of Stacks 02YU, part (2), containing the image of z, the 1-morphism is locally quasi-finite, the replacement read as the composite of the 1-morphism of Stacks 0458 induced by that open subspace. Nothing is added and nothing is weakened. The proof is exists_isOpenSubspace_isLocallyQuasiFinite of ChartShrinkingOpenSubspace -- the same conclusion at the intermediate condition the source's own proof extracts from dim_z(F) = 0 -- composed with the step the source's proof takes from dim_z(F) = 0 to that condition by Stacks 04NV, which is fibreIsLocallyQuasiFiniteNear_of_dimensionAtPoint_eq_zero above. The point of the fibre is the image of z under the comparison spacePointMap of the representing equivalence, which bijective_spacePointMap_representing makes a bijection, so no point of the fibre is excluded by stating the hypothesis on Fsp

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_iff_hasQuasiDMPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MF.** An algebraic stack is quasi-DM exactly when there is a scheme of the site
with a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite 1-morphism to it.

Both implications are carried; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ExistsQuasiDMPresentationOfIsAbsolutelyQuasiDM` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDMOfHasQuasiDMPresentation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_iff_hasQuasiDMPresentation
    (hForward : ExistsQuasiDMPresentationOfIsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (hBackward : IsAbsolutelyQuasiDMOfHasQuasiDMPresentation.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒳 ↔
      HasQuasiDMPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of (1) quasi-DM with (2) the existence of a surjective, flat,
  locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite presentation by a scheme. Both implications
  are carried, as the hypotheses `hForward` (the structure theorem: Stacks 06MD, 06ME, 06G2,
  06G3 are absent) and `hBackward` (Stacks 06MB part (2) is present but the repackaging of the
  Section 04XB local quasi-finiteness of the chart into its HasRelativeProperty form is
  absent)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_hasQuasiDMPresentation
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack with a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite
presentation by a scheme of the site is quasi-DM: the implication (2) ⟹ (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_hasQuasiDMPresentation (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h : HasQuasiDMPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (1): a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite presentation by a scheme of the site makes an algebraic stack quasi-DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_iff_hasQuasiDMPresentation_unconditional
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack is quasi-DM exactly when there is a scheme of the site with a surjective,
flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite 1-morphism to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_iff_hasQuasiDMPresentation_unconditional
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒳 ↔
      HasQuasiDMPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of (1) quasi-DM with (2) the existence of a surjective, flat,
  locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite presentation by a scheme. BOTH implications
  are proved and nothing is carried. (2) implies (1) is Stacks 06MB part (2),
  isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_hasQuasiDMPresentation; (1) implies (2) is the structure theorem,
  hasQuasiDMPresentation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM, whose local half is the chart of
  exists_flat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isLocallyQuasiFinite_chart_at_finiteTypePoint --
  the smooth chart of 06FX with a closed point over the finite type point, the charted
  self-intersection of 04ZP and 04SW, the identity point of 04XH, and the slice cut out by a
  regular sequence in the etale local ring of a fibre (06LC, 06MD, 06LW) shrunk to be locally
  quasi-finite by 06M3 and 06ME -- and whose assembly is
  hasQuasiDMPresentation_of_forall_isLocallyQuasiFinite: the 1-morphism out of the coproduct
  W = coprod_x Z_x, the descent of the three properties along the summand inclusions, and
  surjectivity from the corollary of 06G2. The coproduct lies in the site by
  contains_sigma_of_forall_size_le, which the uniform bound 2 ^ 2 ^ size U_0 on the charts
  supplies -- the finite type points need not be below the cofinality of the site's cutoff, so
  contains_sigma_of_lt_cof does not apply

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEmpty_points_or_isIso_of_mono_to_spec_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MG.** A monomorphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose target is the spectrum
of a field `k` is either a morphism out of an algebraic space with no points, or an
isomorphism.

A field is a zero-dimensional local ring, so the source is a scheme by Stacks 06RZ, and the
dichotomy is then the scheme-level one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_points_or_isIso_of_mono_to_spec_field
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (f : F ⟶ G)
    [Mono f] (Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (eG : G ≅ yoneda.obj Y) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (eY : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y ≅ Spec (.of k)) :
    IsEmpty (points B S hS F) ∨ IsIso f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MH.** A smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite
type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isSmooth
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : F ⟶ G}
    (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
A flat surjective morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source is reduced has reduced
target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MJ.** Local Noetherianity passes from the source of a surjective, flat
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` locally of finite presentation to its target.

This is the case `P = AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian` of
`hasEtaleLocalProperty_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation`, whose two
locality hypotheses hold for local Noetherianity of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MK.** Regularity passes from the source of a surjective, flat morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` locally of finite presentation to its target.

A regular scheme is locally Noetherian, so a regular étale chart of the source witnesses local
Noetherianity of the source; Stacks 06MJ carries that to the target, and
`hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat` then applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_of_fieldSpectrum_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MM, flatness.** Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` admitting a surjective flat
1-morphism from the algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field. Then every 1-morphism to `𝒵` from
the algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field is flat.

Form the canonical 2-fibre product of the given cover `f` with the 1-morphism `g` in question.
Its projection to the source of `f` is flat because that source is the algebraic stack of the
spectrum of a field, so the composite with `f` is flat; `f` being surjective and flat,
**Stacks 06PZ** descends that flatness to `g`.

The companion `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_fieldSpectrum_cover` is the surjectivity
half of the tag, which needs no flatness hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_fieldSpectrum_cover (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (F F' : FieldSpectrum B S hS)
    (f : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F.base ⟶ 𝒵)
    (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F'.base ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_fieldSpectrum_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MM, surjectivity.** Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` admitting a surjective
1-morphism from the algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field. Then every 1-morphism to `𝒵` from
the algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field is surjective.

The spectrum of a field has one point, so a surjection out of its stack leaves `𝒵` with at most
one point; the source of the second 1-morphism has a point, which therefore hits every point of
`𝒵`. Flatness of the given surjection, which Stacks 06MM also assumes, is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_fieldSpectrum_cover (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (F F' : FieldSpectrum B S hS)
    (f : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F.base ⟶ 𝒵)
    (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F'.base ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsSurjective B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_isReducedWithUniquePoint
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isReducedWithUniquePoint (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsReducedWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵,
        HasFlatFieldSpectrumCover B S hS 𝒵,
        HasLocallyOfFiniteTypeFlatFieldSpectrumCover B S hS 𝒵]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint_iff_hasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldSpectrumCover
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic stack `𝒵` over `S` the following are equivalent:

1. `𝒵` is reduced, locally Noetherian, and its space of points `|𝒵|` is a singleton;
2. there is a 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒵` with `k` a field which is locally of finite presentation,
   surjective and flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem
  isReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint_iff_hasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldSpectrumCover
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵 ↔
      HasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldSpectrumCover B S hS 𝒵

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEmpty_points_or_isEquivalenceOver_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MQ.** Let `f : 𝒵' ⟶ 𝒵` be a monomorphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and assume
that `𝒵` admits a 1-morphism from the algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field which is locally
of finite presentation, surjective and flat (condition (2) of **Stacks 06MP**). Then either `𝒵'`
has no points, or `f` is an equivalence over the big fppf site of `S`.

The nonempty case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalenceOver_of_isMonomorphism_of_fieldSpectrumCover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_points_or_isEquivalenceOver_of_isMonomorphism
    (𝒵' 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒵' ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B S hS f)
    (hcov : HasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldSpectrumCover B S hS 𝒵) :
    IsEmpty (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒵') ∨
      Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver 𝒵'.val.val.p 𝒵.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isMonomorphism_fullSubcategoryInclusion
declarations.doc:
**The last assertion of Stacks 06MR.** The inclusion of a strictly full subcategory of an
algebraic stack `𝒵` over `S` which is itself an algebraic stack is representable by algebraic
spaces and a monomorphism in the sense of **Stacks 04ZW**.

The monomorphy clause is unconditional, by the implication (2) ⟹ (1) of **Stacks 04ZZ** for a
fully faithful 1-morphism. Representability by algebraic spaces is what the source takes from
**Stacks 04Y5**, the inclusion being faithful; the library has the implication (2) ⟹ (3) of
Stacks 04Y5 as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_faithful`,
fed with the bootstrap theorem Stacks 04S6 part (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgebraicStacks.isMonomorphism_fullSubcategoryInclusion
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (P : ObjectProperty 𝒵.val.val.obj)
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒵 P)) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒵 P hP)
declarations.comment: the inclusion morphism of the substack is representable by algebraic spaces and a monomorphism, granting the implication (2) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 04Y5 for the inclusion of a strictly full algebraic subcategory, which is the hypothesis hrep and which the library leaves open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MR, the uniqueness assertion.** Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is
reduced with a singleton space of points, that is, which satisfies condition (1) of
**Stacks 06MN**. Then at most one strictly full subcategory of `𝒵` is an algebraic stack
satisfying condition (2) of **Stacks 06MP**.

Existence is not proved; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒵 : IsReducedWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵)
    {P Q : ObjectProperty 𝒵.val.val.obj}
    (hP : IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵 P)
    (hQ : IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵 Q) : P = Q
declarations.comment: the uniqueness of the substack, with the equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MP read as its condition (2), and granting the implication (2) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 04Y5 for the inclusion of a strictly full algebraic subcategory, which is the hypothesis hrep and which the library leaves open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MR, the existence assertion.** Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is
reduced with a singleton space of points, that is, which satisfies condition (1) of
**Stacks 06MN**. Then some strictly full subcategory of `𝒵` is an algebraic stack satisfying
condition (2) of **Stacks 06MP**.

The subcategory is the essential image of the fully faithful 1-morphism supplied by the carried
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasFullyFaithfulFinitePresentationPresentations` out of the surjective flat cover,
locally of finite type, by the spectrum of a field that condition (3) of **Stacks 06MN** supplies
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_isReducedWithUniquePoint`). It is closed under
isomorphism; the source factors through it by an equivalence of categories, hence by an equivalence
over the big fppf site by **Stacks 003Z**; so it is an algebraic stack by **Stacks 03YQ** and
inherits condition (2) of Stacks 06MP by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.hasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldSpectrumCover_of_isEquivalenceFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack
    (hpres : HasFullyFaithfulFinitePresentationPresentations.{u, w} B S hS)
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒵 : IsReducedWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵) :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty 𝒵.val.val.obj,
      IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵 P
declarations.comment: the existence of the substack, with the equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MP read as its condition (2), granting the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 06MN, which is the hypothesis h06MN, and granting Stacks 04T4 (1), (4), (5) and (6) together with Stacks 06FI, which is the hypothesis hpres; both are quantified over every algebraic stack over S and so restrict no object, and the library discharges neither, its own Stacks 06FI carrying Artin's representability theorem, Stacks 06DC, as an open hypothesis; what is proved is the replacement of the quotient stack by its essential image in Z, with the invariance of condition (2) of Stacks 06MP under an equivalence over the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsUnique_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MR, the first assertion.** Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is reduced
with a singleton space of points. Then exactly one strictly full subcategory of `𝒵` is an algebraic
stack satisfying condition (2) of **Stacks 06MP**.

Existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack` and
uniqueness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack
    (hpres : HasFullyFaithfulFinitePresentationPresentations.{u, w} B S hS)
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒵 : IsReducedWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵) :
    ∃! P : ObjectProperty 𝒵.val.val.obj,
      IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵 P
declarations.comment: existence and uniqueness of the substack assembled, with the equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MP read as its condition (2), granting the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 06MN (h06MN), Stacks 04T4 (1), (4), (5) and (6) together with Stacks 06FI (hpres), and the implication (2) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 04Y5 for the inclusion of a strictly full algebraic subcategory (hrep); all three are quantified over every algebraic stack over S and so restrict no object, and the library discharges none of them

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_of_isReducedWithUniquePoint
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is reduced with a singleton space of points,
that is, which satisfies condition (1) of Stacks 06MN. Then some strictly full subcategory of `𝒵`
is an algebraic stack satisfying condition (2) of Stacks 06MP.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_of_isReducedWithUniquePoint
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒵 : IsReducedWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵) :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty 𝒵.val.val.obj,
      IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵 P
declarations.comment: the existence of the substack, with the equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MP read as its condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsUnique_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_of_isReducedWithUniquePoint
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is reduced with a singleton space of points.
Then exactly one strictly full subcategory of `𝒵` is an algebraic stack satisfying condition (2)
of Stacks 06MP.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_of_isReducedWithUniquePoint
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒵 : IsReducedWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵) :
    ∃! P : ObjectProperty 𝒵.val.val.obj,
      IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵 P
declarations.comment: existence and uniqueness of the substack assembled, with the equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MP read as its condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.selfFiberProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The self-fibre-product `U = Spec(ℚ̄) ×_{Spec(ℚ)} Spec(ℚ̄)`, as a scheme
over `Spec(ℚ̄)` through its second projection.
declarations.statement: abbrev selfFiberProduct : Over cover.left
declarations.comment: the self-fibre-product U of Spec(ℚ̄) over Spec(ℚ), over its second factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isLocallyNoetherian_selfFiberProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The self-fibre-product `U` is not locally Noetherian: `ℚ̄ ⊗_ℚ ℚ̄` is a
ring of Krull dimension zero, so a Noetherian one would be Artinian and have finitely many
primes, whereas the infinite group `Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)` injects into its primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isLocallyNoetherian_selfFiberProduct :
    ¬ IsLocallyNoetherian selfFiberProduct.left
declarations.comment: the cover U is not locally Noetherian, the source's non-noetherianity of X read on its atlas

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isClosed_singleton_selfFiberProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** Every point of the self-fibre-product `U` is closed: `ℚ̄ ⊗_ℚ ℚ̄` is
integral over the field `ℚ̄`, so each of its primes is maximal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_singleton_selfFiberProduct (x : selfFiberProduct.left) :
    IsClosed ({x} : Set selfFiberProduct.left)
declarations.comment: every point of U is closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.galoisGroupEquivSelfFiberProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The points of `U = Spec(ℚ̄) ×_{Spec(ℚ)} Spec(ℚ̄)` are in bijection with
`Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)`: `σ` goes to the point cut out by the kernel of `x ⊗ y ↦ σ(x) y`. This is the source's
`U = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) × Spec(ℚ̄)` on underlying sets.
declarations.statement: def galoisGroupEquivSelfFiberProduct : galoisGroup ≃ selfFiberProduct.left
declarations.comment: U = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) × Spec(ℚ̄) on points: the points of U are in bijection with the absolute Galois group

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.selfFiberProductAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The action of `Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)` on the self-fibre-product `U` over `Spec(ℚ̄)`:
the base change along the structure morphism of `Spec(ℚ̄)` of the Galois action on `Spec(ℚ̄)`,
so it moves the first projection and fixes the second.
declarations.statement: def selfFiberProductAction : galoisGroup →* Aut selfFiberProduct
declarations.comment: the action of the absolute Galois group on U over Spec(ℚ̄)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.constantGaloisGroupScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The absolute Galois group of `ℚ` with the discrete topology, viewed as a
constant group scheme over `Spec(ℚ̄)` as in **Stacks 03YW**. This is the group scheme `G` the
source lets act on `U`.
declarations.statement: abbrev constantGaloisGroupScheme : Grp (Over cover.left)
declarations.comment: G: the absolute Galois group with the discrete topology as a constant group scheme over Spec(ℚ̄)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.selfFiberProductAction_actsFreely
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The Galois group acts freely on the self-fibre-product `U`: the first
projection `U ⟶ Spec(ℚ̄)` is equivariant, and the Galois action on `Spec(ℚ̄)` is already free by
this library's **Stacks 02Z6**.
declarations.statement:
theorem selfFiberProductAction_actsFreely :
    Space.ActsFreelyOnNonemptyPoints selfFiberProduct galoisGroup
      (selfFiberProductAction B₀ hQ hK)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.selfFiberProductAction_transitive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The Galois group acts transitively on the points of `U`: every prime of
`ℚ̄ ⊗_ℚ ℚ̄` is the kernel of `x ⊗ y ↦ τ(x) y` for some Galois element `τ`, and `σ` moves the
prime of `τ` to the prime of `τ σ⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
theorem selfFiberProductAction_transitive (x y : selfFiberProduct.left) :
    ∃ σ : galoisGroup, (selfFiberProductAction B₀ hQ hK σ).asIso.hom.left x = y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The action of `G`, viewed as the constant group scheme over `Spec(ℚ̄)` of
**Stacks 03YW**, on `U` (**Stacks 022Z**): the action map `G ×_{Spec(ℚ̄)} U ⟶ U` which on the
summand of `G ×_{Spec(ℚ̄)} U` indexed by `σ` is the automorphism `selfFiberProductAction σ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction : ModObj constantGaloisGroupScheme.X selfFiberProduct
declarations.comment: the action of G, as the constant group scheme over Spec(ℚ̄), on U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction_eq
declarations.statement:
theorem constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction_eq (σ : galoisGroup) :
    letI := constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction B₀ hQ hK
    constantGroupSchemeLeg selfFiberProduct σ ≫ γ[constantGaloisGroupScheme.X, selfFiberProduct] =
        (selfFiberProductAction B₀ hQ hK σ).asIso.hom ∧
      ∀ {T : Over cover.left} (x : T ⟶ selfFiberProduct),
        (toUnit T ≫ constantGroupSchemePoint galoisGroup cover.left σ :
            T ⟶ constantGaloisGroupScheme.X) • x =
          x ≫ (selfFiberProductAction B₀ hQ hK σ).asIso.hom
declarations.comment: the action of the constant group scheme G on U is the Galois action on summands and on constant points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isFreeAction_constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The constant group scheme `G` acts freely on `U`, in the sense of
**Stacks 07S1**: for every scheme `T` over `Spec(ℚ̄)` the group `G(T)` of locally constant maps
`T → Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)` acts freely on `U(T)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFreeAction_constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction :
    letI := constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction B₀ hQ hK
    IsFreeAction constantGaloisGroupScheme.X selfFiberProduct
declarations.comment: the constant group scheme G acts freely on U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.exists_smul_eq_constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The constant group scheme `G` acts transitively on `U`: for any two points
`u, v` of `U` some point of `G ×_{Spec(ℚ̄)} U` lies over `u` under the projection and over `v`
under the action map.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smul_eq_constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction (u v : selfFiberProduct.left) :
    letI := constantGaloisGroupSchemeAction B₀ hQ hK
    ∃ z : (constantGaloisGroupScheme.X ⊗ selfFiberProduct).left,
      (snd constantGaloisGroupScheme.X selfFiberProduct).left z = u ∧
        (γ[constantGaloisGroupScheme.X, selfFiberProduct]).left z = v
declarations.comment: the constant group scheme G acts transitively on U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The algebraic space `X = U/G` of the example: the fppf sheaf quotient of
the self-fibre-product by the Galois action, as in **Stacks 02Z3**.
declarations.statement: abbrev galoisSelfProductQuotient : (BigFppfOver B cover.left hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 0
declarations.comment: X = U/G, the fppf sheaf quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isAlgebraicSpace_galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `X = U/G` is an algebraic space over `Spec(ℚ̄)`; this is the source's
remark that the example is even an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_galoisSelfProductQuotient :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B cover.left hS (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isLocallyNoetherian_galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `X` is not locally Noetherian: `U ⟶ X` is an étale atlas, and an
étale-local property of an algebraic space holds on every étale chart as soon as it holds at
all, while `U` is not locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isLocallyNoetherian_galoisSelfProductQuotient :
    ¬ Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B cover.left hS
      (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
      (fun T : Scheme.{0} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T)
declarations.comment: X is not locally Noetherian, the failure Definition 06MU excludes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.canonicalPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The morphism `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ U ⟶ X` of the example: the diagonal followed
by the projection onto the quotient.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalPoint :
    yoneda.obj (Space.baseTerminal B cover.left hS) ⟶ galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU
declarations.comment: the morphism x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ U ⟶ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isIso_canonicalPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS, the point of the example.** The morphism `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is *not* an
isomorphism. If it were, `X` would be represented by `Spec(ℚ̄)`, hence locally Noetherian; but
`X` is not locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement: theorem not_isIso_canonicalPoint : ¬ IsIso (canonicalPoint B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isReduced_galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06MS.** `X` is reduced, witnessed by the reduced étale atlas `U ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_galoisSelfProductQuotient :
    Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B cover.left hS
      (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
      (fun T : Scheme.{0} ↦ IsReduced T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isNoetherian_galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `X` is not a Noetherian algebraic space in the sense of **Stacks 03EA**,
because it is not locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isNoetherian_galoisSelfProductQuotient (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{0})) :
    ¬ Space.IsNoetherian B cover.left hS hZ (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.mono_canonicalPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The morphism `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is a monomorphism, because `Spec(ℚ̄)` is
the terminal object of the big fppf site over `Spec(ℚ̄)`: this is the source's remark that `x`
is a monomorphism since `X` is an algebraic space over `ℚ̄`.
declarations.statement: theorem mono_canonicalPoint : Mono (canonicalPoint B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.nonempty_points_galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `X` has a point, namely the class of `x`; with
`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.subsingleton_points_galoisSelfProductQuotient` it is the
only one.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_points_galoisSelfProductQuotient :
    Nonempty (Space.points B cover.left hS (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isFiniteTypePoint_canonicalFieldPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The class of `x` is a finite type point of `X` in the sense of
**Stacks 06EG**: it is the image of the closed point of `U` cut out by the diagonal under the
étale chart `U ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypePoint_canonicalFieldPoint :
    Space.IsFiniteTypePoint B cover.left hS (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
      ((canonicalFieldPoint B₀ hQ hK B hS hU).class B cover.left hS _)
declarations.comment: x is a (locally) finite type point of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.eq_class_canonicalFieldPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** The algebraic space `X = U/G` has exactly one point, and it is the class of
`x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_class_canonicalFieldPoint
    (p : Space.points B cover.left hS (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)) :
    p = (canonicalFieldPoint B₀ hQ hK B hS hU).class B cover.left hS _
declarations.comment: X has exactly one point, namely the class of x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.nonempty_unique_points_galoisSelfProductQuotient
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06MS.** The space of points of `X = U/G` is a singleton.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_unique_points_galoisSelfProductQuotient :
    Nonempty (Unique
      (Space.points B cover.left hS (galoisSelfProductQuotient B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.not_isEquivalence_substackInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS, the assertion about the morphism of Stacks 06MR.** Let `P` be any object
property of `X` of the kind **Stacks 06MR** produces, that is one which is closed under
isomorphism and cuts out an algebraic stack satisfying condition (2) of **Stacks 06MP**. Then
the inclusion `X_P ⟶ X` is *not* an equivalence over the big fppf site, which is this library's
notion of an isomorphism of algebraic stacks.

Stacks 06MR asserts that exactly one object property of `X` has that kind, so this says that
the morphism Stacks 06MR constructs for `X` is not an isomorphism. Quantifying over all
candidates rather than naming the one Stacks 06MR constructs avoids the two undischarged
hypotheses under which this library proves the existence half of Stacks 06MR, and makes the
statement stronger rather than weaker.

If the inclusion were an equivalence, condition (2) of Stacks 06MP would transport to `X`, and
condition (1) — in particular local Noetherianity — would follow; but `X` is not locally
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isEquivalence_substackInclusion
    (P : ObjectProperty (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU).val.val.obj)
    (hP : Stack.IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{0, w} B cover.left hS
      (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) P) :
    ¬ Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
      (Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) P
        hP.2.choose).hom)
declarations.comment: the morphism Stacks 06MR constructs for X is not an isomorphism: for every object property of X satisfying the conditions of Stacks 06MR, its substack inclusion is not an equivalence over the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isReducedWithUniquePoint_quotientStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `X`, as an algebraic stack, satisfies the hypothesis of **Stacks 06MR**,
condition (1) of **Stacks 06MN**: it is reduced and its space of points is a singleton.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReducedWithUniquePoint_quotientStack :
    Stack.IsReducedWithUniquePoint B cover.left hS (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
declarations.comment: X, as an algebraic stack, is reduced with exactly one point: the hypothesis of Lemma 06MR

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isMonomorphism_canonicalPointStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is a monomorphism of algebraic stacks in the sense of
**Stacks 04ZW**: it is fully faithful because `x` is a monomorphism of sheaves, and a fully
faithful 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonomorphism_canonicalPointStack :
    Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B cover.left hS
      (canonicalPointStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
declarations.comment: x is a monomorphism of algebraic stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_canonicalPointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS: `x` is the morphism constructed in Lemma 06MR.** The strictly full
subcategory of `X` cut out by `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is a substack of the kind **Stacks 06MR**
produces for the reduced one-point algebraic stack `X`: it is closed under isomorphism, its full
subcategory is an algebraic stack, and that algebraic stack satisfies condition (2) of
**Stacks 06MP**. Moreover `x` factors through the inclusion of that substack by a 1-morphism whose
underlying functor is an equivalence of categories, so `x` *is* the inclusion morphism of
Lemma 06MR up to equivalence. And that inclusion morphism is *not* an isomorphism: it is not an
equivalence over the big fppf site, because `X` is not locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_canonicalPointSubstack :
    Stack.IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{0, w} B cover.left hS
        (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) ∧
      ∃ hP : Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{0, w} B cover.left hS
          (Stack.fullSubcategoryBased (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
            (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)),
        ∃ t : Stack.schemeStack.{0, w} B cover.left hS (baseFieldSpectrum B hS).base ⟶
            Stack.fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
              (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) hP,
          Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor t.hom) ∧
            Nonempty (t ≫ Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
              (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) hP ≅
                canonicalPointStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU ≫ 𝟙 _) ∧
          ¬ Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
            (Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
              (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) hP).hom)
declarations.comment: x is the morphism constructed in Lemma 06MR, and it is not an isomorphism: the substack of X cut out by x is closed under isomorphism, algebraic and satisfies the conditions of 06MP, x factors through its inclusion by an equivalence, and that inclusion is not an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_iff_eq_canonicalPointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS: `x` is the morphism constructed in Lemma 06MR.** The substack of `X` cut out
by `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is *the* strictly full subcategory of `X` which Stacks 06MR produces: a
strictly full subcategory of `X` is an algebraic stack satisfying the conditions of
**Stacks 06MP** if and only if it is the substack cut out by `x`.

Uniqueness is the argument of Stacks 06MR. Its input, that the inclusion of a strictly full
algebraic substack is a monomorphism, holds because `X` is an algebraic space: such a substack is
a stack in setoids, hence an algebraic space by **Stacks 04SZ**, so its inclusion is
representable by algebraic spaces by **Stacks 02ZZ**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_iff_eq_canonicalPointSubstack
    (Q : ObjectProperty (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU).val.val.obj) :
    Stack.IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{0, w} B cover.left hS
        (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) Q ↔
      Q = canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU
declarations.comment: x is the morphism constructed in Lemma 06MR: the substack cut out by x is the unique strictly full subcategory of X which is an algebraic stack satisfying the conditions of 06MP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.le_canonicalPointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS: `x` is the morphism constructed in Lemma 06MR, the uniqueness half.** Every
strictly full subcategory of `X` of the kind **Stacks 06MR** produces — closed under isomorphism,
algebraic, and satisfying condition (2) of **Stacks 06MP** — is contained in the substack cut out
by `x`.

This is one half of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient`
`.isReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack_iff_eq_canonicalPointSubstack`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_canonicalPointSubstack
    (Q : ObjectProperty (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU).val.val.obj)
    (hQ' : Stack.IsReducedLocallyNoetherianUniquePointSubstack.{0, w} B cover.left hS
      (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) Q) :
    Q ≤ canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU
declarations.comment: x is the morphism constructed in Lemma 06MR: every strictly full subcategory of X with the properties of Lemma 06MR is contained in the substack cut out by x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isResidualGerbeAt_canonicalPointSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS: `Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is the residual gerbe of `X` at `x`.** The residual gerbe of
`X` at `x` exists in the sense of **Stacks 06MU (1)** — `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X` is a monomorphism from
a reduced algebraic stack with a single point mapping to `x` — and the strictly full subcategory
cut out by `x` meets the specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of
**Stacks 06MT** that defines the residual gerbe of **Stacks 06MU (2)**: it is a reduced, locally
Noetherian algebraic stack with exactly one point, lying over `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isResidualGerbeAt_canonicalPointSubstack :
    Stack.HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism B cover.left hS
        (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) (canonicalStackPoint.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) ∧
      Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt B cover.left hS (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
        (canonicalStackPoint.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
        (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
declarations.comment: Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ X is the residual gerbe of X at x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.isLocallyOfFiniteType_canonicalPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS.** `x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ U ⟶ X` is locally of finite type: the diagonal
`Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ U` is a closed immersion, `U` being separated over `Spec(ℚ̄)`, and `U ⟶ X` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_canonicalPoint :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B cover.left hS (canonicalPoint B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
declarations.comment: x : Spec(ℚ̄) ⟶ U ⟶ X is locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalGaloisQuotient.ne_and_isReducedUniquePointSubstackAt_canonicalPointSubstack_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MS: imposing that residual gerbes be locally Noetherian is necessary in
Definition 06MU.** Drop the local Noetherianity clause from the specification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of the residual gerbe, leaving
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsReducedUniquePointSubstackAt`: a strictly full subcategory which is a
reduced algebraic stack with exactly one point, lying over `x`. Then two *distinct* strictly full
subcategories of `X` meet it at `x` — the substack cut out by `x` and all of `X` — and both
inclusions are monomorphisms of algebraic stacks; so the residual gerbe would not be unique. The
local Noetherianity clause is exactly what tells them apart: the substack cut out by `x` is the
residual gerbe of `X` at `x`, and all of `X` is not locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem ne_and_isReducedUniquePointSubstackAt_canonicalPointSubstack_top :
    canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU ≠ ⊤ ∧
      Stack.IsReducedUniquePointSubstackAt B cover.left hS (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
        (canonicalStackPoint.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) ∧
      Stack.IsReducedUniquePointSubstackAt B cover.left hS (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
        (canonicalStackPoint.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) ⊤ ∧
      (∀ (P : ObjectProperty (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU).val.val.obj)
        (hP : Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{0, w} B cover.left hS
          (Stack.fullSubcategoryBased (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) P)),
        Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B cover.left hS
          (Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) P hP)) ∧
      Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt B cover.left hS (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
        (canonicalStackPoint.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) (canonicalPointSubstack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) ∧
      ¬ Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt B cover.left hS (quotientStack.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU)
        (canonicalStackPoint.{w} B₀ hQ hK B hS hU) ⊤
declarations.comment: imposing that residual gerbes are locally Noetherian is necessary in Definition 06MU: without that clause the substack cut out by x and all of X are two distinct reduced one-point substacks over x with monomorphic inclusions, and only the first is locally Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 06MT are equivalent.** A point of an algebraic stack over
`S` is the image of the singleton space of points of a monomorphism to it exactly when it is the
image of the singleton space of points of a monomorphism with reduced source.

The implication (2) ⟹ (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_reduced`, which the source calls
immediate; the implication (1) ⟹ (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism`,
which passes to the reduction of Stacks 0509.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x ↔
      HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2) are equivalent, granting the existence half of Stacks 0509 at the whole point set — that every algebraic stack over S has a reduction, a reduced closed substack whose inclusion is surjective on points — which is the hypothesis hreduction. That hypothesis is quantified over every algebraic stack over S, mentions neither the stack nor the point the conclusion ranges over, and so restricts no object; the library does not have it, its Stacks 050C recording the reduction as a predicate for that reason

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Conditions (2) and (3) of Stacks 06MT are equivalent.** A point of an algebraic stack over
`S` is the image of the singleton space of points of a monomorphism with reduced source exactly
when it is the image, under a monomorphism, of a point of the spectrum of a field covering the
source surjectively and flatly.

Both directions are the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) of **Stacks 06MN**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isReducedWithUniquePoint_iff_hasFlatFieldSpectrumCover`, applied to the
source of the monomorphism, which is left unchanged. Going forwards, the unique point of the
source has a preimage on the cover because the cover is surjective; going backwards, the image
of the chosen point of the cover is a point of the source, and the source has at most one
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x ↔
      HasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Conditions (1) and (3) of Stacks 06MT are equivalent.** The implication (1) ⟹ (3) is
(1) ⟹ (2) followed by (2) ⟹ (3); the implication (3) ⟹ (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_flatFieldCover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x ↔ HasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3) are equivalent, granting the existence half of Stacks 0509 at the whole point set — that every algebraic stack over S has a reduction — which is the hypothesis hreduction, used only for the forward implication. That hypothesis is quantified over every algebraic stack over S, mentions neither the stack nor the point the conclusion ranges over, and so restricts no object; the library does not have it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 06MT are equivalent.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over
`S` and let `x` be a point of `|𝒳|`. Some *reduced* algebraic stack admits a monomorphism to `𝒳`
whose space of points is a singleton mapping to `x` if and only if some algebraic stack does.

The forward implication is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_reduced`,
which the source calls immediate. For the converse the source replaces the given `𝒵` by its
reduction, and so does this proof. The reduction is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_reduction`,
the reduced closed substack of **Stacks 0509** on the whole of `|𝒵|`; its inclusion
`j : 𝒵_red ⟶ 𝒵` is a monomorphism, being representable by algebraic spaces as a closed immersion
and fully faithful as the inclusion of a full subcategory, so `j` composed with the given
monomorphism is one by **Stacks 04ZY**. The space `|𝒵_red|` is a singleton because `j` is
surjective on points by the choice of the reduction and injective on them by **Stacks 0500**,
`|𝒵|` being a singleton; and the unique point of `𝒵_red` maps to the unique point of `𝒵`, hence
to `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x ↔
      HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2) are equivalent, unconditionally: the reduction is the theorem `exists_reduction` (Stacks 0509), so nothing is assumed. This supersedes the base's `hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism`, which carries `hreduction`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MT, the equivalence of conditions (1), (2) and (3).** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack
over `S` and let `x` be a point of `|𝒳|`. The following are equivalent:

1. some algebraic stack admits a monomorphism to `𝒳` whose space of points is a singleton mapping
   to `x`;
2. some reduced algebraic stack does;
3. some algebraic stack `𝒵` admits a monomorphism `f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` and a surjective flat 1-morphism
   `z : Spec(k) ⟶ 𝒵` from the spectrum of a field, with `x = f(z)`.

The equivalence of (1) and (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism`
and that of (2) and (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    List.TFAE
      [HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x,
        HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x,
        HasFlatFieldCoverMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1), (2) and (3), unconditionally: (1) iff (2) is `hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism_iff_hasSingletonPointMonomorphism` of this file, proved from the theorem `exists_reduction`, not the base's `hreduction`-carrying version

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsUnique_isResidualGerbeAt
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `x` be a point of `|𝒳|` such that some
algebraic stack whose space of points is a singleton mapping to `x` admits a monomorphism to
`𝒳` (`HasSingletonPointMonomorphism`). Then there is exactly one strictly full subcategory
`𝒵_x ⊂ 𝒳` which is a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack whose space of points is a
singleton mapping to `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isResidualGerbeAt
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (h : HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x) :
    ∃! P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P
declarations.comment: the final assertion: under the equivalent conditions there is a unique strictly full subcategory of X which is a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack whose space of points is a singleton mapping to x; unconditional, through this file's (1) iff (2) and the unconditional 06MR

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 06MT.** The one-point substack of condition (1) can be chosen
reduced.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1), the existence of the residual gerbe of X at x, read as condition (2) of the three equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MT

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbe
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MU, part (2): the residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x`, as an algebraic stack.** The
source takes it to be the strictly full subcategory `𝒵_x ⊂ 𝒳` produced by **Stacks 06MT**, that
is, the one cut out by an object property of `𝒳` meeting the specification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt`: closed under isomorphism, with full subcategory a
reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack having exactly one point, lying over `x`.

That object property `P` and the proof `hP` that it meets the specification are the data of this
definition. They are the defining property of the object being defined — what the source supposes
when it says that, the residual gerbe existing, it *is* `𝒵_x` — and not a substitute for an
unproved result: the algebraic stack returned is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack` at `P`, whose algebraicity is one of the
conjuncts of `hP`.

Nothing here picks `P` out. Uniqueness of the object property, and with it the definite article
in "*the* residual gerbe", is the final assertion of Stacks 06MT; the library proves it as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isResidualGerbeAt_of_bootstrap`, and the existence of such an
object property relative to Stacks 06FI, as `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_hasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism`, both in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.ResidualGerbeEquivalentConditions`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev residualGerbe
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property))
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hP : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P) :
    AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS
declarations.comment: part (2), the residual gerbe as an algebraic stack: the strictly full subcategory of X cut out by an object property meeting the specification IsResidualGerbeAt of Stacks 06MT

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbeInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MU, part (2): the inclusion of the residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x`.** The residual
gerbe is a *strictly full subcategory* of `𝒳`, and this is the inclusion 1-morphism `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳`
that makes it one: `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fullSubcategoryInclusion` at the object property
witnessing the specification.

The inclusion is fully faithful, being the inclusion of a full subcategory
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.full_fullSubcategoryInclusion` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.faithful_fullSubcategoryInclusion`), and it satisfies the monomorphy
clause of **Stacks 04ZW** by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.mono_representingMaps_fullSubcategoryInclusion`. That it
is also representable by algebraic spaces, and so a monomorphism, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isMonomorphism_fullSubcategoryInclusion`, the last
assertion of Stacks 06MR, in a module downstream of this one.
declarations.statement:
def residualGerbeInclusion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property))
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hP : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P) :
    residualGerbe B S hS 𝒳 x P hP ⟶ 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (2), the inclusion of the residual gerbe into X as a strictly full subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRegularStack_of_isReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint
declarations.doc:
A reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack over `S` whose space of points of
**Stacks 04XG** is a singleton is regular.

Reducedness and singletonness give a surjective flat 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒵` out of the spectrum
of a field by **Stacks 06MN**. Against a locally Noetherian smooth surjective scheme atlas
`V ⟶ 𝒵`, the 2-fibre product `Spec k ×_𝒵 V` is represented by an algebraic space which is smooth
over `Spec k`, hence regular by **Stacks 06M1**, and whose projection to `V` is flat and
surjective, so `V` is regular by **Stacks 06MK**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularStack_of_isReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h : IsReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵) :
    IsRegularStack B S hS 𝒵

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_factorization_of_isResidualGerbeAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MW.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `x` be a point of `|𝒳|` and
assume the residual gerbe `𝒵_x` of `𝒳` at `x` exists, i.e. an object property `P` of `𝒳`
satisfies the specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of **Stacks 06MT**. Let
`f` be a 1-morphism to `𝒳` from the algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field, some point of
which maps to `x`. Then `f` factors through the inclusion `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳`: there is a 1-morphism `g`
to the full subcategory selected by `P` and a 2-isomorphism `g ≫ (𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳) ≅ f`.

The factorisation is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_factorization_of_hasUniquePointOver`, which
uses only the one-point clause of `IsResidualGerbeAt`. It needs the inclusion `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳` to be a
monomorphism, so representable by algebraic spaces; the source has this from Stacks 04Y5, the
inclusion being fully faithful, and the library has the implication (2) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 04Y5 as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_faithful`,
from the bootstrap theorem Stacks 04S6 part (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_of_isResidualGerbeAt
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hP : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P)
    (F : FieldSpectrum B S hS) (f : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F.base ⟶ 𝒳)
    (t : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F.base))
    (ht : AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f t = x) :
    ∃ g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS F.base ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hP.2.choose,
      Nonempty (g ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP.2.choose ≅ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MX.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `x` be a point of its space of
points of **Stacks 04XG**, let `𝒵` be an algebraic stack over `S` satisfying condition (2) of
