**Stacks 06MP**, and let `f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` be a monomorphism whose image on points is exactly `{x}`.
Then the residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x` exists — some object property of `𝒳` satisfies the
specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of **Stacks 06MT** — and `f` factors
through the inclusion of that full subcategory by a 1-morphism whose underlying functor is an
equivalence of categories.

The object property is the essential image of the functor underlying `f`. The monomorphism `f`
is fully faithful by **Stacks 05UK**, so the factorization through the essential image is an
equivalence of categories, hence an equivalence over the big fppf site by **Stacks 003Z**; the
full subcategory is therefore an algebraic stack by **Stacks 03YQ** and inherits condition (2)
of Stacks 06MP, which makes it reduced, locally Noetherian and one-point by the implication
(2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 06MP. Its point lies over `x` because the factorization 2-commutes and the
image of `|f|` is `{x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isMonomorphism
    (𝒳 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B S hS f)
    (h𝒵 : HasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldSpectrumCover B S hS 𝒵)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (himg : Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f) = {x}) :
    ∃ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj)
      (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P)),
      IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P ∧
        ∃ g : 𝒵 ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hP,
          Functor.IsEquivalence (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor g.hom) ∧
            Nonempty (g ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP ≅ f)
declarations.comment: with the equivalent conditions of Stacks 06MP read as its CONDITION (2), `Dualizing`-style condition (1) being unavailable here: the library proves only (2) => (1) of 06MP, its (1) => (2) resting on fppf descent of flatness (05VY, 06Q0) which is not carried, and there is no transport of `IsReducedStack`/`IsLocallyNoetherianStack` — both `HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas` — along an equivalence over the site. Otherwise unconditional. The uniqueness of the subcategory is NOT claimed: that is Stacks 06MR, which carries the representability hypothesis of 04Y5 (2) => (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MY, the Deligne–Mumford assertion for monomorphisms.** A monomorphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` is Deligne–Mumford.

A monomorphism is representable by algebraic spaces — the first conjunct of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism`, Stacks 04ZW — and a 1-morphism
representable by algebraic spaces is Deligne–Mumford, so the monomorphism condition on the
represented base changes is not needed. The source argues instead that the relative diagonal of a
monomorphism is an isomorphism and that an isomorphism of algebraic spaces is unramified; the
route taken here reaches the same conclusion from less.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_of_isMonomorphism (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hf : IsMonomorphism B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsDM B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MY, the separatedness assertion for monomorphisms.** A monomorphism of algebraic
stacks over `S` is separated.

Every algebraic space representing a base change of a monomorphism has monomorphic structural
morphism, so that morphism is a monomorphism of presheaves (Stacks 042M) and hence separated
(Stacks 042N); so the monomorphism is separated in the relative sense of Stacks 04XB, and its
relative diagonal is therefore proper by Stacks 04YS.

The source argues instead that the relative diagonal of a monomorphism is an isomorphism and that
an isomorphism of algebraic spaces is proper; the route taken here reaches the same conclusion
without that comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isMonomorphism (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hf : IsMonomorphism B S hS f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MY, the separatedness assertion for immersions.** An immersion of algebraic stacks
over `S` is separated.

An immersion is a monomorphism by Stacks 0504, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_isMonomorphism`. This is the reduction the
source makes when it says that the same is true for immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isImmersion (j : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j) :
    IsSeparated B S hS j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MY, the Deligne–Mumford assertion for immersions.** An immersion of algebraic
stacks over `S` is Deligne–Mumford.

An immersion is representable by algebraic spaces — the first conjunct of Stacks 04YL, part (3) —
and a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces is Deligne–Mumford, so the immersion condition
on the represented base changes is not needed. The source reduces the assertion to the
monomorphism case, an immersion being a monomorphism by Stacks 0504; the route taken here reaches
the same conclusion from less. The separatedness assertion of Stacks 06MY for immersions, which
does use the immersion condition, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement: theorem isDM_of_isImmersion (j : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j) : Stack.IsDM B S hS j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MZ, the Deligne–Mumford clause.** The source of a monomorphism into a
Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack is Deligne–Mumford.

The monomorphism is a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism by Stacks 06MY, so part (5) of Stacks 050L
applies to it. The statement is made at an arbitrary monomorphism, which is the form in which
Stacks 06MZ's own proof uses it; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_of_isMonomorphism (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hf : IsMonomorphism B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒵

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MZ, the quasi-Deligne–Mumford clause.** The source of a monomorphism into a
quasi-Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack is quasi-Deligne–Mumford.

The quasi-Deligne–Mumford counterpart of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_of_isMonomorphism`, through part (6) of
Stacks 050L.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isMonomorphism (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hf : IsMonomorphism B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒵

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MZ, the separatedness clause.** The source of a monomorphism into a separated
algebraic stack is separated.

The monomorphism is a separated 1-morphism by Stacks 06MY, so part (7) of Stacks 050L applies to
it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isMonomorphism (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hf : IsMonomorphism B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ 𝒵

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MZ, the quasi-separatedness clause.** The source of a monomorphism into a
quasi-separated algebraic stack is quasi-separated.

The quasi-separated counterpart of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isMonomorphism`, through part
(8) of Stacks 050L.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isMonomorphism (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hf : IsMonomorphism B S hS f) (h𝒳 : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ 𝒵

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_division_identityArrowOpens_of_isoSpecField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04S4 applied to the open and closed piece through the identity.**  A groupoid scheme
whose object scheme is the spectrum of a field, whose arrow scheme is zero-dimensional and whose
pre-relation is unramified, separated, locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite can be
divided by the piece of its arrow scheme through the identity, and the quotient is the spectrum
of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_division_identityArrowOpens_of_isoSpecField {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (iso : G.objects.left ≅ Spec (.of k))
    [IsLocallyArtinian G.arrows.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.source.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.target.left]
    [Unramified (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [IsSeparated (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite (prod.lift G.target G.source).left]
    (u : G.objects.left) :
    ∃ (P : OpenFiniteSubgroupoid G)
      (D : Division G P.subgroupoid P.inclusion P.objects_eq),
      Set.range P.inclusion.mapArrows.left.base = {G.identity.left.base u} ∧
        IsField Γ(D.quotient.left, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the division of the groupoid of a flat field-valued presentation by the open and closed piece of its arrow scheme through the identity, with the quotient the spectrum of a field: the step of the proof which produces the field k_0 of invariants

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N0.** A DM, locally Noetherian, reduced algebraic stack whose point space is a
singleton admits a field `k` and a surjective étale 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒵`.

The implication is carried as the hypothesis `hCover`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ExistsSurjectiveEtaleFieldCoverOfReducedSingletonDM` for exactly which
cited inputs are absent and why no part of the chain can be run without them.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover
    (hCover : ExistsSurjectiveEtaleFieldCoverOfReducedSingletonDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒵 : IsReducedLocallyNoetherianSingletonDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒵) :
    HasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵
declarations.comment: a DM, locally Noetherian, reduced algebraic stack with a singleton point space admits a surjective etale 1-morphism from the spectrum of a field. The implication is carried as the hypothesis `hCover`: the source's first step is the direction (1) => (2) of Stacks 06MP, of which this library proves only the converse, and Stacks 06FF, 06LZ and 04S4 are absent too

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N0.** A DM, locally Noetherian, reduced algebraic stack whose point space is a
singleton admits a field `k` and a surjective étale 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒵`.

The field-valued point is produced in two steps. **Stacks 06MP**, part (1) ⟹ (2), gives a
surjective, flat, locally finitely presented `ξ : Spec k ⟶ 𝒵`; and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isEtale_fieldSpectrum_cover_of_flat_fieldSpectrum_cover` divides
the groupoid of that flat presentation by the open subgroupoid through the identity and returns
an étale 1-morphism out of the spectrum of the field of invariants. Surjectivity of that
1-morphism is read off the point space: `|𝒵|` is a subsingleton and the algebraic stack of the
spectrum of a field has a point. The DM hypothesis is used at the division, in the absolute form
of **Stacks 050D** part (5), turned into DM-ness over `S` by **Stacks 050N** part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover_unconditional
    (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒵 : IsReducedLocallyNoetherianSingletonDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒵) :
    HasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover.{u, w} B S hS 𝒵
declarations.comment: a DM, locally Noetherian, reduced algebraic stack with a singleton point space admits a surjective etale 1-morphism from the spectrum of a field. The field-valued point comes in two steps: Stacks 06MP (1) => (2) supplies a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented xi : Spec k -> Z, and the groupoid (U, R, s, t, c) of that flat presentation, with U = Spec k and R = U x_Z U, is divided by the open and closed subgroupoid P through the identity, whose quotient U_bar = Spec k_0 is the spectrum of the field of invariants. The division is exists_division_identityArrowOpens_etale_pointGroupoid, on the four conclusions of Stacks 04S4 in exists_division; it is run at the de-realization of the self-intersection groupoid, whose object and arrow spaces are representable by isRepresentable_objects_pointGroupoid_fieldSpectrum and isRepresentable_arrows_pointGroupoid_fieldSpectrum, the latter being condition (2) of Stacks 06LZ read on the base site at the dimension bound dimension_relation_le_zero_fieldSpectrum, i.e. Stacks 06FF against the quasi-DM hypothesis through Stacks 050H part (5). Etaleness of U_bar -> Z follows the source's steps 6 and 8 rather than its Stacks 04XD reading: the divided groupoid is the restriction of the descended groupoid (U_bar, R_bar, s_bar, t_bar, c_bar) along the finite locally free surjection U -> U_bar, so [U/R] -> [U_bar/R_bar] is an equivalence by Stacks 046T (nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_quotientStackMap_realizationHom, whose clause (1) is full faithfulness of the evaluations of the descent morphism and whose clause (2) is that its map on objects is an fppf covering), [U/R] -> Z is an equivalence by Stacks 04WY (nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_canonicalMap), and s_bar is etale by Division.etale_descended_source, which is Stacks 047W at unramifiedness through etale_source_of_flat_of_isOpenImmersion_identity rather than the computation of Omega_{R_bar/U_bar} that Stacks 04R9 gives the source. Stacks 04M9 then makes the projection S_{U_bar} -> [U_bar/R_bar] of Stacks 044R etale (isRelativelyEtale_quotientStackProjection_realization), and two instances of Stacks 0457 carry that verdict across the equivalence with Z and down the universe lift of the source, giving quotientProjectionSchemeStackMap, which is etale in the sense of Stacks 0CIL by isEtale_of_isRelativelyEtale. The DM hypothesis enters only at the division, in the absolute form of Stacks 050D part (5), turned into DM-ness over S by Stacks 050N part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isOpenSubspace_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N2, with the conclusion read on an open subspace of the chart.** Let `𝒳` be an
algebraic stack, let `U` be an algebraic space with a 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` which is flat and
locally of finite presentation, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a field-valued point and let
`F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` with projection `p : F ⟶ U`. If `F ⟶ Spec k` is unramified at `z ∈ |F|` then
there is an open subspace `V ⊆ U`, in the sense of **Stacks 02YU**, part (2), whose point set
contains `p(z)` and for which the composite of the 1-morphism of **Stacks 0458** induced by `V`
with `f` is étale.

This is the source's own conclusion, obtained from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isEtale_unconditional` the way
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isOpenSubspace_isLocallyQuasiFinite` is obtained from
Stacks 06ME, with `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_comp_of_eq_essImage` for the transport.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isEtale
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (z : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g))
    (hz : FibreIsUnramifiedNear.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g z) :
    ∃ (V : Subfunctor U) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V),
      AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
          (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) z ∈
        spacePointMap B S hS U (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU).val
            (BasedFunctor.id (fibredCategory B S hS U).val) ''
          Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        IsEtale B S hS (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS hV.1 hU V.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the conclusion read on an open subspace of the algebraic space, as the source reads it: the composite of the 1-morphism of Stacks 0458 induced by an open subspace containing the image of the given point of the fibre with the given 1-morphism is etale. Nothing is added to exists_openSubstack_isEtale_unconditional: its open substack is carried to an open subspace with the same point set by exists_isOpenSubspace_property_eq_essImage, and the etaleness is carried across the Stacks 0506 factorization of that subspace's 1-morphism through the substack's inclusion by isEtale_comp_of_eq_essImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N2.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack, let `U` be an algebraic space with a
1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` which is flat and locally of finite presentation, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a
field-valued point, and let `F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` with projection `p : F ⟶ U` and structure
1-morphism `q : F ⟶ Spec k`. If `q` is unramified at `z ∈ |F|` then, after replacing `U` by an
open subspace containing `p(z)`, the 1-morphism `U ⟶ 𝒳` is étale.

The proof is the source's. The open substack `W` is the locus `W(f)` of **Stacks 06M5** on which
`f` is étale, carried as the data `W` with `hW`, and its compatibility with the base change along
`g` is carried as `hBaseChange`. The step from the source's pointwise hypothesis to étaleness of
the fibre near `z` is **Stacks 06LU** — unramified plus flat plus locally of finite presentation
gives étale — which the library has for morphisms of algebraic spaces
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_of_isFlat_of_isUnramified`) but not for 1-morphisms of
algebraic stacks; it is carried as `hFibreEtale`, stated over `Spec k`, which is where the source
applies it. Given those, the conclusion is that `p(z) ∈ |W|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_isEtale
    (_hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (_hfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (W : OpenSubstack (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU))
    (hW : IsEtale B S hS (W.inclusion ≫ f))
    (hFibreEtale : ∀ V : OpenSubstack (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g),
      IsUnramified B S hS
          (V.inclusion ≫ fibreStructureMorphism B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) →
        IsEtale B S hS
          (V.inclusion ≫ fibreStructureMorphism B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g))
    (hBaseChange : ∀ V : OpenSubstack (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g),
      IsEtale B S hS
          (V.inclusion ≫ fibreStructureMorphism B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) →
        V.pointSet B S hS ⊆
          AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
              (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) ⁻¹' W.pointSet B S hS)
    (z : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g))
    (hz : FibreIsUnramifiedNear.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g z) :
    AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
        (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) z ∈ W.pointSet B S hS ∧
      IsEtale B S hS (W.inclusion ≫ f)
declarations.comment: after replacing the algebraic space by an open subspace containing the image of the given point of the fibre, a flat, locally finitely presented 1-morphism whose fibre over a field-valued point is unramified at that point is etale. Three inputs are carried: the data `W` with `hW` and the hypothesis `hBaseChange`, which are the two clauses of Stacks 06M5 at etaleness, absent from this library; and `hFibreEtale`, which is Stacks 06LU for 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over the field-valued point, available in this library only for morphisms of algebraic spaces. The deduction of the conclusion from them is proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isEtale_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N2.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack, let `U` be an algebraic space with a
1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` which is flat and locally of finite presentation, let `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a
field-valued point, and let `F = U ×_𝒳 Spec k` with projection `p : F ⟶ U` and structure
1-morphism `q : F ⟶ Spec k`. If `q` is unramified at `z ∈ |F|` then, after replacing `U` by an
open subspace containing `p(z)`, the 1-morphism `U ⟶ 𝒳` is étale.

The proof is the source's, and nothing is carried. The open substack `W` is the locus `W(𝒫, f)`
of assertion (A) of **Stacks 06M3** at `𝒫 = ` **unramifiedness** — the entry of the list of
**Stacks 06M5** whose base-change clause holds for an *arbitrary* base change, and so the entry
that applies to the base change along a field-valued point. It exists by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isRelativePropertyLocus_of_hasRelativePropertyLocusOnSpaces` at
the entry-(3) instances
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativePropertyLocusOnSpaces_isUnramified` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativePropertyLocusBaseChange_isUnramified` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/LocalSourceLemmaUnramified.lean`, the source's `𝒬` being
local finite type, which `f` has because it is locally of finite presentation
(**Stacks 0464**).

The conclusion `p(z) ∈ |W|` is the maximality half of assertion (B),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointSet_subset_preimage_of_hasRelativeProperty`, at the open substack
of `F` that the fibre hypothesis supplies. That step consumes unramifiedness in the relative
sense of **Stacks 04XB** while the fibre hypothesis and the étaleness criterion are stated at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsUnramified` (**Stacks 0CIT**), and *both* directions of that
comparison are available here because every 1-morphism in sight is representable by algebraic
spaces: `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_unramified_of_isUnramified` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_of_hasRelativeProperty_unramified`, whose étale-smooth
diagram comes from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSurjectiveEtaleSmoothDiagram_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`
and not from **Stacks 0CIA**. Given that comparison, an open `W` with `hW` and the base-change containment
`hBaseChange` are not needed as hypotheses.

Étaleness of `f|_W` is **Stacks 06LU** for 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_fullSubcategoryInclusion_comp_of_isUnramified`, applied to the
restriction of `f` to `W`, which is flat and locally of finite presentation because `f` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_isEtale_unconditional
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (z : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (fibreOverFieldPoint B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g))
    (hz : FibreIsUnramifiedNear.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g z) :
    ∃ W : OpenSubstack (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS U hU),
      AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
          (fibreProjection B S hS 𝒳 U hU k hk toBase f g) z ∈ W.pointSet B S hS ∧
        IsEtale B S hS (W.inclusion ≫ f)
declarations.comment: after replacing the algebraic space by an open subspace containing the image of the given point of the fibre, a flat, locally finitely presented 1-morphism whose fibre over a field-valued point is unramified at that point is etale. Nothing is carried: the open substack is the locus W(P, f) of assertion (A) of Stacks 06M3 at P = unramified -- the entry of the list of Stacks 06M5 whose base-change clause holds for an arbitrary base change, which is why it and not the etale entry applies to a base change along a field-valued point -- produced by exists_isRelativePropertyLocus_of_hasRelativePropertyLocusOnSpaces from the entry-(3) instances of LocalSourceLemmaUnramified, and the conclusion that the image of the given point of the fibre lies in it is the maximality half of assertion (B) at the open substack the fibre hypothesis supplies. The comparison of the two renderings of unramifiedness, Stacks 0CIT against the relative notion of Stacks 04XB, is available in both directions for a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces, by hasSurjectiveEtaleSmoothDiagram_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces, and needs nothing of Stacks 0CIA. Stacks 06LU for 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks is not carried but proved, and it is what turns the locus into the etaleness of the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyDM_iff_isDeligneMumfordStack_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N3.** An algebraic stack is DM exactly when it is Deligne–Mumford — equivalently,
by **Stacks 03YO**, exactly when there is a scheme of the site carrying a representable,
surjective, étale 1-morphism to it.

Both directions are proved and nothing is assumed. The implication (2) ⟹ (1) — equivalently
(3) ⟹ (1), these being the same condition here — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyDM_of_isDeligneMumfordStack`, off part (1) of
**Stacks 06MB**. The substantial direction (1) ⟹ (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM` of this file: the source's
étale chart at one finite type point, with the size bound uniform in the point
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isRelativelyEtale_chart_size_le_of_isFiniteTypePoint`), fed to
the family assembly
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM_of_forall_exists_chart`, which
builds the index type, puts the coproduct in the site, and produces the surjective relatively
étale 1-morphism out of it
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDeligneMumfordStack_of_forall_isRelativelyEtale`).

The substantial direction, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM`,
reduced to the chart construction `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ExistsEtaleChartFamilyOfIsAbsolutelyDM`,
is proved and not carried as a hypothesis. The statement cannot be placed in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.DeligneMumfordPresentationTheorem`:
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.EtaleChartFamilySizeBound`, which this file needs for the
family assembly, imports that module, so naming
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM` there would be an import
cycle.

The attribute below records where each step of the source's argument is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_iff_isDeligneMumfordStack_unconditional
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒳 ↔
      IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val.val
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) DM with (2) Deligne-Mumford and (3) the existence of a surjective etale presentation by a scheme; (2) and (3) are the same condition here, since Stacks 03YO defines Deligne-Mumford that way. The implication (2) => (1) is proved, from Stacks 06MB part (1); the structure theorem (1) => (3) is PROVED, not carried, as existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM of this file -- the chart at ONE finite type point with the uniform size bound (exists_isRelativelyEtale_chart_size_le_of_isFiniteTypePoint) fed to the family assembly existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM_of_forall_exists_chart. The statement binds only the containment hZ of the terminal scheme, which the absolute Deligne-Mumford condition is stated at, and the algebraic stack 𝒳, and nothing stands for the structure theorem. The CHART CONSTRUCTION it runs on, the source's etale chart at each finite type point together with the site-membership of their coproduct, is isolated as ExistsEtaleChartFamilyOfIsAbsolutelyDM, and delivers the presentation by existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM_of_existsEtaleChartFamily. Everything the source does after the charts is proved, in isDeligneMumfordStack_of_forall_isRelativelyEtale: the 1-morphism out of the coproduct W = ∐_x Z_x is exists_stackMap_comp_iso_sigmaOver_of_lt_cof, its surjectivity is exists_isSurjective_stackMap_of_finiteTypePoints_subset_iUnion_range (resting on 06R7 and the corollary of 06G2 rather than on any property of the assembled chart), and its relative etaleness is isRelativelyEtale_of_isColimit_of_forall_isRelativelyEtale, the descent of the relative property of 03YK along the summand inclusions. NO TAG of the construction is carried. Stacks 06N0 is hasSurjectiveEtaleFieldSpectrumCover_unconditional, at its own binders: the division of the groupoid of the flat field-valued presentation by the open and closed subgroupoid through the identity is exists_division_identityArrowOpens_of_isoSpecField, on identityOpenFiniteSubgroupoid and mono_prodLift_of_unramified; the two tags it rests on are proved -- all four conclusions of 04S4 are exists_division and condition (2) of 06LZ is isRepresentable_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_over_field; the construction carrying the stack-level flat presentation to a GroupoidScheme is the de-realization of the self-intersection groupoid, on isRepresentable_objects_pointGroupoid_fieldSpectrum and isRepresentable_arrows_pointGroupoid_fieldSpectrum; and the etaleness of Spec k_0 -> Z is isOpenImmersion_descended_identity and etale_descended_source read off the presentation through the quotient stack of the divided groupoid, by isEtale_quotientProjectionSchemeStackMap across the 046T equivalence nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_quotientStackMap_realizationHom, rather than by 04XD. So the source's unramified field-valued point at a finite type point follows outright, by exists_relativelyUnramified_fieldSpectrum_point_of_isFiniteTypePoint, whose own binders are its statement's. The step before it is PROVED and not carried: the residual gerbe exists, by 06G3 (1) => (3) (existsLocallyOfFiniteTypeResidualGerbe, which needs neither Artin's theorem 06DC nor 04Y5 (2) => (3), cutting the gerbe out of the target instead), its inclusion is a monomorphism (AlgebraicStacks.isMonomorphism_fullSubcategoryInclusion) and the gerbe is a reduced, locally Noetherian, one-point DM algebraic stack, which is exactly the hypothesis of 06N0 (isReducedLocallyNoetherianSingletonDM_of_isResidualGerbeAt, by 06MZ at that monomorphism). So 06G3 (1) => (3) is not carried either. Stacks 06MP (1) => (2) and both halves of 06MM are available. What else is missing is the body of the source's argument at a single finite type point -- the affine V etale over F = U x_X Spec k, its closed point with residue field finite separable over k, the regular sequence, and the slicing -- of which two steps are available: from the source's phi(m_u) O_{V,v} = m_v of 02GF, the regular sequence is exists_mem_maximalIdeal_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_fiberStalk_of_smooth, which produces it GENERATING the maximal ideal of the fibre stalk and not merely cutting it to dimension zero (the fibre stalk of a smooth morphism is regular, so a minimal generating family selected inside phi(m_u) by exists_fn_mem_maximalIdeal_ofList_map_eq_maximalIdeal is regular by 00NQ), and the residue computation O_{T,v} = kappa(v) off it is map_maximalIdeal_comp_eq_of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_fiberStalk, read on the scheme-theoretic fibre by isField_fiberStalk_comp_of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_fiberStalk. Both clauses of 02GF that body needs are proved as well, each off the unramifiedness of F -> U that the monomorphy of Z_x -> X gives: the PRODUCTION of phi(m_u) O_{V,v} = m_v, and with it the sequence generating m_v, is exists_fn_mem_maximalIdeal_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_stalk_of_unramifiedAt (with exists_isAffineOpen_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_stalk_of_unramifiedAt reading it as regular functions on an affine open, the source's first shrinking), and its passage to the ETALE local ring where 06MD reads its hypothesis is exists_fn_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_etaleLocalRing_of_unramifiedAt across the faithful flatness of 05VP and the square of local rings of 05VU, with forall_isRegular_etaleLocalRingMap_germ_of_isRegular_chartLocalRing the same passage in the germ shape FibreIsRegularSequenceAt is written in, quantifier over etale neighbourhoods included (it costs nothing, by etaleLocalRingMap_etaleLocalRingGerm_eval_eq), so that the fibre hypothesis of 06MD is reduced to a regular sequence in the ordinary local ring of a scheme chart of the fibre; the SECOND clause of 02GF for the slice, the transport of the finite separability of kappa(v)/k along O_{V,v} ->> O_{T,v}, is unramifiedAt_comp_of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_fiberStalk, on bijective_residueFieldMap_of_isPreimmersion, with unramifiedAt_comp_of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_stalk the same statement at a generating sequence read in O_{V,v} -- where the sequence above is produced -- the two agreeing over a field-valued point of the base by ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_fiberStalk_of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal. The SLICING POINT of that body is proved too, with everything both slicing lemmas read off it: exists_isClosed_isAffineOpen_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_finiteSeparable_of_unramified of SmoothSliceSeparablePoint takes an unramified q : V -> U of schemes with V nonempty and smooth over Spec k and returns the closed point v of 056U, the regularity of O_{V,v}, the sequence of regular functions on an affine open of U whose germs generate m_v as a regular sequence, and the residue field extension in the shape the criterion of 02GF reads it; the two come stated over DIFFERENT renderings of kappa(v) as an extension -- 056U through evaluation of global sections of Spec k, the criterion over kappa(pi v) through residueFieldMap -- and the reconciliation is finite_separable_residueFieldMap_of_finite_separable_Gammaevaluation of the same file, the two algebra structures sitting in one scalar tower by Gammaevaluation_naturality, with isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth_over_field the scheme form of the regularity (056S on stalks through 02IT) and unramifiedAt_comp_of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_stalk_over_field the unramifiedness of the slice with the hypothesis on the base discharged, the local ring of Spec k being the field itself. The slicing sequence in the etale local ring is likewise available off the hypotheses the assembly PRODUCES rather than off a chart square: exists_fn_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_etaleLocalRing_of_isUnramified of FibreSlicingSequenceFromIsUnramified asks only for Space.IsUnramified of the projection F -> U and regularity of F, discharging the chart-square hypotheses itself by unramified_chartMap_of_isUnramified (what Space.IsUnramified says, 03ZH part (1)) and isRegularLocalRing_chartLocalRing (06M1's etale-local regularity carried to a prescribed small etale neighbourhood by 03E8 and read on the stalk by 02IT). What remains of the body is its ASSEMBLY at one finite type point, and that is now exactly the identifications and the plumbing. The relative unramifiedness of exists_relativelyUnramified_fieldSpectrum_point_of_isFiniteTypePoint is NOT carried: read at a chart it is Space.IsUnramified of the projection F -> U of the fibre F = U x_X Spec k, by isUnramified_fibreSpaceProjection_of_relativeProperty of FibreProjectionUnramified, which carries the relative condition to the projection by 045C (hasRelativeProperty_baseChange_algebraicStacks) and reads it on the representing morphism by the 04XB bridge (hasRelativeProperty_iff_prop_representingMap); with the regularity of F that gives the slicing sequence in the etale local ring off the stack-level hypotheses alone, exists_fn_isRegular_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_etaleLocalRing_fibre of the same file. declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyDM_iff_isDeligneMumfordStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N3.** An algebraic stack is DM exactly when it is Deligne–Mumford — equivalently,
by **Stacks 03YO**, exactly when there is a scheme of the site with a representable, surjective,
étale 1-morphism to it.

Both implications are carried; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAbsolutelyDMOfExistsEtalePresentation` for what each one stands for
and why.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_iff_isDeligneMumfordStack
    (hForward : ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (hBackward : IsAbsolutelyDMOfExistsEtalePresentation.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒳 ↔
      IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val.val
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of (1) DM with (2) Deligne-Mumford and (3) the existence of a
  surjective etale presentation by a scheme; (2) and (3) are the same condition here, since
  Stacks 03YO defines Deligne-Mumford that way. Both implications are carried, as the
  hypotheses `hForward` (the structure theorem: Stacks 06MD, 06N0, 06N2, 06G2, 06G3 are absent)
  and `hBackward` (Stacks 06MB part (1) is present but the bridge from the Section 04XB form of
  an etale chart to the smooth-diagram flatness of Stacks 06PW is absent)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyDM_of_isDeligneMumfordStack
declarations.doc:
A Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack is DM: the implication (2) ⟹ (1), equivalently (3) ⟹ (1),
these being the same condition here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_of_isDeligneMumfordStack (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val.val) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: the implication (2) => (1), equivalently (3) => (1), these being the same condition here: an algebraic stack admitting a surjective etale presentation by a scheme is DM

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N4.**
Given `φ : x ⟶ y` strongly cartesian over `p`, an existing fibre product
`p x ×_{p y} p z` in `𝒞`, and a strongly cartesian morphism `a : w ⟶ z` in `𝒮`
lying over the second projection of that fibre product (as recorded by `hw` and `ha`),
the fibre product `x ×_y z` exists in `𝒮`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) {x y z : 𝒮} (φ : x ⟶ y) (g : z ⟶ y)
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map φ) φ]
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map φ) (p.map g)]
    (w : 𝒮) (a : w ⟶ z)
    (hw : p.obj w = Limits.pullback (p.map φ) (p.map g))
    (ha : p.map a = eqToHom hw ≫ Limits.pullback.snd (p.map φ) (p.map g))
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map a) a] :
    Limits.HasPullback φ g

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.pullbackIsoOfIsStronglyCartesian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N4.**
In the situation of `hasPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian` the fibre product `x ×_y z`
is canonically isomorphic to `w`: both are limits of the same cospan, `w` by the limit
square built from the strongly cartesian morphisms `φ` and `a`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackIsoOfIsStronglyCartesian
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) {x y z : 𝒮} (φ : x ⟶ y) (g : z ⟶ y)
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map φ) φ]
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map φ) (p.map g)]
    (w : 𝒮) (a : w ⟶ z)
    (hw : p.obj w = Limits.pullback (p.map φ) (p.map g))
    (ha : p.map a = eqToHom hw ≫ Limits.pullback.snd (p.map φ) (p.map g))
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map a) a] [Limits.HasPullback φ g] :
    Limits.pullback φ g ≅ w

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.hasPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N5, existence half.**
In a fibred category `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞`, if `φ : x ⟶ y` is strongly cartesian over `p` and
the fibre product of `p φ` and `p g` exists in `𝒞`, then the fibre product of `φ` and
`g` exists in `𝒮`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.IsFibered.hasPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFibered]
    {x y z : 𝒮} (φ : x ⟶ y) (g : z ⟶ y)
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map φ) φ]
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map φ) (p.map g)] :
    Limits.HasPullback φ g

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.snd_isStronglyCartesian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N5, second projection strongly cartesian.**
Under the same hypotheses the second projection `Limits.pullback.snd φ g : x ×_y z ⟶ z`
is strongly cartesian over `p`, since it is the canonical isomorphism `x ×_y z ≅ w`
followed by the strongly cartesian morphism `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.IsFibered.snd_isStronglyCartesian
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFibered]
    {x y z : 𝒮} (φ : x ⟶ y) (g : z ⟶ y)
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map φ) φ]
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map φ) (p.map g)]
    [Limits.HasPullback φ g] :
    Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p
      (p.map (Limits.pullback.snd φ g)) (Limits.pullback.snd φ g)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.map_isPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N5, image square is a fibre product square.**
Under the same hypotheses `p` sends the fibre product square of `φ, g` in `𝒮` to a
fibre product square in `𝒞`: the image `p (x ×_y z)`, with the images of the two
projections, is the fibre product of `p φ` and `p g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.IsFibered.map_isPullback_of_isStronglyCartesian
    (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFibered]
    {x y z : 𝒮} (φ : x ⟶ y) (g : z ⟶ y)
    [Functor.IsStronglyCartesian p (p.map φ) φ]
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map φ) (p.map g)]
    [Limits.HasPullback φ g] :
    IsPullback (p.map (Limits.pullback.fst φ g)) (p.map (Limits.pullback.snd φ g))
      (p.map φ) (p.map g)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.hasPullback
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be fibred in groupoids and let `gx : x ⟶ y`, `gz : z ⟶ y` be morphisms of `S`. If
the fibre product of `p.map gx` and `p.map gz` exists in `C`, then the fibre product of `gx` and
`gz` exists in `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.hasPullback
    (p : S ⥤ C) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    {x y z : S} (gx : x ⟶ y) (gz : z ⟶ y)
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map gx) (p.map gz)] :
    Limits.HasPullback gx gz

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.map_isPullback
declarations.doc:
For any fibre product `x ×_y z` in `S`, realized by a pullback square with vertex `P` and
projections `pr₁ : P ⟶ x`, `pr₂ : P ⟶ z`, the image `p.obj P` together with `p.map pr₁` and
`p.map pr₂` is a fibre product of `p.map gx` and `p.map gz` in `C`: `p` carries the pullback
square of `S` to a pullback square of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.map_isPullback
    (p : S ⥤ C) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    {x y z : S} (gx : x ⟶ y) (gz : z ⟶ y)
    [Limits.HasPullback (p.map gx) (p.map gz)]
    {P : S} (pr₁ : P ⟶ x) (pr₂ : P ⟶ z)
    (hP : IsPullback pr₁ pr₂ gx gz) :
    IsPullback (p.map pr₁) (p.map pr₂) (p.map gx) (p.map gz)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.exists_factorization_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.exists_factorization_isFiberedInGroupoids
    {𝒞 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} 𝒞]
    {𝒳 : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} 𝒳] (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    {𝒴 : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} 𝒴] (q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hF : F ⋙ q = p) :
    ∃ (𝒳' : Type (max u₁ u₃ v₁ v₃)) (_ : Category.{max v₁ v₃} 𝒳')
      (r : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒞) (a : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳') (t : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒴),
      r.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧
      (a ⋙ r = p) ∧ Nonempty (IsEquivalenceOver p r a) ∧
      (t ⋙ q = r) ∧ t.IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧
      (a ⋙ t = F)

declarations.name: amelioration_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06N8** (uniqueness of the factorization of 4.35.16 / 06N7).

Let `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`. Suppose `F`
is factored in two ways through categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`:
`𝒳 ⟶[a] 𝒳' ⟶[f] 𝒴` and `𝒳 ⟶[b] 𝒳'' ⟶[g] 𝒴`, where

* `a`, `b` are equivalences (over `𝒞`);
* the two factorizations agree with `F`: `a ⋙ f ≅ F` and `b ⋙ g ≅ F`.

Then there is an equivalence `h : 𝒳'' ⥤ 𝒳'` **over `𝒴`** (i.e. `h.IsEquivalence` together
with `h ⋙ f ≅ g`) such that `b ⋙ h ≅ a`. In particular the intermediate category is unique
up to equivalence over `𝒴`, compatibly with the first legs.

The conclusion uses none of the remaining data of 06N8 — the structure functors
`p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞`, `q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞`, `p' : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒞`, `p'' : 𝒳'' ⥤ 𝒞`, their fiberedness in
groupoids, that of `f` and `g`, and the compatibilities `a ⋙ p' = p`, `b ⋙ p'' = p`,
`f ⋙ q = p'`, `g ⋙ q = p''` — so it is stated in the general form below, which
specializes to 06N8 in the fibred setting.
declarations.statement:
theorem amelioration_unique
    {𝒞 : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} 𝒞]
    {𝒳 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} 𝒳]
    {𝒴 : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} 𝒴]
    {𝒳' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} 𝒳']
    {𝒳'' : Type u₅} [Category.{v₅} 𝒳'']
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (a : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳') (b : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳'')
    (f : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒴) (g : 𝒳'' ⥤ 𝒴)
    (ha_equiv : a.IsEquivalence) (hb_equiv : b.IsEquivalence)
    (hleft : a ⋙ f ≅ F) (hright : b ⋙ g ≅ F) :
    ∃ (h : 𝒳'' ⥤ 𝒳') (_ : h.IsEquivalence) (_ : h ⋙ f ≅ g),
      Nonempty (b ⋙ h ≅ a)

declarations.name: kolmogorov_iff_of_locallyClosed_cover
declarations.doc:
If a covering `U` of `X` consists of locally closed subsets, then `X` is Kolmogorov if and only
if each `U i` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem kolmogorov_iff_of_locallyClosed_cover
    {I : Type*} (U : I → Set X)
    (hcov : ⋃ i, U i = Set.univ)
    (hlc : ∀ i, IsLocallyClosed (U i)) :
    T0Space X ↔ ∀ i, T0Space (U i)

declarations.name: quasiSober_iff_of_open_cover
declarations.doc:
If a covering `U` of `X` consists of open subsets, then `X` is quasi-sober if and only if each
`U i` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSober_iff_of_open_cover
    {I : Type*} (U : I → Set X)
    (hcov : ⋃ i, U i = Set.univ)
    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) :
    QuasiSober X ↔ ∀ i, QuasiSober (U i)

declarations.name: sober_iff_of_open_cover
declarations.doc:
If a covering `U` of `X` consists of open subsets, then `X` is sober if and only if each `U i`
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem sober_iff_of_open_cover
    {I : Type*} (U : I → Set X)
    (hcov : ⋃ i, U i = Set.univ)
    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) :
    StacksSober X ↔ ∀ i, StacksSober (U i)

declarations.name: Topology.t0Space_of_isOpenMap_of_finite_fibres
declarations.doc:
If `π : U → X` is an open surjection from a `T0Space`, and `π` identifies exactly the pairs
related by the image of `(t, s) : R → U × U` for a map `t` with finite fibres, then `X` is
Kolmogorov.

This generalizes Stacks 06NA: soberness of `U` is weakened to `T0Space U`, only `t` is assumed to
have finite fibres, and the lifting of generalizations along `s` and `t` is not assumed. See the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem t0Space_of_isOpenMap_of_finite_fibres {R U X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace U] [T0Space U]
    [TopologicalSpace X] (s t : R → U) (π : U → X) (hπ_open : IsOpenMap π)
    (ht_fin : Function.HasFiniteFibres t) (hπ_surj : Function.Surjective π)
    (hπ_rel : ∀ u u' : U, π u = π u' ↔ Function.SourceTargetRel s t u u') :
    T0Space X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_comp_of_fppf_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06NB (flat).** If `f ≫ g` is flat and the singleton family
consisting of `f` is refined by an fppf covering of `Y`, then `g` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_comp_of_fppf_refinement
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Flat (f ≫ g)]
    (h : ∃ 𝒰 : Y.Cover.{v} Scheme.fppfPrecoverage,
      Nonempty (𝒰.toPreZeroHypercover.Hom (PreZeroHypercover.singleton f))) :
    Flat g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp_of_fppf_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06NB (locally finite type).** If `f ≫ g` is locally of finite type
and the singleton family consisting of `f` is refined by an fppf covering of `Y`, then `g` is
locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp_of_fppf_refinement

The morphism from a scheme to the open subspace corresponding to the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_etaleImage
declarations.doc:
The kernel pair of an étale scheme morphism is an étale equivalence
relation on its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_etaleImage
    {R : BigFppfOver B S hS} (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) f f) :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation
      (prod.lift ((Over.post B.inclusion).map s)
        ((Over.post B.inclusion).map t))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoequalizer_factor_through_etaleImage
declarations.doc:
The image open subspace is the fppf sheaf quotient of `U` by the kernel
pair of the original map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoequalizer_factor_through_etaleImage
    {R : BigFppfOver B S hS} (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) f f)
    (f' : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X'.toFunctor) (hfactor : f' ≫ X'.ι = f) :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology B S hS
    ∃ (hRsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj R))
      (hUsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj U)),
      let RF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj R, hRsh⟩
      let UF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨yoneda.obj U, hUsh⟩
      let XF : Sheaf J (Type u) := ⟨X'.toFunctor, hX'.1.isSheaf⟩
      let sf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map s⟩
      let tf : RF ⟶ UF := ⟨yoneda.map t⟩
      let ff : UF ⟶ XF := ⟨f'⟩
      let w : sf ≫ ff = tf ≫ ff := by
        apply Sheaf.hom_ext
        change yoneda.map s ≫ f' = yoneda.map t ≫ f'
        exact (isPullback_of_factors_comp_mono X'.ι hfactor hfactor hR).w
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ ff w))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_etale_surjective_lift_openSubspaceOfPoints_range_yoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NF, the whole of its factorisation clause.** Let `U` be an object of the big
fppf category over `S` and `f : h_U ⟶ X` an étale morphism to an algebraic space over `S`.
Then the subspace `X'` of `X` cut out by the image of `|U|` is an open subspace, and `f`
factors through it by a morphism which is surjective — both on point sets and after every
represented base change — and étale.

The four assertions correspond exactly to the four declarations into which the source's
sentence "*then `f` factors through a surjective étale morphism `f' : U → X'`*" is split: the
induced morphism, which here is the canonical `CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.lift` and so needs no
choice; the factorisation `f' ≫ X'.ι = f`, which is `CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.lift_ι` and
holds by `rfl`; surjectivity; and étaleness. That `X'` is an open subspace with point set the
image of `|U|` is the source's own appeal to Tag 03BZ, and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_openSubspaceOfPoints` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_ι_openSubspaceOfPoints`.

**What is not proved.** The source's second sentence — that `R = U ×_X U` equals `U ×_{X'} U`,
that it is an étale equivalence relation, and that `X'` is the quotient `U/R` — is not
addressed. So the covering set of Tag 06NF is incomplete and the attribute carries a part
string naming only the factorisation clause. Closing the rest needs Tag 0262, whose three
parts are proved in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Presentation.KernelPair`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_etale_surjective_lift_openSubspaceOfPoints_range_yoneda
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS
        (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X
          (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) f))) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf
        (Subfunctor.lift f (range_le_openSubspaceOfPoints_range_pointsMap f)) ∧
      Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U)
        (Subfunctor.lift f (range_le_openSubspaceOfPoints_range_pointsMap f))) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf
        (Subfunctor.lift f (range_le_openSubspaceOfPoints_range_pointsMap f))
declarations.comment: factorisation: induced morphism, factorization, surjective, étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_finite_etale_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NG.** An algebraic space over `S` admitting a finite étale surjective morphism
from a scheme over `S` has a representable open subspace whose point set is dense: such a
space is reasonable, so Stacks 03JI applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_finite_etale_cover
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {U : BigFppfOver B S hS} (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
    (hfin : IsFinite B S hS f) (_hetale : IsEtale B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor X, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_codimensionZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NH.** A Zariski locally quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` — for instance
a quasi-separated one — has a dense open subspace which is a scheme, and every point of
codimension `0` of the space lies in that subspace. The subspace is the schematic locus of
Tag 03JH.

Zariski local quasi-separatedness is the absolute notion of Tag 03BS part (4), as in the
source; by Tag 03W7 it is equivalent to the notion over `S`, which is how the proof uses it. The
containment `hZ` of the terminal scheme in the site is the argument of that absolute notion; it
holds in every big fppf site, by `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_terminal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_codimensionZero
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor F, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι) ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS F, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.denseRange_schematicLocus_of_isZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver
declarations.doc:
The schematic locus of a Zariski locally quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` is dense
in its space of points; so that space has a dense open subspace which is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem denseRange_schematicLocus_of_isZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver B S hS F) :
    DenseRange (pointsMap B S hS (schematicLocus B S hS F).toFunctor
      (schematicLocus B S hS F).ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.t0Space_points_of_isZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver

Two points of the space of points of a Zariski locally quasi-separated algebraic space over

Every irreducible closed subset of the space of points of a Zariski locally quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stacksSober_points_of_isZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparatedOver
