declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.isStackification_functoriality
declarations.doc:
**The stackification of the inertia is the inertia of the stackification.** Let `(𝒞, J)` be a
site, let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` be a fibred category over `𝒞` and let `G : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳'` be the stackification
of `𝒳` (Stacks 02ZN): a 1-morphism `hG` of fibred categories over `𝒞` whose target `p'` is a
stack, such that (`hmor`) for every `U` and all `x`, `y` in `𝒳_U` the induced map
`Mor(x, y) ⟶ Mor(G x, G y)` of presheaves on `𝒞/U` is locally injective and locally surjective,
its target being a sheaf, and such that (`hobj`) every object `x'` of `𝒳'` admits a covering
sieve `R` of `p'.obj x'` with `x'|_V` in the essential image of `𝒳_V ⥤ 𝒳'_V` for every
`f : V ⟶ p'.obj x'` in `R`.

Then the inertia `I_{𝒳'}` is a stack over `𝒞`, and the functoriality 1-morphism
`I_G : I_𝒳 ⥤ I_{𝒳'}`, `(x, α) ↦ (G x, G α)`, is a stackification of the inertia `I_𝒳`: it is a
1-morphism of fibred categories over `𝒞` and it satisfies the same two conditions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem RelativeInertia.isStackification_functoriality
    {p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞} {p' : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒞} {G : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳'} {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} [p.IsFibered]
    (hG : p.IsFibredOneMorphism p' G) (hp' : p'.IsStack J)
    (hmor : haveI : p'.IsFibered := hp'.isFibered
      ∀ (U : 𝒞) (x y : p.Fiber U),
        Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (J.over U)
            (Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.morPresheafMap hG x y) ∧
          Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (J.over U)
            (Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.morPresheafMap hG x y))
    (hobj : ∀ x' : 𝒳', ∃ R ∈ J (p'.obj x'), ∀ ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ (f : V ⟶ p'.obj x'), R f →
      ∃ (y : 𝒳) (φ : G.obj y ⟶ x'), p'.IsStronglyCartesian f φ) :
    haveI : p'.IsFibered := hp'.isFibered
    haveI : (RelativeInertia.toBase p).IsFibered :=
      RelativeInertia.isFibered p p (𝟭 𝒞) inferInstance (Functor.isFibredOneMorphism_id p)
    haveI : (RelativeInertia.toBase p').IsFibered :=
      RelativeInertia.isFibered p' p' (𝟭 𝒞) hp'.isFibered (Functor.isFibredOneMorphism_id p')
    (RelativeInertia.toBase p').IsStack J ∧
      ∃ hIG : (RelativeInertia.toBase p).IsFibredOneMorphism (RelativeInertia.toBase p')
          (RelativeInertia.functoriality p p' G hG.comp_eq),
        (∀ (U : 𝒞) (A B : (RelativeInertia.toBase p).Fiber U),
            Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (J.over U)
                (Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.morPresheafMap hIG A B) ∧
              Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (J.over U)
                (Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.morPresheafMap hIG A B)) ∧
          ∀ A' : RelativeInertia p', ∃ R ∈ J ((RelativeInertia.toBase p').obj A'),
            ∀ ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ (f : V ⟶ (RelativeInertia.toBase p').obj A'), R f →
              ∃ (A : RelativeInertia p)
                (φ : (RelativeInertia.functoriality p p' G hG.comp_eq).obj A ⟶ A'),
                (RelativeInertia.toBase p').IsStronglyCartesian f φ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.inheritedPrecoverage_hasIsos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NU**, axiom (1) of a site: a family consisting of a single isomorphism of `𝒮` is a
covering, because an isomorphism is strongly cartesian and its image is an isomorphism of `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
instance inheritedPrecoverage_hasIsos [Precoverage.HasIsos K] :
    Precoverage.HasIsos (p.inheritedPrecoverage K)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.inheritedPrecoverage_isStableUnderComposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NU**, axiom (2) of a site: refining a covering by coverings again gives a covering,
because a composition of strongly cartesian morphisms is strongly cartesian (Stacks 02XL) and the
images compose to a covering of `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
instance inheritedPrecoverage_isStableUnderComposition
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition K] :
    Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition (p.inheritedPrecoverage K)
declarations.comment: Axiom (2): coverings are stable under composition.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.inheritedPrecoverage_hasPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NU**, the existence half of axiom (3) of a site: given a covering `{ x i ⟶ x }` of
`𝒮` and a morphism `y ⟶ x`, the fibre products `x i ×_x y` exist. This is Stacks 06N5, applied to
the strongly cartesian morphism `x i ⟶ x` and the fibre product of the images, which exists in `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
instance inheritedPrecoverage_hasPullbacks [p.IsFibered] [HasPullbacks 𝒞] :
    (p.inheritedPrecoverage K).HasPullbacks
declarations.comment: Axiom (3), existence of the fibre products.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.inheritedPrecoverage_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06NU**, the covering half of axiom (3) of a site: the family of projections
`{ x i ×_x y ⟶ y }` of a covering `{ x i ⟶ x }` along `y ⟶ x` is again a covering. Both conditions
transfer from `{ x i ⟶ x }` by the two base-change lemmas above.
declarations.statement:
instance inheritedPrecoverage_isStableUnderBaseChange [p.IsFibered] [HasPullbacks 𝒞]
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderBaseChange K] :
    Precoverage.IsStableUnderBaseChange (p.inheritedPrecoverage K)
declarations.comment: Axiom (3), the base change of a covering is a covering.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.inheritedTopology
declarations.doc:
The Grothendieck topology on a fibred category `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` inherited from a topology `J` on the
base: the topology generated by the collection `CategoryTheory.Functor.inheritedPrecoverage` of
Stacks 06NU, whose covering families are the families of strongly `p`-cartesian morphisms whose
family of images covers in `(𝒞, J)`.
declarations.statement: def inheritedTopology (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) : GrothendieckTopology 𝒮

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and let `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of fibred categories over `𝒞`
(Stacks 02XP), so that `F ⋙ q = p` and `F` preserves strongly cartesian morphisms. Then `F` is a
continuous and a cocontinuous functor between the topologies that `𝒳` and `𝒴` inherit from `𝒞`
(Stacks 06NV).
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsFibredOneMorphism.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
    [HasPullbacks 𝒞] (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) {p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞} {q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞} {F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴}
    [p.IsFibered] [q.IsFibered] (hF : p.IsFibredOneMorphism q F) :
    F.IsContinuous (p.inheritedTopology J) (q.inheritedTopology J) ∧
      F.IsCocontinuous (p.inheritedTopology J) (q.inheritedTopology J)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.inverseImageCompSheafToPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of the morphism of topoi induced by a 1-morphism of fibred categories is
plain restriction along `F.op`: as a functor to presheaves on `𝒳` it is `sheafToPresheaf` followed
by precomposition with `F.op`, with no sheafification intervening.
declarations.statement:
def IsFibredOneMorphism.inverseImageCompSheafToPresheafIso :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology J).1
    F.sheafPushforwardContinuous A (p.inheritedTopology J) (q.inheritedTopology J) ⋙
        sheafToPresheaf (p.inheritedTopology J) A ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (q.inheritedTopology J) A ⋙ (whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj F.op

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.inverseImage_obj_obj_obj
declarations.doc:
The formula `f⁻¹(𝒢)(x) = 𝒢(F x)`: the sections of the inverse image of a sheaf `𝒢` on `𝒴`
over an object `x` of `𝒳` are the sections of `𝒢` over `F x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFibredOneMorphism.inverseImage_obj_obj_obj :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology J).1
    ∀ (𝒢 : Sheaf (q.inheritedTopology J) A) (x : 𝒳),
      ((F.sheafPushforwardContinuous A (p.inheritedTopology J)
            (q.inheritedTopology J)).obj 𝒢).obj.obj (Opposite.op x) =
        𝒢.obj.obj (Opposite.op (F.obj x))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.preservesFiniteLimits_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
The inverse image `f⁻¹` of the morphism of topoi induced by a 1-morphism of fibred categories
preserves finite limits.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFibredOneMorphism.preservesFiniteLimits_inverseImage [HasFiniteLimits A] :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology J).1
    PreservesFiniteLimits (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous A (p.inheritedTopology J)
      (q.inheritedTopology J))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.directImageCompSheafToPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
The direct image of the morphism of topoi is the right Kan extension along `F.op`, taken on
sheaves: as a functor to presheaves on `𝒴` it is `sheafToPresheaf` followed by `F.op.ran`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsFibredOneMorphism.directImageCompSheafToPresheafIso
    [∀ (G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A), F.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology J).2
    F.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A (p.inheritedTopology J) (q.inheritedTopology J) ⋙
        sheafToPresheaf (q.inheritedTopology J) A ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (p.inheritedTopology J) A ⋙ F.op.ran

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibredOneMorphism.sheafAdjunctionInheritedTopology
declarations.doc:
The morphism of topoi `f : Sh(𝒳) ⟶ Sh(𝒴)` induced by a 1-morphism of fibred categories `F`,
as the adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*` between the two inherited sites, with `f⁻¹` the restriction
`F.sheafPushforwardContinuous` and `f_*` the right Kan extension `F.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsFibredOneMorphism.sheafAdjunctionInheritedTopology
    [∀ (G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A), F.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology J).1
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology J).2
    F.sheafPushforwardContinuous A (p.inheritedTopology J) (q.inheritedTopology J) ⊣
      F.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous A (p.inheritedTopology J) (q.inheritedTopology J)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStackInGroupoids_of_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` and `q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞` be stacks in groupoids over
`𝒞` and let `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories over `𝒞`, that is `F ⋙ q = p`.
If `F` makes `𝒳` a category fibred in groupoids over `𝒴`, then `𝒳` is a stack in
groupoids over `𝒴` for the topology `J𝒴` inherited from `(𝒞, J)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInGroupoids_of_isFiberedInGroupoids
    (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) (J𝒴 : GrothendieckTopology 𝒴)
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴)
    (hp : IsStackInGroupoids.{w} p J) (hq : IsStackInGroupoids.{w} q J)
    (hF₁ : F ⋙ q = p)
    (hF₂ : F.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hJ𝒴 : IsInheritedTopology.{w} q J J𝒴) :
    IsStackInGroupoids.{w} F J𝒴

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsGerbe
declarations.doc:
A *gerbe* over the site `(𝒞, J)` is a category `p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` over `𝒞` which is a stack in
groupoids over `𝒞` (Stacks 02ZI), locally nonempty, and locally connected.
declarations.statement: def IsGerbe (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isGerbeOver_iff_of_isEquivalenceOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P0**, in the relative form: a 1-morphism over `𝒴` that is an equivalence over
`𝒴` makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴` exactly when its target is one. The source statement is the
case `𝒴 = 𝒞`, `q = 𝟭 𝒞`, where `IsGerbeOver J (𝟭 𝒞) ·` is being a gerbe over the site
`(𝒞, J)` by `isGerbeOver_id_iff` and being an equivalence over `𝒴` is being an equivalence
over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_iff_of_isEquivalenceOver {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} {q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞}
    {F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴} {F' : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒴} {a : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳'} (ha : a ⋙ F' = F)
    (e : Functor.IsEquivalenceOver F F' a) :
    IsGerbeOver J q F ↔ IsGerbeOver J q F'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isGerbe_of_factorization_iff_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P1**. Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞` and `F ⋙ q : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` be stacks in
groupoids over `𝒞` and let `J𝒴` be the topology on `𝒴` inherited from `(𝒞, J)`. Let
`F = a ⋙ F'` be a factorization of `F` through an equivalence `a` over `𝒞` with `F'` fibred in
groupoids — a factorization of exactly the kind Stacks 06N7 produces. Then clause (1) of
Stacks 06P1 — that `F'` is a gerbe over the site `(𝒴, J𝒴)` — holds exactly when clause (2) does,
that is exactly when `IsGerbeOver J q F`.

Since the right-hand side does not mention the factorization, this also says that clause (1) holds
for one such factorization exactly when it holds for every one, which is the source's parenthesis
"for some (equivalently any)".

The equivalence `a` is asked to be an equivalence over `𝒞`, as the source asks and as Stacks 06N7
delivers, not over `𝒴`: `CategoryTheory.isGerbeOver_iff_of_isEquivalenceOver`, the relative
Stacks 06P0, assumes the latter, and 06N7's factorization does not satisfy it — see
`StacksFrontier.CategoryTheory.Sites.Gerbe.BaseEquivalence`, which supplies the version used here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbe_of_factorization_iff_isGerbeOver {𝒳' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} 𝒳']
    {F' : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒴} {a : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒳'} (ha : a ⋙ F' = F)
    (e : Functor.IsEquivalenceOver (F ⋙ q) (F' ⋙ q) a)
    (hp' : Functor.IsStackInGroupoids.{max u₃ v₃} (F' ⋙ q) J)
    (hq : Functor.IsStackInGroupoids.{max u₃ v₃} q J) (hF' : F'.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hJ𝒴 : Functor.IsInheritedTopology.{max u₃ v₃} q J J𝒴) :
    F'.IsGerbe.{max u₃ v₃} J𝒴 ↔ IsGerbeOver J q F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P2**. `F` makes `𝒳` a *gerbe over* `𝒴`, where `q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞` fibres `𝒴` over the
site `(𝒞, J)` and `F ⋙ q` fibres `𝒳` over it: both fibrations are fibred in groupoids, every
object of `𝒴` is locally in the image of `F`, and every morphism of a fibre of `q` between
`F`-images is locally the `F`-image of a morphism of a fibre of `F ⋙ q`. The last two
conditions are Stacks 06P1 (2)(a) and (2)(b).
declarations.statement: structure IsGerbeOver (J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver.twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P3**. Let `𝒳' = 𝒴' ×_𝒴 𝒳` be the 2-fibre product over `𝒞` of `G : 𝒴' ⥤ 𝒴`
and `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴`, where `𝒳` sits over `𝒞` by `F ⋙ q` and `𝒴'` by `G ⋙ q`. If `F` makes `𝒳`
a gerbe over `𝒴` and `𝒴'` is fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`, then the first projection makes
`𝒳'` a gerbe over `𝒴'`.

Both local conditions are pulled back along `G`: an object of `𝒳` over a member of a covering
whose `F`-image is a restriction of `G y'` is the second component of an object of `𝒳'` over
that member whose first component is a restriction of `y'`, and a morphism of `𝒳` matching
the `G`-image of `b'` is the second component of a morphism of `𝒳'` whose first component is
the restriction of `b'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsGerbeOver.twoFibreProduct {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} (hF : IsGerbeOver J q F)
    (hG : (G ⋙ q).IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsGerbeOver J (G ⋙ q) (fst (G ⋙ q) (F ⋙ q) q G F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver.of_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P4**. Let `𝒳' = 𝒴' ×_𝒴 𝒳` be the 2-fibre product over `𝒞` of `G : 𝒴' ⥤ 𝒴`
and `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴`. If every object of `𝒴` is locally in the image of `G` — the condition
`CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver.locally_essSurj` for `G` — and the first projection makes `𝒳'` a
gerbe over `𝒴'`, then `F` makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`.

This is the converse direction of Stacks 06P3: the two local conditions are descended along
`G`. For the first, an object `y'` of `𝒴'` whose `G`-image restricts `y` is refined by a
covering along which `𝒳'` has objects over `y'`, and their second components are objects of
`𝒳` whose `F`-images restrict `y`. For the second, two restrictions of `x₁` and `x₂` and the
comparison isomorphisms `G y' ≅ F x₁|_V`, `G y' ≅ F x₂|_V` obtained from `b` assemble into two
objects of `𝒳'` with the *same* first component `y'`, so that the identity of `y'` is a
morphism of a fibre between their images; local fullness of the first projection then supplies
the morphism of `𝒳` wanted.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsGerbeOver.of_twoFibreProduct {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hFq : (F ⋙ q).IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hGsurj : ∀ {U : 𝒞} (y : 𝒴), q.obj y = U → ∃ S ∈ J U,
      ∀ ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ (f : V ⟶ U), S f → ∃ (y' : 𝒴') (ψ : G.obj y' ⟶ y), q.IsHomLift f ψ)
    (h : IsGerbeOver J (G ⋙ q) (fst (G ⋙ q) (F ⋙ q) q G F)) :
    IsGerbeOver J q F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_iff_identity_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P6.** A group algebraic space is separated over its base exactly when its
identity section is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_identity_isClosedImmersion (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) :
    IsSeparated 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom ↔
      IsClosedImmersion 𝒞 S hS (η[G.obj.X]).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallySeparated_iff_identity_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P6.** A group algebraic space is locally separated over its base exactly when
its identity section is an immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySeparated_iff_identity_isImmersion (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) :
    IsLocallySeparated 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom ↔
      IsImmersion 𝒞 S hS (η[G.obj.X]).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparated_iff_identity_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P6.** A group algebraic space is quasi-separated over its base exactly when its
identity section is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_iff_identity_isQuasiCompact (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) :
    IsQuasiSeparated 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom ↔
      IsQuasiCompact 𝒞 S hS (η[G.obj.X]).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFreeAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06P8.** A group object over `B` acts freely on `X` when its
action is free on the points of every scheme over `B`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFreeAction (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : 𝒞.Contains S)
    (B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (G X : Over B) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFreeAction_iff_mono_leftSMul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06P9.** An action of a group algebraic space is free exactly when the
action–projection morphism `G ×_B X ⟶ X ×_B X`, `(g, x) ↦ (g · x, x)`, is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFreeAction_iff_mono_leftSMul (G X : Over B) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X] :
    IsFreeAction 𝒞 S hS B G X ↔ Mono (ModObj.leftSMul G X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.inertiaGroupoid
declarations.doc:
The groupoid `(G, R', s', t', c')` in algebraic spaces over `B` built from a groupoid
`(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over `B`: its object space is the stabilizer `G/U`, its
arrow space is `R' = R ×_{s, U} G`, and its source, target and composition are the morphisms
`s'`, `t'` and `c'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inertiaGroupoid
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B
declarations.comment: the groupoid (G, R', s', t', c')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inertiaComparison_comp_toBase
declarations.doc:
The comparison `[G/R'] ⟶ ℐ_{[U/R]}` composed with the structure functor of the inertia of
`[U/R]` is the structure functor of `[G/R']`: it is a 1-morphism of categories over the big fppf
site.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaComparison_comp_toBase (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    (inertiaComparison G).toFunctor ⋙ RelativeInertia.toBase (quotientStack G).p =
      (quotientStack (inertiaGroupoid G)).p
declarations.comment: second assertion: the comparison [G/R'] ⟶ I_{[U/R]} is over the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inertiaComparisonForgetfulIso
declarations.doc:
Composing the comparison `[G/R'] ⟶ ℐ_{[U/R]}` with the forgetful 1-morphism `ℐ_{[U/R]} ⟶ [U/R]`
gives the 1-morphism `[G/R'] ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 046Q induced by the forgetful morphism of groupoids
`(G, R', s', t', c') ⟶ (U, R, s, t, c)`, by an isomorphism of functors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inertiaComparisonForgetfulIso
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    ((inertiaComparison G).toFunctor ⋙ RelativeInertia.π (quotientStack G).p) ≅
      (quotientStackMap (inertiaForgetful G)).toFunctor
declarations.comment: second assertion: the comparison is a 1-morphism over [U/R]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_inertiaComparison
declarations.doc:
The underlying functor of the comparison `[G/R'] ⟶ ℐ_{[U/R]}` is an equivalence of categories:
the quotient stack of the inertia groupoid `(G, R', s', t', c')` is the inertia stack of `[U/R]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_inertiaComparison (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    (inertiaComparison G).toFunctor.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: second assertion: I_{[U/R]} = [G/R'], the comparison is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inertiaQuotientStackSquare
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over `B` with stabilizer group algebraic
space `G/U` (Stacks 0448), the 2-commutative square

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
[G/R'] ----> [U/R]
```

of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site: the apex is the stack `𝒮_G` of the stabilizer,
the horizontal arrows are the 1-morphism of Stacks 0458 induced by `G → U` and the projection of
Stacks 044R for the inertia groupoid `(G, R', s', t', c')` of Stacks 06PB, and the vertical
arrows are that projection for `(U, R, s, t, c)` and the 1-morphism of Stacks 046Q induced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.inertiaForgetful`. The filler is the 2-isomorphism
of Stacks 046Q.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inertiaQuotientStackSquare (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology C S hS
    let Q : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨quotientStack G, isStackInGroupoids_quotientStack G⟩
    let I : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨quotientStack (inertiaGroupoid G), isStackInGroupoids_quotientStack (inertiaGroupoid G)⟩
    let W : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨liftedFibredCategory G.objects, isStackInGroupoids_liftedFibredCategory G.objects⟩
    Bicategory.TwoCommSq
      (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (liftedQuotientStackProjection G) : W ⟶ Q)
      (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (quotientStackMap (inertiaForgetful G)) : I ⟶ Q)
declarations.comment: the canonical square, lower-left corner as the quotient stack [G/R'] of 06PB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaQuotientStackSquare
declarations.doc:
The square

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
[G/R'] ----> [U/R]
```

of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inertiaQuotientStackSquare` is a 2-fibre product (Stacks 003Q) in the
bicategory of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site, i.e. the diagram is 2-cartesian.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaQuotientStackSquare
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (inertiaQuotientStackSquare G)
declarations.comment: that square is 2-cartesian, lower-left corner as the quotient stack [G/R'] of 06PB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_quotientStackInertiaSquare
declarations.doc:
Assume `B → S` and `(U, R, s, t, c)` as in Stacks 044Q (1). Let `G/U` be the stabilizer group
algebraic space of the groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` (Stacks 0448). Then the canonical diagram

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
ℐ_{[U/R]} --> [U/R]
```

of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackInertiaSquare` is 2-cartesian, i.e. a 2-fibre product
in the sense of Stacks 003Q, in the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf
site (Stacks 02XS).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_quotientStackInertiaSquare
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (quotientStackInertiaSquare G)
declarations.comment: the canonical square with corners S_G, S_U, I_[U/R], [U/R] is 2-cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_quotientStackInertiaSquareInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
Assume `B → S` and `(U, R, s, t, c)` as in Stacks 044Q (1) and let `G/U` be the stabilizer
group algebraic space of `(U, R, s, t, c, e, i)` (Stacks 0448). Then the canonical diagram

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
ℐ_{[U/R]} --> [U/R]
```

is 2-cartesian in the 2-category of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site (Stacks 02ZK).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_quotientStackInertiaSquareInGroupoids
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (quotientStackInertiaSquareInGroupoids G)
declarations.comment: that square, in the 2-category of stacks in groupoids, is 2-cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isGerbeOver_quotientStackMap
declarations.doc:
The induced morphism of quotient stacks `[f] : [U/R] ⟶ [U'/R']` makes `[U/R]` a gerbe over
`[U'/R']` as soon as `f : U ⟶ U'` and `R ⟶ R'|_U` are surjective maps of fppf sheaves: the first
hypothesis is local surjectivity of the map of object spaces, the second asks that an arrow of
`R'` between the images of two local points of `U` lift, after an fppf covering, to an arrow of
`R` between those points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGerbeOver_quotientStackMap
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    {G H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B}
    (f : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.Hom G H)
    (hobj : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective
      (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS) f.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects)
    (harr : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver C S hS)
      (a b : G.objects.obj.obj (Opposite.op T))
      (r' : H.arrows.obj.obj (Opposite.op T)),
      H.source.hom.app (Opposite.op T) r' =
        f.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects.app (Opposite.op T) a →
      H.target.hom.app (Opposite.op T) r' =
        f.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects.app (Opposite.op T) b →
      ∃ R ∈ BigFppfOver.topology C S hS T,
        ∀ ⦃V : BigFppfOver C S hS⦄ (i : V ⟶ T), R i →
          ∃ r : G.arrows.obj.obj (Opposite.op V),
            G.source.hom.app (Opposite.op V) r =
              G.objects.obj.map i.op a ∧
            G.target.hom.app (Opposite.op V) r =
              G.objects.obj.map i.op b ∧
            f.toGroupoidHom.mapArrows.app (Opposite.op V) r =
              H.arrows.obj.map i.op r') :
    CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver
      (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS)
      (quotientStack H).p
      (quotientStackMap f).toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isGerbeOver_quotientStackToBase_trivialAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PF.** Let `G` be a group algebraic space over `B` and endow `B` with the trivial
action of `G`. The structure arrow `[B/G] ⟶ B` turns `[B/G]` into a gerbe over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_quotientStackToBase_trivialAction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_toQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PG.** The object presheaf of a pre-relation surjects onto its quotient sheaf.

A point of the quotient is represented by a section over the spectrum of a field in the site;
the quotient map is a surjection of fppf sheaves, so that section lifts to `U` on a covering,
and the spectrum of a residue field of a member of the covering is again an object of the
site and gives a field-valued point of `U` dominating the original one.

This also discharges the surjectivity clause of **Stacks 06PH**, that `X ⟶ X/G` is surjective
for a free action of a group algebraic space: the quotient `X/G` of [Stacks, Tag 044J] is the
quotient sheaf of the pre-relation of the action, so that clause is this lemma at that
pre-relation. It is stated here for an arbitrary pre-relation, which is more general and uses
neither freeness of the action nor flatness of `G ⟶ B`; the remaining clauses of Stacks 06PH —
algebraicity of `X/G`, flatness and local finite presentation of `X ⟶ X/G`, and the fppf
torsor property — are not proved here and nothing in this file assumes them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_toQuotientSheaf (j : PreRelation R U) :
    IsSurjective site S hS (toQuotientSheaf j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFppfTorsor_actionQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PH.** For a free action of a group algebraic space which is flat and locally of
finite presentation over the base, `X` is an fppf torsor over `X/G` under the group `G` pulled
back to `X/G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfTorsor_actionQuotientSheaf
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace site S hS B) (G X : Over B) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace site S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace site S hS X.left)
    (hfree : IsFreeAction site S hS B G X) (hflat : IsFlat site S hS G.hom)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation site S hS G.hom) :
    IsFppfTorsor site S hS (actionQuotientPresheaf G X)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_actionQuotientSheaf hB G X hG hX hfree hflat hfp)
      (groupOverQuotient hB.isSheaf G X) (sourceOverQuotient G X)
      (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback site S hS G.hom (actionQuotientToBase hB.isSheaf G X) hG
        (isAlgebraicSpace_actionQuotientSheaf hB G X hG hX hfree hflat hfp) hB)
      hX
declarations.comment: X is an fppf G-torsor over X/G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PJ**, the implication from the existence of a suitable restriction to
algebraicity. Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` and let
`f : (U', R', s', t', c') ⟶ (U, R, s, t, c)` exhibit its source as the restriction of its target
along `g = f_U : U' ⟶ U`. If the saturation map `U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ R ⟶ U` is a surjection of
fppf sheaves and `s', t'` are flat and locally of finite presentation, then the quotient stack
`[U/R]` is an algebraic stack.

Stacks 06FI, which is not in the library, is carried as the hypothesis `h06FI`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_restriction
    (G G' : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (f : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.Hom G' G)
    (h06FI : ∀ H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B,
      Space.IsFlat C S hS H.source.hom → Space.IsFlat C S hS H.target.hom →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.source.hom →
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.target.hom →
            IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack H))
    (hrestriction : IsPullback f.toGroupoidHom.mapArrows
      (prod.lift G'.toGroupoidInFunctors.source G'.toGroupoidInFunctors.target)
      (prod.lift G.toGroupoidInFunctors.source G.toGroupoidInFunctors.target)
      (prod.map f.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects f.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects))
    (hsaturation : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS)
      ((GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.fiberProductSnd
        (ObjectProperty.homMk f.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects : G'.objects ⟶ G.objects)
        G.target ≫ G.source).hom))
    (hsource : Space.IsFlat C S hS G'.source.hom)
    (htarget : Space.IsFlat C S hS G'.target.hom)
    (hsourceFP : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G'.source.hom)
    (htargetFP : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G'.target.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G)
declarations.comment: the implication from the existence of the restriction to algebraicity, for a groupoid exhibited by `hrestriction` as the restriction along `g`, with Stacks 06FI carried as a hypothesis; the converse, which needs Stacks 044X, 044V, 04T4, 046N and 04WY, is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_restrictionAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PJ**, the implication from the existence of the restriction to algebraicity, in
the form the source states it. Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B`
and let `g : U' ⟶ U` be a morphism of algebraic spaces such that the saturation map
`U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ R ⟶ U` is a surjection of fppf sheaves and the source and target of the
restriction `(U', R', s', t', c')` of `(U, R, s, t, c)` along `g` are flat and locally of finite
presentation. Then the quotient stack `[U/R]` is an algebraic stack.

Stacks 06FI, which is not in the library, is carried as the hypothesis `h06FI`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_of_restrictionAlong
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    {U' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS} (g : U' ⟶ G.objects)
    (h06FI : ∀ H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B,
      Space.IsFlat C S hS H.source.hom → Space.IsFlat C S hS H.target.hom →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.source.hom →
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.target.hom →
            IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack H))
    (hsaturation : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS)
      ((GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.fiberProductSnd g G.target ≫ G.source).hom))
    (hsource : Space.IsFlat C S hS
      (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionSource G g).hom)
    (htarget : Space.IsFlat C S hS
      (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionTarget G g).hom)
    (hsourceFP : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
      (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionSource G g).hom)
    (htargetFP : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
      (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionTarget G g).hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G)
declarations.comment: the implication from the existence of the restriction to algebraicity, for the canonical restriction of Stacks 044B along `g`, with Stacks 06FI carried as a hypothesis; the converse, which needs Stacks 044X, 044V, 04T4, 046N and 04WY, is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_iff_restrictionAlong
declarations.doc:
Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B`. The
quotient stack `[U/R]` is an algebraic stack if and only if there is a morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` of
algebraic spaces over `S` such that

1. the saturation map `U' ×_{g, U, t} R ⟶ R ⟶ U` is a surjection of fppf sheaves, and
2. the source and target of the restriction of `(U, R, s, t, c)` along `g` are flat and locally of
   finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_iff_restrictionAlong
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G) ↔
      ∃ (U' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (g : U' ⟶ G.objects),
        Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS)
          ((GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.fiberProductSnd g G.target ≫ G.source).hom) ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionSource G g).hom ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionTarget G g).hom ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
          (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionSource G g).hom ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
          (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionTarget G g).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_action_iff_exists_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PK.** Let a group algebraic space `G` over an algebraic space `B` act on an
algebraic space `X` over `B`. The quotient stack `[X/G]` of the action groupoid of
**Stacks 0444** is an algebraic stack exactly when there is a morphism `φ : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic
spaces over `B` for which

1. `G ×_B X' ⟶ X`, `(g, x') ↦ g • φ x'`, is a surjection of fppf sheaves, and
2. both projections to `X'` of the space of triples `{(x₁, g, x₂) : φ x₁ = g • φ x₂}`, the fibre
   product `X' ×_{φ, X, a} (G ×_B X')`, are flat and locally of finite presentation.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_action_iff` with the
biconditional of **Stacks 06PJ** it takes supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_iff_restrictionAlong`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_action_iff_exists_cover
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (G X : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X.left)
    (A : Space.ActionGroupoidConstruction B G X hG hX) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack A.groupoid) ↔
      ∃ (X' : Over B.obj) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X'.left) (φ : X' ⟶ X),
        let a : G ⊗ X' ⟶ X := (𝟙 G ⊗ₘ φ) ≫ γ[G, X]
        Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS) a.left ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (pullback.fst φ.left a.left) ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS (pullback.fst φ.left a.left) ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (pullback.snd φ.left a.left ≫ (snd G X').left) ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
          (pullback.snd φ.left a.left ≫ (snd G X').left)
declarations.comment: for any action groupoid construction of Stacks 0444

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_groupoidOfAction_iff_exists_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PK for the action groupoid of Stacks 0444 that the library builds.** The quotient
stack `[X/G]` is an algebraic stack exactly when there is a morphism `φ : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic
spaces over `B` for which `G ×_B X' ⟶ X`, `(g, x') ↦ g • φ x'`, is a surjection of fppf sheaves
and both projections to `X'` of the space of triples `{(x₁, g, x₂) : φ x₁ = g • φ x₂}` are flat
and locally of finite presentation.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_groupoidOfAction_iff` with the
biconditional of Stacks 06PJ it takes supplied as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_action_iff_exists_cover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_groupoidOfAction_iff_exists_cover
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (G X : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X.left) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS
        (quotientStack (Space.groupoidOfAction B G X hG hX).groupoid) ↔
      ∃ (X' : Over B.obj) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X'.left) (φ : X' ⟶ X),
        let a : G ⊗ X' ⟶ X := (𝟙 G ⊗ₘ φ) ≫ γ[G, X]
        Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS) a.left ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (pullback.fst φ.left a.left) ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS (pullback.fst φ.left a.left) ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (pullback.snd φ.left a.left ≫ (snd G X').left) ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
          (pullback.snd φ.left a.left ≫ (snd G X').left)
declarations.comment: for the action groupoid of Stacks 0444 that the library builds

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_action_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PK.** Let a group algebraic space `G` over an algebraic space `B` act on an
algebraic space `X` over `B`. The quotient stack `[X/G]` of the action groupoid is an algebraic
stack exactly when there is a morphism `φ : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` for which
`G ×_B X' ⟶ X`, `(g, x') ↦ g • φ x'`, is a surjection of fppf sheaves and both projections to
`X'` of the space of triples `{(x₁, g, x₂) : φ x₁ = g • φ x₂}` are flat and locally of finite
presentation.

Stacks 06PJ, the same criterion for an arbitrary groupoid in algebraic spaces, is not in the
library and is carried as the hypothesis `h06PJ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_action_iff
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : C.Contains S)
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (G X : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X.left)
    (A : Space.ActionGroupoidConstruction B G X hG hX)
    (h06PJ : ∀ H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B,
      IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack H) ↔
        ∃ (U' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (g : U' ⟶ H.objects),
          Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS)
            ((GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.fiberProductSnd g H.target ≫ H.source).hom) ∧
          Space.IsFlat C S hS
            (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionSource H g).hom ∧
          Space.IsFlat C S hS
            (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionTarget H g).hom ∧
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
            (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionSource H g).hom ∧
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
            (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrictionTarget H g).hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack A.groupoid) ↔
      ∃ (X' : Over B.obj) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS X'.left) (φ : X' ⟶ X),
        let a : G ⊗ X' ⟶ X := (𝟙 G ⊗ₘ φ) ≫ γ[G, X]
        Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS) a.left ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (pullback.fst φ.left a.left) ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS (pullback.fst φ.left a.left) ∧
        Space.IsFlat C S hS (pullback.snd φ.left a.left ≫ (snd G X').left) ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS
          (pullback.snd φ.left a.left ≫ (snd G X').left)
declarations.comment: with Stacks 06PJ, the same criterion for an arbitrary groupoid in algebraic spaces, carried as the explicit hypothesis h06PJ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_trivialAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PL**, the implication from flatness and local finite presentation to
algebraicity. Let `G` be a group algebraic space over an algebraic space `B` over `S` and endow
`B` with the trivial action of `G`. If `G` is flat and locally of finite presentation over `B`,
then the quotient stack `[B/G]` is an algebraic stack.

Stacks 06FI, which is not in the library, is carried as the hypothesis `h06FI`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_trivialAction
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (G : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left)
    (A : Space.ActionGroupoidConstruction B G (𝟙_ (Over B.obj)) hG B.property)
    (h06FI : ∀ H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B,
      Space.IsFlat C S hS H.source.hom → Space.IsFlat C S hS H.target.hom →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.source.hom →
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.target.hom →
            IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack H))
    (hflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.hom)
    (hlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack A.groupoid)
declarations.comment: the implication from flat and locally of finite presentation to algebraic, with Stacks 06FI carried as a hypothesis; the converse, which rests on Stacks 06PK, is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isAlgebraicStack_trivialAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PL, the converse implication.** Let `G` be a group algebraic space over an
algebraic space `B` over `S`, endow `B` with the trivial action of `G`, and suppose the quotient
stack `[B/G]` is an algebraic stack. Then `G ⟶ B` is flat and locally of finite presentation.

The converse of **Stacks 06PJ**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_restrictionAlong_of_isAlgebraicStack`, supplies the citation of
**Stacks 06PK** that the source's proof makes, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_trivialActionCriterion` is the
rest of the argument; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isAlgebraicStack_trivialAction
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (G : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left)
    (A : Space.ActionGroupoidConstruction B G (𝟙_ (Over B.obj)) hG B.property)
    (h : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack A.groupoid)) :
    Space.IsFlat C S hS G.hom ∧ Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.hom
declarations.comment: the converse implication, from algebraicity to flat and locally of finite presentation, with nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_trivialAction_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PL.** Let `G` be a group algebraic space over an algebraic space `B` over `S` and
endow `B` with the trivial action of `G`. The quotient stack `[B/G]` is an algebraic stack if and
only if `G ⟶ B` is flat and locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_quotientStack_trivialAction_iff
    (B : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (G : Over B.obj) [GrpObj G]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS G.left)
    (A : Space.ActionGroupoidConstruction B G (𝟙_ (Over B.obj)) hG B.property) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack A.groupoid) ↔
      (Space.IsFlat C S hS G.hom ∧
        Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_isSurjective_twoCommSq_fst
declarations.doc:
Surjectivity of a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` descends along a
surjective 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴`: if some 2-commutative square over the cospan `(g, f)` has
surjective first projection, then `f` is surjective.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_isSurjective_comp
declarations.doc:
If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is surjective, then so is its
second factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_isSurjective_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsSurjective B S hS (f ≫ g)) : IsSurjective B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (1): the relative sheaf of automorphisms of `x`.** For a 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks and an algebraic-space-valued point `x : Z ⟶ 𝒳`, the 2-fibre
product

```text
Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) = Z ×_{x, 𝒳} ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴}
```

of `x` with the forgetful 1-morphism of the relative inertia, read in the 2-category of
categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`. Its objects over a scheme `W` are
the triples of a point `z` of `Z` over `W`, an object `(a, α)` of the relative inertia over `W` —
that is, an object `a` of `𝒳` over `W` together with an automorphism `α` of `a` killed by `f` —
and a vertical isomorphism `x(z) ≅ a`; so a section over `W` is an automorphism of `x(z)` killed
by `f`, which is what the source calls an automorphism of `x` over `W` relative to `𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    CatFiberedInGroupoids (BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative sheaf of automorphisms, Z ×_{x, X} I_{X/Y}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (1): `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` is an algebraic space.** The relative sheaf of
automorphisms of an algebraic-space-valued point `x : Z ⟶ 𝒳` of an algebraic stack is
represented by an algebraic space over `S`.

Stacks 050Q makes the forgetful 1-morphism `ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` of the relative inertia representable
by algebraic spaces — only the representability of the two diagonals, the second clause of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack`, is used for that — and `Z` represents the stack of
`Z`, so Stacks 0300 applies to the cospan `(x, ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x)
declarations.comment: part (1): Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (1): `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` is an algebraic space over `Z`.** The projection
of the relative sheaf of automorphisms of `x` to the stack of `Z` is representable by algebraic
spaces, so — together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpace`, which
makes its source an algebraic space — it is a morphism of algebraic spaces with target `Z`.

This is Stacks 0302 for the base change of the representable 1-morphism `ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` of
Stacks 050Q along `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x)
declarations.comment: part (1): Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) is an algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.automorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: the sheaf of automorphisms of `x`.** For an algebraic-space-valued point
`x : Z ⟶ 𝒳` of an algebraic stack, the 2-fibre product

```text
Isom_𝒳(x, x) = Z ×_{x, 𝒳} ℐ_𝒳
```

of `x` with the forgetful 1-morphism of the inertia. This is the object the last paragraph of
Stacks 06PP writes `Isom_𝒳(x, x)`: part (1) of that definition when `𝒴` is an algebraic space,
in which case the relative inertia of `𝒳` over `𝒴` is the absolute inertia of `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def automorphismSpaceOverSpace
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    CatFiberedInGroupoids (BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: the sheaf of automorphisms of x, Z ×_{x, X} I_X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_automorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: `Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is an algebraic space.** The sheaf of automorphisms of an
algebraic-space-valued point of an algebraic stack is represented by an algebraic space over
`S`: Stacks 050Q for the absolute inertia projection, together with Stacks 0300.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_automorphismSpaceOverSpace
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS (automorphismSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ x)
declarations.comment: Isom_X(x, x) is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_automorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: `Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is an algebraic space over `Z`.** The projection of the sheaf
of automorphisms of `x` to the stack of `Z` is representable by algebraic spaces — Stacks 0302 for
the base change of the representable 1-morphism `ℐ_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of Stacks 050Q along `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_automorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (automorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ x)
declarations.comment: Isom_X(x, x) is an algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: the sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`.** For two
algebraic-space-valued points `x₁, x₂ : Z ⟶ 𝒳` of an algebraic stack, the 2-fibre product

```text
Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) = Z ×_{(x₁, x₂), 𝒳 × 𝒳, Δ} 𝒳
```

of the pair `(x₁, x₂)` with the diagonal of `𝒳`. Its objects over a scheme `W` are the
quadruples of a point `z` of `Z` over `W`, an object `a` of `𝒳` over `W` and two vertical
isomorphisms `x₁(z) ≅ a`, `x₂(z) ≅ a`, so a section over `W` is an isomorphism
`x₁(z) ≅ x₂(z)` of the fibre of `𝒳` over `W` — which is what the last paragraph of Stacks 06PP
calls the *sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`*.

This is the presentation of `Isom` that the diagonal conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 045G are
stated with, and it is the one
`CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.DiagonalFibre.equivalenceOver` identifies with the presheaf
of vertical morphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`. The equivalent iterated form the source writes,
`(Z ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} Z) ×_{Z × Z, Δ_Z} Z`, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.absoluteIsomorphismCategory`
cut down by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.absoluteIsomorphismDiagonalSubcategory`; this file does not
prove the comparison of the two forms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isomorphismSpaceOverSpace
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    CatFiberedInGroupoids (BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: the sheaf of isomorphisms from x₁ to x₂, as the fibre of the diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_isomorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` is an algebraic space.** The sheaf of isomorphisms from one
algebraic-space-valued point of an algebraic stack to another is represented by an algebraic
space over `S`.

It is the base change of the diagonal of `𝒳` along the pair `(x₁, x₂)`, the diagonal is
representable by algebraic spaces because `𝒳` is an algebraic stack, and `Z` represents the stack
of `Z`; so this is Stacks 0300.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_isomorphismSpaceOverSpace
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomorphismSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: Isom_X(x₁, x₂) is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_isomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` is an algebraic space over `Z`.** Its projection to the stack
of `Z` is representable by algebraic spaces — Stacks 0302 for the base change of the diagonal of
`𝒳` along the pair `(x₁, x₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_isomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (isomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: Isom_X(x₁, x₂) is an algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): the relative sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`.** For a
1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, two algebraic-space-valued points
`x₁, x₂ : Z ⟶ 𝒳` and a 2-morphism `α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f`, the 2-fibre product

```text
Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂) = Z ×_{(x₁, x₂, α), 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳, Δ_f} 𝒳
```

of the twisted point of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomorphismTwistedPoint` with the
relative diagonal of `f`. Its sections over a scheme `W` are the isomorphisms
`x₁(z) ≅ x₂(z)` of the fibre of `𝒳` over `W` whose image under `f` is the component of `α` at
`z`, which is what the source calls the *relative sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`*.

The source writes the same object as the iterated fibre product
`(Z ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} Z) ×_{Z ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} Z, Δ^α} Z`; that is the fibre of `Δ^α` and this is the
fibre of `Δ_f` along the twisted point, which is the form the representability of the relative
diagonal is stated for. This file does not prove the comparison of the two forms, nor the
comparison with the explicit sub-presheaf
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    CatFiberedInGroupoids (BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (2): the relative sheaf of isomorphisms, as the fibre of the relative diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is an algebraic space.** The relative sheaf
of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂` lifting `α` is represented by an algebraic space over `S`.

It is the base change of the relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` along the twisted point; the
relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces as soon as the diagonals of `𝒳` and `𝒴`
are (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal`), which they are
because `𝒳` and `𝒴` are algebraic stacks, and `Z` represents the stack of `Z`; so this is
Stacks 0300.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (2): Isom^α_{X/Y}(x₁, x₂) is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is an algebraic space over `Z`.** Its
projection to the stack of `Z` is representable by algebraic spaces — Stacks 0302 for the base
change of the relative diagonal of `f` along the twisted point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (2): Isom^α_{X/Y}(x₁, x₂) is an algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP.** The presheaf `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` of isomorphisms of two
algebraic-space-valued points of an algebraic stack: its sections over `W` are the pairs
consisting of a point `z` of `Z` over `W` and an isomorphism `x₁(z) ≅ x₂(z)` in the fibre category
of `𝒳` over `W`, and its restriction maps are `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointRestrict`.

This is the object the last paragraph of Stacks 06PP calls `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)`, the *sheaf of
isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`*. That it is represented by an algebraic space over `Z` is the
other half of that definition and is not asserted here; neither is its part (1), the group law
on the relative sheaf of automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isomSpaceOverSpace (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the sheaf of isomorphisms from one algebraic-space-valued point to another

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2).** The presheaf `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` of isomorphisms of two
algebraic-space-valued points of `𝒳` lifting a given 2-morphism `α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f` of the
target: it is the sub-presheaf of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpace` cut out by the
condition that the image of the isomorphism under `f` be the prescribed component of `α`.

That it is represented by an algebraic space over `Z` is the remaining half of Stacks 06PP part
(2) and is not asserted here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: part (2): the sheaf of isomorphisms lifting a 2-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_isomSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: the sheaf of isomorphisms of two algebraic-space-valued points of an
algebraic stack is an algebraic space over `Z`.** The structure morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceProj` to `Z` is representable by algebraic spaces,
because its fibre over every scheme-valued point of `Z` is the sheaf of vertical morphisms
between two scheme-valued points of `𝒳`, an algebraic space by condition (2) of Stacks 045G;
`Z` is an algebraic space, so Stacks 02YS applies.

This is the representability half of Stacks 06PP, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpace` constructs the sheaf of.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_isomSpaceOverSpace
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: the sheaf of isomorphisms is an algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP part (2): the sheaf of isomorphisms lifting a 2-morphism is an algebraic space
over `Z`.** It is the fibre product of `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` and `Z` over `Isom_𝒴(f x₁, f x₂)` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isPullback_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace`, and all three of those are
algebraic spaces over `S`, so Stacks 04T9 applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (2): the sheaf of isomorphisms lifting a 2-morphism is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_equivalenceOver_isomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` is the sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`.** The
2-fibre product `Z ×_{(x₁, x₂), 𝒳 × 𝒳, Δ} 𝒳` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomorphismSpaceOverSpace` is equivalent, as a category over `Z`, to
the category of elements of the presheaf on the category of elements of `Z` whose sections over a
point `a` are the vertical morphisms `x₁(a) ⟶ x₂(a)` of `𝒳`. Those are exactly the isomorphisms
`x₁(a) ≅ x₂(a)` of the fibre of `𝒳`, the fibres of an algebraic stack being groupoids
(Stacks 003V), so this is the statement that the 2-fibre product the last paragraph of
Stacks 06PP writes `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` is the *sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`*.

This is `CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.DiagonalFibre.equivalenceOver` read at the pair
`(x₁, x₂) = AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomorphismPairPoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalenceOver_isomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (isomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂).toFunctor
      (PresheafOfCategories.discreteProjection
        (TwoFibreProductOver.DiagonalFibre.vertHomPresheaf 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          (isomorphismPairPoint B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂).hom.w)))
declarations.comment: the sheaf of isomorphisms from x₁ to x₂: the 2-fibre product is that sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_equivalenceOver_relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is the sheaf of isomorphisms lifting `α`.**
The 2-fibre product `Z ×_{(x₁, x₂, α), 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳, Δ_f} 𝒳` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpace` is equivalent, as a category over
`Z`, to the category of elements of the presheaf on the category of elements of `Z` whose
sections over a point `a` are the vertical morphisms `x₁(a) ⟶ x₂(a)` of `𝒳` whose image under
`f` is the comparison isomorphism carried by the twisted point at `a`, that is the component
`α_a`. So the object part (2) defines is the *relative sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂`*
that the source says it is.

This is `CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.RelativeDiagonalFibre.equivalenceOver` —
Stacks 04XT — read at the twisted point
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomorphismTwistedPoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalenceOver_relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (relativeIsomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α).toFunctor
      (PresheafOfCategories.discreteProjection
        (TwoFibreProductOver.RelativeDiagonalFibre.relVertHomPresheaf
          𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          (relativeIsomorphismTwistedPoint B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α).w f.hom.hom.w)))
declarations.comment: part (2): the 2-fibre product is the sheaf of isomorphisms lifting α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_isomorphismTotalPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP: the sheaf `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` on the big fppf site is an algebraic space over
`Z`.** The presheaf whose sections over `W` are the pairs of a point `z` of `Z` over `W` and an
isomorphism `x₁(z) ≅ x₂(z)` is an algebraic space over `S`, so together with its structure
morphism to `Z` it is the algebraic space over `Z` that the last paragraph of Stacks 06PP
asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_isomorphismTotalPresheaf
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomorphismTotalPresheaf B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: Isom_X(x₁, x₂) as a presheaf over Z on the big fppf site is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismTotalPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): the sheaf `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` on the big fppf site is an
algebraic space over `Z`.** The presheaf whose sections over `W` are the pairs of a point `z` of
`Z` over `W` and an isomorphism `x₁(z) ≅ x₂(z)` lifting the component `α_z` is an algebraic space
over `S`, so together with its structure morphism to `Z` it is the algebraic space over `Z` that
part (2) asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismTotalPresheaf (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomorphismTotalPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (2): Isom^α_{X/Y}(x₁, x₂) as a presheaf over Z on the big fppf site is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismGroupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
`Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` as a group algebraic space over `Z`: the presheaf on the big fppf site
whose sections over `W` are the pairs of a point `z` of `Z` over `W` and an automorphism of `x(z)`
killed by `f`, together with its structure morphism to `Z`, the group law given by composition of
automorphisms, and the algebraicity of that presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeAutomorphismGroupAlgebraicSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z hZ
declarations.comment: part (1): Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) is a group algebraic space over Z, group law and algebraicity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismGroupPresheaf
declarations.doc:
The presheaf of groups on the category of elements of `Z` whose sections at a point `a` of
`Z` are the vertical automorphisms of `x(a)` killed by `f`, with composition as the group law and
restriction along a morphism of `Z` as the restriction map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeAutomorphismGroupPresheaf :
    ((algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: part (1): the group law on Isom_{X/Y}(x, x), as a presheaf of groups over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj
declarations.doc:
The presheaf of relative automorphisms of `x`, read over the category of elements of `Z`, is a
*group object* of the cartesian monoidal category of presheaves of sets on that category: its
unit, multiplication and inverse are the identity automorphism, composition and the inverse
automorphism, taken pointwise over the points of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj :
    GrpObj (relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)
declarations.comment: part (1): the group-object structure on Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj_mul
declarations.doc:
The multiplication of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj` is
composition of relative automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj_mul
    (a : ((algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ)
    (φ : (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj
      (relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)
      (relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)).obj a) :
    letI := relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x
    (MonObj.mul (X := relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)).app a φ =
      (φ.1 * φ.2 : RelativeAutomorphism B S hS Z hZ f x a.unop)
declarations.comment: part (1): the multiplication of the group object is composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj_one
declarations.doc:
The unit of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj` is the identity
automorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj_one
    (a : ((algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ)
    (t : (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit
      (((algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)).obj a) :
    letI := relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x
    (MonObj.one (X := relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)).app a t =
      (1 : RelativeAutomorphism B S hS Z hZ f x a.unop)
declarations.comment: part (1): the unit of the group object is the identity automorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj_inv
declarations.doc:
The inverse of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj` is the inverse
automorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj_inv
    (a : ((algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ)
    (φ : RelativeAutomorphism B S hS Z hZ f x a.unop) :
    (GrpObj.inv (X := relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)
      (self := relativeAutomorphismPresheafGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x)).app a φ = φ⁻¹
declarations.comment: part (1): the inverse of the group object is the inverse automorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.RelativeAutomorphismSpace.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_comparison
declarations.doc:
**The group structure on `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` over `Z`.** The comparison 1-morphism is an
equivalence over `Z` from the category of elements of the presheaf of groups of relative
automorphisms of `x` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismGroupPresheaf`) to
`Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) = Z ×_{x, 𝒳} ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_comparison :
    Nonempty (CategoryTheory.IsEquivalenceOver
      (PresheafOfCategories.discreteProjection (relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x))
      (relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x).toFunctor
      (comparison B S hS Z hZ f x))
declarations.comment: part (1): the group structure on Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.RelativeAutomorphismSpace.nonempty_equivalenceOver_comparison
declarations.doc:
**`Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` is the presheaf of relative automorphisms, as a category over `Z`**:
there is a `StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver` from the projection of the category of
elements of the presheaf of relative automorphisms of `x` to the projection
`Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) ⟶ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalenceOver_comparison :
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (PresheafOfCategories.discreteProjection (relativeAutomorphismPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x))
      (relativeAutomorphismSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x).toFunctor)
declarations.comment: part (1): Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) is the presheaf of groups of relative automorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.RelativeAutomorphismSpace.inertiaObj_mul
declarations.doc:
**The multiplication of relative automorphisms is the composition law of the relative
inertia.** The object of the relative inertia attached to the product `φ * ψ` of two
relative automorphisms of `x` at a point of `Z` is the value at the corresponding object of
`ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴} ×_𝒳 ℐ_{𝒳/𝒴}` of `CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition`, the composition law
`((x, α), (x', α'), β) ↦ (x, α ∘ β⁻¹ ∘ α' ∘ β)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaObj_mul {a : (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj}
    (φ ψ : RelativeAutomorphism B S hS Z hZ f x a) :
    inertiaObj B S hS Z hZ f x (φ * ψ) =
      (CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.composition f.hom.hom.toFunctor 𝒳.val.val.p).obj
        (inertiaPair B S hS Z hZ f x φ ψ)
declarations.comment: part (1): the group law is the composition law of 050R pulled back along x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.RelativeAutomorphismSpace.inertiaObj_one
declarations.doc:
**The unit of the group of relative automorphisms is the neutral section of the relative
inertia.** The object of the relative inertia attached to the identity relative automorphism of
`x` at a point `a` of `Z` is the value of `CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.neutralSection`,
`x ↦ (x, id_x)`, at `x(a)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaObj_one {a : (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj} :
    inertiaObj B S hS Z hZ f x (1 : RelativeAutomorphism B S hS Z hZ f x a) =
      (CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.neutralSection f.hom.hom.toFunctor).obj
        (x.hom.hom.toFunctor.obj a)
declarations.comment: part (1): the unit is the neutral element of 050R pulled back along x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.RelativeAutomorphismSpace.inertiaObj_inv
declarations.doc:
**The inverse of the group of relative automorphisms is the inverse of the relative
inertia.** The object of the relative inertia attached to `φ⁻¹` is the value at the object
attached to `φ` of `CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.inverse`, `(x, α) ↦ (x, α⁻¹)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaObj_inv {a : (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj}
    (φ : RelativeAutomorphism B S hS Z hZ f x a) :
    inertiaObj B S hS Z hZ f x φ⁻¹ =
      (CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.inverse f.hom.hom.toFunctor).obj
        (inertiaObj B S hS Z hZ f x φ)
declarations.comment: part (1): the inverse is the inverse of 050R pulled back along x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeAutomorphismTotalPresheaf
declarations.doc:
The presheaf `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutomorphismTotalPresheaf`, whose sections over
`W` are the pairs of a point `z` of `Z` over `W` and an automorphism of `x(z)` killed by `f`, is
an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeAutomorphismTotalPresheaf (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeAutomorphismTotalPresheaf B S hS Z hZ f x)
declarations.comment: part (1): Isom_{X/Y}(x, x) as a presheaf over Z on the big fppf site is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_relativeIsomorphismDiagram
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, two algebraic-space-valued points
`x₁, x₂ : Z ⟶ 𝒳` and a 2-morphism `α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f` of the target, there are a 1-morphism `H`
from the isomorphism category of `x₁`, `x₂` to that of `x₁ ≫ f`, `x₂ ≫ f` which keeps the two
points of `Z` and applies `f` to the isomorphism between them, and a 1-morphism `Δ` from `Z` to the
latter whose value at `z` is the pair `(z, z)` with comparison isomorphism `α_z`.

The 2-fibre product of `H` along `Δ` is the category of isomorphisms `x₁ ≅ x₂` lifting `α`; that
it is represented by an algebraic space over `Z` is the remaining half of part (2) and is not
asserted here. The witnesses are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.absoluteIsomorphismImageBasedFunctor` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomorphismTwistedDiagonalBasedFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_relativeIsomorphismDiagram
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    let PX := absoluteIsomorphismCategory B S hS Z hZ 𝒳 x₁ x₂
    let PY := absoluteIsomorphismCategory B S hS Z hZ 𝒴 (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)
    ∃ (H : PX.val ⥤ᵇ PY.val)
      (Δ : (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val ⥤ᵇ PY.val),
      (∀ A : PX.val.obj,
        HEq (H.toFunctor.obj A).x A.x ∧
        HEq (H.toFunctor.obj A).y A.y ∧
        HEq (H.toFunctor.obj A).iso.hom
          (f.hom.hom.toFunctor.map A.iso.hom)) ∧
      (∀ A : (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ).val.val.obj,
        HEq (Δ.toFunctor.obj A).x A ∧
        HEq (Δ.toFunctor.obj A).y A ∧
        HEq (Δ.toFunctor.obj A).iso.hom
          (α.hom.hom.toNatTrans.app A))
declarations.comment: part (2): functorial map and twisted diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): the relative sheaf of isomorphisms from `x₁` to `x₂` lifting `α`,
in the iterated form the source writes it in.** The 2-fibre product

```text
Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂) = (Z ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} Z) ×_{Z ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} Z, Δ^α} Z
```

of the map `H` on absolute isomorphism categories induced by `f` along the twisted diagonal
`Δ^α` determined by `α`. Its objects over a scheme `W` are the isomorphisms `x₁(z) ≅ x₂(z)` of
the fibre of `𝒳` over `W` whose image under `f` is the component of `α` at `z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    CatFiberedInGroupoids (BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (2): Isom^α_{X/Y}(x₁, x₂) as the iterated fibre product of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): the iterated form of `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is an algebraic
space.** It is the base change of the twisted diagonal `Δ^α` along `H`; `Δ^α` is representable by
algebraic spaces and `Z ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} Z` is represented by an algebraic space, so this is
Stacks 0300.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (2): the iterated form of Isom^α_{X/Y}(x₁, x₂) is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpaceProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PP, part (2): the iterated form of `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is an algebraic space
over `Z`.** Its structure 1-morphism to the stack of `Z` has an algebraic space as source and the
stack of `Z` as target, so it is representable by algebraic spaces by Stacks 02ZZ; together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpace` it is
therefore a morphism of algebraic spaces with target `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpaceProj (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (relativeIsomorphismIteratedSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (2): the iterated form of Isom^α_{X/Y}(x₁, x₂) is an algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_cartesianRelativeInertiaSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PQ, the left square.** Both squares of the diagram of Stacks 06PQ are 2-fibre
