products of algebraic stacks: the right one is the defining base-change square of Stacks 04T2,
and this provides the left one, a comparison 1-morphism from the relative inertia of the base
change to the relative inertia of `π`, with the prescribed action on objects and automorphisms,
exhibiting the left square as a 2-fibre product in the 2-category of algebraic stacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cartesianRelativeInertiaSquare :
    Nonempty (CartesianRelativeInertiaSquare B S hS π f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04T2, second assertion: the 2-categorical universal property.** The canonical
square of a cospan of algebraic stacks over `S` is a 2-fibre product in the 2-category of
algebraic stacks, and not merely in the ambient 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids:
the square underlying it is the canonical one there, which is a 2-fibre product
unconditionally, and the 2-category of algebraic stacks is a full sub-2-category.

This is also the **right square of Stacks 06PQ**, whose left square is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_cartesianRelativeInertiaSquare`: the right square of the
diagram there is the defining base-change square of the cospan `(π, f)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquare
declarations.doc:
Let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation and let `G/U` be the stabilizer group
algebraic space of the presenting groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)`. Then

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
ℐ_𝒳  ------>  𝒳
```

is a fibre product diagram, i.e. a 2-fibre product in the sense of Stacks 003Q, given Groupoids in
Spaces, Lemma 06PC and the second assertion of Stacks 06PB as the hypothesis `Z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquare
    (Z : InertiaQuotientStackInput B S hS P) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (inertiaPresentationSquare B S hS P Z)
declarations.comment: the diagram is 2-cartesian, given Stacks 06PC and Stacks 06PB part 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquare
declarations.doc:
The diagram of the stabilizer, the object space, the inertia of `𝒳` and `𝒳` attached to a
presentation `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` is a fibre product diagram, given Groupoids in Spaces, Lemma 06PC with the
inertia stack of `[U/R]` in its lower-left corner.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquare
    (Z : InertiaQuotientStackInput B S hS P) :
    Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (inertiaPresentationSquare B S hS P Z))
declarations.comment: the diagram is a fibre product diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquareAlgebraicStacks
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation. Let `G/U` be
the stabilizer group algebraic space associated to the presenting groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)`.
Then

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
ℐ_𝒳  ------>  𝒳
```

is a 2-fibre product diagram in the 2-category of algebraic stacks over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquareAlgebraicStacks :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (inertiaPresentationSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS P)
declarations.comment: the diagram is 2-cartesian in the 2-category of algebraic stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquareAlgebraicStacks
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` with a
presentation `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳`, the diagram of the algebraic stack of the stabilizer, the algebraic
stack of the object space, the inertia of `𝒳` and `𝒳` is a fibre product diagram in the
2-category of algebraic stacks over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquareAlgebraicStacks :
    Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
      (inertiaPresentationSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS P))
declarations.comment: the diagram is a fibre product diagram of algebraic stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_presentationInertiaSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PR.** Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` — in
particular an algebraic stack — and let `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` be a presentation (Stacks 04TI). Let `G/U` be
the stabilizer group algebraic space associated to the groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)` (Stacks 0448).
Then

```
𝒮_G  ------>  𝒮_U
 |             |
 v             v
ℐ_𝒳  ------>  𝒳
```

is a fibre product diagram, i.e. a 2-fibre product in the sense of Stacks 003Q.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaPresentationSquare` at the canonical
input of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inertiaQuotientStackInput`, so the proof is the proof of the
source — immediate from Groupoids in Spaces, Lemma 06PC
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inertiaQuotientStackSquareFibred` together with the
second assertion of Stacks 06PB) pasted onto the inertia square of Stacks 06R5 for the
presentation — and the only datum it consumes is the presentation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_presentationInertiaSquare :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (presentationInertiaSquare P)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_isTwoFibreProduct_presentationInertiaSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PR**, in propositional form: for a presentation `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` the diagram of the
stack of the stabilizer, the stack of the object space, the inertia of `𝒳` and `𝒳` is a fibre
product diagram.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isTwoFibreProduct_presentationInertiaSquare :
    Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (presentationInertiaSquare P))
declarations.comment: the diagram is a fibre product diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PS.** An implication between two properties of morphisms of algebraic spaces
over `S` induces the same implication for 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`: the
existential smooth-diagram criterion of Stacks 06FM is monotone in the property it tests.

The same diagram witnesses both: its top horizontal morphism is a morphism of algebraic spaces
and has the first property, hence the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_mono
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P P' : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hPP' : ∀ {U V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u},
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U → IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V →
      ∀ (g : U ⟶ V), P g → P' g)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P f) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P' f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PU.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` *is locally
quasi-finite* when it is quasi-DM (**Stacks 04YW**), locally of finite type (**Stacks 06FS**,
part (1)), and for every field-valued point of `𝒴` the fibre of `f` over it has discrete space of
points.

A field-valued point is a field `k` contained in the site together with a structure morphism
`Spec(k) ⟶ S` and a 1-morphism from the algebraic stack `Spec(k)` represents to `𝒴`; the fibre is
the apex of the canonical 2-fibre-product square of that 1-morphism with `f`, and its points
carry the topology of **Stacks 04XL**.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyQuasiFinite {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PW.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *flat* when it passes the
existential smooth-diagram test of Stacks 06FM at flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces:
there are algebraic spaces `U`, `V` over `S`, a smooth 1-morphism `a` from the category fibred in
groupoids of `U` to the source which is surjective on objects, a smooth 1-morphism `b` from the
one of `V` to the target, and a morphism `h : U ⟶ V` making the square 2-commute, with `h` a flat
morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFlat {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PX.** The composite of two flat 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is flat.

Stacks 06PW is condition (2) of Stacks 06FM at flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces, on the
nose (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_iff_hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram`), so
this is Stacks 06FP at that property: flatness is smooth local on the source-and-target by
**Stacks 06FC** and stable under composition by **Stacks 03MN**, which is the source's own
proof.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A base change of a flat 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is flat: if `P` is a 2-fibre
product of the cospan `(g, f)` and `f` is flat, then the projection `P.fst` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_twoFibreProduct_fst_descent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06PZ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S` with `g` surjective and flat, and let `P` exhibit `𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳`. If the base change
`𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` is flat, then `f` is flat.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_of_isFlat_twoFibreProduct_fst` with its
hypothesis discharged by [Stacks Project, Tag 05VY].
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_twoFibreProduct_fst_descent
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hgsurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hfst : IsFlat B S hS P.fst) :
    IsFlat B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q0.** Let `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`. If
`𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` is flat and `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is surjective and flat, then `𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` is flat.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_of_comp_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat` with
its hypothesis discharged by [Stacks Project, Tag 05VY].
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hfsurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hfflat : IsFlat B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q2, part (1).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *locally of finite
presentation* when it passes the universal smooth-diagram test of Stacks 06FM at local finite
presentation of morphisms of algebraic spaces: every 2-commutative square of algebraic spaces
over `f` whose two vertical 1-morphisms are smooth and whose every comparison 1-morphism to a
2-fibre product is smooth has its top horizontal morphism locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q2, part (2).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *of finite
presentation* when it is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFinitePresentation {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q3**, the local assertion. The composite of two 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` which are locally of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation.

Stacks 06Q2 part (1) is condition (1) of Stacks 06FM at local finite presentation of morphisms of
algebraic spaces, so this is Stacks 06FP at that property, transported across the equivalence of
conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 06FM. Local finite presentation is smooth local on the
source-and-target by **Stacks 06FC** and stable under composition by **Stacks 03XQ**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFinitePresentation_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q3**, the global assertion. The composite of two 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` of finite presentation is of finite presentation.

Being of finite presentation is being locally of finite presentation together with being
quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Stacks 06Q2, part (2)); the first conjunct composes by the
local assertion above, the second by **Stacks 050W** and the third by **Stacks 050K**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) (hg : IsFinitePresentation B S hS g) :
    IsFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q4**, the local assertion. A base change of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
`S` which is locally of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation: if `P` is a 2-fibre
product of the cospan `(g, f)` and `f` is locally of finite presentation, then the projection
`P.fst` is locally of finite presentation.

This is the base-change remark **Stacks 06FQ** at local finite presentation of morphisms of
algebraic spaces, transported across the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) of **Stacks 06FM**,
since Stacks 06Q2 part (1) is the universal criterion where Stacks 06FQ concludes about the
existential one. Local finite presentation is smooth local on the source-and-target by
**Stacks 06FC** and stable under base change by **Stacks 03XR**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_baseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFinitePresentation_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q4**, the global assertion. A base change of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
`S` of finite presentation is of finite presentation.

Being of finite presentation is being locally of finite presentation together with being
quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Stacks 06Q2, part (2)); the first conjunct base changes by the
local assertion above, the second by **Stacks 050V** and the third by **Stacks 050F**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    IsFinitePresentation B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFiniteType_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc: A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` of finite presentation is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_of_isFinitePresentation
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    IsFiniteType B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is locally of finite presentation is locally
of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `f ≫ g` is
locally of finite presentation and `g` is locally of finite type, then `f` is locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q7.** An open immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` is locally of finite
presentation.

By Stacks 04YL the 1-morphism is representable by algebraic spaces and every algebraic space
representing a base change of it along a scheme-valued point of the target has open immersion
structural morphism, hence by Stacks 06CN has structural morphism locally of finite
presentation. That is the relative property of Stacks 03YK at local finite presentation of
morphisms of algebraic spaces, which Stacks 06FM equates with the universal smooth-diagram test
defining local finite presentation of the 1-morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isOpenImmersion
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsOpenImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q8.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If the base change
`𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` of `f` along `g` is locally of finite presentation, then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_baseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgs : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hglfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (hbase : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).snd) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp_of_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Q9.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S`. If `f ≫ g` is locally of finite presentation and `f` is surjective, flat and locally of
finite presentation, then `g` is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp_of_fppf
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hfsurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hfflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hflfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_fibre_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QA.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is
surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then for every object `U` of the big fppf
site of `S` and every object `y` of the fibre of `𝒴` over `U` there is an fppf covering of `U`
such that over every member of it `y` is isomorphic to the image of an object of `𝒳`.

The covering is a covering sieve of the big fppf topology of `S`, and the isomorphism over a
member `k : V ⟶ U` is a morphism `f(x) ⟶ y` lying over `k`, which in a category fibred in
groupoids is exactly an isomorphism `f(x) ≅ y|_V` of the fibre over `V`. The covering produced is
a one-member one; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_scheme_lift_of_isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fppfCovering_fibre_lift
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hlfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : 𝒴.val.val.p.Fiber U),
      ∃ R ∈ BigFppfOver.topology B S hS U,
        ∀ ⦃V : BigFppfOver B S hS⦄ ⦃k : V ⟶ U⦄, R.arrows k →
          ∃ (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (α : (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom).obj x ⟶ y.1),
            𝒴.val.val.p.IsHomLift k α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QC.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` makes `𝒳` a *gerbe
over* `𝒴` when its underlying functor makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴` in the sense of Stacks 06P2,
for the fppf topology on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsGerbeOver {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbe
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QC.** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` *is a gerbe* when there is an algebraic
stack `𝒴` representable by an algebraic space over `S` and a 1-morphism `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` making `𝒳` a
gerbe over `𝒴`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsGerbe (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_algebraicSpace_isGerbeOver_isoClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QD.** If an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is a gerbe, then the fppf sheafification
of the presheaf `U ↦ Ob(𝒳_U)/≅` is (the universe lift of) an algebraic space `F`, and `𝒳` is a
gerbe over the algebraic stack `𝒴` representable by `F` by a 1-morphism inducing the unit of the
sheafification on isomorphism classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebraicSpace_isGerbeOver_isoClasses (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsGerbe B S hS 𝒳) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.val.p.IsFibered := (CatFiberedInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒳.val).isFibered
    ∃ F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F ∧
      ∃ (e : F ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ sheafifiedIsoClasses B S hS 𝒳)
        (𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴), IsGerbeOver B S hS g ∧
          letI : 𝒴.val.val.p.IsFibered :=
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒴.val).isFibered
          ∃ eY : 𝒴.val.val.p.isoClassPresheaf ≅ F ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1},
            Functor.isoClassMap (Functor.isFibredOneMorphism_of_isFiberedInGroupoids
              (CatFiberedInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒴.val)
              (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p g.hom)) ≫ eY.hom ≫ e.hom =
              (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS).toSheafify (isoClassPresheaf B S hS 𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_isGerbeOver_isoClassSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QD.** If an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is a gerbe, then the fppf sheafification
of the presheaf `U ↦ Ob(𝒳_U)/≅` is (the universe lift of) an algebraic space `F`, and `𝒳` is a
gerbe over `F`: there are an algebraic stack `𝒴` represented by `F` through an equivalence `E`
over the site (Stacks 04SV) and a 1-morphism `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` making `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`, such that
the sheafification unit sends the class of `x` to the section of `F` named by the class of
`g(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGerbeOver_isoClassSpace
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsGerbe B S hS 𝒳) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.val.p.IsFibered := (CatFiberedInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒳.val).isFibered
    ∃ F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F ∧
      ∃ (e : F ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ sheafifiedIsoClasses B S hS 𝒳)
        (𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
        (E : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          𝒴.val.val.p (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
        (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴), IsGerbeOver B S hS g ∧
          letI : 𝒴.val.val.p.IsFibered :=
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒴.val).isFibered
          ∀ (U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ) (c : (isoClassPresheaf B S hS 𝒳).obj U),
            e.inv.app U (((BigFppfOver.topology B S hS).toSheafify
              (isoClassPresheaf B S hS 𝒳)).app U c) =
              ULift.up (PresheafOfCategories.elementsIsoClassEquiv F E U.unop
                ((Functor.isoClassMap (Functor.isFibredOneMorphism_of_isFiberedInGroupoids
                  (CatFiberedInGroupoids.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒴.val)
                  (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p g.hom))).app U c))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QE.** In a 2-fibre-product square of algebraic stacks over `S` with cospan
`(f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴, g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)`, if `f` makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴` then the projection to `𝒴'` makes
the apex a gerbe over `𝒴'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_of_isTwoFibreProduct {𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴} (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P) (hf : IsGerbeOver B S hS f) :
    IsGerbeOver B S hS P.snd

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_of_snd_of_isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QF.** Let

```text
𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳
↓     ↓
𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴
```

be a 2-fibre-product square of algebraic stacks over `S`, given as a 2-commutative square `P`
over the cospan `(f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴, g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)` with the 2-categorical universal property, so that
`P.pt` is `𝒳'` and `P.snd` is the base change of `f`. If `g` is surjective, flat and locally of
finite presentation and `P.snd` makes `𝒳'` a gerbe over `𝒴'`, then `f` makes `𝒳` a gerbe over
`𝒴`.

This is the descent direction; the base-change direction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_of_isTwoFibreProduct`, Stacks 06QE.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_of_snd_of_isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴}
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hgsurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS g) (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hglfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (hgerbe : IsGerbeOver B S hS P.snd) :
    IsGerbeOver B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_section_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**A section of a gerbe over an algebraic space is flat and locally of finite presentation.**
Let `π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒰` make `𝒳` a gerbe over an algebraic stack `𝒰` which is representable by an
algebraic space, and let `x : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a section of `π`. Then `x` is flat and locally of finite
presentation.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_section_of_isGerbeOver` this is **Stacks
06QG** part (3), at the source's generality; the three parts of the tag are assembled in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.GerbeSectionClassifyingStack`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_single_cover_section_factorisation_of_isGerbeOver` produces a
surjective, flat, locally finitely presented `q : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒳` out of the algebraic stack of an object
of the site together with a `γ : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒰` with `γ ≫ x = q` on the nose, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_factorisation`
turns such a factorisation into the conclusion by the **Stacks 06NR** step and the descent along
`q`. The three representability data that step needs are the two instances of
`isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_pt` at the cospans `(q, q)` and `(q, x)` and **Stacks 04SV** for
the slice of the site over `V`; the leg `q` is representable by algebraic spaces by condition (3)
of **Stacks 045G**, its source being the algebraic stack of an object of the site, and the leg `x`
by **Stacks 045G** condition (2) through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isAlgebraicStack`, its source being
representable by an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_section_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒰 𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒰) (x : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳) (hx : x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 𝒰)
    (hπ : IsGerbeOver B S hS π)
    (h𝒰 : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒰.val) :
    IsFlat B S hS x ∧ IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS x
declarations.comment: part (3): flatness and local finite presentation of the section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_section_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
Let `π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` making `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`,
and let `x : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` be a section of `π`, i.e. a 1-morphism with a 2-isomorphism
`x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 𝒴`. Then `x` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_section_of_isGerbeOver
    (π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (x : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳) (hx : x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 𝒴)
    (hπ : AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbeOver B S hS π) :
    IsSurjective B S hS x
declarations.comment: part (3): surjectivity only; (1), (2), flatness and finite presentation unproved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_grpObj_nonempty_equivalenceOver_quotientStackOfAction_of_section_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QG.** Let `π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒰` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` to the
algebraic stack `𝒰` of an algebraic space `Z` over `S`, let `x : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a section of `π` — a
1-morphism together with a 2-isomorphism `x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 𝒰` — and let `π` make `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒰`.
Write `G = Isom_𝒳(x, x)` for the automorphism sheaf of the section, an algebraic space over `Z`
through `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceProj`. Then

1. `G` carries the structure of a group algebraic space over `Z`, and the quotient stack of its
   *trivial* action on `Z` is equivalent, over the big fppf site of `S`, to `𝒳`;
2. `G ⟶ Z` is flat and locally of finite presentation;
3. `x` is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation.

Part (1) is stated as the existence of a group algebraic space `G'` over `Z` together with an
isomorphism of `G'` with `G` *over `Z`*; that `G'` is the stabilizer of the self-intersection
groupoid of **Stacks 04T4** (4), whose group law is groupoid composition — composition of
automorphisms of `x` — by **Stacks 0447**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizer_mul_comp_arrow`), and which is all of
the arrow space of that groupoid because for a section its source and target agree. The
equivalence is the canonical 1-morphism of Stacks 04T4 (5), carried across the identification of
the self-intersection groupoid with the trivial-action groupoid of its stabilizer.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_grpObj_nonempty_equivalenceOver_quotientStackOfAction_of_section_of_isGerbeOver
    (π : 𝒳 ⟶ Stack.algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ)
    (hx : x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 (Stack.algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ))
    (hπ : IsGerbeOver B S hS π) :
    (∃ (G : Over (⟨Z, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS).obj) (hGrp : GrpObj G)
        (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.left)
        (_ι : G ≅ Over.mk (Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ x x)),
        letI : GrpObj G := hGrp
        letI : ModObj G (𝟙_ (Over (⟨Z, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS).obj)) :=
          ModObj.trivialAction G _
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (Stack.quotientStackOfAction (⟨Z, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) G (𝟙_ _) hG hZ).p
          𝒳.val.val.p)) ∧
      Space.IsFlat B S hS (Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ x x) ∧
      Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ x x) ∧
      Stack.IsSurjective B S hS x ∧ IsFlat B S hS x ∧
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.source_eq_target_selfIntersectionPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QG, part (1): the action is trivial**, read on the presentation datum of
Stacks 04T4 (4) and (5): the groupoid in algebraic spaces it builds from a section of a gerbe has
one and the same source and target, so it is the groupoid of a group algebraic space acting
trivially on the object space.
declarations.statement:
theorem source_eq_target_selfIntersectionPresentation
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) (π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hx : x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 𝒴) :
    (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.source =
      (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid.target
declarations.comment: part (1): the self-intersection groupoid of a section of a gerbe has equal source and target, so the group algebraic space of part (1) acts trivially

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_canonicalMap_of_section_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QG, part (1): the canonical equivalence.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`,
let `π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` make `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`, let `x : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` be a section of `π`, let `𝒴` be
represented by an algebraic space `U` and let the self-intersection `𝒴 ×_{x, 𝒳, x} 𝒴` be
represented by an algebraic space `R` — which it is, by Stacks 04T4 (1). Then the canonical
1-morphism `x_can : [U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` of the presentation datum of Stacks 04T4 (4) and (5) is an
equivalence over the big fppf site of `S`.

Full faithfulness is Stacks 04T4 (6) and needs no hypothesis beyond the presentation data;
essential surjectivity on each fibre is the local essential surjectivity of the section, glued by
effective descent in the quotient stack against the `Mor`-sheaf condition on `𝒳`, and a
1-morphism of fibred categories which is fully faithful and essentially surjective on every fibre
is an equivalence over the site.

The source states the equivalence at the quotient stack of the trivial action of
`G = Isom_𝒳(x, x)`. That is this equivalence: the self-intersection groupoid has equal source and
target (`source_eq_target_selfIntersectionPresentation`), hence is the groupoid of the trivial
action of its stabilizer group of **Stacks 0447** on the object space, and that stabilizer is
`Isom_𝒳(x, x)` over the object space. The passage is
`exists_grpObj_nonempty_equivalenceOver_quotientStackOfAction_of_section_of_isGerbeOver`, in the
namespace `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.GerbeSectionClassifyingStack`, where the whole of Stacks 06QG
is assembled.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_canonicalMap_of_section_of_isGerbeOver
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val) (π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hx : x ≫ π ≅ 𝟙 𝒴)
    (hπ : CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) 𝒴.val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor π)) :
    Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
      (Stack.quotientStack (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).groupoid).p
      𝒳.val.p
      (selfIntersectionPresentation eU eR h𝒳).canonicalMap.toFunctor)
declarations.comment: part (1): the canonical 1-morphism out of the quotient stack of the self-intersection groupoid is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_of_equivalenceOver_quotientStack
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let `U` be an algebraic space
over `S`, let `G` be a group algebraic space flat and locally of finite presentation over `U`,
and let `g : U ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If the base change
of `f` along `g` is isomorphic, as an object over `U`, to the quotient stack `[U/G]` of the
trivial action of `G` on `U`, then `f` makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_of_equivalenceOver_quotientStack
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (U : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : ofAlgebraicSpace.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgsurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS g) (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hglfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (G : Over U.obj) [GrpObj G] (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.left)
    (_hGflat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.hom)
    (_hGlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.hom)
    (A : Space.ActionGroupoidConstruction U G (𝟙_ (Over U.obj)) hG U.property)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.snd.hom)
      (quotientStackToBase A.groupoid).toFunctor) :
    IsGerbeOver B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_of_hasClassifyingFppfCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QH, the implication (2) ⟹ (1), packaged.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
`S` which fppf-locally on its target is the classifying stack of a flat, locally finitely
presented group algebraic space makes its source a gerbe over its target.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_of_equivalenceOver_quotientStack`
with the data of clause (2) bundled into `HasClassifyingFppfCover`, which is the form a consumer
that has clause (2) as a hypothesis — or has just produced it — can use.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_of_hasClassifyingFppfCover
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h : HasClassifyingFppfCover.{u, w} B S hS f) :
    IsGerbeOver B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.hasClassifyingFppfCover_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**The reduction step of Stacks 06QH, (1) ⟹ (2): clause (2) descends along a surjective, flat,
locally finitely presented base change.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
over `S` and let `h : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If the base
change of `f` along `h` satisfies clause (2) of Stacks 06QH, then so does `f`.

This is the step by which the source's proof of (1) ⟹ (2) replaces `𝒴` first by a scheme
smoothly covering it and then by the member of an fppf covering of that scheme: the covering
1-morphism `g : U ⟶ 𝒴'` produced for the base change is composed with `h`, which keeps it
surjective (**Stacks 04ZT**), flat (**Stacks 06PX**) and locally of finite presentation
(**Stacks 06Q3**), and the two 2-fibre-product squares are pasted (**Stacks 003Q**), the pasted
rectangle having the *same* apex and second leg as the inner square — so the identification of
that apex with `[U/G]` over `U` is carried over unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasClassifyingFppfCover_of_baseChange
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hhsurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS h) (hhflat : IsFlat B S hS h)
    (hhlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f h) (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hbc : HasClassifyingFppfCover.{u, w} B S hS Q.snd) :
    HasClassifyingFppfCover.{u, w} B S hS f
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2): the reduction along a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_iff_hasClassifyingFppfCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QH.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are
equivalent:

1. `f` makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`;
2. there are an algebraic space `U` over `S`, a group algebraic space `G` over `U` which is flat
   and locally of finite presentation over `U`, and a surjective, flat, locally finitely
   presented 1-morphism `U ⟶ 𝒴` such that the base change `𝒳 ×_𝒴 U` is isomorphic over `U` to
   the quotient stack `[U/G]` of the trivial action of `G` on `U`.

Clause (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.HasClassifyingFppfCover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_iff_hasClassifyingFppfCover
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsGerbeOver B S hS f ↔ HasClassifyingFppfCover.{u, w} B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QI, flatness and local finite presentation.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S` which makes `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴` is flat and locally of finite
presentation.

Choose a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented `p : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳` from an algebraic space. The
comparison `𝒲 ×_𝒳 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒲 ×_𝒴 𝒲` is a base change of the relative diagonal `Δ_f` by
**Stacks 04Z1**, hence locally essentially surjective by Stacks 06P1 (2)(b); its composite with
the first projection of `𝒲 ×_𝒴 𝒲` is the first projection of `𝒲 ×_𝒳 𝒲`, a base change of `p`. So
Stacks 06NR for 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks makes the first projection
`𝒲 ×_𝒴 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒲` flat and locally of finite presentation. That projection is the base change of
`p ≫ f` along itself, and `p ≫ f` is locally essentially surjective by Stacks 06QA for `p` and
Stacks 06P1 (2)(a); so **Stacks 045D** makes `p ≫ f` flat and locally of finite presentation,
and **Stacks 06Q0** and **Stacks 06Q9** cancel `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsGerbeOver B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS f ∧ IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f
declarations.comment: flat and locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QI**, surjectivity. A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` whose underlying
functor exhibits its source as a gerbe over its target for the localized big fppf topology is
surjective.

Stacks 06P1 (2)(a) lifts an object of a fibre of the target along a covering sieve; the sieve
contains an arrow from a field spectrum, so an object over a field lifts after a field
extension, which is surjectivity on objects in the sense of Stacks 06D4; and Stacks 04XI
identifies that with surjectivity of the map on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_isGerbeOver
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      𝒴.val.val.p (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom)) :
    IsSurjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isGerbeOver_quotientStackToBase_overArrowStabilizerQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QJ, the geometric half of the implication (2) `⟹` (1).** The structure arrow
`[U/R] ⟶ X` of **Stacks 044R** of the groupoid read over `X = U/R'` makes the quotient stack a
gerbe over `X`.

The criterion is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isGerbeOver_quotientStackToBase_of_locallyFull`
(**Stacks 06PE** for the 1-morphism of **Stacks 0DUH**); its surjectivity clause is Stacks 06PG
and its local-fullness clause is **Stacks 046O**, both in the sieve form the criterion asks
for.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_quotientStackToBase_overArrowStabilizerQuotient
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS
      (Space.quotientSheaf (arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation G)).obj) :
    CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver (BigFppfOver.topology C S hS)
      (fibredCategory C S hS (arrowStabilizerQuotientSpace G hX).obj).val.p
      (quotientStackToBase (overArrowStabilizerQuotient G hX)).toFunctor
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (1): the quotient stack is a gerbe over U/(R/S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.mono_arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 043C part (2) for `R/S`: `j' = (t', s')` is a monomorphism.** This is the step of
the proof of **Stacks 06QJ**, the implication (2) `⟹` (1), which makes the quotient `R' = R/S` of
the arrow space by the stabilizer action a relation on the object space; with the
pre-equivalence-relation clause of **Stacks 043X** it is an equivalence relation.

Two sections of `R'` over a test object with the same source and the same target lift, after an
fppf covering, to arrows of `R` with the same source and the same target, and two such arrows lie
in a single orbit of the stabilizer: the loop `c(a, i(b))` at their common target carries one to
the other. So they already agree in `R'`, and `R'` is an fppf sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Mono (arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation G)
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (1): j' = (t', s') is a monomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isEquivalenceRelation_arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation
declarations.doc:
**The quotient `R' = R/S` of the arrow space by the stabilizer action is an equivalence
relation on the object space** — **Stacks 043C** part (4). This is the step of the proof of
**Stacks 06QJ**, the implication (2) `⟹` (1), after which the quotient `X = U/R'` is an algebraic
space by **Stacks 04S6**.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalenceRelation_iff_mono_and_isPreEquivalenceRelation` an
equivalence relation is exactly a monomorphic pre-equivalence relation, and the two halves are
`mono_arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation` and
`isPreEquivalenceRelation_arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation`. Nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceRelation_arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    CategoryTheory.IsEquivalenceRelation
      (arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation G).target
      (arrowStabilizerQuotientPreRelation G).source
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (1): j' = (t', s') is an equivalence relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection_of_isGerbe
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QJ, the implication (1) `⟹` (2).** If an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is a gerbe,
then the forgetful 1-morphism `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of its inertia is flat and locally of finite
presentation.

Let `𝒳 ⟶ Y` make `𝒳` a gerbe over an algebraic space `Y` and choose a smooth groupoid presentation
`𝒳 ≃ [U/R]` (Stacks 04T3). The composite `[U/R] ⟶ Y` is a gerbe, so for its restriction
`ψ : U ⟶ Y` the arrows cover the related pairs `U ×_Y U`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallySurjective_of_isGerbeOver_restrictedMorphism`), and the
stabilizer of the groupoid is flat and locally of finite presentation
(`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isFlat_stabilizer_of_isLocallySurjective`, the
argument of Stacks 06PL and Stacks 06PJ). The automorphism sheaves of `𝒳` are, fppf-locally,
these stabilizers (Stacks 044V), and flatness and local finite presentation descend
(Stacks 041W, Stacks 041T); that is clause (2), by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_inertiaProjection_iff_isomSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection_of_isGerbe
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsGerbe B S hS 𝒳) :
    IsFlat B S hS (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbe_iff_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QJ.** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is a gerbe if and only if the forgetful
1-morphism `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of its inertia is flat and locally of finite presentation.

The implication (1) `⟹` (2) is
`isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection_of_isGerbe`, and the implication
(2) `⟹` (1) is `isGerbe_of_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbe_iff_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    IsGerbe B S hS 𝒳 ↔
      IsFlat B S hS (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳) ∧
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
          (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbe_of_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` whose inertia projection `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is flat and locally of
finite presentation is a gerbe: there are an algebraic space `X` and a 1-morphism `𝒳 ⟶ X` making
`𝒳` a gerbe over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbe_of_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_inertiaProjection
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳))
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (Stack.inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    IsGerbe B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1): an algebraic stack whose inertia projection is flat and locally of finite presentation is a gerbe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_presentationStabilizer
declarations.doc:
If the inertia projection `ℐ_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is flat, then for
every presentation `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` the structure morphism `G ⟶ U` of the stabilizer group algebraic
space of the presenting groupoid is a flat morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_presentationStabilizer
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    Space.IsFlat B S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizer P.groupoid).hom
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (1): flatness of the stabilizer of a presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_presentationStabilizer
declarations.doc:
If the inertia projection `ℐ_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of an algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is locally of finite
presentation, then for every presentation `[U/R] ⟶ 𝒳` the structure morphism `G ⟶ U` of the
stabilizer group algebraic space of the presenting groupoid is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_presentationStabilizer
    (hlfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizer P.groupoid).hom
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (1): local finite presentation of the stabilizer of a presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_gerbeOver_reducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QK.** Let `𝒵` be a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack over `S` whose
space of points is a singleton. Then there is an algebraic stack `Z` over `S` which is
representable by an algebraic space, a 1-morphism `π : 𝒵 ⟶ Z` making `𝒵` a gerbe over `Z`, and
`Z` is again reduced, locally Noetherian with a single point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_gerbeOver_reducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint
    (𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒵 : Stack.IsReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint B S hS 𝒵) :
    ∃ Z : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS,
      IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z.val ∧
        (∃ π : 𝒵 ⟶ Z, IsGerbeOver B S hS π) ∧
          Stack.IsReducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint B S hS Z
declarations.comment: The field cover of Stacks 06MP (1) implies (2), the flatness and local finite presentation of the inertia and their fppf descent, Stacks 06QJ (2) implies (1), the gerbe 1-morphism being surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by Stacks 06QI, and the conclusion about the base by Stacks 06MP (2) implies (1) applied to the composite from the field spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_gerbeOver_reducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒵` be a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic stack over `S` whose space of points is a
singleton. Then there is an algebraic stack `Z` over `S` which is representable by an algebraic
space, a 1-morphism `π : 𝒵 ⟶ Z` making `𝒵` a gerbe over `Z`, and `Z` is again reduced, locally
Noetherian with a single point.
declarations.statement: alias exists_gerbeOver_reducedLocallyNoetherianWithUniquePoint_unconditional
declarations.comment: unconditional. The field cover of Stacks 06MP (1) implies (2), the flatness and local finite presentation of the inertia and their fppf descent, Stacks 06QJ (2) implies (1) cited from GerbeOfFlatInertia, the gerbe 1-morphism being surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by Stacks 06QI, and the conclusion about the base by Stacks 06MP (2) implies (1) applied to the composite from the field spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
declarations.doc: The target of a flat surjective morphism of schemes with reduced source is reduced.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Flat f] [Surjective f] [IsReduced X] : IsReduced Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06MK.** Regularity passes from the source of a surjective, flat morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` locally of finite presentation to its target.

A regular scheme is locally Noetherian, so a regular étale chart of the source witnesses local
Noetherianity of the source; Stacks 06MJ carries that to the target, and
`hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat` then applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isSurjective_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular T)
declarations.comment: the same statement in the descent chapter

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.largestTargetOpen
declarations.doc: The supremum of the opens of the target over which `f` has the property `P`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def largestTargetOpen (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.Opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.property_largestTargetOpen
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 06QP.** A target-local property holds over the largest open.
declarations.statement:
lemma property_largestTargetOpen (P Q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hQ : IsDescentMorphismClass Q) [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Scheme.precoverage Q)]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : P (f ∣_ largestTargetOpen P f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.le_largestTargetOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06QP.** Every open over which the property holds lies in the
largest open.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_largestTargetOpen (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (U : Y.Opens) (hU : P (f ∣_ U)) : U ≤ largestTargetOpen P f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.range_le_largestTargetOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06QP.** The image of a morphism of the chosen class whose base
change has the property lies in the largest open.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_le_largestTargetOpen (P Q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hQ : IsDescentMorphismClass Q) [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Scheme.precoverage Q)]
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (hg : Q g)
    (hfg : P (pullback.snd f g)) : Set.range g ⊆ (largestTargetOpen P f).1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.largestTargetOpen_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06QP.** The largest open commutes with base change along a
morphism of the chosen class.
declarations.statement:
lemma largestTargetOpen_baseChange (P Q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hQ : IsDescentMorphismClass Q) [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Scheme.precoverage Q)]
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (hg : Q g) :
    largestTargetOpen P (pullback.snd f g) = g ⁻¹ᵁ largestTargetOpen P f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.largestTargetOpen_covering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06QP.** The largest opens of the members of a covering family are
the inverse images of the largest open downstairs.
declarations.statement:
lemma largestTargetOpen_covering (P Q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hQ : IsDescentMorphismClass Q) [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Scheme.precoverage Q)]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} (f : X ⟶ Y) (Y' : I → Scheme.{u})
    (g : ∀ i, Y' i ⟶ Y) (hg : Presieve.ofArrows Y' g ∈ Scheme.precoverage Q Y) (i : I) :
    largestTargetOpen P (pullback.snd f (g i)) = (g i) ⁻¹ᵁ largestTargetOpen P f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isInvariantOpen_largestTargetOpen_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06QQ.** For a groupoid scheme whose source and target maps are
coverings for one of the fppf, syntomic, smooth or étale topologies, the largest open of the
object scheme over which the stabilizer group scheme has a target-local property is
invariant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvariantOpen_largestTargetOpen_stabilizer {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (P Q : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (hQ : IsDescentMorphismClass Q)
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Scheme.precoverage Q)]
    (hs : Presieve.ofArrows (fun _ : Unit => G.arrows.left)
      (fun _ => G.source.left) ∈ Scheme.precoverage Q G.objects.left)
    (ht : Presieve.ofArrows (fun _ : Unit => G.arrows.left)
      (fun _ => G.target.left) ∈ Scheme.precoverage Q G.objects.left) :
    IsInvariantOpen G (largestTargetOpen P (stabilizer G).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QS, the one-chart core.** On a commuting square of étale charts of `f` whose
source and target charts are affine and whose target chart is reduced, the chart morphism
becomes flat and locally of finite presentation over a dense open of the target chart, over
which the module becomes flat over the target and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_chart
    {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    {U V : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)]
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    [IsReduced ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    {p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X} {b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y} (a : U ⟶ V)
    (hpE : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf p)
    (hbE : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf b)
    (hcomm : p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ b)
    (hLFT : AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a)) :
    ∃ W : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V).Opens,
      Dense (W : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a) ∣_ W) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation
        (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a) ∣_ W) ∧
      ∀ u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U,
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a) u ∈ W →
          pointOfEtaleChart B S hS ⟨CostructuredArrow.mk p, hpE⟩ u ∈
              flatLocus B S hS hX f F ∧
            pointOfEtaleChart B S hS ⟨CostructuredArrow.mk p, hpE⟩ u ∈
              finitePresentationLocus B S hS hX F
declarations.comment:
the one-chart core of the proof: Tag 052B read on a commuting square of
affine étale charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QS for a reduced affine base**, step 3 of the source. A finite-type morphism of
algebraic spaces to a reduced affine scheme of the site, together with a module which is
quasi-coherent of finite type on charts, becomes flat, locally of finite presentation and
quasi-compact, and the module flat over the base and of finite presentation, over a dense open
of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_of_isAffine
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)]
    [IsReduced ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)]
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj Z) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    ∃ W : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z).Opens,
      Dense (W : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)) ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f (yoneda.map (openSiteObjectHom B S hS Z W))) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (pullback.snd f (yoneda.map (openSiteObjectHom B S hS Z W))) ∧
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS (pullback.snd f (yoneda.map (openSiteObjectHom B S hS Z W))) ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X,
        pointsEquivScheme B S hS Z (pointsMap B S hS X f x) ∈ W →
          x ∈ flatLocus B S hS hX f F ∧ x ∈ finitePresentationLocus B S hS hX F
declarations.comment: step 3 of the proof: the case of a reduced affine base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_open_genericFlatness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type
with `Y` reduced, and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent of finite type on
charts. Then there is a dense open subspace `W` of `Y` such that the base change of `f` over
`W` is flat, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, and such that `F` is flat over
`Y` and of finite presentation at every point of `X` lying over `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_genericFlatness
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Y, IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hY W ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X,
        pointsMap B S hS X f x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι) →
          x ∈ flatLocus B S hS hX f F ∧
            x ∈ finitePresentationLocus B S hS hX F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_of_isScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QS for a reduced scheme base**, step 2 of the source. This is the general
statement for a base which is represented by an object of the site, where the identity may be
taken as the surjective étale chart witnessing reducedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_of_isScheme
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    [IsReduced ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)]
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj Z) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor (yoneda.obj Z),
      IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS Z) W ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X,
        pointsMap B S hS X f x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι) →
          x ∈ flatLocus B S hS hX f F ∧
            x ∈ finitePresentationLocus B S hS hX F
declarations.comment: step 2 of the proof: the case of a reduced scheme base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QT.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
of finite type with `Y` reduced, and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent of
finite type on charts. Then there is a dense open subspace `W` of `Y` such that the base change
of `f` over `W` is flat and of finite presentation, and such that `F` is flat over `Y` and of
finite presentation at every point of `X` lying over `W`.

This is Stacks 06QS refined by the quasi-separatedness hypothesis: that proposition gives
flatness, local finite presentation and quasi-compactness of the base change, and a base change
of a quasi-separated morphism is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_isFinitePresentation
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor Y, IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hY W ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X,
        pointsMap B S hS X f x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι) →
          x ∈ flatLocus B S hS hX f F ∧
            x ∈ finitePresentationLocus B S hS hX F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_isFinitePresentation_of_isScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QT for a base represented by an object of the site.** This is the statement of
the tag for a reduced scheme base, where the identity may be taken as the surjective étale
chart witnessing reducedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_genericFlatness_isFinitePresentation_of_isScheme
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    [IsReduced ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)]
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj Z) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F) :
    ∃ W : Subfunctor (yoneda.obj Z),
      IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS Z) W ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.snd f W.ι) ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X,
        pointsMap B S hS X f x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι) →
          x ∈ flatLocus B S hS hX f F ∧
            x ∈ finitePresentationLocus B S hS hX F
declarations.comment: the case of a base represented by an object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_of_fieldCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QV**, surjectivity. If an algebraic space over `S` receives a surjective
morphism from the spectrum of a field, then every morphism to it from the spectrum of a field
is surjective.

Only the existence of the surjective field-valued morphism is used: it forces the point set of
the target to be a singleton, and the point set of a field spectrum is nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_fieldCover
    (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (f : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ Z)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (k' : Type u) [Field k'] (hk' : B.Contains (Spec (.of k')))
    (b' : Spec (.of k') ⟶ S)
    (g : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b'⟩ : B.obj hk' ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ Z) :
    IsSurjective B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_fieldCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QV**, flatness. If an algebraic space over `S` receives a surjective flat
morphism from the spectrum of a field, then every morphism to it from the spectrum of a field
is flat.

The algebraic-space hypothesis `_hZ` is retained from the source but is not needed: the
argument only uses that the chart `b₀` of `Z` is relatively representable and étale, which is
a hypothesis of the chart condition itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_fieldCover
    (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (f : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ Z)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (k' : Type u) [Field k'] (hk' : B.Contains (Spec (.of k')))
    (b' : Spec (.of k') ⟶ S)
    (g : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b'⟩ : B.obj hk' ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ Z) :
    IsFlat B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_and_singleton_points_iff_hasFlatFieldCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QW**, conditions (1) and (2).  A reduced algebraic space over `S` has exactly
one point if and only if it admits a surjective flat morphism from the spectrum of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_and_singleton_points_iff_hasFlatFieldCover
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced X) ∧
      Nonempty (points B S hS F) ∧ Subsingleton (points B S hS F)) ↔
        HasFlatFieldCover B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFlatFieldCover_iff_hasLocallyOfFiniteTypeFlatFieldCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QW**, conditions (2) and (3).  A surjective flat morphism to an algebraic space
over `S` from the spectrum of a field may be replaced by one that is in addition locally of
finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatFieldCover_iff_hasLocallyOfFiniteTypeFlatFieldCover
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    HasFlatFieldCover B S hS F ↔ HasLocallyOfFiniteTypeFlatFieldCover B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_locallyNoetherian_singleton_iff_hasFinitePresentationCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QX.** A reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S` has exactly one
point if and only if it admits a flat, surjective, locally finitely presented morphism from the
spectrum of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_locallyNoetherian_singleton_iff_hasFinitePresentationCover
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced X) ∧
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian X) ∧
      Nonempty (points B S hS F) ∧ Subsingleton (points B S hS F)) ↔
    HasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldCover B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEmpty_points_or_isIso_of_mono_of_hasFinitePresentationCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QY.** Let `f : Z' ⟶ Z` be a monomorphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, and
suppose `Z` admits a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented morphism from the spectrum of
a field. Then either `Z'` is empty or `f` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_points_or_isIso_of_mono_of_hasFinitePresentationCover
    {Z' Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hZ' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z') (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : Z' ⟶ Z) [Mono f]
    (hcover : HasLocallyOfFinitePresentationFlatFieldCover B S hS Z) :
    IsEmpty (points B S hS Z') ∨ IsIso f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isResidualSpaceAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06QZ, existence.** Every point of an algebraic space carries a residual space:
a monomorphism from a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic space with exactly one point,
whose image on points is that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualSpaceAt (hXalg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    ∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : Z ⟶ X),
      IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_isResidualSpaceAt
declarations.doc:
Every point `x` of an algebraic space `X` over `S` has a unique residual space: there is a
monomorphism `Z ⟶ X` with `Z` a reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic space whose point set is
the singleton `{x}`, and any two such are isomorphic over `X` by exactly one isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isResidualSpaceAt (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    (∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : Z ⟶ X), IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f) ∧
      ∀ (Z Z' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : Z ⟶ X) (f' : Z' ⟶ X),
        IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f → IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f' →
        ∃! e : Z' ≅ Z, e.hom ≫ f = f'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsResidualSpaceAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R0.** A monomorphism `f : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` exhibits `Z` as
a *residual space* of `X` at a point `x` of `|X|` when `Z` is reduced and locally Noetherian,
`|Z|` consists of exactly one point, and that point maps to `x`. Reducedness and local
Noetherianity are the étale-local scheme properties of Stacks 03E6.
declarations.statement:
def IsResidualSpaceAt (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (x : points B S hS X)
    {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : Z ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isReduced_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R1.** A reduced, locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S` with exactly one
point is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isRegular_of_isReduced_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced X))
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian X))
    (hnonempty : Nonempty (points B S hS F)) (hsub : Subsingleton (points B S hS F)) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsRegular X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.largestOpenSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R2**, existence and maximality. For a property `P` of morphisms of algebraic
spaces over `S` which is local on the target for a topology `τ` other than the fpqc topology,
every morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` has a largest open subspace of `Y` over which its restriction has
`P`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def largestOpenSubspace (τ : Topology) (hτ : τ ≠ .fpqc)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} τ B S hS)]
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    {W : {W : Subfunctor Y.obj // IsOpenSubspace B S hS W} //
      HasPropertyOnOpen B S hS P f W ∧
        ∀ V : {V : Subfunctor Y.obj // IsOpenSubspace B S hS V},
          HasPropertyOnOpen B S hS P f V → V.1 ≤ W.1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.factorsThrough_largestOpenSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R2**, part (1). A morphism `g : Y' ⟶ Y` which `τ` admits as a member of a
covering family and along which the base change of `f` has `P` factors through the largest open
locus of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_largestOpenSubspace (τ : Topology) (hτ : τ ≠ .fpqc)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} τ B S hS)]
    {X Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hg : τ.IsMember B S hS g.hom) (hP : P (pullback.snd f g)) :
    ∃ h : Y' ⟶ openObject B S hS (largestOpenSubspace B S hS τ hτ P f).1,
      h ≫ openInclusion B S hS (largestOpenSubspace B S hS τ hτ P f).1 = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.largestOpenSubspace_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R2**, part (2). The largest open locus of a base change of `f` along a morphism
`g` which `τ` admits as a member of a covering family is the inverse image of the largest open
locus of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem largestOpenSubspace_baseChange (τ : Topology) (hτ : τ ≠ .fpqc)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} τ B S hS)]
    {X Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hg : τ.IsMember B S hS g.hom) :
    (largestOpenSubspace B S hS τ hτ P (pullback.snd f g)).1.1 =
      ((largestOpenSubspace B S hS τ hτ P f).1.1).preimage g.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.largestOpenSubspace_covering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R2**, part (3). The largest open locus of the base change of `f` along a member
of a `τ`-covering of its target is the inverse image of the largest open locus of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem largestOpenSubspace_covering (τ : Topology) (hτ : τ ≠ .fpqc)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} τ B S hS)]
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) {I : Type v}
    (Yi : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : ∀ i, Yi i ⟶ Y)
    (hg : τ.IsCovering B S hS (fun i ↦ (Yi i).obj) (fun i ↦ (g i).hom)) (i : I) :
    (largestOpenSubspace B S hS τ hτ P (pullback.snd f (g i))).1.1 =
      ((largestOpenSubspace B S hS τ hτ P f).1.1).preimage (g i).hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsGerbeOver.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R3**. If `𝒳` is a gerbe over `𝒴` and `𝒴` is a gerbe over `𝒵`, then `𝒳` is a
gerbe over `𝒵`.

This is also **Stacks 06R8**, the same statement for morphisms of algebraic stacks: the
source proves 06R8 by citing 06R3, and an algebraic stack is a category fibred in groupoids
over the big fppf site, so the two differ only in the generality of the ambient site.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp (hF : IsGerbeOver J (G ⋙ r) F) (hG : IsGerbeOver J r G) :
    IsGerbeOver J r (F ⋙ G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.stabilizerProjectionOverOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06R4.** The restriction of the stabilizer of a groupoid in algebraic spaces over
an open subspace of the object space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stabilizerProjectionOverOpen
    (W : {W : Subfunctor G.objects.obj // Space.IsOpenSubspace C S hS W}) :
    AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct C S hS (stabilizerToObjects G)
        (Space.openInclusion C S hS W) ⟶ Space.openObject C S hS W
declarations.comment: the stabilizer restricted over an open subspace of the object space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.isInvariantOpen_of_isGreatest_stabilizer
declarations.doc:
