    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f.hom ↔
      (AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
        ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
          (toBase : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
          (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (⟨toBase⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ 𝒴),
          DiscreteTopology
            (points B S hS (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt.val.val
              (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt.val.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UB.** A base change of a locally quasi-finite 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks over `S` is locally quasi-finite: the first projection of any 2-fibre product of the
cospan `(g, f)` is locally quasi-finite as soon as `f` is.

The quasi-DM conjunct is **Stacks 050F** at the exchanged square and local finite type is
**Stacks 06FU**. For the fibre conjunct, a field-valued point `g'` of `𝒴'` gives the outer point
`g' ≫ g` of `𝒴`, and the fibre of the base change over `g'` is by **Stacks 02XD** a 2-fibre
product of the cospan `(f, g' ≫ g)`, whose fibre the hypothesis says has discrete space of
points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.locallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_over_field
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳 ⟶ Spec(k)` be a locally quasi-finite 1-morphism, where `𝒳` is an
algebraic stack over the field `k`, and let `f : V ⟶ 𝒳` be a locally quasi-finite 1-morphism out
of the algebraic stack represented by a scheme `V` of the site with structure morphism
`g : V ⟶ Spec(k)`. Then `g` is locally quasi-finite: it is locally of finite type and locally
quasi-finite as a morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_over_field
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    {𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B (Spec (.of k)) hk}
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B (Spec (.of k)) hk (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hk))))
    (hp : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B (Spec (.of k)) hk p)
    (V : Scheme.{u}) (hV : B.Contains V) (g : V ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (f : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B (Spec (.of k)) hk
      (Over.mk (⟨g⟩ : B.obj hV ⟶ B.obj hk)) ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B (Spec (.of k)) hk f) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.locallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_over_fieldPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UC at a field-valued point of a general base scheme, for the Stacks 06PU notion
of local quasi-finiteness of the chart.** This is
`locallyQuasiFinite_siteMap_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_fieldPoint` with local quasi-finiteness of
`c` read in the sense of **Stacks 06PU**, which is what the source's statement uses; it implies
the **Stacks 04XB** notion by **Stacks 06UA**, since `c` is representable by algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_over_fieldPoint
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (toBase : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    {𝒴₀ : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (W : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (q : 𝒴₀ ⟶ Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (⟨toBase⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)))
    (c : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS W ⟶ 𝒴₀)
    (hq : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS q) (hc : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS c) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (siteMap B S hS (c ≫ q))) ∧
      LocallyQuasiFinite ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (siteMap B S hS (c ≫ q)))
declarations.comment: at a field-valued point of a general base scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UD.** A composite of locally quasi-finite 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S` is locally quasi-finite.

The quasi-DM condition composes by **Stacks 050K** and local finite type by **Stacks 06FT**. For
the third condition, the fibre of `f ≫ g` over a field-valued point `p` of `𝒵` is by
**Stacks 02XD** a 2-fibre product of the cospan `(f, 𝒴_k ⟶ 𝒴)`, where `𝒴_k` is the fibre of `g`
over `p`; both `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴_k ⟶ 𝒴_k` and `𝒴_k ⟶ Spec(k)` are locally quasi-finite by
**Stacks 06UB**, so the discreteness is the case of a target locally quasi-finite over a
field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_tfae_hasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UE.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following
are equivalent: `f` is quasi-DM; every base change of `f` along an algebraic space over `𝒴` has
a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite cover by an algebraic
space; and some algebraic space surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation over `𝒴`
carries a base change of `f` with such a cover.

The hypothesis `hPresentation` is the substantial direction of **Stacks 06MF**, carried in this
library; it is used only for (1) ⟹ (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_tfae_hasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCover
    (hPresentation : Stack.ExistsQuasiDMPresentationOfIsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    [IsQuasiDM B S hS f,
      HasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCoverOnEveryBaseChange B S hS f,
      HasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCoverOnSomeFlatBaseChange B S hS f].TFAE
declarations.comment:
granted the substantial direction of Tag 06MF, the quasi-DM presentation
  theorem, as the hypothesis `hPresentation`, and granted the containment of the terminal
  scheme in the site as the hypothesis `hZ`, which the absolute quasi-DM condition of
  Tag 050D part (6) needs. Only (1) implies (2) uses `hPresentation`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_tfae_hasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCover_unconditional
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are equivalent: `f`
is quasi-DM; every base change of `f` along an algebraic space over `𝒴` has a surjective, flat,
locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite cover by an algebraic space; and some algebraic
space surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation over `𝒴` carries a base change of `f`
with such a cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_tfae_hasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCover_unconditional (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    [IsQuasiDM B S hS f,
      HasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCoverOnEveryBaseChange B S hS f,
      HasQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCoverOnSomeFlatBaseChange B S hS f].TFAE
declarations.comment:
unconditional. The implication (1) implies (2) uses the substantial direction of
  Tag 06MF, the quasi-DM presentation theorem
  hasQuasiDMPresentation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM, which is proved; the containment
  of the terminal scheme in the site that the absolute quasi-DM condition of Tag 050D part (6)
  needs is discharged by AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_terminal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_and_transfersLocalQuasiFiniteness_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, (1) ⟹ (2).** A locally quasi-finite 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks over `S` is quasi-DM, and for every algebraic space `𝒱` over `𝒴` a locally quasi-finite
1-morphism `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` out of an algebraic space has locally quasi-finite composite
`𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱`.

The quasi-DM conjunct is the first conjunct of **Stacks 06PU**. For the second, the projection
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒱` is a base change of `f` and so locally quasi-finite by **Stacks 06UB**, and
**Stacks 06UD** composes it with the given 1-morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_and_transfersLocalQuasiFiniteness_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiDM B S hS f ∧ TransfersLocalQuasiFinitenessOnSpaceBaseChanges B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange_of_isQuasiDM_of_transfers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, (2) ⟹ (3).** If `f` is quasi-DM and transfers local quasi-finiteness to the
projections of its algebraic-space base changes, then each of those base changes has a
surjective, flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite cover by an algebraic
space which is locally quasi-finite over the base.

The cover is the one **Stacks 06UE** produces from the quasi-DM condition; it is locally
quasi-finite in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, hence in the sense of
**Stacks 06PU** by **Stacks 06UA**, and the second conjunct of clause (2) then makes its
composite to the base locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange_of_isQuasiDM_of_transfers
    (hPresentation : Stack.ExistsQuasiDMPresentationOfIsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS
      (BigFppfSite.contains_terminal B))
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (htr : TransfersLocalQuasiFinitenessOnSpaceBaseChanges B S hS f) :
    LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the implication (2) => (3), granted the substantial direction of Tag 06MF as
  `hPresentation`, which is how Tag 06UE is carried in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange_of_onEverySpaceBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, (3) ⟹ (4).** Every algebraic stack has a smooth surjective chart by a scheme
of the site, and a smooth 1-morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, so the
universal clause (3) applied to that chart is clause (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange_of_onEverySpaceBaseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange B S hS f) :
    LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, the quasi-DM conjunct of (4) ⟹ (1).** A locally quasi-finite flat cover of
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` by an algebraic space over one algebraic space `𝒱` surjective, flat and locally of
finite presentation over `𝒴` makes `f` quasi-DM.

The cover is locally quasi-finite in the sense of **Stacks 06PU**, hence in the sense of
Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB by **Stacks 06UA**, which is clause (3) of **Stacks 06UE**;
that lemma's implication (3) ⟹ (1) is the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiDM B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the quasi-DM conjunct of the conclusion of (4) => (1), unconditionally. The
  local finite type and field-valued-fibre conjuncts of (4) => (1) are NOT carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange_of_isQuasiDM_of_transfers_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, (2) ⟹ (3).** If `f` is quasi-DM and transfers local quasi-finiteness to the
projections of its algebraic-space base changes, then each of those base changes has a
surjective, flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite cover by an algebraic
space which is locally quasi-finite over the base.

This is
`...AlgebraicStacks.locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange_of_isQuasiDM_of_transfers`
with its hypothesis, the substantial direction of **Stacks 06MF**, discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasQuasiDMPresentation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange_of_isQuasiDM_of_transfers_unconditional
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (htr : TransfersLocalQuasiFinitenessOnSpaceBaseChanges B S hS f) :
    LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, the local finite type conjunct of (4) ⟹ (1).** A locally quasi-finite flat
cover of `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` by an algebraic space over one algebraic space `𝒱` surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation over `𝒴` makes `f` locally of finite type.

The composite `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱` is locally quasi-finite, hence locally of finite type, and `𝒰` covers
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` by a surjective flat 1-morphism locally of finite presentation, so the projection
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒱` is locally of finite type by **Stacks 06U8**; that projection is the base change
of `f` along `𝒱 ⟶ 𝒴`, so **Stacks 06U7** descends local finite type to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f
declarations.comment: the local finite type conjunct of the conclusion of (4) => (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.discreteTopology_points_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, the field-valued-fibre conjunct of (4) ⟹ (1).** A locally quasi-finite flat
cover of `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` by an algebraic space over one algebraic space `𝒱` surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation over `𝒴` makes the fibre of `f` over *every* field-valued point of
`𝒴` have discrete space of points.

This is the source's reduction of the third condition of **Stacks 06PU** to a field-valued point
which lifts to the chart. The chart being surjective, the fibre `𝒱 ×_𝒴 Spec(k)` has a point, and a
point of an algebraic stack is an equivalence class of field-valued points, so some field
extension `k'/k` carries `v : Spec(k') ⟶ 𝒱` and `e : Spec(k') ⟶ Spec(k)` with `v ≫ g`
2-isomorphic to `e ≫ y`. Over `v` the fibre is discrete, which is
`discreteTopology_points_twoFibreProduct_of_hasLocallyQuasiFiniteFlatSpaceCoverOver`; changing the
cospan leg by that 2-isomorphism (`CategoryTheory.Bicategory.isTwoFibreProduct_reindexSnd`) and
pasting (**Stacks 02XD**) identify the fibre over `v ≫ g` with `(𝒳 ×_𝒴 Spec(k)) ×_{Spec(k)}
Spec(k')`, and that maps onto `𝒳 ×_𝒴 Spec(k)` by a base change of `e`.

`e` is surjective by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_of_fieldSpectrum`, the spectrum of a
field having exactly one point, and it is universally open because its target is the algebraic
stack of the spectrum of a field (**Stacks 06DN** through
`universallyOpen_to_fieldSpectrumStack`), so its base change is open on points by **Stacks 06U1**.
No finiteness of `k'/k` is needed: the source gets openness from flatness and local finite
presentation of a *finite* extension, and universal openness over a field spectrum gives it for
an arbitrary one.
declarations.statement:
theorem discreteTopology_points_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange B S hS f)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (toBase : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (y : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (⟨toBase⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ 𝒴) :
    @DiscreteTopology
      (Stack.points B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val.val
        (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val.property)
      (Stack.pointTopology B S hS
        (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val)
declarations.comment: the field-valued-fibre conjunct of the conclusion of (4) => (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF, (4) ⟹ (1).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` admitting
one algebraic space `𝒱` surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation over `𝒴` whose base
change `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` has a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite
cover by an algebraic space locally quasi-finite over `𝒱` is locally quasi-finite.

The three conjuncts of **Stacks 06PU** are the three preceding theorems.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_locallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UF.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are
equivalent:

1. `f` is locally quasi-finite (**Stacks 06PU**);
2. `f` is quasi-DM (**Stacks 04YW**) and for every algebraic space `𝒱` over `𝒴` every locally
   quasi-finite 1-morphism `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` out of an algebraic space has locally quasi-finite
   composite `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱`;
3. for every algebraic space `𝒱` over `𝒴` there is a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented
   and locally quasi-finite 1-morphism `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` out of an algebraic space whose composite
   `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱` is locally quasi-finite;
4. there are algebraic spaces `𝒰` and `𝒱`, a surjective, flat and locally finitely presented
   1-morphism `𝒱 ⟶ 𝒴`, and a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented and locally
   quasi-finite 1-morphism `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒱` whose composite `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱` is locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_tfae (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f,
        IsQuasiDM B S hS f ∧ TransfersLocalQuasiFinitenessOnSpaceBaseChanges B S hS f,
        LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnEverySpaceBaseChange B S hS f,
        LocallyQuasiFiniteCoverOnSomeFlatSpaceBaseChange B S hS f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_comp_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UG.** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is locally
quasi-finite and its second factor is quasi-DM, then its first factor is locally quasi-finite.

`f` is 2-isomorphic to its graph over `𝒵` followed by the second projection of the canonical
2-fibre product of the cospan `(f ≫ g, g)`. The graph is locally quasi-finite because `g` is
quasi-DM (**Stacks 050I** part (3) and **Stacks 06UA**), the projection is a base change of
`f ≫ g` and so is locally quasi-finite by **Stacks 06UB**, and **Stacks 06UD** composes the
two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_comp_of_isQuasiDM
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsQuasiDM B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UI.** Let `𝒳` be a quasi-DM algebraic stack over `S`. Then the residual gerbe of
`𝒳` at `x` exists for every `x ∈ |𝒳|`: some strictly full subcategory `P` of `𝒳` meets the
specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of **Stacks 06MT**, which by
**Stacks 06MU** is what it means for the residual gerbe at `x` to exist.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_hasQuasiDMPresentation`
— the source's proof, with **Stacks 06S1** already supplied — applied to the substantial
direction of **Stacks 06MF**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasQuasiDMPresentation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ 𝒳)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P
declarations.comment: the residual gerbe of a quasi-DM algebraic stack exists at every point of its space, in the sense of 06MU: some strictly full subcategory meets the 06MT specification IsResidualGerbeAt, i.e. is a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic substack with one point lying over x. Nothing is left open: the source's chart comes from 06MF proved outright (hasQuasiDMPresentation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiDM) and its 06S1 step from isLocallyQuasiFinite_comp_of_mono_to_field

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.EtaleSpecialization.exists_isEtale_specializes_pointsMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UK.** There is an étale morphism of algebraic spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and a
nontrivial specialization of points `x ⤳ x'` in `|X|` with `f x = f x'` in `|Y|`.

The witness is the chart `X = Spec K[y, x_n : n ∈ ℤ]` of its own quotient `Y = X/ℤ` by the
integer shift, at the tail points `x = p_1` and `x' = p_0`: the shift carries `p_0` to `p_1`,
so the two have the same image in `Y`, while `p_1 ⊂ p_0` gives the specialization.

That `Y` is an algebraic space is the algebraicity half of Stacks 02WW,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotient_unconditional`, which is a theorem.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEtale_specializes_pointsMap_eq :
    ∃ (X Y : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of K)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of K)) hS X)
      (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of K)) hS Y)
      (f : X ⟶ Y) (x x' : Space.points B (Spec (.of K)) hS X),
      Space.IsEtale B (Spec (.of K)) hS f ∧ x ≠ x' ∧ x ⤳ x' ∧
        Space.pointsMap B (Spec (.of K)) hS X f x =
          Space.pointsMap B (Spec (.of K)) hS X f x'
declarations.comment: a specialization inside a fibre of an étale morphism of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints.of_coversTop
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasEnoughPoints_of_coversTop
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06UL.** Let `C` be a site and `{U_i}_{i ∈ I}` a family of objects such that
the `U_i` cover the final object (hypothesis (1), see the module docstring) and each
localization `C/U_i` has enough points (hypothesis (2)). Then `C` has enough points.
declarations.statement:

    HasEnoughPoints.{w} J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.of_coversTop

**Stacks 06UL** for `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily`. If a family
of objects covers the final object and each localization at a member of the family has a
conservative family of points, then so does the site itself.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**The relative pullback map on `LQCoh^fbc` at the structure sheaf.**  For a factorization
`𝒬 --pr--> 𝒲 --w--> 𝒳` of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks with direct images `wStar`, `fStar`
on `LQCoh^fbc` identified by `cmp : pr_* ⋙ w_* ≅ f_*`, the relative pullback map at the
structure sheaf of `𝒲`, followed by `f_*` of the identification `pr^*𝒪_𝒲 ≅ 𝒪_𝒬` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyQuasicoherentStructureSheafPullbackIso`:

`w_*𝒪_𝒲 ⟶ f_*(pr^*𝒪_𝒲) ⟶ f_*𝒪_𝒬`.
declarations.statement:
def locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap :
    wStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒲.val.val.p 𝒲.val.property hincW).obj
        (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒲.val.val.p 𝒲.val.property)) ⟶
      fStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS
          𝒬.val.val.p 𝒬.val.property hincP).obj
        (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒬.val.val.p 𝒬.val.property))
declarations.comment: the relative pullback map w_*𝒪_𝒲 ⟶ f_*𝒪_𝒬 at the structure sheaf of the middle stack of a factorization 𝒬 ⟶ 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳 of algebraic stacks, on LQCoh^fbc, for direct images wStar, fStar and an adjunction adjPr with an identification cmp : prStar ⋙ wStar ≅ fStar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentRelativePullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**The relative pullback map in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` at the structure sheaf.**  The coherator `Q` of
**Lemma 0778** applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap`.  Its source and target are
the three-step composite `Q ∘ w_* ∘ i` of **Stacks 077A** at the structure sheaf, so this is a
map

`w_{QCoh, *}𝒪_𝒲 ⟶ f_{QCoh, *}𝒪_𝒬`

in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentRelativePullbackMap :
    (flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed hpres
          hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj
        (wStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒲.val.val.p 𝒲.val.property
          hincW).obj (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒲.val.val.p 𝒲.val.property))) ⟶
      (flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed hpres
          hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj
        (fStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒬.val.val.p 𝒬.val.property
          hincP).obj (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒬.val.val.p 𝒬.val.property)))
declarations.comment: the relative pullback map w_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒲 ⟶ f_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒬 in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), the coherator of Lemma 0778 applied to the map on LQCoh^fbc, over the same data of Proposition 0771 together with the coherator inputs hincX, hclosed, hpres, hls, hlsD, hwp, hsep of Lemma 0778

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.relativePullback
declarations.doc:
**The relative pullback map of a commutative triangle.**  For an adjunction
`f^{-1} ⊣ f_*` and direct images `g_*`, `h_*` to a third category identified by
`c : f_* ⋙ g_* ≅ h_*`, the map

`g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*f^{-1}ℱ`

is `g_*` applied to the unit `ℱ ⟶ f_*f^{-1}ℱ`, followed by `c` at `f^{-1}ℱ`.
declarations.statement: def relativePullback : gstar ⟶ finv ⋙ hstar
declarations.comment: the relative pullback map g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*f^{-1}ℱ of a commutative triangle of morphisms of topoi, stated for an adjunction f^{-1} ⊣ f_*, two direct images and an isomorphism f_* ⋙ g_* ≅ h_* in place of the source's equality of functors

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.relativePullbackMapOfHom
declarations.doc:
**The relative pullback map attached to a morphism `f^{-1}ℱ ⟶ 𝒢`.**  The pullback map
`g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*f^{-1}ℱ` followed by `h_*φ`.
declarations.statement:
def relativePullbackMapOfHom (F : 𝒞) {G : 𝒟} (φ : finv.obj F ⟶ G) :
    gstar.obj F ⟶ hstar.obj G
declarations.comment: the variant g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*𝒢 of the relative pullback map attached to a morphism f^{-1}ℱ ⟶ 𝒢

declarations.name: DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB_isTriangulated_saturated
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Stacks 06UQ, unbounded version).**
For a weak Serre subcategory `B ⊆ A`, the property `D_B(A)` is a strictly full,
saturated, triangulated subcategory of `D(A)`.

theorem derivedCategoryB_isTriangulated_saturated

      (derivedCategoryB B).IsStableUnderRetracts

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate
declarations.doc:
A module-valued functor is adequate if it is the kernel of the base changes of a map of
`A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsAdequate {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] (ι : C ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} A)
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctorOn.{w} ι) : Prop

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.IsLinearlyAdequate
declarations.doc:
A module-valued functor is linearly adequate if it is the kernel of a morphism between
the module-valued functors associated to two finite free modules.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsLinearlyAdequate {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] (ι : C ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} A)
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctorOn.{w} ι) : Prop

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isColimit_mapCocone_of_isAdequate
declarations.doc:
An adequate functor sends filtered colimits of commutative algebras to colimits of
its underlying additive groups.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isColimit_mapCocone_of_isAdequate
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (F : AdequateFunctor.ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, v} A)
    (hF : AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F)
    {I : Type i} [Category.{j} I] [IsFiltered I]
    [UnivLE.{i, max u v}] [UnivLE.{j, max u v}]
    {D : I ⥤ ((CommAlgCat.{max u v} A)ᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ}
    {c : Cocone D} (hc : IsColimit c) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (F.presheaf.mapCocone c))

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.moduleValuedFunctorBaseChangeMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
An adequate functor on a chosen algebra domain commutes with flat base change
along every morphism in that domain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleValuedFunctorBaseChangeMap_bijective {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] (ι : D ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} A)
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctorOn.{w} ι) (hF : IsAdequate ι F)
    {B C : D} (f : B ⟶ C) (hf : RingHom.Flat (ι.map f).hom.toRingHom) :
    Function.Bijective (moduleValuedFunctorBaseChangeMap ι F f)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.exists_coproduct_linearlyAdequate_surjective
declarations.doc:
An adequate functor is a pointwise quotient of a direct sum of
linearly adequate functors.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_coproduct_linearlyAdequate_surjective
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (F : AdequateFunctor.ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, v} A)
    (hF : AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F) :
    ∃ (ι : Type (max u v w))
      (L : ι → AdequateFunctor.ModuleValuedFunctor.{max u v w, v} A),
      (∀ i, AdequateFunctor.IsLinearlyAdequate (𝟭 _) (L i)) ∧
        ∃ (f : (∐ L) ⟶
          (AdequateFunctor.presheafOfModulesUliftFunctor.{max u v, w}
            (AdequateFunctor.algebraRingDiagram.{v} A)).obj F),
          ∀ X, Function.Surjective (f.app X)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.exists_jointlyEpi_isLinearlyAdequate
declarations.doc:
Every adequate module-valued functor carries a jointly epimorphic family of morphisms from
linearly adequate functors.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_jointlyEpi_isLinearlyAdequate
    (K : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1) w, v} A) (hK : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) K) :
    ∃ (J : Type (max (u + 1) (v + 1) w))
      (L : J → ModuleValuedFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1) w, v} A) (g : ∀ j, L j ⟶ K),
      (∀ j, IsLinearlyAdequate (𝟭 _) (L j)) ∧
        ∀ {Z : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1) w, v} A} (a b : K ⟶ Z),
          (∀ j, g j ≫ a = g j ≫ b) → a = b
declarations.comment: the linearly adequate functors jointly cover an adequate functor

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isSeparating_adequateOfLinearPresentation
declarations.doc:
The linearly adequate functors form a separating family for the adequate functors: by
[Stacks, Tag 06UX] every adequate functor is a pointwise quotient of a direct sum of linearly
adequate functors, and each summand is isomorphic to one of the chosen family.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isSeparating_adequateOfLinearPresentation :
    (ObjectProperty.ofObj (adequateOfLinearPresentation.{u, v, w} A)).IsSeparating
declarations.comment: the linearly adequate functors separate the adequate functors

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.Laurent.weightSpace
declarations.doc:
The weight-`k` part of `F(B)` consists of those elements whose images under the constant
and grading maps differ by multiplication by `T k`.
declarations.statement:
public def weightSpace (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctor A) (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule A B) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (k : ℤ) :
    Set (F.obj (Opposite.op (Opposite.op (CommAlgCat.of A B))))

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.Laurent.existsUnique_finsupp_weightSpace_eq
declarations.doc:
Every element of the value of a flat-base-change-compatible module-valued functor on a
graded algebra has a unique finite decomposition into elements of its integer weight spaces.
declarations.statement:
public lemma existsUnique_finsupp_weightSpace_eq (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] (F : ModuleValuedFunctor A) (hF : PreservesFlatBaseChange A F)
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule A B) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    (x : F.obj (Opposite.op (Opposite.op (CommAlgCat.of A B)))) :
    ∃! y : ℤ →₀ F.obj (Opposite.op (Opposite.op (CommAlgCat.of A B))),
      (∀ k, y k ∈ weightSpace A B F 𝒜 k) ∧ y.sum (fun _ z ↦ z) = x

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.Laurent.map_degreeZeroProjection_mem_weightSpace_zero
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism induced by projection of a graded algebra onto degree zero takes every
element of the functor's value into its weight-zero space.
declarations.statement:
public lemma map_degreeZeroProjection_mem_weightSpace_zero (A B : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (F : ModuleValuedFunctor A)
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule A B) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    (x : F.obj (Opposite.op (Opposite.op (CommAlgCat.of A B)))) :
    F.map ((CommAlgCat.ofHom (degreeZeroProjection A B 𝒜)).op.op) x ∈
      weightSpace A B F 𝒜 0

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.exists_lift_from_finite_free_kernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 06V0.** A morphism from the kernel of a morphism between finite free
module-valued functors to a module-valued functor extends to the middle finite free functor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_lift_from_finite_free_kernel
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (M : Type (max u w)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (n m : ℕ) (L : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max u v w, v} A)
    (i : L ⟶ moduleExtensionOfCarrier A (finiteFreeModule.{w} A n))
    (d : moduleExtensionOfCarrier A (finiteFreeModule.{w} A n) ⟶
      moduleExtensionOfCarrier A (finiteFreeModule.{w} A m))
    (φ : L ⟶ moduleExtensionOfCarrier A M) [Mono i] (hd : i ≫ d = 0)
    (h : (ShortComplex.mk i d hd).Exact) :
    ∃ ψ : moduleExtensionOfCarrier A (finiteFreeModule.{w} A n) ⟶
      moduleExtensionOfCarrier A M, i ≫ ψ = φ

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_cokernel_to_moduleExtension
declarations.doc:
The cokernel of a map from an adequate functor to the functor of a module
is adequate.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_cokernel_to_moduleExtension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max u v w, v} A)
    (M : ModuleCat.{w} A)
    (φ : F ⟶ moduleExtension.{w, v} A M)
    (hF : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F) : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) (cokernel φ)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_cokernel
declarations.doc: Cokernels of morphisms between adequate functors are adequate.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isAdequate_cokernel {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {F G : ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, v} A} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F) (hG : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) G) :

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_kernel
declarations.doc: The kernel of a map of adequate module-valued functors is adequate.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isAdequate_kernel {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {F G : ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, v} A} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F) (hG : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) G) :
    IsAdequate (𝟭 _) (kernel φ)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_coproduct
declarations.doc: **Stacks Lemma 06V4, direct sums.** A direct sum of adequate functors is adequate.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isAdequate_coproduct {ι : Type i} [Small.{max u v w} ι]
    (F : ι → ModuleValuedFunctor.{max u v w, v} A) [HasCoproduct F]
    (hF : ∀ a, IsAdequate (𝟭 _) (F a)) :
    IsAdequate (𝟭 _) (∐ F)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_colimit

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.Laurent.naturalTransformation_lifts_of_units_of_flatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
An additive natural transformation of module-valued functors which commutes
with multiplication by units is induced by a morphism of module-valued
functors, provided the target commutes with flat base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naturalTransformation_lifts_of_units_of_flatBaseChange
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (F G : PresheafOfModules.{v} (algebraRingFunctor A))
    (φ : F.presheaf ⟶ G.presheaf)
    (hunit : ∀ (B : ((CommAlgCat.{u} A)ᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ)
      (x : F.obj B) (a : Units ((algebraRingFunctor A).obj B)),
      φ.app B ((a : (algebraRingFunctor A).obj B) • x) =
        (a : (algebraRingFunctor A).obj B) • (φ.app B x : G.obj B))
    (hbase : ∀ {B B' : ((CommAlgCat.{u} A)ᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ} (f : B ⟶ B'),
      letI : Algebra ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B)
          ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B') :=
        ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).map f).hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Flat ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B)
          ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B') →
        ∃ e : TensorProduct ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B)
              ((algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B') (G.obj B) ≃ₗ[
                (algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B'] G.obj B',
          ∀ x : G.obj B,
            e ((1 : (algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B') ⊗ₜ[
              (algebraCommRingFunctor A).obj B] x) = G.map f x) :
    ∃ ψ : F ⟶ G,
      (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf (algebraRingFunctor A)).map ψ = φ

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_of_moduleExtension_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06V6.** Let `A` be a ring and let `0 → M → G → L → 0` be a short exact sequence of
module-valued functors on `Alg_A`, where `M` is the functor `B ↦ B ⊗[A] M` of an `A`-module `M`
and `L` is linearly adequate. Then `G` is adequate.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isAdequate_of_moduleExtension_shortExact {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (G L : ModuleValuedFunctor.{u, u} A)
    (i : moduleExtension.{u, u} A M ⟶ G) (p : G ⟶ L) (hip : i ≫ p = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk i p hip).ShortExact)
    (hL : AdequateFunctor.IsLinearlyAdequate (𝟭 _) L) :
    AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate (𝟭 _) G

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.weightOne_eq_add_images
declarations.doc:
The weight-one part over the symmetric algebra on two copies of a finitely
presented module is the sum of the images from each copy.
declarations.statement:
public lemma weightOne_eq_add_images {A M : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.FinitePresentation A M]
    (F : Laurent.ModuleValuedFunctor A) (hF : AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F)
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule A (SymmetricAlgebra A M)) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    (ℬ : ℕ → Submodule A (SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M))) [GradedAlgebra ℬ]
    (h𝒜 : ∀ m, SymmetricAlgebra.ι A M m ∈ 𝒜 1)
    (hℬ : ∀ m, SymmetricAlgebra.ι A (M × M) m ∈ ℬ 1) :
    let p₁ : SymmetricAlgebra A M →ₐ[A] SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M) :=
      SymmetricAlgebra.lift ((SymmetricAlgebra.ι A (M × M)).comp (LinearMap.inl A M M))
    let p₂ : SymmetricAlgebra A M →ₐ[A] SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M) :=
      SymmetricAlgebra.lift ((SymmetricAlgebra.ι A (M × M)).comp (LinearMap.inr A M M))
    ∀ z, z ∈ AdequateFunctor.Laurent.weightSpace A (SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M)) F ℬ 1 ↔
      ∃ x y, ∃ z₁ z₂ : F.obj (Opposite.op (Opposite.op
          (CommAlgCat.of A (SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M))))),
        x ∈ AdequateFunctor.Laurent.weightSpace A (SymmetricAlgebra A M) F 𝒜 1 ∧
        y ∈ AdequateFunctor.Laurent.weightSpace A (SymmetricAlgebra A M) F 𝒜 1 ∧
        z₁ = F.map ((CommAlgCat.ofHom p₁).op.op) x ∧
        z₂ = F.map ((CommAlgCat.ofHom p₂).op.op) y ∧ z = z₁ + z₂
declarations.comment: degree-one generation by the two factors

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.weightOne_images_disjoint
declarations.doc: The two factor images in weight one have zero intersection.
declarations.statement:
public lemma weightOne_images_disjoint {A M : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.FinitePresentation A M]
    (F : Laurent.ModuleValuedFunctor A) (hF : AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F)
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule A (SymmetricAlgebra A M)) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    (ℬ : ℕ → Submodule A (SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M))) [GradedAlgebra ℬ]
    (h𝒜 : ∀ m, SymmetricAlgebra.ι A M m ∈ 𝒜 1)
    (hℬ : ∀ m, SymmetricAlgebra.ι A (M × M) m ∈ ℬ 1) :
    let p₁ : SymmetricAlgebra A M →ₐ[A] SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M) :=
      SymmetricAlgebra.lift ((SymmetricAlgebra.ι A (M × M)).comp (LinearMap.inl A M M))
    let p₂ : SymmetricAlgebra A M →ₐ[A] SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M) :=
      SymmetricAlgebra.lift ((SymmetricAlgebra.ι A (M × M)).comp (LinearMap.inr A M M))
    ∀ x y, ∀ z₁ z₂ : F.obj (Opposite.op (Opposite.op
        (CommAlgCat.of A (SymmetricAlgebra A (M × M))))),
      x ∈ AdequateFunctor.Laurent.weightSpace A (SymmetricAlgebra A M) F 𝒜 1 →
      y ∈ AdequateFunctor.Laurent.weightSpace A (SymmetricAlgebra A M) F 𝒜 1 →
      z₁ = F.map ((CommAlgCat.ofHom p₁).op.op) x →
      z₂ = F.map ((CommAlgCat.ofHom p₂).op.op) y → z₁ + z₂ = 0 →
        x = 0 ∧ y = 0

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.exists_retraction_of_shortExact_of_baseChange_weightOne
declarations.doc:
An extension of a linearly adequate functor splits if its kernel functor
commutes with flat base change and has a direct weight-one coproduct decomposition.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_retraction_of_shortExact_of_baseChange_weightOne
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {F E L : ModuleValuedFunctor.{u, u} A}
    (i : F ⟶ E) (p : E ⟶ L) (hip : i ≫ p = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk i p hip).ShortExact)
    (hflat : Laurent.PreservesFlatBaseChange A F)
    (hweight : HasWeightOneCoproduct F)
    (hL : AdequateFunctor.IsLinearlyAdequate (𝟭 _) L) :
    ∃ r : E ⟶ F, i ≫ r = 𝟙 F
declarations.comment: splitting under flat base change and weight-one decomposition

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.exists_retraction_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06V7.** An extension of a linearly adequate functor by an adequate functor admits a
retraction onto its kernel term. An adequate functor commutes with flat base change by
Stacks 06UW, and its weight-one part decomposes by Stacks 06UZ, which are the only two
properties of the kernel the splitting uses.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_retraction_of_shortExact {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {F E L : ModuleValuedFunctor.{u, u} A}
    (i : F ⟶ E) (p : E ⟶ L) (hip : i ≫ p = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk i p hip).ShortExact)
    (hF : AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F)
    (hL : AdequateFunctor.IsLinearlyAdequate (𝟭 _) L) :
    ∃ r : E ⟶ F, i ≫ r = 𝟙 F

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_of_shortExact

An adequate functor stays adequate after restriction along a ring homomorphism,

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.adequateFunctorProductEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Adequate module-valued functors over a finite product of rings correspond to families of
adequate module-valued functors over its factors. The inverse equivalence has a componentwise
comparison natural in both the algebra and the family of factors.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def adequateFunctorProductEquivalence (n : ℕ)
    (A : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] :
    { e : (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
        (fun F : ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, v} (∀ i, A i) =>
          IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F)) ≌
        (∀ i : Fin n,
          ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
            (fun F : ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, v} (A i) =>
              IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F)) //
      ProductEquivalenceSpecification n A e }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 06VE (7) for the big `τ`-site, at every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  The comparison `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Descent,
Proposition 03DX carries a tensor product of `𝒪_S`-modules to the tensor product of their
images: `(𝓗 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓘)^a ≅ 𝓗^a ⊗_𝒪 𝓘^a` in `Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`.

This is Stacks 03EL, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorIso`, for the morphism of ringed
topoi attached to the comparison of Stacks 070U, carried across
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.pullbackModulesIsoBaseAssociatedModule`.

No hypothesis is carried, and in particular quasi-coherence is not needed: the statement holds
for arbitrary `𝒪_S`-modules.  06VE states it for `QCoh(𝒪_S)` only because that is the source
category on which its functor is an equivalence, so this is the clause with its hypothesis
dropped rather than added to.

The tensor products are `(Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).obj H`, the sheafification
of the objectwise tensor product of the underlying presheaves of modules (Stacks 05NB); that
functor's value agrees with the bifunctor of Tag 01CA by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.tensorSheafBifunctor_obj_eq`.
declarations.statement:
public def baseAssociatedModuleTensorIso (τ : SiteKind) (H I : S.Modules) :
    (baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor S.sheaf).obj H).obj I) ≅
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            (FibredSite.baseStructureSheaf B S hS τ)).obj
          ((baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj H)).obj
        ((baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj I)
declarations.comment: part (7), big site (Sch/S)_τ at every τ, for arbitrary 𝒪_S-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.essImage_X₂_of_shortExact_big
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (10) on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ`, at every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}` and with no hypothesis.**  Given a short exact
sequence `0 → 𝓕₁ᵃ → 𝓔 → 𝓕₂ᵃ → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_τ` whose outer terms are
quasi-coherent — which at every `τ` is the same as their being `𝓕ᵃ`'s, by Descent,
Proposition 03DX (1) — the middle term `𝓔` is itself in the essential image of
`𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ : QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, namely of `𝓔|_{S_Zar}`.

The source's three steps are
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/BaseExtensionClosure.lean`; of the two
hypotheses they carry, essential surjectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseQuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule` and right
exactness of restriction to `S_Zar` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.epi_baseRestrictModule_map_all`.

This is the clause for the *pullback*-defined `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` of Remark 03FH;
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.exists_isoSections_X₂_of_shortExact_big` is it for the
sections-defined `𝓕ᵃ` of Definition 03DU (3), which is the sheaf the source constructs.
declarations.comment: part (10), big site (Sch/S)_τ at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, for the PULLBACK-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Remark 03FH. The same clause for the sections-defined 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (3) is exists_isoSections_X₂_of_shortExact_big; the two sheaves are identified by baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections, Stacks 070S (1). The clause read as "the middle term is quasi-coherent", which names no functor, is clause (4) of Stacks 0GNC and sits on isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₂_all

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.exists_isoSections_X₂_of_shortExact_big
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (10) on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ` at every `τ`, for the sheaf the source
constructs.**  Given a short exact sequence `0 → 𝓕₁ᵃ → 𝓔 → 𝓕₂ᵃ → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on
`(Sch/S)_τ` whose outer terms are quasi-coherent, there is a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` with
`𝓔 ≅ 𝓕ᵃ`, where `𝓕ᵃ` is the **sections**-defined associated module of Stacks Definition 03DU (3)
— the `τ`-sheafification of `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.essImage_X₂_of_shortExact_big` is the same clause for the
pullback-defined `𝓕ᵃ` of Remark 03FH; this is it read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections`, Stacks 070S (1).  The witness is
`𝓕 = 𝓔|_{S_Zar}`, quasi-coherent by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherent_baseRestrictModule_X₂`, and the isomorphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sectionsIso_X₂_of_shortExact_big`.
declarations.comment: part (10), big site (Sch/S)_τ at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, for the SECTIONS-defined 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (3) — the τ-sheafification of (f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f^*𝓕). The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is essImage_X₂_of_shortExact_big; the two sheaves are identified by baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections, Stacks 070S (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN7 for the big site, and clause (1) of Stacks 06VE for it.**  For every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}` the functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU, from
the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪`-modules on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ`, is fully
faithful.

The two tags assert one thing of one functor, and the clause strings record the scope this
declaration proves — on **one source line**, because a tag registry that reads the attributes
matches a second `stacks` clause only when it is on the same line as the first, and two clause
strings plus the attribute syntax do not fit in a hundred characters unless both are short.  The
0GN7 string therefore no longer ends `; small site S_τ untreated`: that is information about
*where else the tag is registered*, not about the scope proved, and
`big site (Sch/S)_τ, every τ` already states the scope exactly.  The other registrations are
named in the last paragraph below.

06VE's first functor is `QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, whose target is
`Mod` — which is the target below on the nose, `SheafOfModules` over the structure sheaf of
`(Sch/S)_τ` — so clause (1) of 06VE needs no reading through a subcategory.  0GN7 spells the
same functor with target `QCoh((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, and that too is the same statement: full
faithfulness of a functor into a category is full faithfulness into any full subcategory
containing its image, and the image does land in `QCoh` by Stacks 03DV (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`.

What is **not** claimed by either tag here is the source's second functor,
`QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)` into the *small* site of `S` for `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}` — a different
construction, Definition 03DU (4).  It is claimed elsewhere, and 0GN7 quantifies over nothing
beyond these: Definition 03DU gives a small site only at `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}`, so this
declaration together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiRealFullyFaithful.lean`)
and `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh'`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallEtaleLocalBijectivity.lean`) is
every functor the lemma speaks of.  At `τ = Zariski` the *sections*-defined form of the functor
carries the tag too, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedSheafFunctor`.

(The small étale functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallEtaleRingedSite.lean`, and its full
faithfulness rests on `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.unitIsoOnQuasicoherent` of
`SmallEtaleLocalBijectivity.lean`, which proves
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.UnitIsoOnQuasicoherent` with no hypothesis.)
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh (τ : SiteKind) :
    (baseAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS τ).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleNotExact.not_mono_map_two_nsmul_qcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (6), the witness.**  For `S = Spec(ℤ)`, every big fppf site containing it and
every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, the monomorphism `2 : 𝒪_S → 𝒪_S` of
`QCoh(𝒪_S)` is carried by `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` to a morphism of `Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)` that is **not** a
monomorphism.

This is the example the source gives: `2 : 𝔽₂ → 𝔽₂` is not injective and `Spec(𝔽₂)` is an object
of `(Sch/S)_τ`.  Paired with
`AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleNotExact.mono_two_nsmul_unitQcoh`, which says the source
morphism *is* a monomorphism, it is the whole of clause (6).
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_mono_map_two_nsmul_qcoh :
    ¬ Mono ((associatedModuleQcoh B τ).map (2 • 𝟙 unitQcoh.{u}))
declarations.comment: part (6), the witness: at S = Spec(ℤ), on every big site and at every τ, the monomorphism 2 : 𝒪_S → 𝒪_S of QCoh(𝒪_S) has non-monomorphic image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleNotExact.not_preservesMonomorphisms_baseAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06VE (6), as the failure to preserve monomorphisms.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_preservesMonomorphisms_baseAssociatedModuleQcoh :
    ¬ (associatedModuleQcoh B τ).PreservesMonomorphisms
declarations.comment: part (6), as the failure to preserve monomorphisms, at S = Spec(ℤ) on every big site and at every τ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleNotExact.not_preservesFiniteLimits_baseAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (6).**  The functor `QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, is **not**
exact in general: at `S = Spec(ℤ)` it does not preserve finite limits, on every big fppf site
and at every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.

By clause (4) the functor is always right exact, so this is exactly the failure of exactness the
source asserts.  A functor preserving finite limits preserves pullbacks, hence monomorphisms,
which `not_preservesMonomorphisms_baseAssociatedModuleQcoh` of this namespace rules out.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_preservesFiniteLimits_baseAssociatedModuleQcoh :
    ¬ Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits (associatedModuleQcoh B τ)
declarations.comment: part (6): the functor QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) is not left exact, at S = Spec(ℤ), on every big site and at every τ; with part (4) this is the failure of exactness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleSheafHomNotCommute.exists_isQuasicoherent_not_iso_sheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (9).**  Given two quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules `𝓕`, `𝓖` one does **not** have
`(SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, 𝓖))^a = SheafHom_𝒪(𝓕^a, 𝓖^a)` in `Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)` in general: at
`S = Spec(ℤ)`, on every big fppf site containing it and at every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, the two are not isomorphic, for
`𝓕 = Coker(2 : 𝒪_S → 𝒪_S)` and `𝓖 = 𝒪_S`.

This is the example the source gives, and the two halves are the two named statements of this
file: the left-hand side is a zero object
(`AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleSheafHomNotCommute.isZero_associatedModule_sheafHomModules`)
and the right-hand side is not
(`…not_isZero_internalHomSheaf`), the latter for the very reason clause (6) fails —
`Spec(𝔽₂)` is an object of `(Sch/S)_τ`.

`𝓕` is asserted to be **of finite presentation**, which is the source's "even if `𝓕` is of
finite presentation": the failure is not repaired by the hypothesis under which clause (8) holds
on the small sites.  It holds by construction, `𝓕` being the cokernel of a map
`𝒪_S → 𝒪_S` (Stacks 0H96, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFinitePresentation_cokernel`).  See the
implementation notes for why the conjunct is needed and not merely true.

All three modules in play — `𝓕`, `𝓖` and `SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, 𝓖)` — are asserted to be
quasi-coherent, so both sides of the clause are values of the functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)` the clause is about and not of some extension of it to all
`𝒪_S`-modules; that functor is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleNotExact.associatedModuleQcoh`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedModuleSheafHomNotCommute.associatedModuleQcoh_obj` says it agrees
with the `associatedModule` written here on every quasi-coherent module, on the nose.

The universe lift is the canonical fully faithful `Stacks.SheafOfModules.moduleULift`: the
internal Hom of Stacks 03EM on the big site raises the module universe by construction, so the
two sides of the clause are objects of two different categories.  See the implementation notes
of this file; the zero/nonzero dichotomy above is universe-free and is the real content.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isQuasicoherent_not_iso_sheafHom :
    ∃ F G : specInt.{u}.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      F.IsFinitePresentation ∧ (sheafHomModules F G).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ¬ Nonempty ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.moduleULift.{u + 1, u}
            (bigStructureSheaf B τ)).obj
            ((associatedModule B τ).obj (sheafHomModules F G)) ≅
          RingedSite.internalHomSheaf
            (BigFppfOver.baseRingedSite B specInt.{u} (contains_specInt B) τ)
            ((associatedModule B τ).obj F) ((associatedModule B τ).obj G))
declarations.comment: part (9): the sheaf Hom does NOT commute with 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ on the big site, at S = Spec ℤ, and not even when 𝓕 is of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleTensorBifunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (7) at `τ = étale`.**  The functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` into the `𝒪`-modules of the small
étale site of `S` carries the tensor product of two `𝒪_S`-modules to the tensor product of their
images:

`(𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓖)^a ≅ 𝓕^a ⊗_𝒪 𝓖^a`,

naturally in the pair `(𝓕, 𝓖)`, with no hypothesis on `𝓕` or `𝓖`.

This is Modules on Sites, Lemma 03EL — `Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorIso` — for the
morphism of ringed topoi underlying `ε : (S_étale, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` of Stacks 070R and 08H7,
conjugated on both sides by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.pullbackModulesToZariskiIso`.  Its
component at a pair is the objectwise form in which the source states the clause,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleTensorIso`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleTensorBifunctorIso_app`.

With `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleTensorIsoOfComparison` at `τ = Zariski` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleTensorIso` on the big sites, clause (7) is
covered at every functor the lemma quantifies over.
declarations.comment: part (7), small site at τ = étale, for all 𝒪_S-modules; bifunctor form, whose components are the objectwise form in which the source states the clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh'
declarations.doc:
**The small étale half of Stacks 0GN7 and of Stacks 06VE (1), with no hypothesis at all**:
the functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = étale`, from the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪`-modules on `S_étale`, is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh' :
    (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: part (1), small site at τ = étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.essImage_X₂_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (10) at `τ = étale`.**  Given a short exact sequence
`0 → 𝓕₁^a → 𝓔 → 𝓕₂^a → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of `S` — the outer terms being
given as quasi-coherent, which at `τ = étale` is the same as being in the essential image, by
Stacks 03DX (2) — the middle term `𝓔` is in the essential image of
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_étale, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, namely of `𝓔|_{S_Zar}`.

The source's three steps are
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Descent.AssociatedModule.SmallEtaleExtensionReduction`; the one
they carried, right exactness of `ε_*`, is `epi_restrictModule_map` above.
declarations.comment: part (10), small site at τ = étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleInternalHomSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (8) at `τ = étale`.**  For `𝒪_S`-modules `𝓕`, `𝓖` on a scheme `S` with `𝓖`
quasi-coherent and `𝓕` of finite presentation — Stacks 03DL (7) on the site of opens of `S` —

`(SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, 𝓖))^a ≅ SheafHom_𝒪(𝓕^a, 𝓖^a)` in `Mod(S_étale, 𝒪)`,

where `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is the functor of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = étale` in its pullback description
of Remark 03FH, `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, and the internal Hom on the
right is Tag 03EM's on the small étale site.

The proof is the one the module docstring describes: the mate of clause (7),
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.restrictModuleInternalHomIso`, computes the Zariski restriction of
the right-hand side as `SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, ε_* 𝓖^a)`; the unit of the associated-module
adjunction is an isomorphism at the quasi-coherent `𝓖`, Stacks 0GN7, so that restriction is
`SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, 𝓖)`; and the counit is an isomorphism at the right-hand side because that
internal Hom is quasi-coherent, which is clause (6) of Stacks 0GNB and is where the finite
presentation of `𝓕` is spent, through Stacks 03DO for the clause 03DL (7),
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFinitePresentationOnSite_associatedModule`.

Quasi-coherence of `𝓕` is not needed.
declarations.statement:
def associatedModuleInternalHomSheafIso (𝓕 𝓖 : S.Modules)
    (h𝓖 : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent 𝓖)
    (h𝓕 : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite 𝓕) :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.InternalHomModules.sheafHomModules 𝓕 𝓖) ≅
      internalHomSheaf B S hS ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕)
        ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓖)
declarations.comment: part (8), small site at τ = étale, for the pullback-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Remark 03FH and Tag 03EM's internal Hom on S_étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleInternalHomSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (8) at `τ = Zariski`.**  For `𝒪_S`-modules `𝓕` and `𝓖` on a scheme `S`,

`(SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, 𝓖))^a ≅ SheafHom_𝒪(𝓕^a, 𝓖^a)` in `Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`,

where `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is the functor of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` in its pullback
description of Remark 03FH, `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModule`, and the internal
Hom on the right is Tag 03EM's on the small Zariski site of schemes over `S`.

The proof is the source's: the mate of clause (7),
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.restrictModuleInternalHomIso`, computes the restriction of the
right-hand side as `SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, ε_* 𝓖^a)`; the unit of the associated-module adjunction
identifies `ε_* 𝓖^a` with `𝓖`, so that restriction is the left-hand side's source; and the
counit identifies the right-hand side with the associated module of its own restriction.  Both
unit and counit are isomorphisms because `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is an equivalence at `τ = Zariski`,
Stacks 03FG — which is the content of the source's one-sentence argument, and the only thing
clause (8) needs at this topology.

Neither quasi-coherence nor finite presentation of `𝓕` is assumed: they are what the clause
needs at `τ = étale`, where they buy the two isomorphisms that come for free here.
declarations.statement:
def associatedModuleInternalHomSheafIso (𝓕 𝓖 : S.Modules) :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.InternalHomModules.sheafHomModules 𝓕 𝓖) ≅
      RingedSite.internalHomSheafSmall.{u} (smallZariskiRingedSite B S hS)
        ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓕) ((associatedModule B S hS).obj 𝓖)
declarations.comment: part (8), small site at τ = Zariski, for the pullback-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Remark 03FH and Tag 03EM's internal Hom on S_Zar, for all 𝒪_S-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (2) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`.**  The functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4), commutes with direct sums: a
direct sum is a colimit over a discrete index category, so this is the discrete case of
clause (3).

Definition 03DU gives a small site only for `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}`, so with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedModuleQcoh` (the small
site at `τ = étale`) and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_baseAssociatedModuleQcoh` (the
big site, every `τ`) this completes the covering set of the clause.
declarations.comment: part (2), small site at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfSize_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (3) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`.**  The functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4), commutes with all colimits
indexed at the size of the scheme.

Scope as on `preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison`.
declarations.comment: part (3), small site at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesFiniteColimits_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (4) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`.**  The functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4), is right exact, i.e. commutes
with finite colimits.

As on the big site this is not read off clause (3) but assembled from the two factors, the
inclusion of the quasi-coherent modules being right exact because they are a weak Serre
subcategory.
declarations.comment: part (4), small site at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.essImage_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (10) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`.**  Given a short exact sequence
`0 → 𝓕₁^a → 𝓔 → 𝓕₂^a → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on the small Zariski site of `S`, with `𝓕₁` and `𝓕₂`
quasi-coherent on `S`, the module `𝓔` is itself in the essential image of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`.

Restriction along the morphism of ringed sites of Remark 03FH is an equivalence at `τ = Zariski`
(Stacks 03FG), hence exact, so it carries the sequence to a short exact sequence of
`𝒪_S`-modules; by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.essImage_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison_iff`
its outer terms are quasi-coherent, so its middle term is too, quasi-coherent modules on a scheme
being closed under extensions (Schemes, Section 01LA).  The same lemma turns that back into
membership of the essential image.

The clause at `τ = étale` and on the big sites is a different statement and is not implied by
this one; see the implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem essImage_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison
    {C : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS))} (hC : C.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).essImage C.X₁)
    (h₃ : (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).essImage C.X₃) :
    (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).essImage C.X₂
declarations.comment: part (10), small site at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (10) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, in the form the source states it**:
given a short exact sequence `0 → 𝓕₁ → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₃ → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on the small Zariski site of
`S` whose outer terms are quasi-coherent, the middle term is quasi-coherent.

The source states clause (10) as "`𝓔` is quasi-coherent, i.e. `𝓔` is in the essential image of
the functor"; this is the first reading and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.essImage_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison` is the second.  The two
agree by Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = Zariski`,
`essImage_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite`. It is also the third case
of Stacks 0GNB (4) and 0GNC (4) at this site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison
    {C : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS))} (hC : C.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : C.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (h₃ : C.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    C.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (10), small site at τ = Zariski, as quasi-coherence on the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN7 for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, and clause (1) of Stacks 06VE for it.**
The functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` — the pullback of sheaves of
modules along the morphism of ringed sites `(S_Zar, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` of Remark 03FH, with the
coefficient sheaf `T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` of Definition 03DU (2) — from the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪`-modules on the small Zariski site, is fully faithful.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh` (the big
site, every `τ`) and `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh'` (the
small site at `τ = étale`) this completes the covering set of 0GN7: Definition 03DU gives a small
site only for `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}`, so those three statements are every functor the lemma
quantifies over.

0GN7 spells the target `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` where this is `Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, and that is the same
statement for the same reason as at `τ = étale` and on the big site: full faithfulness of a
functor into a category is full faithfulness into any full subcategory containing its image, and
the image lands in `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` by Stacks 03DV (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`;
the corestriction itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcohOnSite` below.  06VE's second
functor has target `Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)`, which is the target here with nothing to read through.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh :
    (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: part (1), small site at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VE] (2) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source
defines.**  The sections-defined `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4), as a functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, commutes with direct sums.

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison`
is the same clause for the pullback-defined functor of [Stacks, Remark 03FH]; this is it read
through `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor`.  06VE's
second functor has target `Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)`, which is the target here on the nose.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedSheafFunctor (I : Type u) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (2), small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor. The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison; the two functors are identified by associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfSize_associatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VE] (3) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source
defines.**  The sections-defined `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` commutes with all colimits indexed at the size of the
scheme.

Scope and route as on
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedSheafFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesColimitsOfSize_associatedSheafFunctor :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (3), small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor. The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is preservesColimitsOfSize_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison; the two functors are identified by associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesFiniteColimits_associatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VE] (4) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source
defines.**  The sections-defined `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` is right exact, i.e. commutes with finite colimits.

Scope and route as on
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_associatedSheafFunctor`; see the
implementation notes of this module for why this is not read off clause (3).
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesFiniteColimits_associatedSheafFunctor :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (4), small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor. The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is preservesFiniteColimits_associatedModuleQcohOfComparison; the two functors are identified by associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.essImage_X₂_of_shortExact_associatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VE] (10) for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source
defines.**  Given a short exact sequence `0 → 𝓕₁ᵃ → 𝓔 → 𝓕₂ᵃ → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on the small
Zariski site of `S`, with `𝓕₁` and `𝓕₂` quasi-coherent on `S` and `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` the sections-defined
functor of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4), the module `𝓔` is itself in the essential image of that
functor.

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.essImage_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison` is the same clause for the
pullback-defined functor of [Stacks, Remark 03FH]; the two functors have the same essential image
by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.essImage_associatedSheafFunctor_iff`, and all three hypotheses
and the conclusion read across it.

The clause in the form the source states it — "`𝓔` is quasi-coherent" — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison`, whose
statement names no functor and so needs no sections-defined counterpart.
declarations.statement:
public theorem essImage_X₂_of_shortExact_associatedSheafFunctor
    {C : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS))} (hC : C.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS).essImage C.X₁)
    (h₃ : (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS).essImage C.X₃) :
    (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS).essImage C.X₂
declarations.comment: part (10), small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor. The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is essImage_X₂_of_shortExactOfComparison; the two functors have the same essential image by essImage_associatedSheafFunctor_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GN7] for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source
defines**: the assignment `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) — the sheaf of `𝒪`-modules on
`S_Zar` whose sections over `f : T → S` are `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor` — is fully faithful on the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules.

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh` is the same statement for the
*pullback*-defined functor of [Stacks, Remark 03FH]; this is it read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor`, which identifies
the two.  Both are 0GN7 at `τ = Zariski`, and the source's own statement is about the sections
description, so the clause is only about the object the source names once this form exists.

0GN7 spells the target `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` where this is `Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`; that is the same
statement for the reason recorded on
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh`, full faithfulness into a
category being full faithfulness into any full subcategory containing the image, and the image
landing in `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` by [Stacks, Tag 03DV] (2).

**This is also clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 06VE] at `τ = Zariski` for the sections-defined
functor**, that clause being the same assertion of full faithfulness; its second functor has
target `Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)`, which is the target here with nothing to read through.  The two attributes
sit together for the same reason they do on
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh` for the pullback-defined
functor.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulAssociatedSheafFunctor :
    (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: part (1), small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor, whose target Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪) is the target 06VE spells for its second functor. The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh

The source's second functor, `QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)` into a **small** site of `S`, is a

**Stacks 06VE (4) for the second functor of the lemma.**  The functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_étale, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, is right exact: the inclusion of the quasi-coherent
modules is right exact, quasi-coherence on a scheme being a weak Serre class, and `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is

**The half of Stacks 06VE (5) that is special to the small étale site.**  The functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Mod(S_étale, 𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, is left exact.

The inclusion of the quasi-coherent modules is left exact because quasi-coherence on a scheme is
a weak Serre class, and `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is left exact because `ε : (S_étale, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` is
flat — an étale morphism is flat, Morphisms, Lemma 02GS, which is Stacks 0GNA for `ε` and gives
the exactness assertion of Stacks 08H8.

    PreservesFiniteLimits (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS)
