declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleTensorIsoOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (7) at `τ = Zariski`.**  The functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` into the `𝒪`-modules of the
small Zariski site of `S` carries the tensor product of two `𝒪_S`-modules to the tensor product
of their images:

`(𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓖)^a ≅ 𝓕^a ⊗_𝒪 𝓖^a`,

naturally in the pair `(𝓕, 𝓖)`.

This is Modules on Sites, Lemma 03EL — `Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorIso` — for the
morphism of ringed topoi underlying `id_{small, Zar, Zar}` of Remark 03FH, conjugated on both
sides by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.pullbackModulesIsoAssociatedModule`.

The functor is the pullback description of Stacks 03DU (4); the clause for the sections
description, which is the one 03DU (4) gives, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSectionsTensorObjIso`.  With
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleTensorBifunctorIso` (small site at `τ = étale`) and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleTensorIso` (big site, every `τ`) this
completes clause (7) at every functor the lemma quantifies over.
declarations.comment: part (7), small site at τ = Zariski, for the PULLBACK-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Remark 03FH, for all 𝒪_S-modules; bifunctor form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleTensorObjIsoOfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (7) at `τ = Zariski`, objectwise** — the form in which the source states it:
`(𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓖)^a = 𝓕^a ⊗_𝒪 𝓖^a`, for the pullback description of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleTensorObjIsoOfComparison (F G : S.Modules) :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj
        ((Functor.uncurry.obj
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} S.sheaf)).obj (F, G)) ≅
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
          (smallZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O)).obj
        ((associatedModule B S hS).obj F, (associatedModule B S hS).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (7), small site at τ = Zariski, for the PULLBACK-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Remark 03FH, for all 𝒪_S-modules; objectwise form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSectionsTensorObjIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VE (7) at `τ = Zariski`, for the sections-defined `𝓕^a` of Stacks 03DU (4).**
For quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules `𝓕`, `𝓖`,

`(𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓖)^a ≅ 𝓕^a ⊗_𝒪 𝓖^a`,

where `𝓕^a` is the sheaf on `S_Zar` whose sections over `f : T → S` are `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleTensorObjIsoOfComparison` read through
Remark 03FH (1), `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoOfSections`, at the three
modules involved.  It is the description Stacks 03DU (4) gives, and so the description every
statement of this tag is about.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleOfSectionsTensorObjIso (F G : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    associatedModuleOfSections B S hS
        ((Functor.uncurry.obj
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} S.sheaf)).obj (F, G)) ≅
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
          (smallZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O)).obj
        (associatedModuleOfSections B S hS F, associatedModuleOfSections B S hS G)
declarations.comment: part (7), small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4), for quasi-coherent 𝒪_S-modules

registrations.comment:
Section 46.5: a sheaf of 𝒪-modules on (Sch/S)_τ is adequate when its
affine-section functors are adequate over the members of a τ-covering of S by affines

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.IsAdequate
declarations.doc: Adequacy of a sheaf of modules on the selected big site.

    {τ : CoveringTopology} {S : Scheme.{u}} (B : BigSite τ S)

declarations.doc: Adequacy descends through an exact Čech equalizer.

    [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] (f : A →+* A')
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, u} A)
    (F' : ModuleValuedFunctor.{w, u} A')

      (F' ≅ (PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀ (restrictScalars f).op
        (algebraRingDiagram A)).obj F))

    IsAdequate (𝟭 _) F

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_affineSectionFunctor
declarations.doc:
[Stacks, Tag 06VI]: for an adequate sheaf of modules `F` on the big `τ`-site over `S`, the
affine-section functor `F_{F, A}` is adequate for *every* affine scheme `Spec A` of the site
over `S`, not only for the members of the covering witnessing adequacy of `F`.

All three steps of the source's proof are supplied by the library:
`Stacks.Adequate.standardAffineRefinement` and `Stacks.Adequate.affineSectionRestriction`, which
discharge `StandardAffineRefinement` and `AffineSectionRestriction`, and
`Stacks.Adequate.standardAffineDescent`, which discharges `StandardAffineDescent`. See the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_affineSectionFunctor
    {τ : CoveringTopology} {S : Scheme.{u}} (B : BigSite τ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B.structureSheaf)
    (hF : IsAdequate B F)
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : Spec A ⟶ S)
    (hA : schemeSizeBelow B.cutoff (Spec A)) :
    AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate
      (AdequateFunctor.siteAlgebraInclusion A (schemeSizeBelow B.cutoff))
      (affineSectionFunctor B F A f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_pullbackSheafOfAmbient
declarations.doc:
[Stacks, Tag 06VJ]: the pullback `f^*𝓕` of an adequate `𝒪`-module `𝓕` on `(Sch/S)_τ` is an
adequate `𝒪`-module on `(Sch/T)_τ`, where `(Sch/S)_τ` and `(Sch/T)_τ` are the localizations at
`S` and at `T` of one ambient big `τ`-site, as they are in the source.

The pullback is the restriction of `𝓕` along the index functor, which is a sheaf by
`isSheaf_pullbackVal`; its affine-section functor at an affine `Spec A` over `T` is the
affine-section functor of `𝓕` at `Spec A` over `S` by `affineSectionFunctor_pullbackSheaf`,
which [Stacks, Tag 06VI] shows to be adequate; and adequacy of `f^*𝓕` follows because the
affine open cover of `T` is a `τ`-covering by affine schemes of the site.

By `BigSite.exists_eq_ofAmbient` every chosen big site is a localization of an ambient big
site, so no generality is lost in stating the lemma this way.

Nothing is assumed beyond adequacy of `𝓕`: Tag 06VI is itself unconditional, so the appeal to
it in the source's proof carries no hypothesis here either. See the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_pullbackSheafOfAmbient (f : T ⟶ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u m} (BigSite.ofAmbient 𝒮 S hS).structureSheaf)
    (hF : IsAdequate (BigSite.ofAmbient 𝒮 S hS) F) :
    IsAdequate (BigSite.ofAmbient 𝒮 T hT) (pullbackSheafOfAmbient 𝒮 hS hT f F)
declarations.comment:
the pullback of an adequate 𝒪-module along a morphism of schemes is adequate,
for the two sites the localizations of one ambient big site, as they are in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_tfae

public theorem isAdequate_tfae (F : SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :

      HasAffineOpenAssociatedKernelCover B F,

      HasAdequatePullbackCover B F,
      HasAssociatedKernelOnEveryAffine B F].TFAE
declarations.comment:
the whole tag as one statement: all five conditions on an 𝒪-module on the big
τ-site over a scheme are equivalent, listed in the source's order and with no hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.cechExact_and_isSheaf_of_isAdequate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VL], the whole statement.**

Let `F` be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big `τ`-site over `S`. Then:

1. for every surjective flat morphism `f : Spec B ⟶ Spec A` between affine objects of the site,
   the extended Čech complex
   `0 → F(Spec A) → F(Spec B) → F(Spec (B ⊗_A B)) → ⋯`
   is exact — at its two left-hand spots, which is the sheaf condition for the one-member
   presieve `{f}`, and at every remaining spot, which is the vanishing of the Čech cohomology of
   `{f}` in every positive degree;
2. `F` satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc covering families of the site; and
3. `F` is a sheaf of `𝒪`-modules for the fppf covering families of the site, that is, its
   underlying presheaf of abelian groups satisfies the fppf sheaf condition; and
4. equivalently, read as a statement about the object rather than about the sheaf axiom, there
   is a sheaf of `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf` — a term of `CategoryTheory.SheafOfModules` over
   `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.fppfStructureSheaf`, the structure sheaf of rings of the site read
   at the fppf topology by [Stacks, Tag 03OJ] — whose underlying presheaf of `𝒪`-modules is
   that of `F`.

Clause (1) is the body of the tag and clauses (2) and (3) are its two "in particular"s, clause
(4) being clause (3) repackaged.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cechExact_and_isSheaf_of_isAdequate
    {τ : CoveringTopology} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (B : BigSite τ S) (F : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B.structureSheaf)
    (hF : IsAdequate B F) :
    letI : HasFiniteLimits B.category := B.hasFiniteLimits_category
    (∀ (X Y : B.category) (f : Y ⟶ X), X ∈ B.affineObjects → Y ∈ B.affineObjects →
        Flat (B.toOver.map f).left → Surjective (B.toOver.map f).left →
          Presieve.IsSheafFor (F.val.presheaf ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{max u m})
              (Presieve.singleton f) ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
              IsZero (Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{0} f)
                F.val.presheaf n)) ∧
      Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcPrecoverageOn B).toGrothendieck F.val.presheaf ∧
      Presheaf.IsSheaf (fppfPrecoverageOn B).toGrothendieck F.val.presheaf ∧
      ∃ G : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B.fppfStructureSheaf, G.val = F.val
declarations.comment:
the whole statement: for an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big `τ`-site over `S`,
the extended Čech complex `0 → F(Spec A) → F(Spec B) → F(Spec (B ⊗_A B)) → ⋯` of every surjective
flat morphism of affines of the site is exact at every spot -- at the two left-hand spots as the
sheaf condition for the one-member presieve, at the rest as the vanishing of the Čech cohomology
in positive degrees -- and the two `in particular` conclusions, the fpqc sheaf condition and
being a sheaf of `𝒪`-modules for the fppf coverings, the latter both as the sheaf axiom for the
fppf topology and as a term of the category of `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isZero_rightDerived_sections_of_isAdequate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (3).** Let `𝓕` be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big `τ`-site
`(Sch/S)_τ` over a scheme `S`. For every affine scheme `U` over `S` belonging to the site,
`H^q(U, 𝓕) = 0` for all `q > 0`, where `H^q(U, −)` is the `q`-th right derived functor of
sections over `U` on abelian sheaves on the site, applied to the abelian sheaf underlying `𝓕`.

This is [Stacks, Tag 03F9] at the collection of affine objects of the site and the collection
of finite affine `τ`-coverings of those objects: the objects occurring in such a covering are
affine by `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isAffine_product_of_mem_affineCov`, the coverings are
cofinal by `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.affineCovCofinal`, and the Čech cohomology of an adequate
module vanishes on them by `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.cechCohomology_isZero_of_isAdequate`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem BigSite.isZero_rightDerived_sections_of_isAdequate (B : BigSite τ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B.structureSheaf) (hF : IsAdequate B F)
    (U : B.category) [IsAffine U.left.obj] (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero ((((sheafSections B.topology AddCommGrpCat.{max u m}).obj (op U)).rightDerived q).obj
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf B.structureSheaf).obj F))
declarations.comment:
(3): for an adequate 𝒪-module F on (Sch/S)_τ and every affine scheme U over S,
H^q(U, F) = 0 for all q > 0; cohomology is the right derived functor of sections over U of the
abelian sheaf underlying F

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.adequateCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (4).** For an adequate `𝒪`-module `𝓕` on a chosen big `τ`-site
`(Sch/S)_τ` over a scheme `S`, the canonical isomorphism

`H^q(S, 𝓕|_{S_Zar}) ≅ H^q((Sch/S)_τ, 𝓕)`

in every degree `q`, where `𝓕|_{S_Zar}` is `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.zariskiRestrictModule` and
cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections of the underlying abelian sheaves.
It is the Grothendieck edge isomorphism of the composite `Γ(S_Zar, −) ∘ (−)|_{S_Zar} = Γ`, the
higher direct images of `𝓕` vanishing by
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.higherZariskiRestrictionVanishing`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def BigSite.adequateCohomologyIso (F : SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf)
    (hF : IsAdequate B F) (q : ℕ) :
    ((zariskiGlobalSections S).rightDerived q).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf S.ringCatSheaf).obj (B.zariskiRestrictModule.obj F)) ≅
      (B.globalSections.rightDerived q).obj ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf B.structureSheaf).obj F)
declarations.comment:
(4): for an adequate 𝒪-module F on (Sch/S)_τ, the canonical isomorphism
H^q(S, F|_{S_Zar}) = H^q((Sch/S)_τ, F) in every degree q, cohomology being the right derived
functor of global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isIso_etaleRestrictionComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (2).** Let `𝓕` be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big `τ`-site
`(Sch/S)_τ` over a scheme `S`. The restriction `𝓕|_{S_étale}` of `𝓕` to the small étale site of
`S` is the quasi-coherent module associated to `𝓕|_{S_Zar}`: the canonical comparison
`(𝓕|_{S_Zar})^a ⟶ 𝓕|_{S_étale}` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem BigSite.isIso_etaleRestrictionComparison
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) (hF : IsAdequate B F) :
    IsIso (B.etaleRestrictionComparison E hSE hle F hF)
declarations.comment:
(2), for the small étale site of any big étale site whose schemes are schemes of
(Sch/S)_τ: the restriction F|_{S_étale} of an adequate 𝒪-module F is the quasi-coherent module
associated to F|_{S_Zar}, the canonical map (F|_{S_Zar})^a → F|_{S_étale} being an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isIso_etaleSiteRestrictionComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (2) for the small étale site `S_étale` of `(Sch/S)_τ` itself.** Let `𝓕`
be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big `τ`-site `(Sch/S)_τ`, for any of the five
topologies, and let `S_étale` be the small étale site of `S` in the same category of schemes,
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.etaleSite`. The restriction `𝓕|_{S_étale}` is the quasi-coherent module
associated to `𝓕|_{S_Zar}`: the canonical comparison `(𝓕|_{S_Zar})^a ⟶ 𝓕|_{S_étale}` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem BigSite.isIso_etaleSiteRestrictionComparison
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) (hF : IsAdequate B F) :
    IsIso (B.etaleRestrictionComparison B.etaleSite B.contains_etaleSite B.etaleSite_cutoff.le
      F hF)
declarations.comment:
(2): for an adequate 𝒪-module F on (Sch/S)_τ the restriction F|_{S_étale} to the
small étale site of S is the quasi-coherent module associated to F|_{S_Zar}, the canonical map
(F|_{S_Zar})^a → F|_{S_étale} being an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isQuasicoherent_zariskiRestrictModule
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (1).** Let `𝓕` be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big `τ`-site
`(Sch/S)_τ` over a scheme `S`. The restriction `𝓕|_{S_Zar}` of `𝓕` to the small Zariski site of
`S` is a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module on the scheme `S`.

The sections of `𝓕|_{S_Zar}` over the basic open `D(a)` of an affine open `U` are the base change
of the sections over `U` along `𝒪(U) → 𝒪(D(a))`, by
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.affineOpenBaseChange`, hence their localization away from `a`.
declarations.comment:
(1): for an adequate 𝒪-module F on (Sch/S)_τ the restriction F|_{S_Zar} is a
quasi-coherent 𝒪_S-module on the scheme S

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.nonempty_associatedModuleFunctor_obj_iso
declarations.doc:
**The pullback of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module is its associated module `𝓕^a`** of
[Stacks, Tag 03DU], whose sections over `T/S` are the global sections of the pullback of `𝓕` to
`T`. This is the description of `𝓕^a` as a pullback in Descent, [Stacks, Tag 03FH], which
[Stacks, Tag 06VN] invokes. After `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.exists_baseOverTopology` substitutes
the topology it is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSectionsSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem BigSite.nonempty_associatedModuleFunctor_obj_iso (B : BigSite τ S)
    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (B.associatedModuleFunctor.obj F ≅
      B.associatedModule F (isSheaf_associatedPresheaf B F))
declarations.comment:
`F^a` is the pullback of `F` under the morphism of ringed topoi
`((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` whose pushforward is restriction to `S_Zar`

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.associatedModuleAdeq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VN], the functor `u`.** The associated-module functor
`u : QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Adeq(𝒪)`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, on a chosen big `τ`-site over `S`; it lands in the
adequate modules by [Stacks, Tag 06VK].

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.restrictModuleQCoh
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VN], the functor `v`.** Restriction to the small Zariski site of `S` as a
functor `v : Adeq(𝒪) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_S)`, `𝓖 ↦ 𝓖|_{S_Zar}`, on a chosen big `τ`-site over `S`; it
lands in the quasi-coherent modules by [Stacks, Tag 06VM] (1).

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.adeqAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VN], the adjunction.** On a chosen big `τ`-site over `S`, for each of the
five topologies, the associated-module functor `u : QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Adeq(𝒪)` is left adjoint to
restriction `v : Adeq(𝒪) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_S)`, so `Hom_{𝒪_S}(𝓕, v𝓖) = Hom_𝒪(u𝓕, 𝓖)`
(`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.adeqAdjunction.homEquiv`). It is the pullback–pushforward adjunction
of the morphism of ringed sites `((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`, restricted to the two full
subcategories.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def BigSite.adeqAdjunction (B : BigSite τ S) :
    B.associatedModuleAdeq ⊣ B.restrictModuleQCoh
declarations.comment:
the adjunction `u ⊣ v` between `QCoh(𝒪_S)` and `Adeq(𝒪)`, whose hom-set
bijection is `Hom_{𝒪_S}(F, vG) = Hom_𝒪(uF, G)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isIso_adeqAdjunction_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VN], the unit.** The unit `𝓕 → vu𝓕` of the adjunction between
`QCoh(𝒪_S)` and `Adeq(𝒪)` is an isomorphism at every quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module, on a chosen
big `τ`-site over `S` for each of the five topologies.
declarations.comment: the map `F → vuF` is an isomorphism for every `F` in `QCoh(𝒪_S)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleAdeq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VN], consequence of the unit.** `u : QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Adeq(𝒪)` is fully
faithful, on a chosen big `τ`-site over `S` for each of the five topologies: the unit
`𝓕 → vu𝓕` of the adjunction `u ⊣ v` is an isomorphism at every object of `QCoh(𝒪_S)`
(`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isIso_adeqAdjunction_unit_app`).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def BigSite.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleAdeq (B : BigSite τ S) :
    B.associatedModuleAdeq.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment:
consequence of `F → vuF` being an isomorphism: `u : QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ Adeq(𝒪)` is fully
faithful

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_sheafification
declarations.doc:
[Stacks, Tag 06VP]: let `F` be a presheaf of `O`-modules on the big `τ`-site over `S`. If
for *every* affine scheme `Spec A` over `S` belonging to the site the functor `F_{F, A}` is
adequate, then the sheafification of `F` is an adequate `O`-module.

The sheafification enters as a locally injective and locally surjective map `η : F ⟶ G.val` to a
sheaf of modules `G`, and the conclusion is adequacy of `G`. The hypothesis `htop` is the input
of the source's proof; it is a theorem at `m = u`,
`Stacks.Adequate.affineAdequateSheafTopology`, and open for a general `m`, and it is kept as a
hypothesis here because the statement ranges over sheaves of modules of value universe
`max u m`; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_sheafification
    {τ : CoveringTopology} {S : Scheme.{u}} (B : BigSite τ S)
    (htop : AffineAdequateSheafTopology.{u, m} B)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{max u m} B.structureSheaf.obj)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B.structureSheaf) (η : F ⟶ G.val)
    (hinj : PresheafOfModules.IsLocallyInjective B.topology η)
    (hsurj : PresheafOfModules.IsLocallySurjective B.topology η)
    (hF : ∀ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : Spec A ⟶ S),
      schemeSizeBelow B.cutoff (Spec A) →
        AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate
          (AdequateFunctor.siteAlgebraInclusion A (schemeSizeBelow B.cutoff))
          (presheafAffineSectionFunctor B F A f)) :
    IsAdequate B G
declarations.comment:
assuming `AffineAdequateSheafTopology.{u, m}`, which is a theorem for `m = u`
(`Stacks.Adequate.affineAdequateSheafTopology`) and open for a general `m`

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_sheafification'
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VP].** Let `S` be a scheme and let `F` be a presheaf of `O`-modules on the
big `τ`-site over `S`. If for *every* affine scheme `Spec A` over `S` belonging to the site the
functor `F_{F, A}` is adequate, then the sheafification of `F` is an adequate `O`-module.

The sheafification enters, as in `Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_sheafification`, as a locally
injective and locally surjective map `η : F ⟶ G.val` to a sheaf of modules `G`, which is the
universal property of the associated sheaf; the conclusion is adequacy of `G`.

Nothing is assumed beyond the source's own hypothesis: the input of the source's proof that was
named `Stacks.Adequate.AffineAdequateSheafTopology` is discharged by
`Stacks.Adequate.affineAdequateSheafTopology_of_moduleExtensionSheaf` applied to
`Stacks.Adequate.affineModuleExtensionSheaf`, which is the proof of
`Stacks.Adequate.affineAdequateSheafTopology` and is spelled out here because that declaration
lives in a file importing this one. The attribute sits here rather than on
`Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_sheafification`, which is this statement under that input as an
assumption and which the proof of this one calls.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_sheafification'
    {τ' : CoveringTopology} {S' : Scheme.{u}} (B' : BigSite τ' S')
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{max u m} B'.structureSheaf.obj)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B'.structureSheaf) (η : F ⟶ G.val)
    (hinj : PresheafOfModules.IsLocallyInjective B'.topology η)
    (hsurj : PresheafOfModules.IsLocallySurjective B'.topology η)
    (hF : ∀ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : Spec A ⟶ S'),
      schemeSizeBelow B'.cutoff (Spec A) →
        AdequateFunctor.IsAdequate
          (AdequateFunctor.siteAlgebraInclusion A (schemeSizeBelow B'.cutoff))
          (presheafAffineSectionFunctor B' F A f)) :
    IsAdequate B' G

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VQ] (3).** Let `0 → 𝓕₁ → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₃ → 0` be a short exact sequence of
`𝒪`-modules on the chosen big `τ`-site over `S`. If `𝓕₁` and `𝓕₃` are adequate, then `𝓕₂` is
adequate.

As in the source: over every affine scheme `Spec A` of the site the induced sequence of
affine-section functors is short exact, because `H¹` of the adequate `𝓕₁` vanishes on affines
([Stacks, Tag 06VM] (3), through
`Stacks.Adequate.shortExact_affineSections_of_isAdequate`); its outer terms are adequate
([Stacks, Tag 06VI]), so its middle term is adequate ([Stacks, Tag 06V8] on the algebras of the
site, `Stacks.Adequate.affineAdequateExtensions`). The values of the modules lie in the universe
of the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_of_shortExact
    (T : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf)) (hT : T.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsAdequate B T.X₁) (h₃ : IsAdequate B T.X₃) :
    IsAdequate B T.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.abelian_adequate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VQ] (1).** The adequate `𝒪`-modules on the chosen big `τ`-site over `S`
form an abelian category: they contain the zero sheaf and are closed under kernels, cokernels
and finite products inside the abelian category of all sheaves of modules on the site.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def abelian_adequate : Abelian (adequate.{u, u} B).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.exact_ι_adequate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VQ] (2).** The inclusion of the adequate `𝒪`-modules into all `𝒪`-modules
on the chosen big `τ`-site over `S` is exact: it preserves finite limits and finite colimits,
kernels and cokernels of adequate modules being adequate.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_ι_adequate :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (adequate.{u, u} B).ι ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits (adequate.{u, u} B).ι

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.hasColimits_adequate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VQ] (4).** The category of adequate `𝒪`-modules on the chosen big
`τ`-site over `S` has all small colimits, and the inclusion into all `𝒪`-modules preserves them:
a colimit of adequate modules formed in all `𝒪`-modules is adequate.

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_directImage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VR] for the direct image.** Let `f : T ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes and let `𝓕` be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big
`τ`-site over `T`. Then the direct image `f_*𝓕` is an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big
`τ`-site over `S`.

The direct image is restriction along the base-change functor `Φ` of the two sites, with the
scalars transported along the first projection `ν` of the fibre squares
(`Stacks.Adequate.directImage`); `hbc` says that `Φ` and `ν` are base change along `f`. Over an
affine `Spec A` of the site over `S` the affine sections of `f_*𝓕` are `B ↦ 𝓕(T ×_S Spec B)`,
the degree-zero case of `Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_rightDerived_sectionsAlong_baseChangeFamily`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_directImage
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} C.structureSheaf) (hF : IsAdequate C F)
    (hqc : QuasiCompact f) (hqs : QuasiSeparated f) (hbc : IsBaseChangeAlong B C f Φ ν) :
    IsAdequate B ((directImage.{u, u} B C Φ ν).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_higherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06VR] for the higher direct images.** Let `f : T ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes and let `𝓕` be an adequate `𝒪`-module on a chosen big
`τ`-site over `T`. Then every higher direct image `R^i f_*𝓕` is an adequate `𝒪`-module on a
chosen big `τ`-site over `S`.

`R^i f_*` is the `i`-th right derived functor of `Stacks.Adequate.directImage`, the source's
definition. It is the sheafification of the presheaf `V ↦ H^i(V ×_S T, 𝓕)`
(`Stacks.Adequate.higherDirectImageIsoSheafification`), whose affine sections over `Spec A` are
`B ↦ H^i(T ×_S Spec B, 𝓕)` because evaluation is exact; these are adequate by
`Stacks.Adequate.isAdequate_rightDerived_sectionsAlong_baseChangeFamily`, so the sheafification
is adequate by [Stacks, Tag 06VP].

The statement assumes nothing beyond the source. The typeclass arguments of
`Stacks.Adequate.higherDirectImage` are supplied by proved instances on the two sites: the
sheafification of abelian presheaves and the identification of its weak equivalences with the
locally bijective maps are `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.hasSheafify_addCommGrpCat` and
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.wEqualsLocallyBijective_addCommGrpCat`, and the injectives in the
category of sheaves of modules on the site over `T` are
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.enoughInjectives_sheafOfModules`, which is [Stacks, Tag 01DU] on that
site (sheaves of modules on it form a Grothendieck abelian category).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdequate_higherDirectImage
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} C.structureSheaf) (hF : IsAdequate C F)
    (hqc : QuasiCompact f) (hqs : QuasiSeparated f) (hbc : IsBaseChangeAlong B C f Φ ν)
    (i : ℕ) :
    IsAdequate B ((higherDirectImage.{u, u} B C Φ ν i).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.derivedQuasicoherentComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VT.** The canonical comparison functor `D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` from the
derived category of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules to the complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules with
quasi-coherent cohomology: the derived functor of the exact inclusion, factored through
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedQuasicoherentComparison :
    DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonCommShift
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06VT.** The comparison functor is compatible with translation of complexes.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedQuasicoherentComparisonCommShift :
    (derivedQuasicoherentComparison.{w} X).CommShift ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDerived.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonIsTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VT.** The comparison functor preserves distinguished triangles, so it is an exact
functor of triangulated categories.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedQuasicoherentComparisonIsTriangulated :
    (derivedQuasicoherentComparison.{w} X).IsTriangulated

declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineEtale_hasConservativeFamily
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{u}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentModule.abelian_of_closure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06VZ.**  If the source and the target of a groupoid in algebraic spaces
`(U, R, s, t, c)` over `A` are flat, the quasi-coherent modules on it form an abelian category.

Kernels and cokernels are computed on the underlying `𝒪_U`-modules, which are quasi-coherent by
the kernel and cokernel clauses of Stacks 03M1(3).  A transition morphism is carried along a
cokernel because an inverse image of `𝒪`-modules is a left adjoint, and along a kernel because
the inverse images along `s`, along `c ≫ s` and along `e ≫ s` are left exact: `s` is flat,
`c` is a base change of `s` by Stacks 043Z, and `e ≫ s` is the identity.  The flatness of `t` is
not used, being equivalent to that of `s` in a groupoid.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def abelian_of_closure (hs : IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht : IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom) :
    Abelian (QuasicoherentModule B S hS G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_overPost
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W0.** The canonical localization functor from the slice of a category fibred in
groupoids at an object `x` to the schemes over the scheme `x` lies over is an equivalence of
categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_overPost {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (x : 𝒳) :
    (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inducedTopology_overPost
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W0.** The canonical localization functor identifies the localization at `x` of
the associated topology with the localization of the base topology at the scheme `x` lies
over, so it is an equivalence of sites and not merely of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem inducedTopology_overPost {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (x : 𝒳) :
    (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).inducedTopology
        (τ.over (p.obj x).left) =
      (associatedTopology B S hS p τ).over x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.presheafPullback
declarations.doc:
The pullback of a presheaf on a category fibred in groupoids to
the big fppf site of the scheme underlying an object `x`: restrict to the slice at `x`, then
transport across the localization equivalence of Stacks 06W0.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev presheafPullback
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (x : 𝒳)
    {A : Type t} [Category.{s} A] (F : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    (Over (p.obj x).left)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
The restriction of the pulled-back presheaf to the small étale
site of the same scheme, for an étale site with the same size cutoff.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev restrictToSmallEtale
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (E : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (h : E.cutoff = B.cutoff)
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (x : 𝒳)
    {A : Type t} [Category.{s} A] (F : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    (SmallEtale E (p.obj x).left.1
      (show E.Contains (p.obj x).left.1 from by simpa [h] using (p.obj x).left.2))ᵒᵖ ⥤ A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smallEtaleBaseMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W2.** The morphism of the big étale category of schemes below an arrow of a
category fibred in groupoids: the fppf and étale cutoffs agree, so the scheme morphism
underlying the arrow is a morphism of the étale site's bounded category.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleBaseMorphism {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y) :
    E.obj (p.obj x).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x) ⟶
      E.obj (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y)
declarations.comment: the morphism of schemes below an arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictionPushforwardComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W2.** The comparison `c_φ : F|_{V_ét} ⟶ a_{small, *}(F|_{U_ét})` from the
restriction of a presheaf at the target of an arrow `φ : x ⟶ y` to the direct image, along the
underlying morphism of schemes, of its restriction at the source.

The direct image on small étale sites is precomposition with base change, so the target is
spelled as such.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionPushforwardComparison {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y)
    {A : Type t} [Category.{s} A] (F : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    restrictToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp y F ⟶
      (smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ)).op ⋙
        restrictToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp x F
declarations.comment: the comparison with the direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictionPushforwardComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W2.** On a small étale object `W` over `V`, the comparison with the direct image
is restriction of `F` along the arrow of `𝒳` between the cartesian lifts of `W` and of its base
change, characterized by lying over the projection of the base-change square.

This specifies the comparison map, rather than merely producing one.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictionPushforwardComparison_app {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y)
    {A : Type t} [Category.{s} A] (F : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A)
    (W : SmallEtale E (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y)) :
    letI : (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).IsEquivalence :=
      isEquivalence_overPost B S hS p hp x
    letI : (Over.post (X := y) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).IsEquivalence :=
      isEquivalence_overPost B S hS p hp y
    let f := smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ
    let V' := (smallEtaleInclusion B E h (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y)).obj W
    let U' := (smallEtaleInclusion B E h (p.obj x).left.1
      (contains_base B E h S hS p x)).obj ((smallEtaleBaseChange E f).obj W)
    let y' := (Over.post (X := y) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).inv.obj V'
    let x' := (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).inv.obj U'
    let εy := (Over.post (X := y) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).asEquivalence.counit.app V'
    let εx := (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).asEquivalence.counit.app U'
    ∀ φ' : x'.left ⟶ y'.left, φ' ≫ y'.hom = x'.hom ≫ φ →
      B.inclusion.map (p.map φ').left ≫ B.inclusion.map εy.left =
        B.inclusion.map εx.left ≫ E.inclusion.map (pullback.fst W.obj.hom f) →
      (restrictionPushforwardComparison B E h S hS p hp φ F).app (Opposite.op W) =
        F.map φ'.op

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictionPushforwardComparison_naturality
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06W2.** The comparison with the direct image is natural in the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictionPushforwardComparison_naturality {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y)
    {A : Type t} [Category.{s} A] {F G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (η : F ⟶ G)
    (W : SmallEtale E (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y)) :
    letI : (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).IsEquivalence :=
      isEquivalence_overPost B S hS p hp x
    letI : (Over.post (X := y) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).IsEquivalence :=
      isEquivalence_overPost B S hS p hp y
    let y' := (Over.post (X := y) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).inv.obj
      ((smallEtaleInclusion B E h (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y)).obj W)
    let x' := (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).inv.obj
      ((smallEtaleInclusion B E h (p.obj x).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x)).obj
        ((smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ)).obj W))
    (restrictionPushforwardComparison B E h S hS p hp φ F).app (Opposite.op W) ≫
        η.app (Opposite.op x'.left) =
      η.app (Opposite.op y'.left) ≫
        (restrictionPushforwardComparison B E h S hS p hp φ G).app (Opposite.op W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictToSmallEtale_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W3.** The restriction of an étale sheaf on a category fibred in groupoids to the
small étale site of the scheme an object lies over is a sheaf, not merely a presheaf whose
sheafification is of interest.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictToSmallEtale_isSheaf {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (x : 𝒳)
    (F : Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p (etaleTopology B)) (Type (max (u + 1) t))) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf
      (SmallEtale.topology E (p.obj x).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x))
      (restrictToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp x F.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictionInverseImageComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W3.** The comparison `c_φ : a_{small}^{-1}(F|_{V_ét}) ⟶ F|_{U_ét}` from the
inverse image of the restriction at the target of an arrow `φ : x ⟶ y` to the restriction at
its source, the mate of the direct-image comparison of Stacks 06W2 under the
pullback–pushforward adjunction on small étale sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionInverseImageComparison {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y)
    (F : Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p (etaleTopology B)) (Type (max (u + 1) t))) :
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ)).sheafPullback
        (Type (max (u + 1) t))
        (SmallEtale.topology E (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y))
        (SmallEtale.topology E (p.obj x).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x))).obj
      (restrictToSmallEtaleSheaf B E h S hS p hp y F) ⟶
    restrictToSmallEtaleSheaf B E h S hS p hp x F
declarations.comment: the comparison with the inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasConservativeFamily_siteKind
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W4.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` be a category fibred in groupoids and let
`τ ∈ {Zar, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`. Then the site `𝒳_τ` has enough points: it has a
conservative family of points.

The site `𝒳_τ` is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedTopology`, the topology `𝒳`
inherits along `p` from the localization at `S` of the big `τ` topology (Stacks 06TP). The
proof is the one of the source: `hasConservativeFamily_associatedTopology` reduces to the
localizations of the big site, which have enough points by Stacks 06VX.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasConservativeFamily_siteKind (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (τ : SiteKind) :
    (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p τ).HasConservativeFamily.{u + 1}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.pushforwardSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
The pushforward formula for a presheaf along a functor into a category fibred
in groupoids.
The projection from the two-fibre product to `𝒳` pulls the presheaf back by
restriction; its global sections compute the right Kan extension at `y`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pushforwardSectionsEquiv
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hf : f ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (c : p𝒴.ChoiceOfPullbacks)
    {V : 𝒞} (y : p𝒴.Fiber V) (ℱ : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ (G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w), f.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    (f.op.ran.obj ℱ).obj (op y.1) ≃
      Presheaf.globalSections
        ((TwoFibreProductOver.snd (Over.forget V) p𝒳 p𝒴 (c.sliceFunctor y) f).op ⋙ ℱ)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.pushforwardSectionsEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
At a pair in the two-fibre product, the section corresponding to a pushforward
section is obtained by restricting along the comparison arrow to `y` and then
applying the counit of the right Kan extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforwardSectionsEquiv_apply
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hf : f ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (c : p𝒴.ChoiceOfPullbacks)
    {V : 𝒞} (y : p𝒴.Fiber V) (ℱ : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ (G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w), f.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G]
    (s : (f.op.ran.obj ℱ).obj (op y.1))
    (P : TwoFibreProductOver (Over.forget V) p𝒳 p𝒴 (c.sliceFunctor y) f) :
    ((Presheaf.globalSectionsEquivSections
        ((TwoFibreProductOver.snd (Over.forget V) p𝒳 p𝒴 (c.sliceFunctor y) f).op ⋙ ℱ))
      (pushforwardSectionsEquiv p𝒳 p𝒴 f h𝒴 hf c y ℱ s)).1 (op P) =
      (f.op.ranCounit.app ℱ).app (op P.y)
        ((f.op.ran.obj ℱ).map (P.iso.inv ≫ c.map P.x.hom y).op s)
declarations.comment: componentwise characterization by the right Kan counit

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.pushforwardSectionsEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc: The pushforward identification commutes with maps of presheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforwardSectionsEquiv_naturality
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hf : f ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (c : p𝒴.ChoiceOfPullbacks)
    {V : 𝒞} (y : p𝒴.Fiber V) (ℱ 𝒢 : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ (G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w), f.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G]
    (η : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢) (s : (f.op.ran.obj ℱ).obj (op y.1)) :
    pushforwardSectionsEquiv p𝒳 p𝒴 f h𝒴 hf c y 𝒢
        (((f.op.ran.map η).app (op y.1)) s) =
      (pushforwardSectionsEquiv p𝒳 p𝒴 f h𝒴 hf c y ℱ s) ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft
          (TwoFibreProductOver.snd (Over.forget V) p𝒳 p𝒴 (c.sliceFunctor y) f).op η

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isRepresentableMorphism_iff_forall_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W7.** A morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of
`S` is representable if and only if every presheaf `x ↦ Hom(F x, y)` on the source category is
representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableMorphism_iff_forall_isRepresentable
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Type v} [Category.{u + 1} 𝒳] [Category.{u + 1} 𝒴]
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hF : F ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳)
    (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p𝒳 p𝒴 F ↔
      ∀ y : 𝒴, (F.op ⋙ yoneda.obj y).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isLeftAdjoint_of_isRepresentableMorphism
declarations.doc:
A representable 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of
`S` has a right adjoint: its value at `y` is a representing object for the presheaf
`x ↦ Hom(F x, y)`, which exists by Stacks 06W7.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_of_isRepresentableMorphism (hF : F ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳)
    (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hrep : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism p𝒳 p𝒴 F) :
    F.IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isContinuous_rightAdjoint
declarations.doc:
The right adjoint of a representable 1-morphism is continuous for the topologies associated
(Stacks 06TP) to a topology `τ` on the underlying category of schemes: `F` is cocontinuous by
Stacks 06NW, and a right adjoint of a cocontinuous functor is continuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_rightAdjoint (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) :
    letI : F.IsLeftAdjoint :=
      isLeftAdjoint_of_isRepresentableMorphism B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 F hF h𝒳 h𝒴 hrep
    F.rightAdjoint.IsContinuous (Stack.associatedTopology B S hS p𝒴 τ)
      (Stack.associatedTopology B S hS p𝒳 τ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isMorphismOfSites_rightAdjoint
declarations.doc:
The right adjoint of a representable 1-morphism defines a morphism of sites from the
associated site of `𝒳` to that of `𝒴`: it is continuous, and the left exact left adjoint of its
pushforward on sheaves is the pushforward along `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_rightAdjoint (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) :
    letI : F.IsLeftAdjoint :=
      isLeftAdjoint_of_isRepresentableMorphism B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 F hF h𝒳 h𝒴 hrep
    IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1} F.rightAdjoint (Stack.associatedTopology B S hS p𝒴 τ)
      (Stack.associatedTopology B S hS p𝒳 τ)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.ranIsoRestrictionOfAdjunction
registrations.comment: the presheaf direct image along the right adjoint is restriction

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.sheafPushforwardCocontinuousIso
registrations.comment: agreement of the two direct images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ringStructureSheafCore_overPost
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W9.** The canonical localization equivalence of Stacks 06W0 carries the structure
sheaf of the schemes over `(p.obj x).left` to the restriction of the structure sheaf of `𝒳` to
the slice at `x`, including all restriction maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringStructureSheafCore_overPost
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology) (x : 𝒳) :
    (Over.forget x).op ⋙ (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj =
      (Over.post (X := x) (p ⋙ Over.forget (B.obj hS))).op ⋙
        (baseRingStructureSheaf B (p.obj x).left.1 (p.obj x).left.2 τ hτ).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.sheafPushforwardContinuous_baseStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W9.** The equivalence of Stacks 06W0 is an equivalence of *ringed* sites
`(𝒳_τ/x, 𝒪_𝒳|_x) ≌ ((Sch/U)_τ, 𝒪)`: the direct image along it of the structure sheaf of the big
`τ`-site of `U = p(x)` *is* the structure sheaf of `𝒳` restricted to the slice at `x`.

The two sites are identified by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.localizationEquivalence` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDenseSubsite_localizationEquivalence`, and the structure sheaves by
this equality, which is an equality and not merely an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafPushforwardContinuous_baseStructureSheaf
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology) (x : 𝒳) :
    ((localizationEquivalence B S hS p hp x).functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous
        CommRingCat.{u} ((associatedTopology B S hS p τ).over x)
        (τ.over (B.obj (p.obj x).left.2))).obj
        (baseStructureSheaf B (p.obj x).left.1 (p.obj x).left.2 τ hτ) =
      (structureSheaf B S hS p hp τ hτ).over x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.sheafPushforwardContinuous_baseRingStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06W9**, the same equivalence of ringed sites read on the underlying sheaves of
(not necessarily commutative) rings, which is the form the categories of sheaves of modules are
indexed by: the transport of the base sheaf of rings along the localization equivalence is the
restriction of the sheaf of rings of `𝒳` to the slice at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafPushforwardContinuous_baseRingStructureSheaf
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology) (x : 𝒳) :
    ((localizationEquivalence B S hS p hp x).functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous
        RingCat.{u} ((associatedTopology B S hS p τ).over x)
        (τ.over (B.obj (p.obj x).left.2))).obj
        (baseRingStructureSheaf B (p.obj x).left.1 (p.obj x).left.2 τ hτ) =
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).over x
declarations.comment: equivalence of ringed sites, underlying sheaves of rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.presheavesOfModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WB, part (1).** A presheaf of modules on a category fibred in groupoids `𝒳` over
the schemes over `S` is a presheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules, and `PMod(𝒪_𝒳)` is the category they form,
with morphisms the morphisms of presheaves of modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev presheavesOfModules
declarations.comment: part (1), the category of presheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WB, part (2).** A presheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules is an `𝒪_𝒳`-module, or a sheaf of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules, when it is an fppf sheaf, that is, when its underlying presheaf of abelian
groups satisfies the sheaf condition for the fppf topology on `𝒳`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsModule : ObjectProperty (presheavesOfModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.modules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WB, part (2).** The category `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on a category fibred in
groupoids `𝒳` over the schemes over `S`: presheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules that are fppf sheaves,
with morphisms the morphisms of presheaves of modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePushforwardComparison_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WC.** The direct-image comparison of a presheaf of modules below an arrow of `𝒳`
is natural in the module, at an arbitrary universe for the sections of the module.

On underlying abelian presheaves this is the naturality of Stacks 06W2, which holds for
presheaves with values in any category, and putting the module structure on the comparison does
not change it on sections. No universe inequality is needed: the direct image of presheaves of
modules is restriction of scalars followed by reindexing, and exists at every module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictModulePushforwardComparison_naturality
    {F F' : PresheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj} (α : F ⟶ F') :
    (restrictModuleToSmallEtaleFunctor.{u, v, w, m} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ y).map α ≫
        restrictModulePushforwardComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ F' =
      restrictModulePushforwardComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ F ≫
        (PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{m}
          (F := smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ))
          (smallEtaleStructureComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ)).map
          ((restrictModuleToSmallEtaleFunctor.{u, v, w, m} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ x).map α)
declarations.comment: functoriality of the direct-image comparison in the module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePullbackComparison_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WC.** The comparison map `c_φ` is natural in the module.

The square for `c_φ` is the square for the direct-image comparison carried across the
pullback–direct image adjunction along `a_{small}^♯`, using that `c_φ` is by definition the mate
of that comparison: naturality of the adjunction isomorphism on the left turns the left-hand
composite into a mate, naturality on the right does the same for the right-hand composite, and
the two mates agree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePushforwardComparison_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictModulePullbackComparison_naturality
    {F F' : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj} (α : F ⟶ F') :
    (PresheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
          (F := smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ))
          (smallEtaleStructureComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ)).map
        ((restrictModuleToSmallEtaleFunctor.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ y).map α) ≫
          restrictModulePullbackComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ F' =
      restrictModulePullbackComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ F ≫
        (restrictModuleToSmallEtaleFunctor.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ x).map α
declarations.comment: functoriality of the comparison map in the module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePullbackComparisonNatTrans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WC.** The comparison map `c_φ` below an arrow `φ : x ⟶ y` of `𝒳`, as a natural
transformation from the restriction at `y` followed by `a_{small}^*` to the restriction at
`x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictModulePullbackComparisonNatTrans :
    restrictModuleToSmallEtaleFunctor.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ y ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
          (F := smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ))
          (smallEtaleStructureComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ) ⟶
      restrictModuleToSmallEtaleFunctor.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ x
declarations.comment: the comparison map as a natural transformation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smallEtaleStructureComparison
declarations.doc:
The map `a_{small}^♯ : 𝒪_{V_ét} ⟶ a_{small, *}𝒪_{U_ét}` of structure sheaves below an arrow
`φ : x ⟶ y` of `𝒳`: the comparison of Stacks 06W2 for the structure sheaf of `𝒳`, conjugated by
the identifications of Stacks 06W9 of its restrictions with the structure sheaves of the small
étale sites.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallEtaleStructureComparison {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y)
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology) :
    (SmallEtale.structureSheaf E (p.obj y).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p y)).obj ⟶
      (smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ)).op ⋙
        (SmallEtale.structureSheaf E (p.obj x).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x)).obj
declarations.comment: the map of structure sheaves below an arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePushforwardComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WC.** The comparison of Stacks 06W2 for a presheaf of modules on `𝒳` is a
morphism of presheaves of modules over the map `a_{small}^♯` of structure sheaves: the
restriction at `y` maps to the direct image of the restriction at `x`.

This is the compatibility of the comparison map with `a_{small}^♯` asserted by the source.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictModulePushforwardComparison {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y)
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj) :
    restrictModuleToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp y τ hτ F ⟶
      (PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{m}
          (F := smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ))
          (smallEtaleStructureComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ)).obj
        (restrictModuleToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp x τ hτ F)
declarations.comment: compatibility of the comparison map with the map of structure sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePullbackComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WC.** The comparison map
`c_φ : a_{small}^*(F|_{V_ét}) ⟶ F|_{U_ét}` of `𝒪_{U_ét}`-modules below an arrow `φ : x ⟶ y` of
`𝒳` lying over a morphism of schemes `a : U ⟶ V`: the mate, under the
pullback–direct image adjunction along `a_{small}^♯`, of the comparison of Stacks 06W2 for the
presheaf of modules `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictModulePullbackComparison
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj) :
    (PresheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
        (F := smallEtaleBaseChange E (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ))
        (smallEtaleStructureComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ)).obj
        (restrictModuleToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp y τ hτ F) ⟶
      restrictModuleToSmallEtale B E h S hS p hp x τ hτ F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePullbackComparison_adjunct
declarations.doc:
The comparison map of Stacks 06WC is characterized by its mate being the comparison of
Stacks 06W2 for the presheaf of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictModulePullbackComparison_adjunct
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj) :
    (PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{u}
        (smallEtaleStructureComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ)).homEquiv _ _
        (restrictModulePullbackComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ F) =
      restrictModulePushforwardComparison B E h S hS p hp φ τ hτ F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.moduleFunctoriality
declarations.doc:
The two functors on presheaves of modules induced by a morphism of
categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleFunctoriality (hf : f ⋙ pY = pX) :
    ModuleFunctoriality.{u, v, w, m, v', w'} B S hS pX pY hpX hpY f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.modulePullback
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of sheaves of modules along a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids, in an arbitrary module universe: objectwise restriction of modules along `f`, with
scalars transported along `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ringStructureSheafCore_obj_eq`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullback :
    SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq τ hτ) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ)
declarations.comment: the inverse image, in an arbitrary module universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.moduleSheafAdjunction
declarations.doc: The inverse image of sheaves of modules is left adjoint to the direct image.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleSheafAdjunction :
    modulePullback.{u, v, w, max u v w m v' w', v', w'} B S hS p q hp hq f hf τ hτ ⊣
      moduleSheafPushforward.{u, v, w, m, v', w'} B S hS p q hp hq f hf τ hτ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.moduleSheafFunctoriality
declarations.doc:
The adjoint pair of inverse- and direct-image functors on sheaves of modules induced by a
1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleSheafFunctoriality :
    ModuleSheafFunctoriality.{u, v, w, m, v', w'} B S hS p q hp hq f hf τ hτ
declarations.comment: the adjoint pair on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.quasicoherentModules
declarations.doc:
The category of quasi-coherent modules on the fppf ringed site of a category fibred in
groupoids over the schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev quasicoherentModules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WH.** The inverse image of sheaves of modules along a 1-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of `S` preserves quasi-coherence.

The inverse image is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.modulePullback`, which on underlying presheaves of
modules is restriction along the 1-morphism followed by the change of scalars identifying the
two structure presheaves; and the slices of a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids are
equivalences by Stacks 06W0.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳] [Category.{w} 𝒴]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hf : f ⋙ q = p)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{max u v w m}
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq B.topology le_rfl))
    [M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    ((modulePullback.{u, v, w, max u v w m} B S hS p q hp hq f hf
      B.topology le_rfl).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_forall_objectInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WI.**  A sheaf of modules on the associated fppf site of a category fibred in
groupoids is quasi-coherent if and only if its inverse image `x^*𝓕` is a quasi-coherent sheaf on
the big fppf site `(Sch/U)_fppf` of the scheme `U = p(x)`, for every object `x` of `𝒳`.

Necessity is stability of quasi-coherence under restriction to a slice site, transported along
the equivalence of ringed sites `𝒳_fppf/x ≌ (Sch/U)_fppf`.  Sufficiency is Stacks 03DN for the
family of all objects of `𝒳`, which covers the final object: quasi-coherence is a local and
intrinsic property, so no further input is needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_forall_objectInverseImage
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∀ x : 𝒳, (objectInverseImage B S hS p hp x M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModuleToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WJ.** The restriction `x^*F|_{U_ét}` at an object `x` of a presheaf of modules on
`𝒳` to the small étale site of the scheme `U` below `x`: restrict the underlying abelian
presheaf as in Stacks 06W1, then transport the scalars through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.localStructurePresheafIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictModuleToSmallEtale {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (x : 𝒳)
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes) (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj) :
    PresheafOfModules.{m}
      (SmallEtale.structureSheaf E (p.obj x).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x)).obj
declarations.comment: the restriction to the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsLocallyQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WJ.** A presheaf of modules over the structure sheaf of a category fibred in
groupoids is *locally quasi-coherent* when it is a sheaf for the étale topology and, at every
object `x` of `𝒳`, its restriction to the small étale site of the scheme below `x` is a
quasi-coherent sheaf of modules.

The source calls the notation nonstandard; it is the condition under which the module is
determined by quasi-coherent modules on the small étale sites of the objects.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsLocallyQuasicoherent {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{m}
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj) :
    Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_etale_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WK.** A quasi-coherent module on a category fibred in groupoids is a sheaf for the
inherited étale topology.

This is the first conjunct of clause (1) of the source, local quasi-coherence being the étale
sheaf condition together with quasi-coherence of the restrictions to the small étale sites, and
it is the first step of the source's proof: quasi-coherence of `F` in the sense of Stacks 06WG
asserts in particular that `F` is a sheaf for the inherited fppf topology, and the inherited
étale topology is coarser.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_etale_of_isQuasicoherent {𝒳 : Type v} [Category.{w} 𝒳]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp
      (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hF : ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p B.topology) F.presheaf,
      SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
        (⟨F, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{m}
          (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp B.topology le_rfl))) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p (etaleTopology B)) F.presheaf
declarations.comment: the étale sheaf condition, which is the first conjunct of clause (1), in the forward direction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentFppf_iff_isLocallyQuasicoherent_and_isIso_sheafifiedRestrictComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WK.** A presheaf of modules `F` on a category fibred in groupoids `𝒳` over
`(Sch/S)_{fppf}` is quasi-coherent (Stacks 06WG) if and only if

1. `F` is locally quasi-coherent (Stacks 06WJ), and
2. for every arrow `φ : x ⟶ y` of `𝒳` the comparison map
   `c_φ : f_{small}^*(F|_{V_ét}) ⟶ F|_{U_ét}` of Stacks 06WC, read on sheaves of modules on the
   small étale site of the scheme `U` below `x`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentFppf_iff_isLocallyQuasicoherent_and_isIso_sheafifiedRestrictComparison
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj) :
    IsQuasicoherentFppf B S hS p hp F ↔
      ∃ hlqc : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp F,
        ∀ {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y),
          IsIso (sheafifiedRestrictComparison B E h S hS p hp F φ (hlqc.2 x).1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of presheaves of modules along a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S` preserves local quasi-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_modulePullback
    (G : PresheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hG : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS q hq G) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS (f ⋙ q) hp
      ((modulePresheafPullback.{u, v, w, v', w', m} B S hS q hq f hp).obj G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyQuasicoherentModules_colimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WM (1).** The category `LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of locally quasi-coherent modules has
colimits, and they agree with colimits in `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`: local quasi-coherence is closed under
colimits computed in `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`, the full subcategory therefore has them, and its
inclusion preserves them.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasicoherentModules_colimits :
    (∀ (K : Type u) [Category.{u} K],
      (isLocallyQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape K) ∧
      HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (locallyQuasicoherentModules.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp) ∧
      PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (isLocallyQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp).ι
declarations.comment: (1): LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳) has colimits and they agree with colimits in Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyQuasicoherentModules_abelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WM (2).** The category `LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is abelian, with kernels and cokernels
computed in `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`: local quasi-coherence is closed under kernels and cokernels, so
the full subcategory is abelian and its inclusion into `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasicoherentModules_abelian :
    (isLocallyQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp).IsClosedUnderKernels ∧
      (isLocallyQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp).IsClosedUnderCokernels ∧
      Nonempty (Abelian (locallyQuasicoherentModules.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp)) ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits (isLocallyQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp).ι ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (isLocallyQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp).ι
declarations.comment: (2): LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳) is abelian with kernels and cokernels computed in Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳), i.e. the inclusion is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_twoOutOfThree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WM (3).** In a short exact sequence `0 → 𝓕₁ → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₃ → 0` of
`Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`, if two of the three terms are locally quasi-coherent then so is the third.
A cokernel and a kernel of a morphism of locally quasi-coherent modules are locally
quasi-coherent by Stacks 06WM (2); for the middle term the restriction to the small étale site of
the scheme below an object is exact, so it carries the sequence to a short exact sequence there,
and an extension of quasi-coherent modules on a small étale site is quasi-coherent (Descent,
Lemma 0GNB).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_twoOutOfThree
    (T : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B))))
    (hT : T.ShortExact) :
    (IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₁.val →
        IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₂.val →
          IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₃.val) ∧
      (IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₂.val →
        IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₃.val →
          IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₁.val) ∧
      (IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₁.val →
        IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₃.val →
          IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp T.X₂.val)
declarations.comment: (3): in a short exact sequence of Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳), if two out of three terms are locally quasi-coherent so is the third

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_etaleInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WM, clause (5).** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category fibred in groupoids
and let `F`, `G` be locally quasi-coherent sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_étale`, with `F` of
finite presentation on `𝒳_étale`. Then the internal Hom `𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G)` of
`Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` is locally quasi-coherent.

Local quasi-coherence is étale-local on the object
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_restrictModuleToSmallEtale_of_etaleCover`), and
every covering of an object of `𝒳_étale` is refined by arrows lying over a jointly surjective
family of étale morphisms
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etaleCovering_le_of_mem_associatedTopology`);
at the members of such a refinement of a covering on which `F` is finitely presented the claim is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_restrictSheafToSmallEtale_etaleInternalHom`. The
hypothesis that `F` is locally quasi-coherent is part of the source's statement; the argument does
not use it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_etaleInternalHom
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (_hF : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp F.val)
    (hG : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp G.val)
    (hfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp (etaleInternalHom B S hS p hp F G).val
declarations.comment: (5): for F, G in LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳) with F of finite presentation on 𝒳_ét, the internal Hom 𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G) of Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳) is locally quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WM**, clause (4). The tensor product in `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)` of two locally
quasi-coherent sheaves of modules on a category fibred in groupoids is locally quasi-coherent.

The tensor product is the sheafification, for the associated étale topology, of the objectwise
tensor product. Its restriction to the small étale site of the scheme below an object `x` is the
tensor product there of the restrictions of the two factors, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModuleEtaleTensorSheafIso`: restriction commutes with the
objectwise tensor product because that is sectionwise, and with sheafification because the
restriction functor of Stacks 06W1 is cocontinuous as well as continuous. Quasi-coherence of a
tensor product on a ringed site is
`Stacks.Modules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_sheafificationTensorObjUlift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf
    (E : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (h : E.cutoff = B.cutoff)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hF : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp F.val)
    (hG : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp G.val) :
    letI := hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS p hp
    letI := wEqualsLocallyBijective_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS p hp
    IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, _, u, u}
        (structureSheaf B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
          (etaleTopology_le_topology B))).obj F).obj G).val
declarations.comment: (4): the tensor product in Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳) of two locally quasi-coherent modules is locally quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The tensor clause of Stacks 06WV (5) and of Stacks 06WN (2), for the quasi-coherence of
Stacks 03DL (6), on a site satisfying the hypotheses of this section**: the tensor product of
two sheaves of modules which are quasi-coherent in the sense of
`SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite` is again quasi-coherent in that sense.  That is the
quasi-coherence the notion `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of Stacks 06WG is defined by, and not Mathlib's
predicate.

**The hypotheses of this section exclude the site of Stacks 06WG**, which is why both clause
strings say so.  Of the five, the fibred fppf site of a category fibred in groupoids over
`(Sch/S)_fppf` satisfies three and fails two; the two failures are
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_univLE_associatedSite`, the size hypothesis, which at that
site's universes reads `UnivLE.{u + 1, u}`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_hasBinaryProducts_twoLabel`, binary products, which such a
category generally lacks for want of a final object.  See
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/Quasicoherent/Descent/FibredTensorHypotheses.lean`, where
the five are settled one by one.  So this statement does not instantiate to the source's clause,
and the source's clause is not proved anywhere on this development.

The proof is the proof of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf` run through
`SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, the identification of the two
predicates on a site whose objects and morphisms are small relative to the universe of the
sections — which is the extra hypothesis `UnivLE.{max u v w, w}` and the only thing separating
the two statements.  It is not removable: on a big site, whose objects live one universe above
its sections, the two predicates genuinely differ.

What is *not* asserted is the rest of Stacks 06WN (2), namely that the tensor products formed in
`Mod(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪)`, `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪)` and `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` agree.  Those are formed in different
categories, where sheafification is a different functor, so the agreement is not a consequence
of this statement and the comparison is not available; hence the qualified clause string, as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.colimits_quasicoherentModules_of_descent` for part (1).
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O)))
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨O.obj, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O.obj) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        ((isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))⟩).obj (F)).obj (G))).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**The tensor clause of Stacks 06WV (5) and of Stacks 06WN (2), for the quasi-coherence of
Stacks 03DL (6)**, for the tensor product of the monoidal category `Mod(𝒪)` itself.  Together
with `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf` this is the
covering set of the clause at the source's predicate, the development carrying both
descriptions of the tensor product.

As there, the hypotheses of this section **exclude the fibred fppf site of Stacks 06WG**, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_univLE_associatedSite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_hasBinaryProducts_twoLabel`; hence the qualified clause
strings.
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorObj
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O)))
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.quasicoherentOnSiteTensorBifunctor
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product as a bifunctor on the quasi-coherent modules of Stacks 03DL (6)**: the
restriction of the tensor product of `Mod(𝒪)` to the full subcategory cut out by that
quasi-coherence.  It exists exactly because that tensor product preserves that
quasi-coherence, which is the tensor clause of Stacks 06WV (5).

On the fibred fppf site of Stacks 06WG this subcategory is `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.quasicoherentModules`), but the hypotheses of this section do
not hold at that site — see
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_univLE_associatedSite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_hasBinaryProducts_twoLabel` — so this bifunctor is not the
one the source asserts; hence the qualified clause strings.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quasicoherentOnSiteTensorBifunctor :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory ×
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.existsUnique_hom_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WN(2).**  Restricted to a pair of quasi-coherent modules with sections in
independent universes, the tensor product formed on an associated site of the fibred category is
the tensor product in the ambient category of sheaves of modules on that site: every bilinear
map into a sheaf of modules there has a unique linear factorization through the pure-tensor map.
This is the universal property the source asserts of the common tensor product on the Zariski,
étale and fppf sites; it is proved here for all five associated sites, and the factorization is
tested against every sheaf of modules, not only the quasi-coherent ones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_hom_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent (τ : SiteKind)
    (F : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, m} B S hS p hp)
    (G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, n} B S hS p hp)
