    (H : SheafOfModules.{max u m n} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ))
    (b : Stacks.Modules.BilinearMap (structureSheaf B S hS p hp τ).obj
      F.obj.val G.obj.val H.val) :
    ∃! f : tensorSheafMixed B S hS p hp τ ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)
        ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G) ⟶ H,
      ∀ (U : 𝒳ᵒᵖ) (x : F.obj.val.obj U) (y : G.obj.val.obj U),
        f.val.app U ((toTensorSheafMixed B S hS p hp τ
          ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)
          ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G)).app U x y) = b.app U x y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.internalHomSheaf_val_eq_fppf
declarations.doc:
The internal Hom of two quasi-coherent modules on a category fibred in groupoids has the
same underlying presheaf of modules on each of the five associated sites as on the fppf one; in
particular on the Zariski and étale ones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem internalHomSheaf_val_eq_fppf (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, w, u} B S hS p hp) :
    ((ringedSite B S hS p hp τ).internalHomSheaf
        ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)
        ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G)).val =
      ((ringedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).internalHomSheaf F.obj G.obj).val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
The internal Hom of a finite locally free quasi-coherent module into a quasi-coherent module
on a category fibred in groupoids is quasi-coherent on the fppf associated site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, w, u} B S hS p hp)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite F.obj) :
    ((ringedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).internalHomSheaf F.obj G.obj).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product of a pair of quasi-coherent modules with sections in independent
universes, formed on the fppf site of a category fibred in groupoids, is quasi-coherent.**  This
is the object whose universal property is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.existsUnique_hom_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent`, so the tensor
product of quasi-coherent modules is again a quasi-coherent module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent
    (F : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, m} B S hS p hp)
    (G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, n} B S hS p hp) :
    (tensorSheafMixed B S hS p hp .fppf ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp .fppf).obj F)
      ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp .fppf).obj G)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.quasicoherentModules_colimits_siteAgreement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WN (1).**  For a category fibred in groupoids `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf`, the
category `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` has colimits, and they agree with the colimits in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, in
`Mod(𝒳_τ, 𝒪_𝒳)` for each of the coarser inherited topologies — in particular in
`Mod(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪_𝒳)` and `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` — and in `LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`: the inclusion into
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, the reading functors into `Mod(𝒳_τ, 𝒪_𝒳)` and the inclusion into `LQCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
preserve them.  Colimits are indexed by categories in the universe of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentModules_colimits_siteAgreement (E : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    (h : E.cutoff = B.cutoff) :
    HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS p hp) ∧
      PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)).ι ∧
      (∀ τ : SiteKind,
        PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (toSiteModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS p hp τ)) ∧
      PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (toLocallyQuasicoherentModules B S hS p hp E h)
declarations.comment: (1): QCoh(O_X) has colimits and they agree with colimits in Mod(X_Zar, O_X), Mod(X_et, O_X), Mod(O_X) and LQCoh(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.internalHomSheaf_quasicoherent_siteAgreement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WN (3).**  Let `𝓕` and `𝓖` be quasi-coherent modules on a category fibred in
groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`.  Then `𝓕` is finite locally free for the fppf topology if and only
if it is for the étale, and if and only if for the Zariski topology (indeed for each of the five
topologies); the internal homs `ℋom(𝓕, 𝓖)` computed in `Mod(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪_𝒳)`, `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`
and `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` agree; and when `𝓕` is finite locally free for any one of these topologies the
common value is an object of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomSheaf_quasicoherent_siteAgreement
    (F G : quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS p hp) :
    (∀ τ : SiteKind, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite F.obj ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)) ∧
    (∀ τ : SiteKind,
      (ringedSite B S hS p hp τ).internalHomSheaf ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)
          ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G) =
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.comparisonPushforward.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1}
          (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology_le_fppf B S hS p τ)
          (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)).obj
          ((ringedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).internalHomSheaf F.obj G.obj)) ∧
    (∀ τ : SiteKind,
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F) →
        ((ringedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).internalHomSheaf F.obj G.obj).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
declarations.comment: (3): for F, G in QCoh(O_X) the internal homs computed in Mod(X_Zar, O_X), Mod(X_et, O_X) and Mod(O_X) agree, F being finite locally free does not depend on the topology, and for F finite locally free the common value is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.sheafTensor_quasicoherent_siteAgreement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WN (2).**  For quasi-coherent modules `𝓕` and `𝓖` on a category fibred in
groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`, the tensor products `𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖` computed in `Mod(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪_𝒳)`,
`Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` and `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` agree — the one computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, read for each coarser
topology, is the one computed for that topology — and the common value is an object of
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`; it is moreover quasi-coherent on each of the coarser sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafTensor_quasicoherent_siteAgreement
    (F G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, w, u} B S hS p hp) :
    (∀ τ : SiteKind, Nonempty ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.comparisonPushforward.{v, w, u, u}
        (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology_le_fppf B S hS p τ)
        (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)).obj
        (((sheafTensor B S hS p hp .fppf).obj F.obj).obj G.obj) ≅
      ((sheafTensor B S hS p hp τ).obj ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)).obj
        ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G))) ∧
    (((sheafTensor B S hS p hp .fppf).obj F.obj).obj G.obj).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
    (∀ τ : SiteKind, (((sheafTensor B S hS p hp τ).obj
      ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)).obj
        ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
declarations.comment: (2): for F, G in QCoh(O_X) the tensor products computed in Mod(X_Zar, O_X), Mod(X_et, O_X) and Mod(O_X) agree and the common value is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_inverseImage_of_isStackificationEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WQ.** If a 1-morphism `F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf category of `S` induces an equivalence of stackifications, then the morphism of topoi
`Sh(𝒳_fppf) ⟶ Sh(𝒴_fppf)` of Stacks 06TS is an equivalence.

The functor displayed is the inverse image of that morphism of topoi, which by Stacks 06TS is
restriction along `F`; the morphism of topoi is an equivalence exactly when its inverse image
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_inverseImage_of_isStackificationEquivalence
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 : Type v₁} [Category.{u} 𝒳] {𝒴 : Type v₂} [Category.{u} 𝒴]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hF : p.IsFibredOneMorphism q F)
    (heq : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      hF.IsStackificationEquivalence (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).1
    (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (max t u v₁ v₂))
      (p.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (q.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_modulePullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WR, the `Mod` clause.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S`. If `f` induces an equivalence of stackifications,
then the inverse image of sheaves of modules of Stacks 06WE is an equivalence
`Mod(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.

Equivalence of stackifications makes `f` a dense subsite inclusion for the associated fppf
topologies, by the engine of Stacks 06WQ; the structure sheaf of `𝒳` is the restriction along
`f` of that of `𝒴`, so the inverse image *is* restriction of sections, and the Comparison
Lemma for sheaves of modules applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_modulePullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 : Type u} [Category.{u} 𝒳] {𝒴 : Type u} [Category.{u} 𝒴]
    (p : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : 𝒴 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (hF : p.IsFibredOneMorphism q f)
    (heq : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      hF.IsStackificationEquivalence (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    (modulePullback.{u, u, u, u, u, u} B S hS p q hp hq f hF.comp_eq
      B.topology le_rfl).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_quasicoherentPullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WR, the `QCoh` clause.** If `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` induces an equivalence of
stackifications, then the inverse image of quasi-coherent modules is an equivalence
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.

Fullness and faithfulness come from the equivalence on all modules, since `QCoh` is a full
subcategory; essential surjectivity needs in addition that `f^*` reflects quasi-coherence,
which is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_modulePullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_quasicoherentPullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence
    (heq : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      hF.IsStackificationEquivalence (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    (quasicoherentPullback B S hS p q hp hq f hF).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_modulePullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence_anyUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WR, the `Mod` clause.**  Let `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S`.  If `f` induces an equivalence of stackifications,
then the inverse image of sheaves of modules of Stacks 06WE is an equivalence
`Mod(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, for modules with sections in any universe containing `u`.

`f` is a dense subsite inclusion for the associated fppf topologies (Stacks 06WQ), restriction of
abelian sheaves along it is an equivalence
(`isEquivalence_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_isStackificationEquivalence`), and the structure
sheaf of `𝒳` is the restriction along `f` of that of `𝒴`, so the Comparison Lemma for sheaves of
modules applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_modulePullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence_anyUniverse
    (heq : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      hF.IsStackificationEquivalence' (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    (modulePullback.{u, v₁, w, max u m, v₂, w} B S hS p q hp hq f hF.comp_eq
      B.topology le_rfl).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the Mod clause: f^* is an equivalence Mod(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_𝒳), for categories fibred in groupoids in arbitrary universes and modules in any universe containing that of the rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_quasicoherentPullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence_anyUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WR, the `QCoh` clause.**  Let `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S`.  If `f` induces an equivalence of stackifications,
then the inverse image of quasi-coherent modules is an equivalence `QCoh(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, for
modules with sections in any universe containing `u`.

Fullness and faithfulness come from the `Mod` clause, since `QCoh` is a full subcategory;
essential surjectivity needs in addition that `f^*` reflects quasi-coherence, which holds because
`f` is cover-dense (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_modulePullback'`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_quasicoherentPullback_of_isStackificationEquivalence_anyUniverse
    (heq : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      hF.IsStackificationEquivalence' (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    (quasicoherentPullback'.{u, v₁, w, max u m, v₂, w} B S hS p q hp hq f
      hF.comp_eq).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the QCoh clause: f^* is an equivalence QCoh(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), for categories fibred in groupoids in arbitrary universes and modules in any universe containing that of the rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackModulePullback
declarations.doc:
The functor `ℱ ↦ x^*ℱ`, the inverse image of sheaves of modules of Stacks 06WE along the
canonical projection `x : 𝒮_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R.
declarations.comment: the inverse image of modules along the canonical map from the object space, the first step of the forward functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientPrestackQuasicoherentPullback
declarations.doc:
The restriction of quasi-coherent modules along the stackification map `[U/_pR] ⟶ [U/R]`: the
inverse image of modules of Stacks 06WE, which preserves quasi-coherence by Stacks 06WH.
declarations.statement:
def quotientPrestackQuasicoherentPullback (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} C S hS (quotientStack G).p
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_quotientStack G) ⥤
      FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} C S hS (quotientPrestack G).p
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_quotientPrestack G)
declarations.comment: the restriction of quasi-coherent modules along the stackification map of the pointwise quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackQuasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)` over `S` with quotient stack `𝒳 = [U/R]`,
the category of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules is equivalent to the category of quasi-coherent
modules on `(U, R, s, t, c)`, by `ℱ ↦ (x^*ℱ|_{U_étale}, α)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentEquivalenceGroupoid
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid `(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces, the category of quasi-coherent modules
on the quotient stack `[U/R]` is equivalent to the category of quasi-coherent modules on
`(U, R, s, t, c)`, by the functor `ℱ ↦ (x^*ℱ|_{U_étale}, α)` with `α` the transport of the
canonical 2-morphism of Stacks 044S through the comparison maps of equation 076R.
declarations.comment: the equivalence QCoh(𝒪_{[U/R]}) ≌ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c), with functor ℱ ↦ (x^*ℱ|_{U_étale}, α)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.colimits_quasicoherentModules
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic stack `𝒳`, the category `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` has colimits, and they agree with
colimits in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`: the inclusion `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` preserves them.
declarations.comment: part (4): QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) has colimits and they agree with colimits in Mod(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentInclusion_rightExact_not_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WV (3).**  The inclusion `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is right exact for every
algebraic stack `𝒳`, but it is **not** exact in general: on every big fppf site there is an
algebraic stack, namely `Spec(ℤ)`, for which it is not exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentInclusion_rightExact_not_exact :
    (∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
        (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS),
        PreservesFiniteColimits
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
            (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
              .fppf)).ι) ∧
      ∀ B : BigFppfSite.{u}, ∃ 𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B specInt.{u} (contains_specInt B),
        ¬ (PreservesFiniteLimits
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
              (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B specInt.{u} (contains_specInt B) 𝒳.val.val.p
                𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids .fppf)).ι ∧
          PreservesFiniteColimits
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
              (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B specInt.{u} (contains_specInt B) 𝒳.val.val.p
                𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids .fppf)).ι)
declarations.comment: part (3): the inclusion QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is right exact, and on every big site the algebraic stack Spec(ℤ) is one for which it is not exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.GroupoidPresentation.quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WV (1).**  A presentation `[U/R] → 𝒳` of an algebraic stack — a smooth groupoid
`(U, R, s, t, c)` in algebraic spaces over `S` and an equivalence `[U/R] → 𝒳` (Stacks 04TI) —
induces a canonical equivalence `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ≌ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)`.

It is the inverse image along the presenting equivalence, `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_{[U/R]})`,
followed by the equivalence of Stacks 06WT,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentEquivalenceGroupoid`.
declarations.statement:
def GroupoidPresentation.quasicoherentEquivalence {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (P : GroupoidPresentation B S hS 𝒳.val.val) :
    FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids ≌ Space.QuasicoherentModule B S hS P.groupoid
declarations.comment: part (1): a presentation [U/R] → 𝒳 induces a canonical equivalence QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ≌ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.abelianQuasicoherentModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WV (2).**  The quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack form an abelian
category.

By Stacks 04T3 the stack has a presentation `[U/R] → 𝒳` by a smooth groupoid; its source and
target are smooth, hence flat, so `QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)` is abelian by Stacks 06VZ, and part (1)
transports the abelian structure to `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
instance abelianQuasicoherentModules (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    Abelian (FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.preservesColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentInclusion'
declarations.doc:
**Colimits of quasi-coherent modules are fppf-module colimits.**  The inclusion of the
quasi-coherent modules into all module sheaves for the associated fppf topology preserves all
small colimits; this is the comparison half of the colimit clause of Stacks 06WN(1), again with
both hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.inclusion_preservesColimits_of_span` discharged and only the
standing essential smallness left assumed.

Right exactness of the inclusion functor, Stacks 06WV(3), is this statement: the source
derives it from the agreement of colimits, Stacks 06WV(4).

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WV (5) for Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent`**: the tensor product of
two quasi-coherent sheaves of modules on a site is quasi-coherent.  Quasi-coherence is a local
condition, and over a common refinement of the two coverings on which the factors are presented,
the tensored presentation presents the tensor product.

The quasi-coherence here is Mathlib's — a covering of the final object carrying
`SheafOfModules.Presentation`s — and *not* the `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite` of
Stacks 03DL (6), which is the notion `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of Stacks 06WG means; hence the qualified
clause string.  The clause for that notion is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf` below, which is this
statement plus `SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite` and so carries one
further size hypothesis on the site.

This is also the site-level form of Stacks 01CE (3), which is a statement about a ringed space
and is tagged there, on `AlgebraicGeometry.tensorSheaf_isQuasicoherent` in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Modules/TensorProduct/Basic.lean`.
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O)))
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨O.obj, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O.obj) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        ((isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))⟩).obj (F)).obj (G))).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherent_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WV (5) for Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent`**, for the tensor product
of the monoidal category `Mod(𝒪)` itself: given quasi-coherent sheaves of modules `F` and `G`,
the tensor product `F ⊗_𝒪 G` formed in `Mod(𝒪)` is quasi-coherent.  This is the shape in which
the source states the clause;
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf` is the same statement for the
explicit model of that tensor product as a sheafified objectwise tensor product, and the two
together are the covering set at this predicate, the development carrying both descriptions.
The same pair for the quasi-coherence of Stacks 03DL (6) is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorObj` and
`…isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherent_tensorObj
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O)))
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj F G).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.quasicoherentTensorBifunctor
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product as a bifunctor on quasi-coherent modules**, `QCoh(𝒪) × QCoh(𝒪) ⥤
QCoh(𝒪)`.  It is the restriction of the tensor product of `Mod(𝒪)` to the full subcategory of
quasi-coherent modules, and it exists exactly because that tensor product preserves
quasi-coherence, which is Stacks 06WV (5): a bifunctor valued in `QCoh(𝒪)` cannot be written
down before the clause is proved.  The quasi-coherence cutting out the subcategory is Mathlib's;
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.quasicoherentOnSiteTensorBifunctor` is the same bifunctor
on the subcategory cut out by the quasi-coherence of Stacks 03DL (6), which is the category
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of Stacks 06WG.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quasicoherentTensorBifunctor :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory ×
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The tensor clause of Stacks 06WV (5) and of Stacks 06WN (2), for the quasi-coherence of
Stacks 03DL (6), on a site satisfying the hypotheses of this section**: the tensor product of
two sheaves of modules which are quasi-coherent in the sense of
`SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite` is again quasi-coherent in that sense.  That is the
quasi-coherence the notion `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of Stacks 06WG is defined by, and not Mathlib's
predicate.

**The hypotheses of this section exclude the site of Stacks 06WG**, which is why both clause
strings say so.  Of the five, the fibred fppf site of a category fibred in groupoids over
`(Sch/S)_fppf` satisfies three and fails two; the two failures are
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_univLE_associatedSite`, the size hypothesis, which at that
site's universes reads `UnivLE.{u + 1, u}`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_hasBinaryProducts_twoLabel`, binary products, which such a
category generally lacks for want of a final object.  See
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/Quasicoherent/Descent/FibredTensorHypotheses.lean`, where
the five are settled one by one.  So this statement does not instantiate to the source's clause,
and the source's clause is not proved anywhere on this development.

The proof is the proof of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf` run through
`SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, the identification of the two
predicates on a site whose objects and morphisms are small relative to the universe of the
sections — which is the extra hypothesis `UnivLE.{max u v w, w}` and the only thing separating
the two statements.  It is not removable: on a big site, whose objects live one universe above
its sections, the two predicates genuinely differ.

What is *not* asserted is the rest of Stacks 06WN (2), namely that the tensor products formed in
`Mod(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪)`, `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪)` and `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` agree.  Those are formed in different
categories, where sheafification is a different functor, so the agreement is not a consequence
of this statement and the comparison is not available; hence the qualified clause string, as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.colimits_quasicoherentModules_of_descent` for part (1).
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O)))
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨O.obj, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O.obj) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        ((isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))⟩).obj (F)).obj (G))).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**The tensor clause of Stacks 06WV (5) and of Stacks 06WN (2), for the quasi-coherence of
Stacks 03DL (6)**, for the tensor product of the monoidal category `Mod(𝒪)` itself.  Together
with `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf` this is the
covering set of the clause at the source's predicate, the development carrying both
descriptions of the tensor product.

As there, the hypotheses of this section **exclude the fibred fppf site of Stacks 06WG**, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_univLE_associatedSite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_hasBinaryProducts_twoLabel`; hence the qualified clause
strings.
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorObj
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w}
      (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O)))
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.quasicoherentOnSiteTensorBifunctor
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product as a bifunctor on the quasi-coherent modules of Stacks 03DL (6)**: the
restriction of the tensor product of `Mod(𝒪)` to the full subcategory cut out by that
quasi-coherence.  It exists exactly because that tensor product preserves that
quasi-coherence, which is the tensor clause of Stacks 06WV (5).

On the fibred fppf site of Stacks 06WG this subcategory is `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.quasicoherentModules`), but the hypotheses of this section do
not hold at that site — see
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_univLE_associatedSite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.not_hasBinaryProducts_twoLabel` — so this bifunctor is not the
one the source asserts; hence the qualified clause strings.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quasicoherentOnSiteTensorBifunctor :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory ×
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O.obj
        (isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf O))).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.existsUnique_hom_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WN(2).**  Restricted to a pair of quasi-coherent modules with sections in
independent universes, the tensor product formed on an associated site of the fibred category is
the tensor product in the ambient category of sheaves of modules on that site: every bilinear
map into a sheaf of modules there has a unique linear factorization through the pure-tensor map.
This is the universal property the source asserts of the common tensor product on the Zariski,
étale and fppf sites; it is proved here for all five associated sites, and the factorization is
tested against every sheaf of modules, not only the quasi-coherent ones.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_hom_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent (τ : SiteKind)
    (F : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, m} B S hS p hp)
    (G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, n} B S hS p hp)
    (H : SheafOfModules.{max u m n} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ))
    (b : Stacks.Modules.BilinearMap (structureSheaf B S hS p hp τ).obj
      F.obj.val G.obj.val H.val) :
    ∃! f : tensorSheafMixed B S hS p hp τ ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)
        ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G) ⟶ H,
      ∀ (U : 𝒳ᵒᵖ) (x : F.obj.val.obj U) (y : G.obj.val.obj U),
        f.val.app U ((toTensorSheafMixed B S hS p hp τ
          ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj F)
          ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp τ).obj G)).app U x y) = b.app U x y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product of a pair of quasi-coherent modules with sections in independent
universes, formed on the fppf site of a category fibred in groupoids, is quasi-coherent.**  This
is the object whose universal property is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.existsUnique_hom_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent`, so the tensor
product of quasi-coherent modules is again a quasi-coherent module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheafMixed_quasicoherent
    (F : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, m} B S hS p hp)
    (G : quasicoherentModules.{u, v, u, n} B S hS p hp) :
    (tensorSheafMixed B S hS p hp .fppf ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp .fppf).obj F)
      ((toSiteModules B S hS p hp .fppf).obj G)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_X₂_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WV (7).**  Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`, for
instance an algebraic stack, and let `0 → 𝓕₁ → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₃ → 0` be a short exact sequence in
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` with `𝓕₁` and `𝓕₃` quasi-coherent.  Then `𝓕₂` is quasi-coherent.

By Stacks 06WI it suffices that `x^*𝓕₂` be quasi-coherent on `(Sch/U)_fppf` for each object `x`
over a scheme `U`.  The functor `x^*` is restriction to `𝒳_fppf/x` followed by an equivalence;
restriction to a localized site is exact (Stacks 03DA), so `x^*` carries the sequence to a short
exact sequence on `(Sch/U)_fppf`, whose middle term is quasi-coherent by Stacks 0GNC (4),
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₂_all`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_X₂_of_shortExact
    {C : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf))}
    (hC : C.ShortExact) (h₁ : C.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (h₃ : C.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    C.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (7): an extension in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent, for every category fibred in groupoids over (Sch/S)_fppf, in particular for every algebraic stack

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_sheafTensor
registrations.comment: part (5): for quasi-coherent F, G the tensor product F ⊗ G computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is quasi-coherent, for every category fibred in groupoids over (Sch/S)_fppf (at τ = fppf)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
registrations.comment: part (6): for F, G in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) with F finite locally free, the internal Hom ℋom(F, G) computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is quasi-coherent, for every category fibred in groupoids over (Sch/S)_fppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesInjectiveObjects_abelianDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WX, part (1).** Direct image along a 1-morphism of fibred categories over the
big fppf category of a scheme carries injective abelian sheaves to injective abelian sheaves,
for the site each side inherits from an arbitrary topology on the base. The direct image is the
right Kan extension along `F.op`, which exists for abelian groups in any universe containing
the objects of the source and the morphisms of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_abelianDirectImage
    [p.IsFibered] [q.IsFibered] (hF : p.IsFibredOneMorphism q F) :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology (τ.over (B.obj hS))).2
    (F.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous AddCommGrpCat.{max v₁ w₂ t}
      (associatedTopology B S hS p τ)
      (associatedTopology B S hS q τ)).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesInjectiveObjects_sheafOfModulesDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WX, part (2).** Direct image along a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of a scheme carries injective sheaves of
`O_𝒳`-modules to injective sheaves of `O_𝒴`-modules, for every topology coarser than the fppf
topology. The direct image is `SheafOfModules.directImageOfEq`, the right Kan extension along
`F.op` with its module structure, which is right adjoint to the inverse image of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_sheafOfModulesDirectImage
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology) :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).2
    (SheafOfModules.directImageOfEq.{u, max v₁ w₂ t} F (associatedTopology B S hS p τ)
      (associatedTopology B S hS q τ) (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq τ hτ)
      (ringStructureSheafCore_eq_sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp
        hτ)).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.abelianDirectImage_preservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WX, part (1).** Direct image under a fibred 1-morphism preserves injective
abelian sheaves, for any of the five associated topologies.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianDirectImage_preservesInjectiveObjects
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 : Type v₁} [Category.{w₁} 𝒳]
    {𝒴 : Type v₂} [Category.{w₂} 𝒴]
    {p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS}
    {p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS}
    [p𝒳.IsFibered] [p𝒴.IsFibered]
    {F : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴} (hF : p𝒳.IsFibredOneMorphism p𝒴 F)
    (τ : SiteKind)
    [∀ (G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{t}), F.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B S hS τ)).2
    (F.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous AddCommGrpCat.{t}
      (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p𝒳 τ)
      (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p𝒴 τ)).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesInjectiveObjects_sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WX, part (1).** Direct image along a 1-morphism of fibred categories over the
big fppf category of a scheme carries injective abelian sheaves to injective abelian sheaves,
for the site each side inherits from an arbitrary topology on the base.

The inverse image is the left adjoint of direct image and preserves finite limits, hence
monomorphisms, and a right adjoint of a monomorphism-preserving functor preserves injectives.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
    [p.IsFibered] [q.IsFibered] (hF : p.IsFibredOneMorphism q F)
    [∀ G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{t}, F.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    letI := (hF.isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology (τ.over (B.obj hS))).2
    (F.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous AddCommGrpCat.{t}
      (associatedTopology B S hS p τ)
      (associatedTopology B S hS q τ)).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesInjectiveObjects_of_adjunction_sheafOfModules_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06WX, part (2).** Direct image along a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids carries injective sheaves of modules to injective sheaves of modules: any functor `G`
right adjoint to the inverse image of modules preserves injective objects.

`G` is the direct image of sheaves of modules; its existence is Stacks 06X0 and is taken as the
hypothesis `adj` rather than constructed, so that the statement is about whichever functor is
adjoint to the inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_of_adjunction_sheafOfModules_pushforward
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology)
    (G : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      SheafOfModules.{t} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{t} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq τ hτ))
    (adj : letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
        (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
      SheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
        (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ) ⊣ G) :
    G.PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exact_sheafPullback_of_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06X1, part (1).** For a faithful 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids
whose source has equalizers, lower shriek `f_!` on abelian sheaves is exact.

Finite colimits are preserved because `f_!` is a left adjoint. Finite limits are preserved by
the criterion of Stacks 04BH: the source has fibre products (Stacks 06WY) and equalizers by
hypothesis, and `f` preserves both (Stacks 06WZ, in the form that places no constraint between
the universes of source and target).
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_sheafPullback_of_faithful
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    [F.Faithful] [HasEqualizers 𝒳]
    [∀ G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{t}, F.op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension G]
    [HasSheafify (associatedTopology B S hS q τ) Ab.{t}] :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
    exactFunctor _ _
      (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback F Ab.{t}
        (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) (associatedTopology B S hS q τ))

theorem injective_sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRightAdjoint_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06X1, the left adjoint.** For a 1-morphism `f` of categories fibred in groupoids
over the big fppf category of `S` and any topology `τ` on the underlying category of schemes,
the inverse image `f⁻¹ : Ab(𝒴_τ) ⥤ Ab(𝒳_τ)` has a left adjoint `f_!`.

The functor `f` is continuous for the associated topologies (Stacks 06NW). The pointwise left Kan
extensions along `f.op` exist because `𝒳` is essentially small and `𝒴` locally small, and
sheafification on `𝒴_τ` exists because `𝒴` is essentially small; so `f_!` is the sheafified
left Kan extension of Stacks 04BG,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_essentiallySmall
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    [EssentiallySmall.{t} 𝒳] [EssentiallySmall.{t} 𝒴] :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
    (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{t}
      (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) (associatedTopology B S hS q τ)).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: f⁻¹ has a left adjoint f_!

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exact_leftAdjoint_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06X1, part (1).** For a faithful 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over
the big fppf category of `S` whose source has equalizers, the left adjoint `f_!` of the inverse
image `f⁻¹ : Ab(𝒴_τ) ⥤ Ab(𝒳_τ)` is exact, for any topology `τ` on the underlying category of
schemes.

The left adjoint is isomorphic to the sheafified left Kan extension, which is exact by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exact_sheafPullback_of_faithful` (Stacks 04BH, with the hypotheses of
that criterion supplied by Stacks 06WY and 06WZ); the pointwise Kan extensions and the
sheafification it uses exist by essential smallness of `𝒳` and `𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_leftAdjoint_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_faithful
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    [F.Faithful] [HasEqualizers 𝒳] [EssentiallySmall.{t} 𝒳] [EssentiallySmall.{t} 𝒴] :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
    letI : (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{t}
        (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) (associatedTopology B S hS q τ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
      isRightAdjoint_sheafPushforwardContinuous_of_essentiallySmall B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp
    exactFunctor _ _ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{t}
      (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) (associatedTopology B S hS q τ)).leftAdjoint

underlying category of schemes.

The inverse image is right adjoint to the functor `f_!`, which is exact by part (1) and so

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lowerShriekForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06X2.** Lower shriek on sheaves of modules agrees, on underlying abelian sheaves,
with lower shriek on abelian sheaves.

Both sides are computed by sheafifying a presheaf-level left adjoint, and at the presheaf level
the two agree because every slice functor of a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids is
an equivalence: that is
`Stacks.ModuleLowerShriek.pullbackCompToPresheafIso`. Without the slice hypothesis the
statement is false, by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForget_not_isomorphic`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lowerShriekForgetIso
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology)
    (hPresheaf :
      letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
        (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
      (PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
        (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ).hom).IsRightAdjoint)
    [∀ G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{t}, F.op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension G]
    [HasWeakSheafify (associatedTopology B S hS q τ) AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    [(associatedTopology B S hS q τ).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{t}] :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
    letI : (PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
      (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ).hom).IsRightAdjoint := hPresheaf
    letI : (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
      (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
      SheafOfModules.instIsRightAdjointPushforward _
    SheafOfModules.pullback.{t} (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ) ⋙
        SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{t} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq τ hτ) ≅
      SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{t} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ) ⋙
        Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback F AddCommGrpCat.{t}
          (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) (associatedTopology B S hS q τ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exact_sheafOfModules_pullback_of_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06X2, part (1).** For a faithful 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids
whose source has equalizers, lower shriek `f_!` on sheaves of modules is exact.

Finite colimits are preserved because `f_!` is a left adjoint. Finite limits are preserved
because `SheafOfModules.toSheaf` reflects them and, composed with `f_!`, is the abelian `f_!`
of Stacks 06X1 (1) up to `lowerShriekForgetIso`, which is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_sheafOfModules_pullback_of_faithful
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)
    (hτ : τ ≤ B.topology) [F.Faithful] [HasEqualizers 𝒳]
    (hPresheaf :
      letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
      letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
      letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
        (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
      (PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
        (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ).hom).IsRightAdjoint)
    [∀ G : 𝒳ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{t}, F.op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension G]
    [HasSheafify (associatedTopology B S hS q τ) AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    [(associatedTopology B S hS q τ).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{t}] :
    letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered
    letI : q.IsFibered := hq.isFibered
    letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
      (τ.over (B.obj hS))).1
    letI : (PresheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
      (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ).hom).IsRightAdjoint := hPresheaf
    letI : (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{t}
      (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ)).IsRightAdjoint :=
      SheafOfModules.instIsRightAdjointPushforward _
    exactFunctor _ _
      (SheafOfModules.pullback.{t}
        (ringStructureSheafCoreHom B S hS p q F τ hp hq hcomp hτ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.injective_sheafOfModules_pushforward_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06X2, part (2).** The inverse image of an injective sheaf of modules is

The inverse image of modules is right adjoint to the exact functor `f_!` of part (1), which

declarations.statement:
theorem injective_sheafOfModules_pushforward_obj
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hcomp : F ⋙ q = p)

    (hPresheaf :
      letI : p.IsFibered := hp.isFibered

      letI := ((hq.isFibredOneMorphism hcomp).isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_inheritedTopology
