registrations.comment: the derived tensor product on a ringed space, with its exactness

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KFlatDerivedPullback.derivedPullback_commShift
declarations.doc:
**The derived pullback commutes with the shift.**  `Lf^*` is the total left derived functor
of degreewise pullback along `Qh`; degreewise pullback and `Qh` both commute with the shift, and
the quasi-isomorphisms of `K(𝒪_Y)` are stable under it, so the derived functor does too.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedPullback_commShift :
  (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback f).CommShift ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KFlatDerivedPullback.derivedPullback_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**The derived pullback is exact**: `Lf^* : D(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` carries distinguished triangles
to distinguished triangles.

Every morphism of `D(𝒪_Y)` is, up to isomorphism of arrows, the image of a morphism between
K-flat complexes: the K-flat objects resolve every object, so their inclusion is a localized
equivalence and the induced functor is essentially surjective on arrows.  Completing such a
morphism to a distinguished triangle of `K(𝒪_Y)` leaves all three vertices K-flat, the third by
`isKFlat_obj₃_of_distTriang`, and the comparison of `Lf^*` is invertible at each of them.  That
is exactly the input of `CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_of_rightExtension`.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedPullback_isTriangulated :
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback f).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KFlatDerivedPullback.isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_of_kFlat
declarations.doc:
**A K-flat complex computes the derived pullback**: on it the canonical comparison
`Lf^* K ⟶ f^* K` is invertible.  This is the clause of Tag 06YJ that says the construction
agrees with degreewise pullback where degreewise pullback is already derived, and it holds for
an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces: the K-flat complexes are a resolving datum for `f^*`,
and the comparison of a left derived functor is invertible on its resolving class.

The two models of the derived categories are binders rather than the file's pinned
`HasDerivedCategory.standard`: every ingredient of the proof is model-free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_of_kFlat
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))]
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) ℤ) (hK : KFlatComplex Y K) :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackComparison f).app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.affineSectionsAcyclic_of_sections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06YK] for the affine-section functor.** The affine-section functor is right
acyclic at a sheaf of modules as soon as its module-valued sections over every algebra of the
site are, evaluation of presheaves of modules being exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineSectionsAcyclic_of_sections (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : Spec A ⟶ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u m} B.structureSheaf)
    (hsec : ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < k →
      ∀ X : (AdequateFunctor.AlgebrasInSite A (schemeSizeBelow B.cutoff))ᵒᵖᵒᵖ,
      IsZero (((affineSectionsFunctor.{u, max u m} B A f ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation
          (AdequateFunctor.algebraRingDiagramOn
            (AdequateFunctor.siteAlgebraInclusion A (schemeSizeBelow B.cutoff)))
          X).rightDerived k).obj F)) :
    AffineSectionsAcyclic.{u, m} B A f F
declarations.comment:
the module-valued half for the affine-section functor: its right derived
functors are computed on sections over the algebras of the site, evaluation of presheaves of
modules being exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at `U` of the derived inclusion of module sheaves into module presheaves
is canonically the module-valued right derived functor of sections over `U`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (U : X.C) (p : ℕ) :
    (SheafOfModules.forget (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).rightDerived p ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj (op U) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (op U)).rightDerived p

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso_cocycles
declarations.doc:
The comparison is the one induced by evaluating the cocycles of an injective
resolution. In particular it is independent of the chosen resolution.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso_cocycles (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (U : X.C) (p : ℕ) (F : SheafOfModules (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (I : InjectiveResolution F) :
    let P := SheafOfModules.forget (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
    let E := SheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (op U)
    let G := PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj (op U)
    let K := (P.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex
    (rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso X U p).hom.app F =
      (G.mapIso (I.isoRightDerivedObj P p)).hom ≫
      (G.mapIso ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctorIso _ _ p).app K)).hom ≫
      ((K.sc p).mapHomologyIso G).inv ≫
      ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctorIso _ _ p).app
        ((G.mapHomologicalComplex _).obj K)).inv ≫
      (I.isoRightDerivedObj E p).inv

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetRestrictedEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
The derived inclusion followed by evaluation at `U` and restriction of scalars to
`O(V)` agrees with derived sections at `U` viewed as `O(V)`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def rightDerivedForgetRestrictedEvaluationIso
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) {U V : X.C} (f : U ⟶ V) (p : ℕ) :
    (SheafOfModules.forget (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).rightDerived p ⋙
        (PresheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj (op U) ⋙
          ModuleCat.restrictScalars
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.map f.op).hom) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (op U) ⋙
        ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.map f.op).hom).rightDerived p

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetRestrictedEvaluationIso_eq
declarations.doc:
The restricted comparison is obtained from the same module-valued comparison,
not chosen independently after restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightDerivedForgetRestrictedEvaluationIso_eq
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) {U V : X.C} (f : U ⟶ V) (p : ℕ)
    (F : SheafOfModules (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (rightDerivedForgetRestrictedEvaluationIso X f p).hom.app F =
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj.map f.op).hom).map
        ((rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso X U p).hom.app F) ≫
      (rightDerivedEvaluationRestrictScalarsIso X f p F).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso_naturality
declarations.doc:
The module-valued comparison commutes with restriction from `V` to `U`, with the
target sections viewed as modules over the ring of sections on `V`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso_naturality (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (p : ℕ) (F : SheafOfModules (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    {U V : X.C} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    (PresheafOfModules.restriction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj f.op).app
        (((SheafOfModules.forget
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).rightDerived p).obj F) ≫
      (rightDerivedForgetRestrictedEvaluationIso X f p).hom.app F =
    (rightDerivedForgetEvaluationIso X V p).hom.app F ≫
      (NatTrans.rightDerived
        (Functor.whiskerLeft (SheafOfModules.forget (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
          (PresheafOfModules.restriction
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj f.op)) p).app F

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
The right derived functor of the inclusion of module sheaves in module presheaves, viewed as
a presheaf of abelian groups, is canonically the cohomology presheaf. This is natural both in the
coefficient sheaf and in objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def rightDerivedForgetCohomologyIso (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (p : ℕ) :
    (SheafOfModules.forget (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).rightDerived p ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj ≅
      SheafOfModules.toSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) ⋙
        Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor X.J p

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteDerivedForget.rightDerivedForgetCohomologyIso_naturality
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification of the derived presheaf with the cohomology presheaf commutes
with restriction along any morphism of the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightDerivedForgetCohomologyIso_naturality (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (p : ℕ)
    (F : SheafOfModules (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) {U V : X.C} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    (((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj).obj
      (((SheafOfModules.forget
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).rightDerived p).obj F)).map f.op) ≫
        ((rightDerivedForgetCohomologyIso X p).hom.app F).app (op U) =
      ((rightDerivedForgetCohomologyIso X p).hom.app F).app (op V) ≫
        (((Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor X.J p).obj
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).obj F)).map f.op)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.statement1
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.**  Fix a complex `G^•` of `O`-modules.  The functor
`F^• ↦ Tot(G^• ⊗_O F^•)` on the homotopy category `K(Mod(O))` is an exact functor
of triangulated categories (Definition 5).

Concretely: there is a functor `Φ : K(Mod(O)) ⥤ K(Mod(O))` together with a
functorial isomorphism `ξ` (a `CommShift ℤ` structure, incorporating the Koszul
signs of tag 0FLG) such that
* `Φ` is additive;
* `Φ` lifts the complex-level functor `F^• ↦ Tot(G^• ⊗_O F^•)` through the
  homotopy quotient -- i.e. `quotF ⋙ Φ ≅ leftTensorComplex ⋙ quotF` -- so it is
  well defined on `K(Mod(O))` (sends homotopic maps to homotopic maps); and
* `Φ`, equipped with the commutation-with-shift datum `ξ`, is a triangulated
  functor: it commutes with the shift up to `ξ` and sends distinguished triangles
  to distinguished triangles.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1
    (G : HomologicalComplex (SheafOfModules (ringSheaf R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    ∃ (Φ : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules (ringSheaf R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤
            HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules (ringSheaf R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      (ξ : Φ.CommShift ℤ),
      Φ.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (quotF R ⋙ Φ ≅ leftTensorComplex R G ⋙ quotF R) ∧
          (letI := ξ; Φ.IsTriangulated)
declarations.comment: the functor F ↦ Tot(G ⊗_O F), the fixed complex on the left

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.statement2
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.**  Fix a complex `G^•` of `O`-modules.  The functor
`F^• ↦ Tot(F^• ⊗_O G^•)` on the homotopy category `K(Mod(O))` is an exact functor
of triangulated categories (Definition 5).

Concretely: there is a functor `Φ : K(Mod(O)) ⥤ K(Mod(O))` together with a
functorial isomorphism `ξ` (a `CommShift ℤ` structure, incorporating the Koszul
signs) such that
* `Φ` is additive;
* `Φ` lifts the complex-level functor `F^• ↦ Tot(F^• ⊗_O G^•)` through the
  homotopy quotient -- i.e. `quotF ⋙ Φ ≅ rightTensorComplex ⋙ quotF`; and
* `Φ`, equipped with the commutation-with-shift datum `ξ`, is a triangulated
  functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2
    (G : HomologicalComplex (SheafOfModules (ringSheaf R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    ∃ (Φ : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules (ringSheaf R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤
            HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules (ringSheaf R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      (ξ : Φ.CommShift ℤ),
      Φ.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (quotF R ⋙ Φ ≅ rightTensorComplex R G ⋙ quotF R) ∧
          (letI := ξ; Φ.IsTriangulated)
declarations.comment: the functor F ↦ Tot(F ⊗_O G), the fixed complex on the right

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat
declarations.doc:
A cochain complex `K` of sheaves of `O`-modules on a ringed site `(C, O)` is **K-flat**
when the total tensor complex `Tot(F ⊗_O K)` is acyclic for every acyclic cochain complex `F`
of sheaves of `O`-modules.
declarations.statement:
abbrev KFlat
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) ℤ) :
      Prop

quasi-isomorphisms of the homotopy category.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatQuasiIso.quasiIso_tensorComplex_of_KFlat
declarations.doc:
Total tensor product with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms:
if the maps on every cohomology sheaf are isomorphisms, so are those induced
by tensoring with `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_tensorComplex_of_KFlat
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) ℤ)
    (hK : CochainComplex.KFlatBifunctor.KFlat (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor R) K)
    {F G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) ℤ}
    (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : ∀ n, IsIso (ShortComplex.leftHomologyMap
      ((HomologicalComplex.shortComplexFunctor _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n).map f))) :
    ∀ n, IsIso (ShortComplex.leftHomologyMap
      ((HomologicalComplex.shortComplexFunctor _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n).map
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplex R).map f).app K)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.kFlat_of_boundedAbove_of_flat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06YQ.** A bounded above cochain complex of flat sheaves of modules is K-flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_of_boundedAbove_of_flat
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) ℤ)
    (hbound : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE n)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w}
      (O := R) (K.X i)) :
    IsKFlat R K

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LocallyBoundedKFlat.kFlat_of_isLocallyBounded_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**A locally bounded complex of flat `𝒪_W`-modules is K-flat.**  This is [Stacks, Tag 06YQ]
with its boundedness hypothesis localized: the complex is only assumed bounded on each member
of some open cover of `W`, which is strictly weaker than being bounded above.

For an acyclic `L^•`, the total complex `Tot(L^• ⊗_{𝒪_W} ℱ^•)` has to be acyclic, and by
`acyclic_of_acyclic_restrict` it is enough that each of its restrictions be.  On an open `V` on
which `ℱ^•` is bounded, `restrictTotalTensorIso` identifies that restriction with
`Tot(L^•|_V ⊗_{𝒪_V} ℱ^•|_V)`; there `ℱ^•|_V` is bounded above with flat terms
(`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.isFlat_restrictModules`, [Stacks, Tag 0E8J] on an open
subspace) hence K-flat by [Stacks, Tag 06YQ], and `L^•|_V` is acyclic because restriction is
exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_of_isLocallyBounded_of_flat
    (F : CochainComplex (RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules W) ℤ)
    (hF : Stacks.SheafOfModules.OnSpace.IsLocallyBounded W F)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
      (O := W.sheaf) (F.X i)) :
    KFlat W F
declarations.comment: with the boundedness hypothesis localized: a complex of flat O_W-modules which is merely LOCALLY bounded — bounded on each member of some open cover of W, which a complex with no global bound above can be — is K-flat. The source states it for a complex bounded above, which is this statement at the one-member cover W = W

declarations.name: colim_of_system_KFlat_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Stacks Lemma 21.17.9 / Tag 06YR).**

Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `D : K_1 → K_2 → K_3 → …` be a system of complexes
of `O`-modules which are K-flat for the tensor product `⊗_O` of Definition 1.  Then the
termwise colimit `colim_i K_i` is K-flat.

The two structural facts of the proof are the two hypotheses of
`colim_of_system_KFlat_isKFlat_of_bifunctor`, and both are theorems here: `⊗_O` commutes
with colimits in each variable because `Mod(O)` is monoidal closed, so `ℱ ⊗_O -` is a left
adjoint (`SheafOfModules.preservesColimitsOfSize_sheafTensor_obj`); and colimits over `ℕ`
are exact in `Mod(O)` by AB5
(`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.hasExactColimitsOfShape_nat`), so a colimit of
acyclic complexes is acyclic (`CochainComplex.KFlat.acyclic_colimit`).
declarations.statement:
theorem colim_of_system_KFlat_isKFlat (D : SystemOfComplexes (ringSheaf O))
    (hD : ∀ i, IsKFlat (ringSheaf O) (sheafTensor O) (D.obj i)) :
    IsKFlat (ringSheaf O) (sheafTensor O) (systemColimit (ringSheaf O) D)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_kFlat_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
Every cochain complex of sheaves of modules on a ringed site receives a quasi-isomorphism
from a K-flat complex. This is the existence assertion of Stacks 06YS.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kFlat_quasiIso
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) (p :
      P ⟶ G),
      IsKFlat X.O P ∧ QuasiIso p

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatResolution.exists_kFlatResolution_ofSize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 06YS with the module universe free of the site.** Every complex of `O`-modules
on a ringed site admits a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex whose
terms are flat: the colimit of the ladder of Stacks 077J, resolved by flat modules.

The object universe `u`, the morphism universe `v` and the module universe `w` are
independent, so the statement applies at a site whose objects lie above the module universe,
such as the small étale site of an algebraic space, a `RingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kFlatResolution_ofSize (G : CochainComplex (ModOfSize.{v, u, w} R) ℤ) :
    ∃ (K : CochainComplex (ModOfSize.{v, u, w} R) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ G),
      CochainComplex.KFlatBifunctor.KFlat
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} R) K ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R)
        (K.X i)) ∧
      QuasiIso f ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Epi (f.f i))
declarations.comment:
with the object and morphism universes of the site independent of the module
  universe, so that it applies at a site whose objects lie above the module universe

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatResolution.exists_kFlatResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 06YS.** Every complex of `O`-modules on a ringed site admits a termwise
surjective quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex whose terms are flat: the colimit of the
ladder of 077J.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kFlatResolution
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} R)) ℤ)
      :
    ∃ (K : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} R)) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ G),
      CochainComplex.KFlatBifunctor.KFlat
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} R) K ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := R) (K.X i)) ∧
      QuasiIso f ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Epi (f.f i))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isKFlat_isFlat_quasiIso_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06YS.** Every cochain complex `G` of modules on a ringed site receives a termwise
surjective quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex whose terms are flat.

The complex is the colimit of the ladder of [Stacks, Tag 077J]. It is K-flat because each rung
is bounded above with flat terms, hence K-flat by [Stacks, Tag 06YQ], and a sequential colimit
of K-flat complexes is K-flat by [Stacks, Tag 06YE]. Its terms are flat because they are
filtered colimits of the flat terms of the rungs ([Stacks, Tag 05NG]), and the comparison is
termwise surjective because each rung is termwise surjective onto a truncation of `G`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isKFlat_isFlat_quasiIso_epi
    (G : CochainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) ℤ) :
    ∃ (K : CochainComplex
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) ℤ) (s : K ⟶ G),
      IsKFlat X.O K ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (K.X i)) ∧
      QuasiIso s ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, Epi (s.f i)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_mapBifunctorMap_id_of_kFlat_right
declarations.doc:
A quasi-isomorphism `α` of K-flat complexes induces a quasi-isomorphism
`Tot(F ⊗ α)` for every complex `F`. This is Stacks 06YT.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_mapBifunctorMap_id_of_kFlat_right
    {P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}

      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
declarations.comment: the quasi-isomorphism in the right tensor factor

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_mapBifunctorMap_id_of_kFlat_left
declarations.doc:
A quasi-isomorphism `α` of K-flat complexes induces a quasi-isomorphism
`Tot(α ⊗ F)` for every complex `F`. This is the mirror image of Stacks 06YT.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_mapBifunctorMap_id_of_kFlat_left
    {P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}
    (α : P ⟶ Q) (hα : QuasiIso α) (hP : IsKFlat X.O P) (hQ : IsKFlat X.O Q)
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
    QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorMap α (𝟙 F) (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      X.O)
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
declarations.comment: the quasi-isomorphism in the left tensor factor

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quasiIso_tensorComplex_obj_map_of_kFlat
declarations.doc:
Stacks 06YT in the `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.tensorComplex` spelling: the quasi-isomorphism
  `α` of
K-flat complexes sits in the right tensor slot. The square whose cancellation gives the
result is the naturality square of `tensorComplex.map r` at `α`, for a K-flat resolution
`r : M ⟶ F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_tensorComplex_obj_map_of_kFlat

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06YU.** The derived tensor product of sheaves of modules on a ringed site exists,
with its canonical natural map to the ordinary total tensor product, its one-sided K-flat
comparisons, and exactness in both variables.

The objects of the site form a type in an arbitrary universe `c`, while its morphisms, the
sections of its structure sheaf and the sections of its modules lie in one universe `u`; the
derived category's hom universe `d` is independent of both.  That is the configuration of a
small étale site, whose objects sit one universe above its morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedTensorProduct :
    Nonempty (DerivedTensorProduct.{c, u, u, d} X)
declarations.comment: existence, for a site whose objects form a type in an arbitrary universe while its morphisms, structure sheaf and modules lie in one universe

`irreducible_def`; `canonicalDerivedTensorProduct_def` is the defining equation.

declarations.doc:

derived categories.  Together with `derivedPullback_isTriangulated_of_isMorphismOfSites` this is
the assertion that `Lf^*` is *exact* as a functor of triangulated categories.

This is `Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposDerivedPullback.derivedPullback_commShift` with its instance
binder discharged; that instance never needed the exactness clause, only the existence of the
derived functor.

presented by a morphism of the underlying sites, at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOnRingedTopoi.derivedPullback_isTriangulated_of_isMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, exactness.**  `Lf^*` is an exact functor of triangulated categories: it carries a
distinguished triangle of `D(O')` to a distinguished triangle of `D(O)`.

This is `Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposDerivedPullback.derivedPullback_isTriangulated` with both of
its inputs discharged — the exactness clause by `pullbackInvertsQuasiIso_isKFlat` and the
instance binder by `hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy`.

    haveI := hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy f hmos
    (derivedPullback f).IsTriangulated

exactness, for a morphism of ringed topoi presented by a morphism of the
underlying sites, at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOnRingedTopoi.derivedPullbackComparison_isIso_of_kFlat_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the computation `Lf^* K^• = f^* K^•`.**  The canonical comparison
`Lf^* K^• ⟶ f^* K^•` is invertible at a K-flat complex `K^•` of `O'`-modules with flat terms: the
derived pullback of such a complex is computed by degreewise pullback.

This is
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposDerivedPullback.isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_of_kFlat_of_flat`
with both of its inputs discharged.  Both hypotheses on `K^•` are the source's, and both are
used: they are the two clauses of the resolving class
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction.IsKFlat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackComparison_isIso_of_kFlat_of_flat
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ)
    (hK : CochainComplex.KFlatBifunctor.KFlat
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.O) K)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := Y.O) (K.X i)) :
    haveI := hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy f hmos
    IsIso ((derivedPullbackComparison f).app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))
declarations.comment:
computation on K-flat complexes with flat terms, for a morphism of ringed topoi
presented by a morphism of the underlying sites, at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOnRingedTopoi.derivedPullbackComparison_isIso_of_boundedAbove_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the computation on a bounded above complex of flat modules.**  A bounded above
complex of flat `O'`-modules is K-flat by Tag 06YQ, so the canonical comparison is invertible
there too.  This is the "in particular" of the source's statement.

This is `isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_of_boundedAbove_of_flat` of
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposDerivedPullback` with both of its inputs discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackComparison_isIso_of_boundedAbove_of_flat
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ)
    (hbound : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE n)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := Y.O) (K.X i)) :
    haveI := hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy f hmos
    IsIso ((derivedPullbackComparison f).app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))
declarations.comment:
computation on bounded above complexes of flat modules, for a morphism of ringed
topoi presented by a morphism of the underlying sites, at RingedTopos.{u, u, u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOnRingedTopoi.isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_kFlat
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the computation.**  The canonical comparison `Lf^* K^• ⟶ f^* K^•` is invertible
at a K-flat complex of `O'`-modules with flat terms: the derived pullback of such a complex is
computed by degreewise pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_kFlat
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ)
    (hK :
      letI := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor_obj_additive.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.O
      @CochainComplex.KFlatBifunctor.KFlat
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
        inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.O)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor_additive.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.O)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor_obj_additive.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.O)
        inferInstance K)

theorem isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app_boundedAbove

    (hbound : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE n)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := Y.O) (K.X i)) :

declarations.comment: computation on bounded above flat complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the derived pullback functor, at independent universes.**  The derived pullback
`Lf^* : D(𝒪') ⥤ D(𝒪)` along a morphism of ringed topoi, the total left derived functor of
degreewise pullback followed by localization.

The two ringed topoi have all six of their universes free, and the geometric datum is the
two-field morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 01D3, part (2); in particular this applies to the
small étale ringed topos `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u}` of an algebraic space,
which `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction.derivedPullback` does not.

The instance argument is `Prop`-valued and is supplied by
`pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor` from a resolving datum for `f^*`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev derivedPullback :
    DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w'} (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
declarations.comment:
the derived pullback functor, for a morphism of ringed topoi whose two ringed
topoi have their object, morphism and structure-ring universes free and unrelated, and whose
geometric datum is a morphism of the underlying topoi rather than of the underlying sites

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullbackComparison
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the canonical comparison, at independent universes.**  The comparison
`Lf^* ⟶ f^*` from the derived pullback to degreewise pullback, whose invertibility on a
resolving class is the computation assertion of Tag 06YY.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev derivedPullbackComparison :
    DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ derivedPullback f ⟶ pullbackOnHomotopy f
declarations.comment:
the canonical comparison `Lf^* ⟶ f^*`, at free and unrelated universes for the
two ringed topoi and for a geometric datum which is a morphism of the underlying topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback_commShift
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, compatibility with shifts, at independent universes.**  The derived pullback
commutes with the shift functors of the two derived categories.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance derivedPullback_commShift : (derivedPullback f).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment:
compatibility of `Lf^*` with the shift, at free and unrelated universes for the
two ringed topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the computation, at independent universes.**  The canonical comparison
`Lf^* 𝒦^• ⟶ f^* 𝒦^•` is invertible at an object of a resolving class for `f^*`: the derived
pullback of such a complex is computed by degreewise pullback.

At the class of K-flat complexes with flat terms, which is the class the source resolves by,
this is the computation assertion of Tag 06YY in the form it states.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackComparison_app
    (P : ObjectProperty
      (HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{w'} (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hP : HasResolutions (Y := Y) P) (hinv : PullbackInvertsQuasiIso f P)
    (K : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{w'} (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (hK : P K) :
    IsIso ((derivedPullbackComparison f).app K)
declarations.comment:
the computation `Lf^*𝒦 = f^*𝒦` on a resolving class, at free and unrelated
universes for the two ringed topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06YY], exactness, for a morphism of ringed topoi.** The derived pullback
`Lf^* : D(𝒪_D) ⟶ D(𝒪_C)` is a triangulated functor. Every morphism of `D(𝒪_D)` is, up to
isomorphism, the image of a morphism between K-flat complexes with flat terms; its mapping cone
is again such a complex, and on such complexes `Lf^*` is computed by the degreewise pullback,
which carries the mapping-cone triangle to a distinguished triangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullback_isTriangulated :
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback f).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment:
exactness of the derived pullback, for a morphism of ringed topoi whose geometric
datum is a morphism of the underlying topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction.derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the derived pullback functor.**  The derived pullback `Lf^* : D(𝒪') ⥤ D(𝒪)`, the
total left derived functor of degreewise pullback followed by localization.

The instance argument is discharged for every morphism of ringed topoi by
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOnRingedTopoi.hasLeftDerivedFunctor_pullbackOnHomotopy`, so
this is the functor Tag 06YY asserts to exist.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev derivedPullback :
    DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction.derivedPullbackComparison
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06YY, the canonical comparison.**  The comparison `Lf^* ⟶ f^*` from the derived
pullback to degreewise pullback, whose invertibility on K-flat complexes with flat terms is the
computation assertion of Tag 06YY.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev derivedPullbackComparison :
    DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ derivedPullback f ⟶ pullbackOnHomotopy f

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.pullbackInvertsQuasiIso_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
**The exactness clause of Stacks 06YY for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi.**
Degreewise pullback along `f` carries a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of
`O`-modules with flat terms to an isomorphism of `D(O')`.

The cone of such a quasi-isomorphism is acyclic and is again K-flat with flat terms, so its
degreewise pullback is acyclic; the conclusion is then read off the image of the mapping-cone
triangle under the triangulated functor `K(f^*)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackInvertsQuasiIso_isKFlat (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    PullbackInvertsQuasiIso f (IsKFlat (Y := Y))
declarations.comment:
exactness on K-flat complexes with flat terms, for an arbitrary morphism of
ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**The unit of the derived Spec–Γ adjunction is invertible.** For every object `M` of `D(R)`
the canonical map `M ⟶ RΓ(Spec R, M^~)` is an isomorphism.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_unit_app_of_quasiIso` fed
with unbounded affine vanishing for the complexes `M̃^•`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiIso_globalSectionsOver_map_tilde`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_unit :
    IsIso (derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction R).val.unit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Derived sheafification is an equivalence** `D(R) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`. This is the
remaining content of [Stacks, Tag 06Z0] for the two edges `~` and (06VT) of its triangle.

Derived sheafification is exact and fully faithful, and its right adjoint, derived global
sections, has zero kernel; by [Stacks, Tag 09J1] that is enough.
declarations.statement: instance derivedTilde_isEquivalence : (derivedTilde R).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsQuasicoherent_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Unbounded derived global sections `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R}) ⥤ D(R)` is an equivalence**, being
right adjoint to the equivalence `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde`. This is the `RΓ(X, -)` edge of
the triangle of [Stacks, Tag 06Z0].
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedGlobalSectionsQuasicoherent_isEquivalence :
    (derivedGlobalSectionsQuasicoherent R).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_counit_app
declarations.doc:
**The counit of the derived Spec–Γ adjunction is invertible on `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`.** For
every object `E` of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})` with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves the canonical map
`RΓ(Spec R, E)^~ ⟶ E` is an isomorphism.

The left adjoint `derivedTilde R ⋙ ι` is fully faithful, the unit being invertible, so its counit
is invertible exactly on its essential image; and `E` is in that essential image because derived
sheafification is essentially surjective onto `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`. The restriction to objects
with quasi-coherent cohomology cannot be dropped: `RΓ(Spec R, E)^~ ⟶ E` fails to be invertible as
soon as some cohomology sheaf of `E` is not quasi-coherent, which is why the adjunction itself is
not an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_counit_app
    (E : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory) :
    IsIso ((derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction R).val.counit.app
      ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).ι.obj E))

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The comparison functor of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] is an equivalence on an affine scheme.** The
canonical functor `D(QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})` is an equivalence of triangulated
categories.

This is the first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 08D9] part (3). It is
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedTilde_isEquivalence_iff_comparison` applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde_isEquivalence`: the `~` edge of [Stacks, Tag 06Z0] is an
equivalence of abelian categories, so the comparison functor is an equivalence exactly when
derived sheafification is.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence (R : CommRingCat.{u}) :
    (derivedQuasicoherentComparison.{u} (Spec R)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDerivedSections.full_derivedSectionsLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The left adjoint of `RΓ(S, -)` is full on an affine scheme**; see
`derivedSectionsLeftAdjointFullyFaithful`.
declarations.statement:
instance full_derivedSectionsLeftAdjoint :
    (derivedBaseExtension S.toRingedSpace).Full
declarations.comment: the left adjoint of derived global sections is fully faithful on an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDerivedSections.faithful_derivedSectionsLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The left adjoint of `RΓ(S, -)` is faithful on an affine scheme**; see
`derivedSectionsLeftAdjointFullyFaithful`.
declarations.statement:
instance faithful_derivedSectionsLeftAdjoint :
    (derivedBaseExtension S.toRingedSpace).Faithful
declarations.comment: the left adjoint of derived global sections is fully faithful on an affine scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDerivedSections.essImage_derivedSectionsLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Every complex of `𝒪_S`-modules with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves is in the essential
image of the left adjoint of `RΓ(S, -)`,** `S` being affine. This is the predicate
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsQCohAll` of the Künneth development, written out.

Pulling `U` back along `S ≅ Spec Γ(S, 𝒪_S)` keeps the cohomology sheaves quasi-coherent, by
[Stacks, Tag 08DW] part (1); over `Spec Γ(S, 𝒪_S)` the result is a derived sheafification by
[Stacks, Tag 06Z0], `AlgebraicGeometry.StandardModel.exists_iso_mapDerivedCategory`; and pushing
that back through `derivedSectionsLeftAdjointIso` and the round trip of the derived pullbacks
along the two directions of the isomorphism exhibits `U` itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_derivedSectionsLeftAdjoint
    (U : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)))
    (hU : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)) j).obj U).IsQuasicoherent) :
    (derivedBaseExtension S.toRingedSpace).essImage U
declarations.comment: the essential image of that left adjoint is the quasi-coherent part

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedTildeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z0 (the tilde edge).** For `X = Spec A` the functor `M ↦ M^~` is an
equivalence of triangulated categories from `D(A)` to `D(QCoh(𝒪_X))`. This is the arrow labelled
`~` in the triangle of Stacks 06Z0; the other two edges, the functor (06VT) and `RΓ(X, -)`, are
not treated here.

The underlying functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv.functor.mapDerivedCategory`, by
definition.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTildeEquiv : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ≌
    DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_isAffine_atModel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 06Z0].** For every affine scheme `X` the comparison functor
`i_X : D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] is an equivalence of triangulated
categories, at every choice of the two derived categories.

`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence` is this statement for `Spec R`
at the locally small model. An affine scheme is isomorphic to `Spec Γ(X, ⊤)` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isoSpec`, and transporting along that isomorphism simultaneously changes
the scheme and the model.

`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_isAffine` is this statement
at the locally small model alone, that is the case `w = u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence_of_isAffine_atModel (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsAffine X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory] :
    (derivedQuasicoherentComparison.{w} X).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: comparison equivalence, any affine scheme at any model

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Z0, degree-zero cohomology.** On an affine scheme the degree-zero cohomology of
derived global sections is the global sections of the degree-zero cohomology sheaf:
`H⁰(RΓ(Spec R, E)) ≅ Γ(Spec R, H⁰(E))` for `E` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`, naturally in `E`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsQuasicoherentCompHomologyIso` in degree zero. Its
normalization on global cycles, which pins it down uniquely, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.globalSectionsCyclesToHomology_comp_derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso :
    derivedGlobalSectionsQuasicoherent R ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0 ≅
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).ι ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Spec R).Modules 0 ⋙
          globalSectionsOver (𝟙 (Spec R))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.globalSectionsCyclesToHomology_comp_derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Z0, the canonical degree-zero comparison.** The degree-zero identification
`H⁰(RΓ(Spec R, E)) ≅ Γ(Spec R, H⁰(E))` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso` sends a global cycle of a complex `K`
with quasi-coherent cohomology to its section of the degree-zero cohomology sheaf: the composite
`Γ(Spec R, Z⁰(K)) ⟶ H⁰(Γ(Spec R, K)) ⟶ H⁰(RΓ(Spec R, Q K)) ⟶ Γ(Spec R, H⁰(Q K)) ⟶
Γ(Spec R, H⁰(K))` is `Γ(Spec R, -)` applied to `K.homologyπ 0`.

Together with naturality this characterizes the isomorphism:
`AlgebraicGeometry.globalSectionsCyclesToHomology` is an epimorphism, being the isomorphism
`Γ(Z⁰(K)) ≅ Z⁰(Γ(K))` followed by `HomologicalComplex.homologyπ`. The content is
`AlgebraicGeometry.globalSectionsHomologyComparison_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem globalSectionsCyclesToHomology_comp_derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso
    (K : CochainComplex (Spec R).Modules ℤ)
    (hK : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) :
    globalSectionsCyclesToHomology (𝟙 (Spec R)) K 0 ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).inv.app
          (((globalSectionsOver (𝟙 (Spec R))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).map
          (globalSectionsComplexComparison (𝟙 (Spec R)) K) ≫
        (derivedGlobalSectionsHomologyZeroIso R).hom.app ⟨DerivedCategory.Q.obj K, hK⟩ ≫
        (globalSectionsOver (𝟙 (Spec R))).map
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (Spec R).Modules 0).hom.app K) =
      (globalSectionsOver (𝟙 (Spec R))).map (K.homologyπ 0)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_counit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06Z0, the counit clause.** On an affine scheme the counit of the canonical derived
sheafification–sections adjunction is invertible at every object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`: derived
sheafification recovers a complex with quasi-coherent cohomology from its derived global
sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction_counit_isIso (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] :
    let _inst : HasDerivedCategory (Spec R).Modules := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    ∀ E : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      IsIso ((derivedTildeGlobalSectionsAdjunction R).val.counit.app
        ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).ι.obj E))

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.exists_adequate_homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z6.** For every module-valued functor `F` there is an adequate
functor `Q F` and a morphism `Q F ⟶ F` of module-valued functors such that every morphism to `F`
from an adequate functor factors uniquely through it.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_adequate_homEquiv
    (F : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1) w, v} A) :
    ∃ (QF : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1) w, v} A)
      (_ : IsAdequate (𝟭 _) QF) (q : QF ⟶ F),
      ∀ (G : ModuleValuedFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1) w, v} A), IsAdequate (𝟭 _) G →
        ∀ φ : G ⟶ F, ∃! ψ : G ⟶ QF, ψ ≫ q = φ

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.moduleValuedFunctor_enoughInjectives
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7.** Module-valued functors on any category of algebras, in
particular the algebras admitted by a big site, have enough injectives.
declarations.statement:
instance moduleValuedFunctor_enoughInjectives (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]
    (R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{w}) :
    EnoughInjectives (PresheafOfModules.{max u v w t} R)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.fullyFaithful_adequateInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (1), the full faithfulness of `i`. The adequate functors
form a full subcategory of the module-valued functors, so their inclusion is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithful_adequateInclusion :
    (adequate.{u, v, max u v w} A).ι.FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.preservesFiniteLimits_adequateInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (1), the left exactness of `i`. The adequate functors are
closed under kernels, so a kernel of adequate functors is already the kernel of the underlying
module-valued functors.
declarations.statement:
public lemma preservesFiniteLimits_adequateInclusion :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (adequate.{u, v, max u v w} A).ι

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.preservesFiniteColimits_adequateInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (1), the right exactness of `i`. The adequate functors are
closed under cokernels, so a cokernel of adequate functors is already the cokernel of the
underlying module-valued functors.
declarations.statement:
public lemma preservesFiniteColimits_adequateInclusion :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (adequate.{u, v, max u v w} A).ι

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.adequateCoreflectionAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (3), the adjunction itself: the functor `Q` of
[Stacks, Tag 06Z6] is a right adjoint to the inclusion `i` of the adequate module-valued
functors into all module-valued functors.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def adequateCoreflectionAdjunction :
    (adequate.{u, v, max (u + 1) (v + 1) w} A).ι ⊣ adequateCoreflection.{u, v, w} A
declarations.comment: part (3), Q is a right adjoint to i

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.preservesFiniteLimits_adequateCoreflection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (3), the left exactness: a right adjoint preserves all
limits, in particular the finite ones.
declarations.statement:
public lemma preservesFiniteLimits_adequateCoreflection :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (adequateCoreflection.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.preservesInjectiveObjects_adequateCoreflection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (4). The functor `Q` transforms injectives into
injectives: it is right adjoint to the exact functor `i`, so [Stacks, Tag 015Z] applies.
declarations.statement:
public lemma preservesInjectiveObjects_adequateCoreflection :
    (adequateCoreflection.{u, v, w} A).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.adequateFunctor_enoughInjectives
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7.** The adequate module-valued functors on the commutative
`A`-algebras have enough injectives: every one of them embeds into the extension of a pure
injective `A`-module, and such an extension is an injective object.
declarations.statement:
public instance adequateFunctor_enoughInjectives {A : Type u} [CommRing A] :
    EnoughInjectives ((adequate.{u, v, max u v w} A).FullSubcategory)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.adequate_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (1), the image of `i` is a weak Serre subcategory. The
adequate module-valued functors are a strictly full subcategory containing the zero functor and
closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions, which is the characterisation of a weak Serre
subcategory of [Stacks, Tag 0754].
declarations.statement:
public instance adequate_isWeakSerreClass :
    (adequate.{u, u, u} A).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (1), the image of i is a weak Serre subcategory

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.adequateInclusion_fullyFaithful_exact_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 06Z7**, part (1), in full and at one instantiation: the inclusion `i`
of the adequate module-valued functors into all module-valued functors on `Alg_A` is fully
faithful and exact, and its image is a weak Serre subcategory.

The three conjuncts other than the last are instantiations of
`AdequateFunctor.fullyFaithful_adequateInclusion`,
`AdequateFunctor.preservesFiniteLimits_adequateInclusion` and
`AdequateFunctor.preservesFiniteColimits_adequateInclusion`, which hold at the wider
`adequate.{u, v, max u v w}`; the last holds at the universes of
`AdequateFunctor.isAdequate_of_shortExact`. This conjunction records that all four are
simultaneously available for one and the same category, namely the module-valued functors on the
`A`-algebras whose carriers lie in the universe of `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adequateInclusion_fullyFaithful_exact_isWeakSerreClass :
    (adequate.{u, u, u} A).ι.Full ∧ (adequate.{u, u, u} A).ι.Faithful ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits (adequate.{u, u, u} A).ι ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (adequate.{u, u, u} A).ι ∧
      (adequate.{u, u, u} A).IsWeakSerreClass

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentKernel
declarations.doc: The tangent kernel, with scalars restricted along the zero section `B → B[N]`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentKernel (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A) :
    Submodule X.algebra (extensionValue A F X)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2): the kernel with its restricted module structure

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentFunctor
declarations.doc: The canonical tangent functor on pairs of algebras and modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tangentFunctor : TangentFunctorData A F

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentDecompositionData
declarations.doc:
The canonical decomposition, specified by the sum of the zero section and the kernel
inclusion as its inverse.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentDecompositionData (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A) :
    TangentDecompositionData A F X

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentMultiplicationData
declarations.doc: Multiplication by the square-zero ideal, specified on pure tensors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentMultiplicationData (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A) :
    {μ : TensorProduct X.algebra X.module (moduleValue A F X.algebra) →ₗ[X.algebra]
        tangentModule A F X //
      ∀ (n : X.module) (y : moduleValue A F X.algebra),
        (μ (TensorProduct.tmul X.algebra n y) : extensionValue A F X) =
          squareZeroInr A X n •
            moduleValueMap A F (squareZeroSection A X) y}

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentDecomposition_fst
declarations.doc: The first coordinate of the canonical decomposition is the augmentation.
declarations.statement:
lemma tangentDecomposition_fst (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A) (x : extensionValue A F X) :
    (tangentDecomposition A F X x).1 =
      moduleValueMap A F (squareZeroAugmentation A X) x
declarations.comment: the augmentation coordinate of the decomposition

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentDecomposition_naturality
declarations.doc: The decomposition is natural for morphisms of pairs, including changes of base algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma tangentDecomposition_naturality {X Y : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (x : extensionValue A F X) :
    tangentDecomposition A F Y (moduleValueMap A F (squareZeroMap A f) x) =
      (moduleValueMap A F f.base (tangentDecomposition A F X x).1,
        (tangentFunctor A F).map f (tangentDecomposition A F X x).2)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentMultiplication_naturality
declarations.doc: The multiplication maps form a natural transformation on the category of pairs.
declarations.statement:
lemma tangentMultiplication_naturality {X Y : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (t : TensorProduct X.algebra X.module (moduleValue A F X.algebra)) :
    (tangentFunctor A F).map f (tangentMultiplication A F X t) =
      tangentMultiplication A F Y
        (TensorProduct.map f.linear (moduleValueMap A F f.base) t)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentModule_subsingleton
declarations.doc: The tangent module of a zero module is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma tangentModule_subsingleton (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A) [Subsingleton X.module] :
    Subsingleton (tangentModule A F X)
declarations.comment: part (5): vanishing at the zero module

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentFunctor_map_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A morphism of pairs whose module map is zero induces the zero tangent map.
declarations.statement:
lemma tangentFunctor_map_eq_zero {X Y : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f.linear = 0) : (tangentFunctor A F).map f = 0
declarations.comment: part (5): zero module maps induce zero tangent maps

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.epi_tangentFunctorAt_map_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Tag 06ZA, corrected.  Stacks erratum.**  Let `I` be an
injective object of the category of module-valued functors on `Alg_A`.  For every `A`-algebra
`B` and every short exact sequence `0 → N₁ → N → N₂ → 0` of `B`-modules, the map
`TI(B, N) → TI(B, N₂)` is an epimorphism.

The source asserts more: that the whole sequence `TI(B, N₁) → TI(B, N) → TI(B, N₂) → 0` is
exact, which in this library is the predicate `AdequateFunctor.HasRightExactTangentFunctor`
of Tag 06ZF.  **The other conjunct, exactness at `TI(B, N)`, is false**, and is refuted by
`AdequateFunctor.not_forall_hasRightExactTangentFunctor_of_injective`: the counterexample
takes the field `k = ℚ`, the algebra `C = k[ε]/(ε²)`, the injective `C`-module
`J = Hom_k(C, k)` and the coinduced functor `I(D) = ∏_{α : D →ₐ C} J`, whose tangent module
`TI(k, V)` is the functions `V^* → J` vanishing at `0`; on `0 → k → k² → k → 0` the function
sending the first-coordinate functional to `0 ≠ j ∈ J` and everything else to `0` is killed
by `TI(k, k²) → TI(k, k)` and is not in the image of `TI(k, k) → TI(k, k²)`, every element of
which takes equal values at `(1, 0)` and `(1, 1)`.

Surjectivity at `TI(B, N₂)` — the statement proved here, and the whole of what the source's
assertion leaves standing — is unaffected: its proof does not use the coequalizer step that
the counterexample refutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_tangentFunctorAt_map_of_injective
    (I : PresheafOfModules.{v} (algebraStructurePresheaf.{v} A)) [Injective I]
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{v} B))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    Epi ((tangentFunctorAt A I B).map S.g)
declarations.comment: Stacks erratum: only the surjectivity at `TI(B, N₂)`. Exactness at `TI(B, N)`, the other conjunct of the source's assertion that `TI(B,N₁) → TI(B,N) → TI(B,N₂) → 0` is exact, is false as stated, and is refuted by `AdequateFunctor.not_forall_hasRightExactTangentFunctor_of_injective`. The module universe of `I` is taken to be the universe of the algebras.

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentTensorEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical tensor-product description of the tangent module of a
finitely presented module, using the second action on both tangent modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentTensorEquiv
    (S : RightExactTangentFunctor.{u, v, w})
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra S.A B]
    (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation B N] :
    let X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A := { algebra := B, module := B }
    let Y : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A := { algebra := B, module := N }
    letI : Module B (tangentModule S.A S.F X) :=
      (secondModuleStructure S X).1
    letI : Module B (tangentModule S.A S.F Y) :=
      (secondModuleStructure S Y).1
    { e : TensorProduct B (tangentModule S.A S.F X) N ≃ₗ[B]
        tangentModule S.A S.F Y //
      ∀ (x : tangentModule S.A S.F X) (n : N),
        e (TensorProduct.tmul B x n) =
          (tangentFunctor S.A S.F).map
            ({ base := AlgHom.id S.A B
               linear := (LinearMap.id : B →ₗ[B] B).smulRight n } : X ⟶ Y) x }

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentModule_prod_bijective
declarations.doc:
A right exact tangent functor carries a binary direct sum of modules to
the direct sum of their tangent modules, via the two projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem tangentModule_prod_bijective
    (T : RightExactTangentFunctor.{u, v, w})
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra T.A B]
    (N₁ N₂ : Type v) [AddCommGroup N₁] [Module B N₁]
    [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module B N₂] :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun x : tangentModule T.A T.F
          ({ algebra := B, module := N₁ × N₂ } : AlgebraModulePair.{v} T.A) =>
        ((tangentFunctor T.A T.F).map
            ({ base := AlgHom.id T.A B
               linear := LinearMap.fst B N₁ N₂ } :
              ({ algebra := B, module := N₁ × N₂ } : AlgebraModulePair.{v} T.A) ⟶
              ({ algebra := B, module := N₁ } : AlgebraModulePair.{v} T.A)) x,
         (tangentFunctor T.A T.F).map
            ({ base := AlgHom.id T.A B
               linear := LinearMap.snd B N₁ N₂ } :
              ({ algebra := B, module := N₁ × N₂ } : AlgebraModulePair.{v} T.A) ⟶
              ({ algebra := B, module := N₂ } : AlgebraModulePair.{v} T.A)) x))

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.secondModuleStructure
declarations.doc:
The second module structure on a tangent module, characterized by the
action induced by multiplication on the module variable.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def secondModuleStructure (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A) :
    { m : Module X.algebra (tangentModule S.A S.F X) //
      ∀ (b : X.algebra) (x : tangentModule S.A S.F X),
        m.toDistribMulAction.toSMul.smul b x =
          secondScalarAction S.A S.F X x b }

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.secondScalarAction_naturality
declarations.doc:
Tangent maps commute with the second scalar action, semilinearly over
their maps of base algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem secondScalarAction_naturality {X Y : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : tangentModule S.A S.F X) (b : X.algebra) :
    (tangentFunctor S.A S.F).map f (secondScalarAction S.A S.F X x b) =
      secondScalarAction S.A S.F Y ((tangentFunctor S.A S.F).map f x) (f.base b)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentMultiplication_smul_second
declarations.doc:
The canonical tangent multiplication map is linear for the second
`B`-module structure on the tangent module.
declarations.statement:
theorem tangentMultiplication_smul_second (S : RightExactTangentFunctor.{u, v, w})
    (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A) (b : X.algebra)
    (t : TensorProduct X.algebra X.module (moduleValue S.A S.F X.algebra)) :
    (secondModuleStructure S X).val.toDistribMulAction.toSMul.smul b
        (tangentMultiplication S.A S.F X t) =
      tangentMultiplication S.A S.F X (b • t)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.secondScalarAction
declarations.doc:
The second scalar operation on a tangent module, induced by multiplication
on the module variable.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def secondScalarAction (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} A)
    (x : tangentModule A F X) (b : X.algebra) : tangentModule A F X

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentMultiplication_smul_second
declarations.doc:
The canonical tangent multiplication map is linear for the second
`B`-module structure on the tangent module.
declarations.statement:
theorem tangentMultiplication_smul_second (S : RightExactTangentFunctor.{u, v, w})
    (X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A) (b : X.algebra)
    (t : TensorProduct X.algebra X.module (moduleValue S.A S.F X.algebra)) :
    (secondModuleStructure S X).val.toDistribMulAction.toSMul.smul b
        (tangentMultiplication S.A S.F X t) =
      tangentMultiplication S.A S.F X (b • t)

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.tangentTensorEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical tensor-product description of the tangent module of a
finitely presented module, using the second action on both tangent modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tangentTensorEquiv
    (S : RightExactTangentFunctor.{u, v, w})
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra S.A B]
    (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation B N] :
    let X : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A := { algebra := B, module := B }
    let Y : AlgebraModulePair.{v} S.A := { algebra := B, module := N }
    letI : Module B (tangentModule S.A S.F X) :=
      (secondModuleStructure S X).1
    letI : Module B (tangentModule S.A S.F Y) :=
      (secondModuleStructure S Y).1
    { e : TensorProduct B (tangentModule S.A S.F X) N ≃ₗ[B]
        tangentModule S.A S.F Y //
      ∀ (x : tangentModule S.A S.F X) (n : N),
        e (TensorProduct.tmul B x n) =
          (tangentFunctor S.A S.F).map
            ({ base := AlgHom.id S.A B
               linear := (LinearMap.id : B →ₗ[B] B).smulRight n } : X ⟶ Y) x }

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.rightExactTangentFunctor_of_shortExact
declarations.doc: Property `(*)` is stable under extensions of module-valued functors.
declarations.statement:

Property `(*)` passes to the quotient in a short exact sequence of

Property `(*)` passes to a pullback of a short exact sequence of
